spec.name: Madreperla Piano Accordion
spec.description: A full-size 41-key, 120-bass piano accordion in Italian mother-of-pearl style: iridescent pearl-mosaic cases trimmed in gold and chrome, gold fan grilles, and a ruby-red gold-edged bellows, shown on the floor with its straps.
spec.layout: STATIC OBJECT, no joints. It stands on y=0 on its two case bottoms, bellows axis along X, in a symmetric composition. The front (+Z) is the grille side, shown to the audience. The treble (right-hand) case sits at -X with the 41-key piano keyboard on its -X end face. The bass (left-hand) case sits at +X with the 120 bass buttons on its +X end face. The bellows spans x -0.14..+0.14 between them, a little open. The back (-Z) carries straps and hardware, which stand 0.05 m out. Heights: treble case 0.54, bass case 0.50, bellows 0.02..0.49, so the silhouette steps down from treble to bass. Cases are 0.30 deep (z -0.15..0.15), 0.21 wide each. The Italian mother-of-pearl style shows in four ways. (1) Every case surface (top, bottom, back, front bezel, end-plate margins) is a pearl MOSAIC: a base slab in pearlShadow, covered with small raised tiles about 0.035 x 0.03 m and 2 mm thick, with 1-2 mm gaps showing the base. Tile colours are chosen deterministically by rng: 50% pearlWhite, 20% pearlCream, 10% each of pearlPink, pearlAqua and pearlLilac. Both cases use this same rule so they read as one set. (2) Every case edge has gold piping (thin 6 mm rods in goldBright) with goldDeep shadow rods beside it. Rhinestones (rhinestoneBlue and rhinestoneRose) sit as small faceted gems at the case corners and the grille centres. (3) The grilles are gold slats on a dark grilleBack recess, with a rosette in the middle. (4) The bellows is ruby red with gold-leaf edging and gold-and-pearl corner guards. Chrome is used for switches, buckles and hooks. Keep every shape simple and blocky: boxes, wedges, short cylinders of 6-10 sides. All the character comes from small coloured parts seated on the faces.

parts.builds: The right-hand (treble) case, a blocky box x -0.35..-0.14, y 0..0.54, z -0.15..0.15. It is pearl-mosaic covered on top, bottom, back and the -X end margins (the keyboard part sits on the -X face at x=-0.35, so leave the keyboard window x -0.35, y 0.03..0.51, z -0.115..0.115 free; mosaic tiles surround it). The bellows-side face at x=-0.14 is a plain pearlCream frame lip 0.012 m deep, which the bellows end frame meets. FRONT +Z: an inset pearl bezel and a dark grilleBack recess about 0.17 wide x 0.44 tall. In the recess sit about 13 goldBright slats radiating as a fan from a point near the bottom centre, each a thin 6-sided rod or box, with a goldDeep shadow slat under alternating ones. A rosette in the middle is a stack of goldBright and goldDeep 10-sided discs with a rhinestoneBlue centre. A labelCream nameplate reading 'BELLINI' (a small gold-bordered plate with tiny black bar glyphs for letters) sits below it on the bezel. TOP (+Y): a chrome register-switch bank at trebleTopSwitches, a 0.12 x 0.05 chrome plate with 6 pearlWhite rocker tabs, each with a tiny goldBright dot, and one larger master switch. Gold piping on every case edge and a rhinestone at each of the 4 top corners and 4 bottom corners, alternating rhinestoneBlue and rhinestoneRose. Four small black rubber feet (0.012 high) are sunk into the bottom so the case rests on y=0. BACK -Z: a goldDeep serial plate and two chrome strap hooks' base plates at shoulderStrapTopA/B and shoulderStrapBottomA/B (the harness part builds the straps themselves). Keep mosaic tiles merged by colour to save parts.
parts.attaches: The keyboard part sits on the -X face (mount keyboardPlane). The bellows meets the +X face at trebleBellowsFace. The harness hooks at the shoulderStrapTop/Bottom mounts on the back face.

parts.builds: The 41-key piano keyboard on the treble case's -X end face. It is a mother-of-pearl-framed keybed: 24 white keys (keyWhite) and 17 black keys (keyBlack). Keys are 0.02 pitch along Y, starting at y=0.03 (the lowest key) up to y=0.51. White keys are boxes about 0.0185 tall (y) x 0.20 long (z -0.10..0.10) x 0.03 thick (x -0.385..-0.355), with 1.5 mm gaps between them showing the felt keybed. Black keys follow the standard grouping (2 black, gap, 3 black, gap, repeating, starting after the first white key as an F-sharp pattern). Each is 0.011 tall (y), 0.11 long (z, sitting on the +Z half: z -0.01..0.10), and 0.045 thick (x -0.40..-0.355). Each black key has a thin chromeDark highlight strip on its top face and its tip is slightly bevelled with a wedge. The keybed is a felt slab (x -0.355..-0.35, y 0.03..0.51, z -0.115..0.115). Framing it: a goldBright rail along the top and bottom ends (y 0.51..0.52 and 0.02..0.03), a pearl-mosaic cap rail along the back z -0.115..-0.125 and along the front z 0.115..0.125 (pearlCream tiles with gold piping, using the same mosaic rule as the cases), and tiny rhinestones at the 4 corners of the frame. A thin labelCream key-cover felt strip with a goldDeep line sits between the keys and the +Z rail. Optionally include small goldBright pitch-marker dots on every C white key's end.
parts.attaches: Sits flush on the treble case -X face at keyboardPlane; its back x=-0.35 touches the case. The top and bottom rails stay inside the case's y range.

parts.builds: The ruby-red folding bellows between the cases, x -0.14..0.14, y 0.02..0.49, z -0.125..0.125, with corner guards reaching 0.13. It is slightly open, with 13 pleats. Each pleat is a sharp V crest, ridge at the full outline (z +-0.125, y 0.02..0.49), valley inset 0.02 m on all four sides. Build each as 4 thin tapered slabs per side or as rectangular loft rings alternating bellowsRed (outer faces), bellowsRedLight (top-facing facets) and bellowsRedDark (valley faces), so every crest reads as a ridge. Along each crest edge a thin goldBright wire (4 mm rod) runs round all four sides, and gold leaf dots sit in every other valley on the front. The four long corners of the bellows each carry corner guards, one every 0.04 m along X: small pearlCream-and-goldBright L-shaped brackets (a box 0.012 x 0.02 and a gold rivet) over the crests, so the corner reads as a gold-and-pearl bound edge. Each end has a pearlCream end frame, a rectangular ring 0.01 deep at x=-0.14 and x=+0.14, with goldBright piping and a thin black felt gasket line. Black reinforcing tape lines run along the top of the bellows on the valley folds. On the front +Z face of the bellows, a centred gold diamond lozenge motif made of 3 small gold diamond extrudes sits at x=0 on the centre pleat, flanked by 2 rhinestoneRose gems.
parts.attaches: End frames meet the treble case at trebleBellowsFace (x=-0.14) and the bass case at bassBellowsFace (x=0.14). The harness bellows strap lies across its top near x=-0.06..0.2.

parts.builds: The left-hand (bass) case, a blocky box x 0.14..0.35, y 0..0.50, z -0.15..0.15, built in the same pearl-mosaic rule and gold piping as the treble case (tile ~0.035, 2 mm raised, same colour split) on top, bottom, back and front bezel. The bellows-side face at x=0.14 is a plain pearlCream lip 0.012 deep. FRONT +Z: an inset pearl bezel and grilleBack recess 0.17 x 0.40, filled with about 9 horizontal-ish goldBright slats (a ladder pattern, slightly fanned) and a smaller rosette with a rhinestoneRose centre. END FACE +X (x=0.35, bassButtonPlane): a pearl-mosaic margin framing a dark felt recess plate, 0.25 (z) x 0.46 (y). It carries 120 bass buttons in 6 rows (z -0.09..+0.09, 0.036 pitch) of 20 (y 0.03..0.47, 0.022 pitch). Each is an 8-sided cylinder, radius 0.0085, height 0.012, projecting to x~0.362 (the part's box reaches 0.38 to allow a little button travel clearance): pearlWhite for most, chrome for the C buttons (every 3rd column in rows 3-4) and goldBright for the E buttons in rows 5-6; each button has a thin chromeDark ring base disc. All buttons of one colour are merged into one part. An air-release button sits at the top rear of the end plate (y 0.478, z -0.10): a red bellowsRedLight disc in a goldBright ring. The case has a top gold piping, rhinestones at its 8 corners (rhinestoneBlue and rhinestoneRose alternating), four black rubber feet sunk into the bottom so the case rests on y=0, and a small goldDeep brand plate on the back. On the back face, a pearl-mosaic region leaves the strap pad area at bassStrapPad free for the harness.
parts.attaches: Bellows end frame meets the -X face at bassBellowsFace (x=0.14). The harness hand-strap pad and bellows strap anchor are on its back and top at bassStrapPad and bellowsStrapAnchor. Buttons rise from the plate at bassButtonPlane (x=0.35).

parts.builds: All the straps and the hardware on them, kept to the back (-Z, out to z=-0.20) and the bellows top. (a) Two shoulder straps, each 0.045 wide and 0.008 thick strapBlack, with stitched goldDeep edge lines and a thin chromeDark centre line. Each runs from its top hook (shoulderStrapTopA/B, on the treble case top at y 0.54) in a loose arc out to z -0.19 and back down to its bottom hook (shoulderStrapBottomA/B at y 0.04 on the back). The lowest point stays at y>=0.015. Each has a chrome slide buckle (a rectangular frame with a bar) at mid-height and a leather end tab with 3 small chrome rivets. Hooks are chrome U-shapes seated on the base plates the treble case builds. Build the arcs as a sweep over a catmull path or as a few segmented boxes. (b) The bass hand-strap: a leather pad (box 0.07 wide x 0.20 tall x 0.02 thick, in leather) centred at bassStrapPad on the back of the bass case, with a strapBlack strap across it, a chrome buckle, gold stitching dots along both edges, and two chrome mounting rivets at each end. (c) The bellows strap: strapBlack, 0.03 wide, anchored on the bass case top at bellowsStrapAnchor on a chrome base plate. It runs along the bellows top (y~0.495, x 0.2 to -0.06) lying flat, ending in a leather tab at bellowsStrapKeeper with a chrome snap stud, and a chrome buckle at x~0.10. A small goldBright tassel (a cone with a 6-sided cap and 3 short rods) hangs from the buckle toward +Z off the bellows front edge. (d) a tiny labelCream tag on the left shoulder strap with a black dot pattern.
parts.attaches: Hooks sit on the treble back plates at shoulderStrapTopA/B and shoulderStrapBottomA/B. The hand strap pad sits on the bass back at bassStrapPad. The bellows strap starts at bellowsStrapAnchor on the bass top and ends at bellowsStrapKeeper on the bellows top.

calls.reasoning:
I'm designing a spec for a piano accordion in an Italian mother-of-pearl style, keeping it as a static object with no joints since it's just a prop. I'm working out realistic proportions, figuring roughly 0.40 m width, and thinking through how it would stand or be positioned on the floor.

Now I'm working out the model's orientation -- deciding whether the bellows axis runs along X with the bass end facing -X and the treble keyboard facing +X, and how the front grille and keyboard would face relative to the +Z direction to match a natural playing position.

I'm working out the keyboard orientation on the treble end face—trying to figure out which direction the keys protrude and how pitch ascends, since in actual playing position the fingers approach from one side with the long axis of the keys running toward the player.

I'm still trying to pin down the correct orientation of the keyboard bars—whether the keys' long axis runs front-to-back or toward the player's hand—based on how the keytops appear in real accordion photos, treating the rows as levers angled from a flat surface.

Working out dimensions: white key width times 24 gives roughly 0.5m height, matching real accordion treble cases around 0.45-0.5m tall. I'm settling on both treble and bass boxes at about 0.52m tall, with depth around 0.25-0.30m and a modest bellows length, plus adding straps for realism.

Now I'm placing the two boxes on the floor with the bellows connecting them at the bottom, keyboard on the vertical face, and the grille facing forward toward the audience—working out the x/y/z extents so the treble box sits correctly on the right side.

I'm working out the bass box extent with buttons included, landing on roughly 0.74 x 0.54 depth proportions, then adjusting the z-depth so the boxes and bellows folds with corner guards fit within a total size around [0.74, 0.54, 0.28].

Now I'm placing the shoulder straps and bass strap flush against the back near z -0.145 to -0.16, keeping boxes resting at z -0.15..0.15. For the finish, I'm going with Italian pearl styling: iridescent mother-of-pearl celluloid in cream, pale pink, aqua, and lilac tones with chrome or gold trim and red/black bellows accented by white pearl corners, building the celluloid as a mosaic of subtly varied pearl-color patches.

I'm adding gold filigree details — a fan-slotted grille, rosette, register switches on the treble top, a fictional "Bellini" logo plate, rhinestones, brass corner guards, gold-leaf bellows edges, and a buckled bass-end bellows strap with an air button, plus a 120-button bass side arranged in six rows of round pearl-topped buttons on the +X face.

Now I'm breaking the accordion into separate parts: the treble box with its pearl-shell body, keyboard, top register switches, and front gold fan grille, and the bass box with its own pearl detailing.

Next is the bass button plate, front grille, straps, and air valve button, followed by the red folded bellows with pleated edges, corner guards, strap, and latch. I'm also figuring out how to handle the straps and hardware—shoulder straps, hand strap, bellows strap—since they span multiple boxes, planning to group them into one harness part positioned along the back plane to avoid overlap conflicts.

I'm reconsidering the breakdown: rather than lumping everything into four parts, I could split the treble side into a case (body, grille, top registers, mosaic) and a separate keyboard part (keys and panel projecting outward), giving five parts total—trebleCase, keyboard, bellows, bassCase, and harness—to better separate ownership of ornamental details like pearl mosaic, gold filigree, and rhinestones.

I'm settling on five parts with a rough polygon budget: trebleCase 200, keyboard 120, bellows 220, bassCase (with buttons and grille) 220, and harness (straps, thumb strap, bellows latch) 100, totaling around 860. I'm now working out floor-level coordinates for each case, deciding whether to add small chrome feet or rubber pads at the base so the cases rest properly at y=0.

Now I'm placing the bellows between the two cases, slightly raised off the floor with corner guards and gold edge trim, and starting to lay out the keyboard section projecting off the treble case's face with white and black keys.

I'm working out the orientation of the keyboard — figuring out which side the player sits on and therefore which end of the keys should have the raised black-key portion, so the geometry near the front versus back matches a real piano layout.

I'm working out the treble case layout: front face gets the gold fan-slotted grille, the top face carries the register switches, and pearl paneling wraps around the keyboard end, top, bottom, and back.

Now I'm settling on a limited color palette — soft pearl whites, creams, pinks, aquas and lilacs for the iridescent case, warm golds for the grille and trim, chrome tones for hardware, and deep reds for the bellows, plus black and key colors for contrast.

I'm also working out the positioning coordinates for key components like the bellows faces, keyboard plane, and bass button plane, figuring out where each piece sits relative to the case geometry.

Now I'm working out the harness strap placement — anchoring shoulder straps to the treble case back at top and bottom points, then draping them as an arc behind the case to approximate how straps hang loosely in a real display mount.

For the bass side, I'm adding a leather hand strap across the back with a buckle, then positioning the bellows strap on the bass case front-lower area with a chrome clasp and loose hanging tail, matching how the real accordion's bellows strap would sit when open.

I should fix the layout to be symmetric around x=0: treble case spanning -0.35 to -0.14 with keys to -0.38, bellows centered from -0.14 to 0.14, and bass from 0.14 to 0.35 with buttons extending to 0.38.

For the bellows itself, I'm planning 14 folds across a 0.28 length, each rendered as paired tapered slabs forming alternating ridges and valleys, with crests scaled outward and valleys inset slightly, colored in alternating red tones with gold accents on the ridges to match the Italian accordion aesthetic.

I'm also adding corner guards — gold or chrome plates with rivet details at the bellows corners — plus pearl-colored end frames where the bellows meets each case, keeping everything static since the instrument doesn't need articulated joints.

For the pearl mosaic pattern, I'm standardizing a tile system across both case boxes: small raised tiles around 0.035 in size, mostly pearl white with a mix of cream, pink, aqua, and lilac accents, separated by thin gaps revealing a shadow underlay, plus rhinestone corners and gold piping along the edges for consistency. For the grille, I'm designing a bezel-framed panel with a recessed dark backing plate and gold bars radiating outward in a fan pattern.

Now I'm fleshing out the treble side's details -- adding a central rosette with a "BELLINI" logo plate, a row of register switches with chrome plate and gold-labeled rocker tabs on top, a decorative gold strip, and on the back a chrome plate with serial number and strap-hook mounts, while laying out coordinate positions for the bellows face mount points.

Adding strap anchor and bellows keeper positions, then working out the keyboard geometry: the box spans roughly y 0.03 to 0.51 giving 24 white keys at about 0.02 spacing, with black keys placed in the standard C#/D# gap, F#/G#/A# pattern between them, plus considering whether a pearl frame should outline the keyboard slot.

Now I'm laying out the keyboard assembly in more detail -- gold rails along the top and bottom edges, a felt key bed, 24 white keys and 17 black keys totaling 41, which checks out. I'm also sketching the bass side case dimensions and figuring the button layout, likely six rows for a standard 120-bass configuration.

Working out button positions and materials...

I'll make the C-note buttons chrome and marked distinctly, keeping the rest pearl white, and merge instances to stay within the part budget. I also need to add the bass air-valve button near the top corner of the button plate as a gold-ringed pearl-red accent, plus gold slats and a rosette on the bass front grille with gold trim along the top.

I'm planning the bellows pleats with gold-wire leaf details, then designing the harness: black shoulder straps with chrome buckles and gold stitching, leather end tabs and hooks, a stitched bass hand strap with chrome buckle, a bellows strap with a snap and small hanging gold tassel, and a "BELLINI" nameplate on the treble side. I'm tallying the part budget, which comes to around 900 total.

Now I'm working out the JSON structure, setting the floor flags for treble and bass true while others stay false, and computing bounding boxes for the harness straps and bellows strap anchors based on their positions along the instrument.

I'm planning a static keyboard build using merged boxes by color, positioning it on the case's -X face with keys extending outward, and working out the spacing for 24 white keys stacked along the Y axis with a 0.02 pitch.

For the black keys, I'm figuring out the F-sharp-starting pattern of sharps/flats across the 24 white keys, checking modular arithmetic on index positions to confirm it yields the correct count of 17 black keys grouped in the standard 3-2-3-2... alternating clusters with gaps for the natural half-steps.

Now I'm thinking through structuring the model as merged geometry boxes without any joint/bone hierarchy, since a static model doesn't require bones.

I'm deciding whether to merge keys by color into just a few parts, or keep them as individual pieces for more detail—given the part budget, merging per color is simpler. I'm also considering adding small design touches like a beveled front lip on the white keys for visual detail where the viewer sees the key ends.

I'm working through the black key geometry now, trying to figure out which axis represents the key's length versus thickness, and where the tip bevel wedge should sit given the ambiguous orientation relative to the player.

Still shaping the wedge geometry...

Shaping the tip wedge...

Now I need to handle merging geometries from different sources—ExtrudeGeometry and BoxGeometry have incompatible structures, so I'm writing a helper to convert everything to non-indexed, strip UV attributes, and combine them with mergeGeometries.

I'm also working out small highlight strip boxes for the black key tops, figuring out thin x-width strips positioned along the z-length to sit on the top face.

Then I'm placing a felt slab box behind the white keys spanning the full y and z range, accounting for the small gaps between keys given their height vs pitch spacing. I'm also setting up the top and bottom rails in gold, deciding their x and y extents relative to the key frame.

Adding the groove line and pearl-mosaic cap rail geometry...

I'll go with the mosaic rule's colour distribution (mostly pearlWhite/cream with small accent percentages) rather than a single pearlCream tile, merging tiles by colour group to keep part count low—roughly 30 tiles per face type across both rails, grouped into about 5 colour parts, each tile a simple 12-triangle box.

Now for the gold piping, I'm thinking through where a thin gold rod can run without eating into the tile space—placing it along the outer corner edge of the rail rather than the inner face so the mosaic still fits within the available width.

Working out the exact placement of the piping rod and tiles on the -X face, trying tight margins around the 0.1155-0.125 z range while keeping everything inside the rail bounds. I decide the rails can be slightly wider since the box limit is ±0.125, and the felt slab spans ±0.115 with cap rails sitting right at the edge from 0.115 to 0.125.

Now I'm sketching the top/bottom rail geometry in gold, spanning z ±0.125 with cap rails running the full y-length, then placing corner rhinestone gems near the four frame corners on the -X rail face to accent the edges.

I'll add tiny rhinestones at the four corners plus small gold dot trim, keeping the rail detailing simple with just a goldDeep groove and gem rather than full rivet rows. I'm also placing a labelCream felt strip with a goldDeep line in the gap between the key ends and the +Z rail, positioned along the case's y-axis span.

I'm checking that the black keys stop at z=0.10 so they don't overlap the key-cover strip starting at 0.1025, which works out fine. I'll skip adding a back felt strip since it's not essential for symmetry, and now I'm thinking about small pitch-marker dots on the C white keys—placing a tiny goldBright cylinder near the exposed end of each white key as a marker.

Adding a bottom shading strip too, though I realize it'll mostly get hidden behind the black keys where they overlap at the boundary—acceptable since it's a minor visual detail.

Thinking about whether to add a thin goldDeep shadow rod filling the gap between the top rail and the topmost key, around y 0.5085–0.51, to make the transition look more grounded; need to check if the same treatment applies at the bottom rail near y 0.03.

Now I'm setting up the mosaic tile system: a seeded RNG picks colors per tile from a palette, with tiles grouped by color into geometry lists, starting with the base slab boxes for the cap rails on each side.

For the y-direction, 15 tiles at 0.032 pitch fit the 0.48 span with 0.03 tile height and 0.002 gaps. For the outer side faces, I'm reworking the z-range so tiles sit just inside the box limit instead of exceeding it — shrinking the base to 0.115-0.123 and placing tiles from 0.123-0.125, then mirroring this approach for the -X face with adjusted x-bounds.

Still working out tile coordinates...

Working out the rail geometry along y 0.03..0.51 with gold top/bottom bands, deciding to keep the piping rod confined to that same y range so it sits cleanly within the rail rather than extending over it. Then placing corner rhinestones near the top rail's -X face, positioned just adjacent to the piping at roughly y=0.515.

Placing the gems using small faceted octahedron-like geometry with alternating colors by z position, mirroring the same setup for the bottom rail at y=0.025. I'm also considering adding a thin goldDeep shadow strip along the rail's -X face as an inlay detail, running the length of the rail at both top and bottom.

Tallying up the parts now — felt, white/black keys, bevel strips, rails, gold inlays, gems, piping, dots — roughly 22 pieces, which feels like a reasonable balance between richness and complexity. I could go further with individual per-key highlights and gloss lines for extra polish since quality is the priority here.

Thinking about small refinements: a thin gold line along the back felt margin, symmetric on both sides, plus tiny gold screw heads on the rails near the ends and center, merged with the deep gold material for consistency.

Writing box helper code...

I need a merge function that normalizes geometries before combining them—converting to non-indexed and stripping UVs so attributes match across box, extrude, cylinder, and icosahedron shapes. I should guard against calling toNonIndexed on already non-indexed geometry since that triggers a warning in newer Three.js versions.

For the black key wedges, I'm defining a tapered shape in local coordinates with absolute x positions and y offsets centered on each key, then extruding it along z with a small depth and positioning it slightly above the white keys.

Now I'm adding a thin darker strip along the top of each black key to catch the light, positioning it to match the wedge's taper near the tip.

I'll settle on a thin highlight strip running along z at x center -0.378, width 0.006, spanning z from 0 to 0.095, and skip adding a second bevel strip. Now I'm working out the y-positions for each white key, placing them with a small gap so the lowest key sits flush against the rail and the top key ends at 0.5085, then moving to figure out the black key placement.

I'm computing the black key centers to align with the gaps between white keys, centering each at roughly 0.04925+0.02i, then moving on to write the tile coloring logic that randomly assigns white, cream, pink, aqua, or lilac tiles, and setting up the loop to place tiles symmetrically on both sides.

Still placing coordinates...

Then I'm adding small pitch dot cylinders along the key edge and bevel highlight/shadow strips on the white key end faces, picking slightly different shades to simulate light catching the beveled edge.

Now I'm setting up the gold fill box near the key gap and starting to write the actual geometry-building code, using a bucket map keyed by color to merge geometries efficiently before export.

I'm planning the buildBellows function using the provided Ctx type, designing an accordion-like bellows structure running along the X axis with 13 pleats spanning from -0.14 to 0.14.

I'm working out the cross-section dimensions and placing crests and valleys so the ends terminate cleanly against end frames, then calculating how many slabs and corner rods this would require against a 200-part budget. Since that's too many parts, I'm rethinking the approach to merge geometries by color into single static pieces without joints, keeping everything on one unparented part.

Writing slab geometry code...

I'm refining the facet coloring further: splitting each valley-to-crest facet into two segments, with the lower portion colored light or dark depending on orientation, and a narrower band near the crest colored solid red to make the ridge read clearly. Then I'm working out how these colored rectangle segments assemble into rings around all four sides, joining properly at the corners.

Now I'm computing the geometry for the inset quads connecting adjacent rings, making sure shared corner points keep the surface continuous, and figuring out a small inward extrusion thickness toward the central axis to give the pleats a bit of depth.

I'm adjusting the frame inner opening dimensions so the valley ring stays visible with a felt gasket gap, then adding a thin black cap/gasket piece behind the opening to show dark interior depth at the bellows end.

Now I'm planning the frame as four pearlCream boxes (top, bottom, front, back) with gold piping rods placed along both the inner and outer edges.

For merging geometries across different colors, I need a helper that normalizes all shapes by stripping UV attributes and converting to non-indexed form before combining them with BufferGeometryUtils, tracking rotated boxes with their transform matrices applied. I'll organize everything into a color-keyed accumulator map that collects geometries before the final merge.

Still arranging the crest rods...

I should also place a lozenge marker on the center pleat crest, which lands exactly at x=0 since it's pleat index 6 of 13. Since the crest is a ridge rather than a flat face, I need to work out how to position the diamond shape across the sloped facets so it sits properly on the V-shaped ridge.

Placing smaller diamonds above and below, then adding a darker gold outline layer behind for depth, plus small rose rhinestone gems flanking the crests of neighboring pleats, with thin wire tracing the crest line between them.

Placing guards on the 7 crest positions along x, centered on each corner crest, I'm designing an L-shaped bracket from two small boxes: one thin box covering the top face near the corner, and another covering the front face, joined to wrap around the edge.

Working out the corner plates now—for each of the four corners I need a horizontal plate wrapping over the ridge in z and a vertical plate wrapping in y, sizing each to span just past the corner point so they overlap cleanly against the crest geometry.

Still placing gold rivet cylinders at each corner bracket, and thinking about whether to add a thin gold piping accent alternating on every other pearl L-bracket for visual contrast.

Now I'm adding black reinforcing tape strips along the top surface at each valley fold, positioning thin black boxes that sit slightly proud of the groove to simulate taped seams across the interior valleys.

I'm checking whether the gold leaf dots placed in the front valleys would actually stay visible or get swallowed by the surrounding facet walls—since the groove geometry rises steeply from the valley, a dot of that radius risks being hidden unless it sits proud enough above the crease.

So I'll place each dot as a small low-poly sphere centered just above the valley floor, sized to fit the groove's width at that height, and repeat this for each valley to get a scattering of gold beads along the front.

spec.name: Madreperla Piano Accordion
spec.description: A 36-key piano accordion with a 60-button bass side, set on the floor and shown in the Italian mother-of-pearl style: celluloid pearl swirls, black piano-lacquer bands, gold trim and a ruby bellows with cream-edged folds.
spec.layout:
STATIC MODEL, joints []. Real size, about 66 cm wide with the bellows half-open. It stands upright on the bottoms of its two cases on y=0, with the bellows axis along X and the front (+Z) facing the viewer. The player's right is world -X, so the TREBLE (piano keyboard) case is at -X and the BASS (button) case is at +X. Left to right in X: treble case [-0.33,-0.14], bellows [-0.14,0.14], bass case [0.14,0.318]. Both cases are 0.41 high and 0.22 deep (z -0.11..0.11). The bellows is smaller, y 0.02..0.39 and z -0.09..0.09, so the cases read as heavy ends with a ruby concertina between them. Front to back in Z: the keyboard and bellows strap stand proud of the front face (z up to 0.14 and 0.10), then the case fronts at z=0.11, then the case backs at z=-0.11, then the harness (straps and pads) from z=-0.11 to -0.17.

STYLE: every case surface is clad in mother-of-pearl celluloid. This is built as geometry, not paint. Each large face is a base slab in pearlWhite with several overlapping, slightly raised, irregular faceted pearl patches (thin extrudes or slabs 1-3 mm proud) in pearlPink, pearlAqua, pearlLilac, pearlCream and pearlShade, like swirled shell. A few small pearlHighlight flecks sit on top. Each face is framed by an inkBlack celluloid band about 6 mm wide, then a thin gold bead rail. Corners carry chrome caps and the underside has four black rubber feet 0.012 high. Rose and teal diamond inlays (roseInlay, tealInlay), repeated as one motif on the treble end face, the bass front panel and the bass-end panel border, tie the cases together. Bellows are ruby red with cream fold edges. All metal is gold or chrome. Every surface is a flat colour, and all detail is small parts seated on the surface.

The OUTER END FACE (x=-0.33) is the show face: a big pearl swirl of 6-8 overlapping patches, a central rosette (a gold lathe ring around a pearlCream disc with 8 rose/teal diamond petals), and an inkBlack border with a gold bead rail. The FRONT FACE (z=0.11) shows pearl patches around the keyboard window x -0.32..-0.14, y 0.04..0.36 (left clear for the keyboard part), plus an inkBlack band above and below it and a gold rail round the window. The TOP FACE (y=0.41) carries a chrome slatted treble grille (about 12 thin chrome slats over a grilleDark recess, x -0.31..-0.17, z -0.06..0.06), a row of 7 register switches near the front top edge (pearlWhite tabs on chromeDark pivots, one gold master switch), a gold edge rail and pearl patches. The BACK FACE (z=-0.11) is a plainer pearl with an inkBlack leatherette strip and 2 chrome strap-anchor plates at the strap mounts. The inner face (x=-0.14) is a chrome bellows frame plate 0.006 thick with 8 screw heads. Four chrome corner caps on the vertical edges and 4 black rubber feet (0.012 high) under the corners at y 0..0.012.

At the inner edge (x -0.165..-0.14) is a key-slip rail, a gold bar with a pearlCream inset and 3 tealInlay diamonds. At the top and bottom ends are pearl keyboard cheek blocks (pearlWhite, with pearlPink/pearlAqua swirl patches and a gold rail) 0.012 tall. A small gold brand plate (with a tiny engraved-look inkBlack line pattern or text) sits centred on the top cheek block.

The tops of the buttons reach x=0.33. FRONT PANEL (z=0.11): a large pearl swirl plate framing a chrome slatted bass grille (about 9 vertical slats over grilleDark, x 0.17..0.29, y 0.08..0.33) with a gold oval brand badge centred above it. TOP: a chrome air-release button on a gold collar, plus a pearl patchwork and a gold edge rail. BACK: pearl with an inkBlack strip and a chrome strap-plate pair.

Each pleat is a rectangular ridge ring (outer size 0.37 high x 0.17 deep) of 4 thin bellowsRed slabs, with angled flank panels in bellowsRedDark running down to inset valley rings (inset 0.012 on every side) between the ridges. Every ridge crest carries a thin bellowsEdge cream ring just proud of the red, the classic white fold edge. The four long corners of the bellows carry full-length corner guards, inkBlack L-profile strips with a gold centre bead and tiny gold studs every pleat, and a gold-and-pearl bellows frame lip at each end (x=-0.14 and x=0.14). A bellows strap on the front: a leather band 0.022 wide, lying at z 0.09..0.10 across the front of the bellows at y 0.2 from bellowsStrapAnchor toward x=-0.04, with stitch dashes in stitch, a gold buckle (frame, tongue and 2 rivets), 5 punched holes (inkBlack) and a loose end with a pointed tip and a pearlWhite keeper loop. A small gold bellows-valve plate sits on the top face at the centre pleat.

parts.builds: Everything on the BACK (z -0.11..-0.17): the player's straps. Two shoulder straps in leather, each a 0.03 wide flat band. The treble strap starts at shoulderStrapAnchorTreble with a chrome anchor loop and hangs down the back with a slight bow to z=-0.15, with a stitch seam in stitch along both edges, a chrome slider buckle with a prong at y=0.10, a padded cushion pad (a thick leather box with chamfered corners, 0.06 wide x 0.10 high x 0.02 thick, with a pearlShade piping line) at y 0.16..0.26, and a tail end near y=0.03 with a gold tip. The bass strap starts at shoulderStrapAnchorBass and mirrors the construction. A bass hand strap pad: at handStrapPadBass a leather panel 0.07 wide x 0.18 high x 0.012 thick on the bass back, with a vertical slot (grilleDark), stitch border, 4 gold rivets and a velvet-look inkBlack band. A pair of small chrome D-rings sit at the bottom back of each case, y 0.04. The back also carries a thin gold maker's plaque on each case-back (0.05 x 0.016, with 3 tiny inkBlack engraved-look lines). The straps seat flat against the back faces, with each strap root on its anchor plate.
parts.attaches: Seats on the case back faces (z=-0.11) at backTreble and backBass. Strap roots at shoulderStrapAnchorTreble and shoulderStrapAnchorBass; the hand pad at handStrapPadBass.

For the aesthetic, I'm picking a mother-of-pearl celluloid finish with iridescent whites, pinks, aqua, and lavender, accented by black piano-pearl inlay lines, gold or chrome fittings, and red bellows trimmed in white and gold.

spec.name: Alebrije Jaguar-Eagle
spec.description: A Oaxacan alebrije painted-wood fantasy beast: a jaguar-bodied creature with a hooked eagle head and beak, spread feathered wings and a feather-fan tail, covered in dot, flower and leaf patterns in hot folk-art colours.
spec.layout: A jaguar-sized, long-bodied quadruped (about 1.6 m of torso) standing on four paws in a neutral rest pose, facing +Z. From the front (+Z): a hooked eagle beak (upper beak fixed to the head, lower beak on the jaw) at z about 1.45, a big round-eyed feathered head at y about 1.4, two round jaguar ears and a feather crest with a pair of banded horns on top, and a short thick neck with a feather ruff. Behind the neck sit the chest and torso (round, heavy, jaguar-shaped), then the hips and haunches. Wings spread straight out sideways at y about 1.3, each with an arm, a forearm, a hand and a fan of long flight feathers swept back, so the tip-to-tip span is about 3.9 m. Four sturdy legs, all separated and straight: the front legs are jaguar legs with round paws and ivory claws, the hind legs are jaguar thighs with eagle shins and talons, and they stand on y = 0. At the back is a long jaguar tail ending in a fan of feathers (z down to about -1.55), with a ridge of leaf-shaped spines along the spine. Style: painted wood. The base is chunky, faceted and blocky (low segment counts). Every surface is a flat colour, and the character comes from many small separate parts seated on the surface: rows and rings of dots (flattened spheres), jaguar rosettes drawn as a dark ring of dots around an orange or pink centre, stripes, leaf and flower motifs, zig-zag trim, and thin dark outlines. Colours are bright and unmixed and sit side by side with no shading. Warm orange and gold on top; cream, pink and turquoise on the belly and under the wings. The same motifs (dot rosette, five-petal flower, leaf) repeat on every part so the model reads as one painted piece.

parts.builds: The jaguar torso and chest. One smooth-skinned loft over hips, spine1 and spine2: a deep round chest (radius about 0.33 at z 0.5), a slightly narrower waist, and round haunches at the hips (radius about 0.32). The loft runs from z -0.9 to z 0.78, with its axis at y about 0.92 and its top at about y 1.22. It is jaguar orange on the back and sides, with a cream belly and chest bib made as sector bands or separate bands on the underside. It also includes a short neck-stub collar at neckBase (a wide faceted ring in gold, with a zig-zag of small cobalt triangles), and a thin ink outline ring at the waist and at the chest. Painted decoration made as many small separate parts seated on the skin with b.stick, scattered by surface hits: about 12 jaguar rosettes on each flank (a ring of 6 to 7 small ink dots around a hotPink or turquoise centre dot), rows of small cream and gold dots along the flanks, a row of cobalt, lime and coral dots down the belly edge, and two bold five-petal flower motifs (a flower is a gold centre with 5 coral or hotPink flattened-sphere petals) on each shoulder and haunch. A turquoise and gold stripe pair follows the flank line from shoulder to hip. Leaf motifs (flattened green cones) fan around each flower. Includes fur-less 'wood' details: a few small bareWood knots seated on the belly.
parts.attaches: Front end meets the head part's neck at neckBase and chestFront. Wings root at wingRootL and wingRootR on the shoulders. Legs meet at shoulderL, shoulderR, hipL and hipR. The tail meets at tailRoot. The dorsal ridge, built by the tail part, sits on the top between dorsalStart and dorsalEnd.

parts.builds: All four legs, rigid-skinned or smooth over their joint chains, and mirrored with s = ±1. FRONT (jaguar): from shoulderL/R down through elbow and wrist to the paw; thick tapering tubes (radius about 0.13 at the shoulder falling to 0.09 at the wrist), a big rounded paw (a squashed faceted sphere about 0.14 wide x 0.09 tall x 0.2 long) whose lowest point touches y = 0, 4 toes as short capsules at the front of the paw, and 4 curved ivory claws (cones in claw) at the toe tips. Paint: jaguar orange with ink stripe rings at the elbow and wrist, a cream paw cuff of three dots around the wrist, a cobalt zig-zag trim band, and a coral dot per toe. HIND (eagle): a heavy jaguar thigh from hipL/R to kneeL/R (radius about 0.2 falling to 0.12) in orange with 3 rosettes on its outer face, then a feathered 'pantaloon' of 8 to 10 overlapping flat turquoise, cobalt, and gold feather blades hanging from the thigh, then a thin yellow scaly eagle shin (beakYellow, radius about 0.05) from knee to hock and from hock to the foot, with ring segments in ink. Each foot is an eagle talon: 3 forward toes and 1 rear toe, each made of 2 capsule segments in beakYellow with ink joint dots and an ivory curved claw (cone) at the tip, so the toes are separated and spread, resting on y = 0 at talonContactL/R. Small hotPink and lime dots on every toe knuckle. All feet touch the floor, sinking at most 2 cm.
parts.attaches: Front legs start at the shoulder mounts (shoulderL/R) just under the torso. Hind legs start at the hip mounts (hipL/R) and are covered by the torso haunch. Feet end at pawContactFL/FR and talonContactL/R on y = 0.

parts.builds: The eagle head, neck, jaw and every head ornament, built with the head scale constant. NECK: a short thick smooth sweep over neck1 and neck2 from neckBase (radius about 0.2 to 0.17) rising forward to headPivot, painted jaguar orange with cream and a few rosette dots, and a ruff of two overlapping rings of 12 broad pointed feather blades (cobalt, turquoise, gold, hotPink alternating) around neck1. HEAD: a chunky faceted skull (sphere about 0.2 in radius, slightly longer in z) at the head joint, in gold, with a cream throat. UPPER BEAK on the head joint: a strongly hooked beak (a loft or sweep from about z 1.05 down to beakTip at [0, 1.33, 1.45] curving down to a sharp point), beakYellow with a beakTip-coloured tip, ink nostril dots, and a gold and hotPink dot row along the ridge. LOWER BEAK on the jaw joint: a shorter pointed wedge under it (z about 1.0 to 1.38) in beakYellow, with a red tongue (flat forked shape), a row of tiny ivory fangs, and a hotPink gape line. EYES: two large round eyes, one on each side at x about ±0.14, y 1.46, z 1.08, with an ink outline disc, eyeWhite ball, cobalt iris, ink pupil and a tiny white highlight, a heavy gold brow ridge above each (a wedge, with ink outline), and 3 dot-lashes. Concentric dot rings of cobalt, coral and lime around the eyes, and 2 small rosettes on each cheek. EARS: two round jaguar ears (flat faceted discs) on top, orange with ink rim and a cream inner disc. CREST: 7 long feather blades fanned up and back behind the ears (lime, turquoise, hotPink, cobalt, gold, with ink tips). HORNS: two upward-curving banded horns (a sweep with alternating hotPink, cream and turquoise bands and a gold tip) between the ears and crest, with a dot at each band joint. Highest point about y 1.8.
parts.attaches: The neck sweep starts buried in the torso at neckBase (y 1.0, z 0.6). The head sits at headPivot. The jaw rides jawPivot. The beak tip ends at beakTip.

parts.builds: Two outstretched eagle wings, mirrored with s = ±1, spread sideways in the rest pose, each over wingShoulder, wingElbow, wingWrist and wingTip (x up to ±1.95). BONES: a thick smooth wing arm sweep (radius about 0.1 tapering to 0.06) along the chain, painted in jaguar orange with ink rosette dots, and a gold cuff at the elbow and wrist. COVERTS: 3 rows of overlapping rounded feather shapes (extrude with smoothing, thickness about 0.015) over the top of the arm, growing in size from the shoulder outward: the first row small and hotPink, the second turquoise with a cream dot, the third cobalt with a gold dot. Each feather carries a small ink rim shape and a coloured central dot. FLIGHT FEATHERS: 8 long secondaries (about 0.7 m) fanned backward (-z) from the forearm and 6 long primaries (about 0.85 m) fanned from the wrist and hand, each a pointed extruded blade with a separate ink centre stripe and a tip cap, alternating cobalt, gold, leafGreen, hotPink and coral, with cream dot rows down each quill, all in a single plane around y 1.3 and separated so that no two feathers overlap in the same layer. The underside has the same feathers in cream and turquoise (a thin slab sat just below each upper feather). The wing leading edge carries a row of lime and cobalt dots, and a single big flower motif (7 petals around a gold centre) sits at the elbow of each wing. The wing is neutral, level and fully extended, with the finger bones separated.
parts.attaches: Roots at wingRootL and wingRootR on the top-side shoulders of the torso at about y 1.2. Feathers extend outward in +/-X and back in -Z.

parts.builds: TAIL: a long jaguar tail, a smooth sweep over tail1 to tail4 from tailRoot (radius about 0.11 tapering to 0.06) that curves gently up at the end, painted jaguar orange with ink ring stripes every 0.1 m as separate band sweeps, and a row of cream and turquoise dots between the stripes. FAN: at tail4 (tailTip) a fan of 9 long feather blades spread in an arc of about 100 degrees up and back (length about 0.4 m, ending near z -1.55), coloured in turn cobalt, turquoise, gold, hotPink, lime, coral, each with an ink tip, a centre stripe and a cream dot, plus a small purple and gold flower motif at the fan root. DORSAL RIDGE: a row of 9 leaf-shaped spines (extruded leaf outlines, about 0.12 m tall and 0.09 wide) standing along the back from dorsalStart to dorsalEnd on the top of the torso, with the colours cycling leafGreen, turquoise, hotPink, gold and cobalt, and with a small cream dot at the base of each. Between them runs a thin ink line sweep along the spine. Everything sits on the surface of the torso top (y about 1.22) and never enters the head or wing boxes.
parts.attaches: The tail is rooted at tailRoot under the hips. The ridge runs on the torso top between dorsalStart (front) and dorsalEnd (rear).

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching out the design for an alebrije jaguar-eagle hybrid: a quadruped jaguar body with an eagle head, beak, wings, and feathered tail, decorated with Oaxacan-style dot patterns, facing forward with wings spread at roughly jaguar scale.

I'm breaking the creature into five parts — body (torso, neck base, painted motifs), legs (jaguar front paws, eagle talon hind legs), head (beak, eyes, crest, horns, fangs), wings, and a feathered tail with ornamental dots and flowers — and now working out joint placements starting from the hips and shoulders relative to the floor.

Still mapping out the joint chain...

Finishing up the hind leg joint, then mirroring the naming scheme to L/R suffixes for both front and hind limbs, with hips parenting the hind legs and spine2 parenting the front legs. I'm reasoning that since the full skeleton is built before any part logic runs, the leg builders just need to look up joints by name and construct bone chains from them.

Now I'm sketching wing joints -- shoulder, elbow, wrist, and hand positions on each side, keeping the total joint count moderate, and planning to skip separate digit joints in favor of rigid claws on the paw bone while laying out the wing span dimensions.

I'm now plotting the tail curve, placing joints progressively back and upward to form a jaguar-like arc ending around z -1.55, with a feather fan spreading from the final tail joint.

Working out the bounding boxes for each body part: torso, haunches, head, neck, wings, and tail, so each component stays proportioned and properly mounted to the body.

I'll assign the dorsal ridge to the tail part instead—a row of nine painted leaf-spikes running from the base of the neck to the tail base, positioned along the spine top. Legs get the thigh pantaloons, head gets horns, keeping each part's ownership distinct while working out the torso's top height for placement.

Now I'm settling on a limited alebrije palette capped around 24 colors—jaguar orange, gold yellow, dark rosette purple, cream, hot pink, turquoise, deep blue, leaf green, red, violet, beak yellow with a darker tip, white and dark eye tones, black ink, and bare wood.

I'm also working out the attachment points for the rig—neck base, head and jaw pivots, shoulder and hip mounts, wing roots, tail root, and dorsal ridge start/end positions—to keep the body parts properly anchored.

For ownership, the body part handles the torso lofted around spine joints while the neck is skinned by the head part, and the legs part owns thighs and paws with hip-to-knee sweeps. I'm setting a polygon budget across parts (body, legs, head, wings, tail) totaling under 900 to stay within limits.

Now I'm laying out the full joint chain from hips through spine1, spine2, neck1, neck2, to head, defining each joint's position and direction vector to shape the creature's posture.

Continuing down, I'm adding the jaw joint hinged near the beak, then mapping out the front leg chain—shoulder, elbow, wrist, paw—for both sides, plus starting the hind leg structure.

Working out hip, knee, hock, and foot placements for the hind leg, following eagle talon anatomy where the thigh angles down-forward and shin bends down-back before the foot points forward again. Now starting the wing joints off the spine.

Placing the shoulder, elbow, wrist, and tip of the wing with forward-angled directions, confirming the left side uses positive X. Then laying out four tail segments trailing back from the hips, and noting the ears will be round jaguar-style tufts on the head alongside the eagle crest.

For the head I'm designing an eagle skull with a hooked upper beak curving down to a sharp tip and a matching lower beak, round brow-ridged eyes, tiny fangs and a forked red tongue tucked inside the mouth for that alebrije touch, plus spiraled painted horns rising above the ears, a seven-feather crest fanning from the back of the head, a feathered neck ruff, and jaguar rosette spots with a concentric dot motif painted across the face. Now I'm settling on the final color palette.

Every surface in this design should carry painted dots, stripes, and leaf or flower motifs rendered as tiny flattened spheres in contrasting colors over thin outlines, with flat single-color low-poly faceted parts throughout rather than actual paint textures. I need to list out all the mounting points next.

I'm planning the buildTailAndRidge function, using the provided Ctx type as given and mapping out the tail joints with a catmull-rom path through them.

Now I'm working out the tail fan geometry, adjusting blade lengths and angles so the spread stays within the bounding box while pointing up and back from the final tail joint.

Tapering blade length with angle so tips stay within bounds, checking max extents fit the silhouette, and planning slight alternating x-offsets between feathers to avoid z-fighting in the fan.

Now I'm sketching a reusable feather builder function that extrudes a leaf-shaped 2D outline along a length direction and width direction, with a sharp tip and smooth sides, parameterized by position, length, width, and color.

Adding feather dot and stripe helpers...

Still working out the tail geometry...

Computing the cap width generically. Now I'm moving to the dorsal ridge—placing nine leaf spines along the torso's top edge between its start and end points, but I realize I can't reliably query the torso surface since it's built by a different function, so I need another approach.

Settling on a fixed height estimate for the torso top (~1.22, dropping slightly toward the back) and embedding the leaf bases just under that surface. Each leaf will be flat like a fin, oriented with its width along the z-axis and height along y, standing upright with thickness along x.

Still defining leaf shape...

Checking the dorsal taper so the leaf base sits correctly even where the haunch narrows—settling on y≈1.2 with a small sink of about 0.025 so the leaf outline starts slightly recessed into the torso surface.

Finishing the leaf outline with a thin stalk at the base, then placing accent dots along the leaf at various heights. For coloring, I'll cycle through leafGreen, turquoise, hotPink, gold, and cobalt. For the bone attachments, since the joint spec only lists tail1-4 but the ridge runs along the torso, I need to map the ridge to spine joints by z-position instead—using spine2 for the forward section, spine1 for the middle, and hips for the rear.

I'm weighing whether to follow the literal joint spec (tail only) versus what's actually correct for a torso-mounted ridge. Since it's unclear if there's strict validation against the listed joints, I'll prioritize rig correctness and use the spine bones since they're available in J anyway. Now I'm sketching the ink line that sweeps along the dorsal path from start to end.

Adjusting to y-0.005 so the line floats correctly. Now sketching the tail: a catmull curve from the root through several waypoints curving down and back, with tapering radii from 0.115 down to 0.065, noting the tail root sits buried in the jaguar's haunches near the hip joint.

For the tail bone chain, I'll skip including the hips joint since it projects outside the path's start and only tail1 should control the root segment, letting it rotate naturally with the rest of the tail bones. Coloring the tail orange to match, and considering whether the underside near the belly should get a cream tint like the rest of the ventral surface.

Now for the ring stripes, I'm thinking through how to sweep closed ring paths around the tail at regular intervals using the tail path's tangent direction at each point to orient the frame correctly—getting a frame from the point and tangent so the rings sit perpendicular to the tail's curve.

For bone weighting, I'm debating whether to assign rigid bones by z-position per joint segment, or use the tube sweep's own frame which should already carry proper skinned bone weights—the latter seems safer for deformation but I need to check what `frame(at, dir)` actually expects.

Instead, I'll compute ring points manually: center from the path position, tangent for orientation, and perpendicular basis vectors via cross product. For radius, I'll use a simple linear taper function rather than matching the smooth spline exactly, then build an 8-sided circumscribed polygon, accounting for the extra reach of flat faces versus the true radius.

I'm placing the ring bands at roughly every 0.1m along the tail, computing the parametric position for each 0.1 increment from 0.15 to 0.65 along the tail's total length, keeping the ring radius slightly larger than the tail radius so it visibly protrudes without looking absurd.

I'm also adding dots between the rings, alternating cream and turquoise, positioned at angles around the tail's cross-section (near the top and sides) using the sweep frame at each point to orient flattened sphere studs stuck onto the surface.

Tallying up parts: tail body plus 6 rings plus roughly 15 dots gets me to about 22 for the tail alone, then I still need the fan (9 feathers each with tip caps, stripes, and front/back dots, adding up fast) and the flower with its center and petals, so I need to keep a close eye on the total part budget to stay under the limit.

Still working out the budget...

Adding the ridge dots (37 total) brings the running count to 103, plus a gold cuff ring at the fan root brings it to 104. For the leaf ribs, I'm placing a thin rod from base to 0.85H with a protruding cream dot near the base where it crosses the rib.

Now I'm working out the leaf's orientation vectors, picking a perpendicular width axis so the lean angle doesn't distort the cross-section, and checking the cross product gives the correct thickness direction.

For the rib dots, I'm figuring out how to place small flattened spheres along the leaf's face so they protrude slightly as raised bumps rather than floating detached, scaling and offsetting them just enough to sit on the surface.

Now I'm working out the leaf positions along z with even spacing and slightly varying heights using a sine-based bell curve, plus the stalk base y positions interpolating down the stem, and setting up a bone function to assign ridge parts to the right z slice before moving on to placing the fan flower.

For the tail, I'm placing the feather roots buried inside the rounded cap at the tip, sinking them near the center so the visible blade portion starts just outside the cap radius, with the fan converging narrowly at the root and widening further along—accounting for the tail's upward curve at the tip.

Checking the fan spacing, feather width (0.1) actually exceeds the arc spacing between adjacent feathers at mid-length (~0.65L), causing significant overlap—unlike wing feathers where non-overlap is required, fan overlap near the tail tip is natural and expected, though I need to watch for z-fighting between coplanar overlapping blades.

I'll alternate thickness offsets of ±0.008 in x between even/odd feathers so neighboring blades don't occupy the same plane, keeping width around 0.085-0.1 so every-other feather (i, i+2) stays just within spacing tolerance at 0.65L. The small cream accent spheres at each feather's midpoint (radius 0.012) should sit fine within this offset scheme.

Now I'm setting the fan's color cycle across its feathers -- cobalt, turquoise, gold, hotPink, lime, coral, repeating for nine feathers -- with ink-colored stripe and tip details on each, subtle on the cobalt ones but still visible. I'm anchoring the feather bones to tail4's joint direction and positioning each feather's root origin relative to the fan's base offset, then placing a small flower accent near the tail where the fan attaches.

I'm working out the flower motif itself -- a gold center sphere with flattened purple petal spheres arranged in a ring around it, oriented using the local up and forward axes so the petals face outward symmetrically on both sides of the tail near the fan root.

Petals stick out slightly but that's fine. Now I'm placing the gold cuff ring along the tail path, trying to avoid overlap with the flower and other rings by spacing them at different fractions of the tail length, and working out segment distances along the path to find the right position.

I'm alternating tail dot colors between cream and turquoise by angle band, keeping the belly as a cream sector around the bottom. For sticking the decorations onto the body, I'm using a helper with embed and scale parameters so pieces sink partially into the geometry and compress along one axis, relying on default bone attachment since none is specified explicitly.

For the ring details, I'm sweeping a closed Catmull-Rom curve through a small set of points to form a thin tube, picking a low segment count for a faceted look and assigning it an explicit bone since it needs to behave rigidly as a closed loop. I'm also laying out an ink-colored polyline along the spine, adjusting the sample points since the torso height varies along its length.

Now I'm sketching a helper function to build feather geometry from a root position and direction vector.

Still shaping the tip cap geometry...

I'm placing a cream dot on top of the ink stripe at the midpoint, then setting up the rod sweep with hexagonal cross-section. For the fan arrangement, I'm computing each feather's angle incrementally from vertical, tilting slightly backward so the tail tip ends up angled up and back rather than perfectly straight.

Checking the tail tangent direction gives roughly 73°, so I'm narrowing the fan's angular range to stay centered there and recalculating each feather's length so the z-extent doesn't push past the box boundary at -1.6 — adjusting the length formula down slightly to keep the maximum reach just under that limit.

I'll shift the tail root slightly and keep feather widths constant while making center feathers longer, with small alternating x-offsets. For the flower, I'm placing petals in a ring around each side using the axis perpendicular to that face, with purple petals, a gold center, and scaled spheres for a flattened petal shape.

spec.name: Alebrije Jaguar-Eagle
spec.description: A chunky painted-wood Oaxacan alebrije: a jaguar's body, legs and tail carrying an eagle's hooked-beak head and two spread feathered wings, covered in rosettes, dot rings, zigzag bands and swirls in saturated flat colours.
spec.layout:
Rest pose, centred on x=0, facing +Z, on four jaguar paws on y=0. Spans z from -1.65 (tail plume) to 1.65 (beak tip), x ±1.8 (wing tips), y 0 to 2.1 (head crest). Front to back: hooked eagle beak (z 1.1 to 1.6), round skull with big amber eyes and a feather crest, a thick raised neck with a feather ruff rising from the chest at z 0.5, a deep-chested jaguar torso (chest z 0.3, waist z -0.1, hips z -0.55) with two wings at the shoulders (spread sideways, rising slightly, feathers trailing backward), four sturdy short legs with oversized paws, and a thick tail running back at z -0.85 that curls up into a fan of eyed feathers.

Style: carved and painted wood. Chunky, simple, faceted shapes (low segment counts, 6 to 10 sides) with painted ornament built as small parts in their own flat colours, seated on the surface. Every part uses the same motifs so the model reads as one hand-painted piece:
(1) Rosette: a ring of 5 to 6 small magenta or blue discs round a turquoise centre disc, on a black outline disc, on the orange coat.
(2) Dot rows: cream dots, sometimes with a black ring under them, in lines along edges and bands.
(3) Zigzag or triangle bands in alternating colours.
(4) Teardrop or leaf shapes in green and pink.
(5) Thin ink-black swirls and outlines (inkBlack) under coloured shapes, so each coloured shape has a dark outline layer, then the colour, then a small cream highlight dot.
Colour goes by place: the coat is warm orange and yellow on top, cream underneath, with blue and violet shadow areas. Head and wings are turquoise, magenta and yellow. Paws and beak are bright yellow. Bare unpainted wood (woodBare) appears only on the claw tips, the underside of the paw pads and a few carved ridge edges. No ground, base or props.

parts.builds: The jaguar body and its painted decoration. One smooth loft (bone: hips, spine, chest) from z -0.85 to 0.6. Stations: hips (z -0.55, width 0.62, height 0.58, centre y 1.0), waist (z -0.1, width 0.5, height 0.52, y 1.03), chest (z 0.3, width 0.68, height 0.7, y 1.08), chest front (z 0.58, width 0.5, height 0.55, y 1.1), round-capped so the head part's neck sweeps from neckBase into it. Coat: coatOrange on top and sides with a coatYellow upper flank, and a cream belly stripe on the underside (use sectors or a countershade paint). A deepBlue saddle stripe along the spine from z 0.4 to -0.7, edged with cream dot rows and magenta triangle (zigzag) trim on both edges, with a row of small carved ridge studs (gold) on spineTop. 12 to 16 jaguar rosettes on each flank (rosette motif: black outline disc, ring of 5 to 6 magenta or deepBlue dots, turquoise centre), scattered with minDist, kept off the belly and clear of the leg and wing mounts. Zigzag bands in violet and skyBlue across the belly. A collar of leaf shapes (leafGreen and lime teardrops) with cream dots round the chest at z 0.5, under the neck. A magenta swirl line sweeping from each shoulder across the flank. Small hip rosettes and a ring of dots at each hip socket and shoulder socket, where the legs meet the body.
parts.attaches: Owns hips, spine and chest. Neck and head start at neckBase and chestFront. Wings mount at shoulderL and shoulderR on the upper sides. The foreleg tops mount at foreShoulderL/R and the hind tops at hindHipL/R. The tail starts at tailRoot.

parts.builds: The eagle neck, head and face. The neck is one thick sweep over neck1, neck2 and head from neckBase to the skull (radius about 0.24 tapering to 0.2), painted turquoise, with a ruff of overlapping feather blades (broad, shaped, in rings round the neck from base to throat): inner ring cream, then yellow, then magenta, then violet tips, each outlined in inkBlack. Skull: a faceted sphere at headCentre (radius about 0.21) in turquoise, with a lighter skyBlue brow ridge over each eye. Eyes: big readable eyes on both sides at the front of the skull (x ±0.15, y 1.74, z 1.08): inkBlack outline disc, cream white disc, eyeAmber iris, black pupil, a tiny cream highlight, with a magenta feather-eyebrow blade above each. Beak: separate upper and lower. The upper beak (on head) is a thick hooked wedge or cone from beakRoot to z 1.6, curving down at the tip (y 1.58), beakYellow with a beakOrange cere at the base and two inkBlack nostril dots. The lower beak (on jaw) is a shorter wedge from the jawHinge to z 1.5, beakOrange, with a thin inkBlack gape line. A crest of 7 to 9 tall feather blades fanned on top and back of the skull rising to y 2.08, in a root-to-tip palette of magenta, yellow, lime, skyBlue, each with a cream dot at the tip. Cheek discs with a dot ring in pink and deepBlue, and a swirl painted down the neck sides.
parts.attaches: The neck starts at the mount neckBase, inside the torso's chest front (chestFront). The head sits at headCentre. The jaw hinges at jawHinge.

parts.builds: Both wings, left and right mirrored, spread sideways and slightly up, feathers trailing back. Each wing has a main arm tube (sweep over wingShoulder, wingElbow, wingWrist, wingTip, radius 0.1 tapering to 0.05) in magenta. Layers (the same on both sides, left x>0): (1) a leading-edge band of coverts, 3 overlapping rows of rounded feather shapes (extruded flat leaves) over the arm top and covering the arm to the wrist: row 1 coatYellow, row 2 turquoise, row 3 magenta, each with an inkBlack outline layer and a row of cream dots. (2) Secondaries (on the secondariesL/R fan joints): 8 broad feathers about 0.55 long trailing back from the elbow to the wrist, alternating skyBlue and deepBlue with violet tips, each with a cream eye-dot and black outline. (3) Primaries (on primariesL/R): 7 long feathers, 0.7 to 0.9 long, fanned outwards and back from the wrist, with colours cycling coatOrange, red, magenta, violet, leafGreen, lime, turquoise, a black stripe down the middle and a cream tip dot or zigzag. Wing tips reach about x ±1.8. A small thumb feather group near the wrist in lime. Flower-like rosette (dot ring) at the shoulder joint. Feathers are flat extruded blades with a slight bevel, spread in a ring or fan.
parts.attaches: Roots at shoulderL and shoulderR on the torso's upper sides (x ±0.3, y 1.3). Nothing touches the legs or the head. A clear gap above the back.

parts.builds: All four jaguar legs, built as sweeps or limb chains over the leg joints (left x>0, right mirrored). Short, thick, with big paws. Upper legs are about 0.15 radius tapering to 0.1; the front legs run straight down (shoulder, elbow, wrist, paw), the hind legs bend with the hock back (hip, knee forward, ankle back, paw). Paws touch y=0 at the foot mounts (footFL/FR/BL/BR), each about 0.12 radius, 0.3 long, in beakYellow, with three rounded toe bumps in front on each paw, and bright cream claw cones (woodBare tips) pointing forward and down, and a paw-pad underside in woodBare and inkBlack. Legs are coatOrange, ringed with bands: alternating turquoise, magenta and cream, each band bordered by inkBlack thin rings, at the elbow/knee and above the paw like painted socks, with rows of cream dots between the bands. Rosettes (dot ring motif) on each upper leg's outer side, and a swirl zigzag line in violet down the inside edge. Shoulder and hip balls (sphere caps) in coatYellow where the legs meet the torso at foreShoulder and hindHip.
parts.attaches: The leg tops sit inside the torso underside at foreShoulderL/R and hindHipL/R. The paws rest on y=0 at the foot mounts.

parts.builds: The jaguar tail and its plume. A tail sweep over tail1 to tail5 from tailRoot (radius 0.13 tapering to 0.07), running back at the waist height and curling up at the end to tailTip. Painted coatOrange with a black ring band every 0.12 m (inkBlack), and between them alternating turquoise and magenta zigzag bands and cream dot rows. At tailTip, a fan of 9 to 11 long feathers (flat extruded blades with a bevel, 0.4 to 0.5 long) on the plume joint, fanned in an arc round the tail tip, leaning up and back, in a peacock-like palette: leafGreen, turquoise, deepBlue with lime and violet. Each feather has an eye motif at the tip (an inkBlack oval, then a skyBlue oval, magenta oval, and a cream dot) and an inkBlack centre stripe. A thick tuft-like carved base cuff at tail5 in gold with small cream dots. Plus a small ridge row of 3 to 4 gold studs along the tail root.
parts.attaches: Starts at the mount tailRoot, inside the rear end of the torso (hips). The plume fan opens at tailTip.

spec.name: Alebrije Jaguar-Eagle
spec.description: A painted-wood Oaxacan alebrije: a jaguar body with eagle head, folded-open wings and feathered tail, covered in dotted and swirled folk-art patterns in bright colours.
spec.layout: Quadruped jaguar standing on four stout legs facing +Z. Chunky rounded wood-carved torso (length about 1.3 m, centre y 0.85) with a long curling tail behind. A thick neck rises forward to a big eagle head with a hooked beak (upper and lower jaw separate), huge round eyes and a feather crest. Two wings spread out sideways and up from the shoulders, each with 5 wide painted feather blades in a root-to-tip rainbow palette. Everything is blocky primitives with a flat colour per part. The style is Oaxacan painted wood: the base colour is overlaid with small parts such as dot rows, spirals, stripes, diamonds and flowers in contrasting colours, with a dark outline and a light highlight on each motif. Paws rest on small round painted plinth discs at floor level only.

parts.builds: Jaguar body: a chunky loft torso in jaguarYellow with a cream belly, a rump and chest bulge, a spine ridge of small alternating magenta and turquoise diamonds, black rosette spots (ring of black dots around a magenta centre) scattered over the flanks and back, a dotted collar band between torso and neck in turquoise and white dots, and a painted saddle blanket pattern of orange zigzag triangles on the back.
parts.attaches: Neck at neckBase, legs at footF and footB mounts, wings at shoulderL and shoulderR, tail at tailRoot.

parts.builds: Four stout jaguar legs with thick thighs, shins and big round paws with cream toe discs and black claws, each in jaguarYellow with black spots and magenta, turquoise and white dotted anklet bands, and a stripe ring at the knee. Each foot stands on a thin round plinth disc in woodBrown with a violet dotted rim. Feet touch y=0.
parts.attaches: Legs start under the torso at the footFL, footFR, footBL and footBR mounts and the leg joints.

parts.builds: Eagle head and neck: a thick neck sweep in jaguarYellow with a white feather-collar of overlapping cream and turquoise cards, a big head with a cream face and a hooked beak made of separate upper jaw (beakGold) and lower jaw (orange) on the jaw joint, a black nostril, large round eyes (black outline, white, turquoise iris, black pupil, white highlight) with a magenta brow ridge above each, a crest of seven tall feather blades (red, orange, magenta, violet, skyBlue fanned back) and a dotted pattern on the cheeks. A pink tongue is inside the lower jaw.
parts.attaches: Neck starts at neckBase on the chest; head centred on headCentre; nothing sits in front of the face.

parts.builds: Two mirrored spread wings rising from the shoulders. Each has a rounded upper-arm shoulder in magenta with white dots, then 5 large extruded feather blades fanning out and up, in a root-to-tip palette (turquoise, leafGreen, skyBlue, violet, red), each blade bordered by a cream outline strip and decorated with a centre line of small dots plus a spiral or diamond motif in contrasting colours, and a row of small covert feathers in orange and yellow along the leading edge.
parts.attaches: Attach at shoulderL and shoulderR joints on the torso top edge.

parts.builds: A long curling tail swept out backward and up, built as a sweep in jaguarYellow with black bands ring pattern, ending in a fan of 5 eagle tail feathers (red, orange, magenta, violet, turquoise with cream tips and dotted centres) plus a small spiral curl accent in turquoise and a row of white dots along its top. Includes a small cluster of back-hip decorative flowers (pink petals, yellow centres, green leaves) at the tail root.
parts.attaches: Starts at tailRoot on the hips; chain tail1 to tail3.

Add 4-5 big knots or burls: outline-coloured hollow rings with glowing glowMagenta and glowViolet orbs inside.
