spec.name: Pandoran Glow-Spire
spec.description: A 3.4 m bioluminescent alien plant in the Avatar/Pandora style: a mossy root mound, a twisting vein-lit stalk, a crown of arching teal fronds with glowing tips, curtains of drooping light-tendrils, and a glowing spore bloom.
spec.layout: Radially symmetric around the Y axis, standing on y=0, with a slight lean toward +Z so the front reads. From the ground up: a low dark mossy mound (r about 1.2, height 0.4) with buttress roots splayed out and tiny glowing mushrooms. A thick S-curving stalk (radius 0.32 at the base to 0.12 at the top, centre line (0,0.35,0) -> (0.08,1.0,0.05) -> (-0.06,1.7,-0.04) -> (0,2.35,0)) with spiral ridges and glowing vein lines winding round it. Two side branches carry glowing pod-bulbs at y 1.2-1.6. At the top (y 2.3) sits a crown of 9 big arching fan fronds in two tiers, rising and curving outward to about r 1.3, each with a darker teal body, light-teal midrib, and a glowing cyan edge and tip. A skirt of long thin tendrils hangs from the crown ring and branch nodes down to y 0.9, each ending in a glowing bulb that alternates cyan, magenta and violet. A glowing bloom of petals and a bright core sits in the crown centre (y 2.4-3.0), with floating spore motes up to y 3.4. Avatar style: lots of dark, cool blue-teal-violet base colours with saturated neon glows concentrated on veins, edges, tips and bulbs, soft rounded organic shapes made from primitives, and tendril curls. All glow pieces are small own-colour parts wrapped in glow(). Nothing else is in the scene: no ground plane beyond the mound.

parts.builds: The ground-hugging base. A flattened faceted mound (lathe or squashed sphere, soil colour with mossDark on top, moss and mossLight patches on upward faces as small separate caps) about r 1.2 and 0.4 high. 6-7 buttress roots as tapered sweeps in trunk/trunkMid that start against the stalk base (r 0.32 at y 0.5) and splay out and down over the mound, 0.8-1.2 m long, ending in the soil at y about 0. Glowing rootlet lines (thin sweeps in glowCyan) run along the tops of the roots. Around the mound sit 12-16 tiny glowing mushrooms or bulb-caps (little lathe domes with a short stem; glowGreen, glowCyan and glowBlue caps, a few magenta) of different sizes (0.05-0.14 m tall), plus 5-8 small moss tufts built of tiny cones in moss/mossLight, 2 small rocks in soil/trunk. All glow parts use glow(). Nothing taller than 0.45 m except the roots where they climb the stalk base.
parts.attaches: Roots end against the stalk at stalkBase (r 0.32); the mound top is at groundCenter. The stalk part starts at y 0.35 and is buried in the mound.

parts.builds: The central trunk and its side branches. A sweep along the S-curve (0,0.35,0) -> (0.08,1.0,0.05) -> (-0.06,1.7,-0.04) -> (0,2.35,0), radius 0.32 at the base falling to 0.12 at the top, section ngon 7-8 for facets, in trunk colour with trunkMid sectors. Spiral ridges: 2-3 helical thin sweeps in trunkLight winding round the stalk and following its surface (use surface hits, loop or sweep.at with a rotating angle). Glowing veins: 2 helical thin sweeps in glowCyan and glowBlue, pulsing in beads: small glowing spheres every 0.18 m along the vein. 5-6 swollen node rings (torus-like sweeps or lathe rings in trunkLight) along the height. Two side branches (sprout or sweep) at the mounts branchL (curving out to +X and up, 0.55 m long) and branchR (to -X and -Z, 0.5 m long). Each ends in a pod-bulb cluster: a podShell sphere of r 0.1 shell with a glowing core inside (magenta or violet) and 3-4 little glow buds around it, plus a tiny curling tendril. A few small leaf stubs (extruded leaf blades in frond/frondLight, 0.2 m) on the lower stalk with glowGreen edges. Top of the stalk finishes in a flared cup collar (lathe, trunkLight, r 0.22) at stalkTop for the crown to sit in.
parts.attaches: Starts buried in the rootMound at stalkBase; ends at stalkTop where the crown and bloom attach; branch tips at branchL and branchR, where hanging tendrils may attach.

parts.builds: The big arching fan fronds. Nine fronds around crownRingCenter (0,2.3,0) at radius 0.2: a lower tier of 5 (azimuths 0, 72, 144, 216, 288 degrees, elevation about 35 degrees above horizontal, reach about 1.3 m radially, arching tips drooping slightly, so tips reach about r 1.3 at y 2.5-2.9) and an upper tier of 4 (azimuths 36+90k, elevation about 65 degrees, reach 0.9, tips at about y 3.1-3.2, r 0.6). Each frond is a gently curved midrib sweep (frondLight, taper 0.035 to 0) plus a wide leaf blade built from an extrude (outline: a broad teardrop fan 0.5 m wide, curved by assembling 3-4 segments of slabs or extrudes along the midrib; frond colour with frondDeep on the underside side segments and frondLight inner segments). 5-7 vein sweeps per frond fanning out from the base to the edge in glowCyan (thin, glow), the outer rim edge as a thin sweep in glowCyan, and a bright glowBlue or glowGreen tip bead (sphere r 0.04, glow). Ruffled scallop edge: small teardrop extrudes along the edges. One frond in the lower tier (azimuth 0, pointing +Z toward the front) is the largest and gets magenta tipped edges as a signature. No hanging tendrils here (those are in another part).
parts.attaches: Frond roots sit in the collar at crownRingCenter (radius crownRingRadius around the Y axis). Bloom and spores sit inside the frond circle above bloomCenter; do not fill the cylinder r<0.25 above y 2.4.

parts.builds: The hanging curtain of glowing tendrils. 22-28 thin drooping tendrils hang from a ring at tendrilRingY 2.25 and radius tendrilRingRadius 0.55 (angles evenly spread plus jitter, from an rng), plus 4-6 from the branch tips at branchL/branchR. Each is a catmull sweep that starts out of the collar, arches outward 0.1-0.3 m and falls in a lazy curve to a bottom y between tendrilBottomY 0.9 and 1.8 (varying lengths, the front ones longer), radius tapering 0.022 to 0.008, coloured in trunkMid with a bead-spaced glowing stripe: small glow spheres every 0.12 m along the tendril in glowCyan / glowBlue (alternating), brighter towards the tips. Every tendril ends in a glowing bulb (sphere or teardrop r 0.04-0.07; glowCyan, glowMagenta, glowViolet in rotation, plus a smaller pale halo-ring of 4-5 mini beads around the largest ones). 6-8 longer tendrils curl at the tip in a small spiral (spiral path). The tendrils sit clear of the stalk (stay at least 0.3 m from the trunk axis below y 2.0) and don't touch the ground.
parts.attaches: Start points on the ring at tendrilRingY / tendrilRingRadius, around the crown collar of the stalk; a few start from the pod clusters at branchL and branchR.

parts.builds: The glowing flower and drifting spores in the middle of the crown. A bud/bloom centred on bloomCenter (0,2.5,0): a bright core (icosahedron or sphere r 0.11, core colour, glow strength 2) in a halo of 2-3 glowing shells (glowCyan, glowGreen small spheres or rings), surrounded by 3 rings of petals: inner ring 8 petals (petalLight, extruded rounded petals 0.2 m, raised about 35 degrees), middle ring 8 (petal, 0.28 m, open 55 degrees), outer ring 6 (glowMagenta-edged, 0.34 m, open 70 degrees); the petals have glowMagenta or glowViolet rim lines and tips. Stamens: 12-16 thin sweeps rising out of the core up to about y 3.0, with a glowing bead at each tip (alternating core and glowCyan). Above it float 30-45 spore motes (tiny spheres r 0.012-0.03, scattered by rng between y 2.7 and 3.4 inside r 0.9, glowCyan, glowGreen, glowViolet, core) and a few seedling puffs (small star-shaped bursts of 6 thin spikes with a glowing centre) at the top. All glow bits are wrapped in glow().
parts.attaches: Sits in the collar at stalkTop / bloomCenter inside the ring of fronds; petals stay below the upper frond tips and clear of the frond blades.

calls.reasoning:
I'm envisioning a Pandora-style bioluminescent plant, something like a Helicoradian with spiraling glowing fronds, hanging tendrils, and bulbous mushroom-like bases, roughly 3 meters tall, and now considering whether it should have static form or articulated joints.

Since this is more scenery than creature, I'll skip joints entirely and keep everything in model space. I'm breaking it into parts: a mossy rooted base with glowing rootlets and small mushrooms, a twisting spiral-ridged trunk with glowing veins, a large fan-shaped crown of radial fronds at the top, drooping bioluminescent tendrils with bulb tips cascading from the crown and lower branches, and a central glowing flower bud with seed pods crowning the whole structure.

I'm now working out the spatial layout -- overall dimensions, mount points at the base, stalk top, crown center, and bloom center, plus anchor points for side branches and the hanging tendril ring -- and settling on a dark violet-teal Pandoran palette for the soil, moss, and trunk colors.

I'm expanding that palette to around two dozen glow and accent colors for the fronds, petals, core, and seed pods, then budgeting part complexity so five main parts stay within the total limit while leaving room to specify spiral parameters and a shared trunk radius function.

I'm defining the trunk's centerline with a gentle S-curve through four points, tapering its radius from base to tip, and establishing it as the parent structure that other parts mount to via a shared "stalkTop" reference and crown ring radius—now ready to write the full spec.

spec.name: Sporeglow Hometree Bloom
spec.description: An Avatar-style Pandora bioluminescent plant: a twisting trunk with glowing fan-leaf fronds, a giant helicoid spiral-flower, drooping tendrils and a root-and-mushroom base.
spec.layout: A stout, gently S-curved trunk rises from a buttressed root flare at the floor to a crown at about y=2.1. From the crown, 6 big fan fronds arc outward and down in a ring, each with glowing veins and rim dots. A tall helicoid spiral-flower (a Pandora 'helicoid spiral' that retracts when touched) rises from the crown centre to y=3.2, its coiled petals glowing cyan. Long thin tendrils hang from the crown and trunk with glowing tips. The base has glowing mushroom and sprout clusters between the roots. Everything is blocky and faceted, with a dark blue-violet body and cyan, magenta and teal glow accents as small parts: veins, dots, rings and tips. Warmer tones on top, cooler below.

parts.builds: Ground-level base: 7 buttress roots flaring from the trunk foot (trunkDark/bark, tapered sweeps sinking slightly into the floor), moss patches (rootMoss) on top faces, a dirt disc (dirt), glowing mushroom caps and small sprout cones scattered between roots (glowTeal, glowMagenta, glowPale dots) and thin glowing root veins (glowCyan).
parts.attaches: Top meets trunk at mount trunkBase; rides joint root.

parts.builds: S-curved faceted trunk swept from trunkBase through trunkMid to crown, radius tapering 0.38 to 0.2 with a swelling at the crown. Ring bands, bark ridges and knots (bark, trunkMid), glowing spiral vein lines and dot rows (glowCyan, glowViolet), moss on upward faces, and a crown collar ring of glowing nodules where fronds, tendrils and flower attach.
parts.attaches: Starts at trunkBase, ends at crown collar at mount crown; rides root, trunk1, trunk2, crown.

parts.builds: Six large fan-leaf fronds around frondRing, spaced 60 degrees apart, each a thick stalk sweeping up and out then arcing down, ending in a broad extruded leaf blade up to 1.2 m across (leafBlue with leafTeal centre, leafEdge rim). Each leaf has a glowing midrib and 4 pairs of side veins (glowCyan, glowTeal), rim dots (glowPale), and a magenta tip. Fronds reach about x/z +-1.3 and droop to y about 1.4.
parts.attaches: Stalks root at the crown collar, mount frondRing; rides joint crown.

parts.builds: Helicoid spiral-flower on joint flower: a short green-teal stem from flowerBase, then 10 overlapping curved petals arranged in a helix rising to flowerTop, each tapering from a wide base to a point (petalPink outer, petalDeep inner), glowing edge lines (glowMagenta), a glowing core bulb (glowCyan), a ring of yellow stamen spikes with glowing tips (stamen, glowPale) at the top, and floating spore dots (glowPale, glowCyan) above.
parts.attaches: Base seated at flowerBase on crown collar; rides joint flower.

parts.builds: About 14 long drooping tendrils hanging from tendrilRing at the crown collar and from trunk nodules lower down, thin catmull sweeps (bark, trunkMid) curving outward and down to y about 0.6, each with a glowing bead sequence (glowViolet, glowTeal) and a bright tip bulb (glowCyan or glowMagenta). A few small side tendrils and hanging seed pods (glowPale).
parts.attaches: Roots at mount tendrilRing and trunk nodules; rides joint crown and trunk2.

Four leveler feet touch y=0 and everything else floats above on the sides' bottom edge y=0.04. Seen from the side, the silhouette is one polygon in (z, y) pairs: (-0.48,0) (0.40,0) (0.40,0.84) (0.47,0.86) (0.47,0.96) (0.15,1.08) (0.074,1.58) (0.22,1.58) (0.22,1.82) (-0.40,1.82) (-0.48,1.25), back to the start. From the front (+Z) to the back it reads as follows. A flat coin-door front, 0.40 m forward, fills the lower body from y 0 to 0.84. Above it an overhanging control deck slopes up from its front lip (z 0.47, y 0.96) to the monitor's bottom edge (z 0.15, y 1.08). The CRT bezel leans back about 9 degrees, running from [0,1.08,0.15] to [0,1.58,0.074]. A deeper backlit marquee box sits on top, its front face at z 0.22. A tall, slightly tapered back tower with a rear service door carries the full height. The two side panels (x ±0.30 to ±0.33, 3 cm thick) are extruded from the silhouette polygon and span the whole height. Everything else sits between them at |x| <= 0.30, except the deck lip and T-molding, which may reach |x| 0.33. The side-art layer sits on the outer faces at |x| 0.33 to 0.345, inset 0.02 m from every edge of the polygon. SYNTHWAVE STYLE: the carcass is near-black indigo (cabinetBlack, shellPurple). Magenta and cyan neon tubes and T-molding run every edge. Glowing parts, made with the glow kit, are the screen scene, the marquee lettering and panel, the neon strips, the buttons' lit caps and the coin-door lights. I'll also add side funnel walls connecting the bezel to the cabinet sides, plus chrome corner brackets at the bezel's four corners made from small L-shaped leg pieces with screw cylinders.

Now I'm designing the speaker grille: a dark metal panel beneath the bezel with a series of thin vertical slots cut into it, flanked by chrome end caps and sitting just in front of the bezel's own depth.

I'm stacking gradient color bands above the horizon line for the sky, going from magenta-pink to deep purple tones with a glow effect, then adding a dark ground box below the horizon.

Now I'm designing a thin bright horizon glow line, then working out the retro sun using horizontal strips with shrinking gaps to create that classic scanline effect.

Building mountain silhouettes...

I'll extrude the shapes slightly in depth and position them back on the correct layer using a helper function. For the receding grid, I'm placing horizontal lines below the horizon with increasing perspective spacing, using a cyan glow color for the scan lines.

Working out convergence math...

I'll color grid verticals and horizontals both as cyan screenLine for palette consistency with the synthwave theme. For placement, I'm positioning the pixel invaders in the sky flanking the sun and deciding where to tuck the spaceship near the ground area without clashing with the grid.

Designing the ship pixel art now...

Now I'm placing two classic pixel invaders in magenta/yellow/cyan near the top corners, sizing them small enough to fit beside the sun without overlapping it, though I need to watch for collisions with the mountains at the horizon.

Designing the pixel patterns for two invader sprite variants, then placing scattered white star boxes in the empty sky areas, avoiding overlap with the sun and invader row.

Simplifying stars to small squares for the twinkle effect, then adding subtle CRT-style scanlines across the screen using thin dark strips at low opacity so they darken slightly without overpowering the glow effects beneath.

Now I'm adding glass highlight streaks in the upper left using thin rotated boxes in a light purple tone for a glint effect, plus a lighter border frame around the window edges to suggest glass thickness.

Working out the bezel geometry: placing a cyan trim just inside the black bezel, then building the bezel itself as top/bottom/side bars with specific widths, heights, and depths to form the outer frame.

Adjusting the metalDark frame to sit at 0.262 inward with thickness 0.013 resolves the overlap with the cyan trim, and the glass layer fits fine inside the recess. I'm also adding small details to the bezel's bottom bar—tiny chrome knobs for brightness controls plus a glowing red LED, positioned along the bottom bar.

Placing chrome knobs and a magenta power LED...

Now I'm positioning chrome L-bracket corner accents at each outer bezel corner, calculating the horizontal and vertical leg offsets so they sit flush against the frame's edges.

Still placing corner screws...

I'm thinking I don't need every part unmerged for quality—merging similar geometry is fine visually even with a high part budget allowed, though I'll name components like screen parts for clarity. I should still add a few distinct touches, like a cyan bezel trim line and a rear black backing plate behind the cabinet shell to suggest CRT depth.

Still positioning box layers...

I'm placing a thin magenta glow strip along the shelf's front edge, computing its world position from the local coordinates, and deciding to skip the side recess walls for simplicity. Now I'm starting to write the helper functions, importing the geometry merging utilities and glow effect needed to build the scene.

Setting up the screen assembly function...

Adding cylinder and extruded shape geometry...

I also realize extrude geometries are non-indexed while boxes are indexed, so I need to convert everything to non-indexed before merging to avoid a mismatch.

For each merged batch I'm calling part() with the combined geometry, applying glow if needed, and placing it at the origin since this part has no joints to ride on.

Now I'm setting up screen dimensions and layering helpers, then building the glowing sky bands as a sequence of boxes stacked at increasing depth with distinct colors.

I'm also checking the ground plane dimensions and verifying I'm staying within the 6-own-color limit across the sky, ground, and sun gradient palette.

Trying to reuse existing palette colors like neonMagenta, gridPurple, and screenGlow for the sky bands rather than inventing new ones, adjusting band heights to keep the horizon glow balanced.

For the sun, I'm picking a gradient that transitions from neonPink/magenta at the bottom through sunOrange to sunYellow at the top, making sure the bottom colors don't clash with the magenta sky band behind them. For the ground, I'll use a very dark purple tone.

Writing sun strip code...

Clipping the top strip so it doesn't exceed the sun's bounds, then coloring bands by vertical position into pink, orange, and yellow gradients. Now I'm sketching the mountain silhouettes as triangular shapes sitting along the horizon line, layered above the sun and ground.

Drawing a neon pink horizon line layered in front of the mountains, then building out a perspective grid with horizontal lines curving toward the vanishing point and vertical lines radiating from it, carefully clipping positions near the edges.

I'm assigning layers: ship and invaders at layer 5, stars in the sky at layer 3, scanlines at layer 6, and the glass bezel with glints at layer 7 in front. I'm also defining a pixel-drawing helper that converts a sprite's row/column grid into positioned boxes with slight gaps between them for a retro pixel look, then starting to lay out the ship sprite using it.

Now I'm placing the ship's laser bolt as small yellow boxes just above it, checking it doesn't clash with the grid lines beneath, and working out positioning for tiny pixel-text score labels like "1UP" and "HI" at the top of the screen, adjusting the invaders' row height so they don't overlap the score text or go past the screen's top edge.

Checking overlap with the sun shape at the center confirms the invaders clear it with margin, and the score text fits comfortably above the invader row within the screen bounds. Now I need to design a small pixel font for the digits and letters needed in the score display.

Working through the text-rendering orientation: since the model faces +Z with its left along +X, a viewer standing in front looking toward -Z sees the model's right on their own left, meaning increasing x actually reads left-to-right for the viewer — so pixel columns and reading direction align correctly without needing to flip anything.

Now I'm positioning the score text: "1UP 0840" starts around x0=-0.245 and spans to about -0.155, while "HI 8400" starts around x0=0.165 and ends near 0.243, keeping both labels comfortably within the viewable width.

I'm adding scanline strips drawn as thin dark boxes stepping down the screen every 0.012 units, layered subtly over the text and ship, plus a glowing glass border frame built from four thin boxes along the top, bottom, and sides.

Now I'm building out the bezel and grille details: back-plate and bezel bars without glow, a dark recessed panel for the grille, and a row of vertical slot cutouts spaced across its width.

Adding the neon cyan top edge line on the grille and narrowing its slot width, then working out the slot spacing formula for 21 slots. I'm also placing chrome knobs on the bottom bar with tick marks and a small red LED glow indicator.

I'm adding a cyan LED indicator on the right, plus corner brackets, screws, and magenta/cyan accent strips on the ledge, along with a subtle curved glass hint for CRT feel. Now I'm writing the matrix composition code for the base transform.

Still writing geometry logic...

Checking the boundary cases - lines with larger |j| get clipped by the sides, vertical lines reach exactly to the screen bottom, and the ground and horizontal lines line up properly at the edges. Now I'm ready to write out the full solution.

spec.name: Neon Cabinet 1984
spec.description: A synthwave 1980s upright arcade cabinet with a glowing magenta and cyan marquee, angled screen, joystick control panel, and neon side art.
spec.layout: Classic upright cabinet. A tapered side-profile body stands on the floor with a recessed kick plate. The front (+Z) has a slanted control panel at about y 0.95 that juts forward, a vertical coin door below it, and a bezel with a screen leaning slightly back above it. A marquee box tops the cabinet and overhangs the front a little. The body is dark indigo-black, with hot magenta and cyan neon stripes, a sunset-gradient side decal built from stacked small plates, a grid and palm motif, and chrome trim. Screen, marquee, buttons and coin slot glow. No ground or extra props.

parts.builds: Main cabinet body: two extruded side panels with the classic stepped profile (tall back, forward-leaning control shelf, notched kick base) in body colour, back panel, front lower panel, top cap, kick plate in kick colour, chrome T-molding strips along the side edges, small feet. Cyan and magenta neon edge strips along the front edges. Overall stays inside its box and rests on the floor.
parts.attaches: Top meets marquee at marqueeBase; front meets the control panel at panelFront and the coin door at coinDoor; sides carry the decal at sideLeft/sideRight.

parts.builds: Slanted control deck jutting forward: sloped purple-black top plate with chrome front lip, a joystick (dark base, chrome shaft, red ball top), six glowing round buttons in red, blue and yellow with dark rims, two coin-style player-start buttons, small neon cyan outline trace and printed-style label stripes as thin parts. Includes the lower coin door: dark plate with two glowing slots, return cups, small chrome plates, and a pink neon frame.
parts.attaches: Rests against the carcass front at panelFront and coinDoor.

parts.builds: Screen area: bezel box frame in black with a recessed tilted CRT glass, glow-green screen face with a small pixel-art scene as parts (alien invaders rows, a ship, score text bars in cyan and magenta), chrome corner bolts, a cyan neon frame inside the bezel, speaker grille slits below the marquee as thin dark bars.
parts.attaches: Sits on the control deck rear edge at screenCentre and is bounded above by the marquee at marqueeBase.

parts.builds: Top marquee box with a slightly overhanging front: dark housing, glowing backlit front sign in magenta with a cyan outline, a stacked striped sun (yellow, orange, pink bands) with a perspective grid and a pair of palm silhouettes as small parts, a chrome top trim, lit LED dots along the bottom edge, and the cabinet name as blocky letter bars.
parts.attaches: Rests on the carcass top at marqueeBase.

parts.builds: Synthwave decals on both side panels, mirrored, built as thin plates seated 4 mm off the sides: a big sunset sun made of horizontal bands in yellow to pink, a purple mountain silhouette, a magenta and cyan perspective grid of lines at the bottom, and diagonal neon stripes with a small star field of white dots. Also a rear back-panel vent grille and an AC power plate with a cord.
parts.attaches: Plates sit on sideLeft and sideRight surfaces of the carcass; the back items on its rear face.

spec.name: Polar Ridge Research Outpost
spec.description: A Firewatch-style flat-colour diorama of a small arctic research station: a burnt-orange stilted cabin with a snowy roof and chimney, a connected lab module with a radome, a guyed radio mast, a wind turbine and a yard of fuel tanks, a snowmobile and a sled, all on a faceted snow drift base with ice crags.
spec.layout: Static diorama on one faceted snow platform, about 8.8 m square, centred on x=0 and standing on y=0. The snow is a low irregular octagonal slab whose flat top sits at y=0.35. The platform reads from the front (+Z), and everything else sits on y=0.35 (feet may sink 0.05). From front to back: a yard strip (z 1.6 to 4.2) with stepping-stone path, snowmobile and sled; the MAIN CABIN centre-left (x -2.9..1.3, z -1.9..1.9, floor y=0.8 on timber piles) with a covered porch and steps facing +Z; a LAB MODULE centre-right (x 2.0..4.0, z -1.8..1.2) joined to the cabin by a short enclosed corridor at x 1.3..2.0; a fuel-tank cluster on the left flank (x -4.3..-3.0, z -1.0..3.2); at the back, the RADIO MAST (back-left, x -3.4, z -3.0, top y 6.6) and the WIND TURBINE (back-right, x 3.0, z -3.1, hub y 5.0, blade radius 1.3). Jagged ice and rock crags fill the back centre (x -2.2..1.2, z -4.4..-3.4, up to y 2.2). Style: Firewatch flat colour. Bold simple blocky silhouettes, sunset palette with warm burnt orange, ochre and cream on lit faces and dusky purple-pink on shadow sides. Each snow mass uses a warm pale snowLit top and a snowShade or snowDeep sliver on its sides or underside. Every window glows warm yellow with a dark frame. Roofs carry a thick snow cap built as separate slabs. Trim is cream. No gradients; every detail is a small part in its own flat colour, seated on the surface. Faceted, low-segment shapes (6 to 8 sides) only.

parts.builds: The platform and everything natural. A faceted octagonal snow slab (radius about 4.3) from y=0 to a flat top at y=0.35: lower rim band in snowDeep, middle band in snowShade, top slabs in snowLit, so the dark underside shows around the edge. Overlapping low drift wedges and humps (snowLit tops, snowShade sides) piled against the building feet, along the back and at the corners, never above y 0.7 near buildings. Back-centre crags at x -2.2..1.2, z -4.4..-3.4: five to seven tall faceted prisms and cones in rock and rockLight, up to y 2.2, with snow caps (snowLit) on top and chunks of iceBlue and iceDeep ice shards leaning among them. Smaller scattered rocks with snow caps at two or three other edge spots, kept out of the building and yard footprints. A packed-snow path of flat stepping stones (snowShade, slightly above the snow top) leading from stairFoot at the porch to the front edge and a second branch toward labDoor. A few small orange survey-flag poles (wood pole, safetyOrange triangle flag) along the path. Slim footprints and sled-track grooves as small dark-snowDeep flat strips are optional. The terrain does not build any building, tank, vehicle, mast or turbine.
parts.attaches: Its top at terrainTop y=0.35 is the floor for every other part; they sink into it by up to 0.05. Path begins at stairFoot and the labDoor step.

parts.builds: The main habitat cabin, the hero building. Eight to ten timber piles (wood, woodDark caps) from y 0.3 to the floor at y 0.8, with a woodDark floor slab. Walls x -2.9..1.3, z -1.9..1.9, from y 0.8 to the eave at y 2.9, in cabinWall with horizontal clapboard lines as thin cabinWallShade strips and cream corner posts and a cream base trim board. Gable roof with its ridge along x at y 3.9 and overhang 0.3: two roofDark slopes plus a thick snowLit snow cap slab on each, a snowShade underside lip, cream fascia boards, and triangular gable ends (cabinWall) with a small glowing round attic window (windowGlow with a frameDark ring) on each end. Front face (+Z): door at x -0.8 (wood, cream frame, small glowing window, brass-like tarpOchre handle), two windows either side at x -2.0 and x 0.4, each with a frameDark frame, windowGlow panes, a cross muntin, a cream sill and snowLit sill snow. The left wall (x -2.9) has two windows. The back wall has one window and a stacked woodDark firewood pile with snow cap beside it. A brick-like chimney (rockLight and rock bricks, snowLit cap) on the roof at x -1.9, z -0.7, top at y 4.4 with three or four stacked smoke puffs of snowShade and snowLit above it (chunky low-poly blobs, a drifting column). A covered porch: deck at y 0.8 from z 1.9 to 2.9, x -1.7..0.1 (wood planks as separate strips), two corner posts, a small shed roof (roofDark with snow cap), a railing with balusters, wide steps (3 treads) down to stairFoot at z 3.5. A hanging lantern by the door (frameDark cage, windowGlow core), a safetyOrange life-ring or a weather sign board beside the door with a simple emblem, an antenna whip and a roof-vent cap on the roof, a cream stripe of icicles (iceBlue small cones) along the front eave. On the cabin's right wall (x 1.3) a doorway at z -0.3 where the corridor joins (just trim the cream frame, no door leaf).
parts.attaches: Stands on terrainTop via piles. Right wall at x 1.3 meets the labModule corridor at corridorJoin. Porch steps end at stairFoot. The chimney top is at chimneyTop. The cabin's roof overhang reaches x 1.6 but stays above y 2.9, so it clears the corridor (top y 2.3).

parts.builds: The science lab annex. A short enclosed corridor from corridorJoin (cabin right wall, x 1.3) to x 2.0, about 1.1 wide (z -0.85..0.25) and y 0.8..2.3: labWhite walls, labTeal roof strip with a snow cap, a small glowing window, a cream door frame at the cabin end. The lab body: x 2.0..4.0, z -1.8..1.2, floor y 0.8 on 6 piles (metalGrey, woodDark caps), walls to y 2.9 in labWhite with horizontal labTeal band stripes at y 1.4 and y 2.6 and safetyOrange corner posts. A low-pitched shed-style roof (labTeal, thick snowLit snow cap, snowShade lip). Front face (+Z at z 1.2): a door at x 3.0 (metalGrey with a safetyOrange stripe, round porthole of windowGlow with frameDark ring), a small landing and two steps down to y 0.35 (z 1.2..1.6), a painted emblem sign above the door made of small parts (a signalRed disc with labWhite snowflake or atom arms). Two wide windows with frameDark frames and windowGlow panes with a tall glowing slit. Side wall x 4.0: a vent grille (stacked metalDark slats) and a round exhaust duct with a cap. Back wall: a cable inlet box (metalDark) at labBackWall. On the roof: a radome, a half-sphere in labWhite (radius 0.7, centre at x 3.0, z -0.8, y 2.9) on a metalDark ring base, with panel seam lines as thin rings in labTeal and a signalRed beacon on top; a Stevenson-style weather screen (white louvered box on four legs) at x 2.5, z 0.5 on the roof; an anemometer (three small cups on a spinner arm, thin mast) on the roof corner. Snow banks piled against the base are in the terrain part, so only build a small snow cap on each step here.
parts.attaches: Corridor meets the mainCabin at corridorJoin. Lab floor mount labFloor, door at labDoor, back wall inlet at labBackWall (the commsPower power cable ends there). Piles stand on terrainTop.

parts.builds: Two tall landmarks at the back, plus their wiring. (1) The radio mast at mastBase x -3.4, z -3.0, top at mastTop y 6.6: a square lattice tower of four metalGrey legs tapering from 0.6 base width to 0.2 at the top, horizontal rungs and diagonal braces every 0.55 m, a small concrete footing (rockLight) with a snow cap, three tiers of guy wires (thin metalDark rods) running to four ground anchors (small rock blocks with a ring) at about 2 m from the base, avoiding the cabin footprint (x -2.9..1.3, z -1.9..1.9), a signalRed and white striped section near the top, a parabolic dish (a lathe bowl in labWhite, a metalDark feed arm) pointing toward +Z-left at y 5.0, a pair of yagi antennas (a thin boom with cross rods) at y 5.7, and a glowing signalRed beacon sphere on top with a small cage. (2) The wind turbine at turbineBase x 3.0, z -3.1: a tapered 8-sided tubular tower in labWhite from base radius 0.22 to 0.1, up to y 4.9, with a rockLight footing and a small safetyOrange door-panel box at the base, a nacelle box (labWhite with a labTeal stripe) at the top, with the hub at turbineHub (z -2.75, y 5.0): a spinner nose cone (safetyOrange), and three tapered blades in labWhite (radius 1.3, flat plates in the XY plane facing +Z, spaced at 120 degrees, one pointing up and slightly angled, with safetyOrange tips). A small tail vane at the back of the nacelle. (3) Power: a small battery and solar array on the ground at x -1.4..0.4, z -3.6..-2.6, three tilted solar panels (frameDark frame, iceDeep cells with thin metalGrey grid lines, snow lightly dusting the upper edge) on metalGrey legs, and a thin black cable (frameDark) drooping from the turbine base to labBackWall as a chain of small straight segments.
parts.attaches: Mast footing sits at mastBase; turbine tower at turbineBase with its hub at turbineHub; power cable ends at labBackWall on the labModule. Everything stands on terrainTop. The turbine blades must stay at y>3.7 above the lab roof radome (top 3.6).

parts.builds: The working yard props, in two zones that must stay out of the cabin footprint (x -2.9..1.6, z -1.9..3.5), the lab footprint (x 1.3..4.1, z -1.9..1.6) and the path. Zone A, left flank, x -4.3..-3.0, z -1.0..3.2 at tankBed (-3.6, 0.35, 1.0): two horizontal cylindrical fuel tanks (8-sided, length 1.5, radius 0.38, one in safetyOrange, one in tarpOchre, with metalDark saddle cradles, cap bands, a filler hatch and a gauge dial) lying along z at x -3.7, a pipe run with a valve wheel in signalRed, a stack of five fuel drums (alternating safetyOrange, labTeal, signalRed with metalDark rim bands and cream stripes) near z 2.6, and a stack of wooden crates (wood, woodDark straps) covered by an ochre tarp with rope ties. Zone B, front right, x 1.6..4.3, z 1.7..4.2: a parked snowmobile at vehiclePark (2.8, 0.35, 2.9) facing +Z, built from a chunky cabinWall body shell and a safetyOrange cowl, a dark seat, windscreen (iceBlue), handlebars, headlight (windowGlow), two front skis (metalDark, curved up at the tips) and a rear tracked belt (a metalDark box with groove rib strips), a snow dusting on its seat. A sled at sledSpot (0.9, 0.35, 3.3) just right of the path, with two wooden runners curled up at the front, slats, a cargo load of two cream-strapped duffel boxes in labTeal and tarpOchre, a rope loop. Also a small cluster of equipment: a snow shovel stuck in a drift and a pair of skis standing against the lab's front corner at x 4.0, z 1.5, kept small, plus a signal-flag pole with a signalRed banner at x 4.0, z 3.6.
parts.attaches: All objects rest on terrainTop. Tanks at tankBed, snowmobile at vehiclePark, sled at sledSpot. It never overlaps the cabin or lab footprints or the stairFoot path.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning an arctic research outpost diorama in a Firewatch-inspired flat color style with warm sunset tones against teal shadows, static with no joints, and sketching out the main structures—cabin, lab module, radio tower, wind turbine, fuel tanks—within a part budget and overall size constraints.

Now I'm working through coordinates: a snow base platform with drifts, rocks, and distant ice crags for the terrain part, then placing the main cabin as an elongated raised structure on stilts above the snow line, defining its wall heights and footprint relative to the base.

I'm adding a pitched roof peak, a front porch with stairs and glowing windows, and choosing the color palette—rust red/orange walls, dark teal roof, with firewatch-inspired accents of ochre, dusky pink, and purple-blue, plus a chimney with smoke puffs. Then I'm sketching a second building, a lab module connected to the cabin via an enclosed corridor on its right side.

I'm refining the lab module's dimensions and adding a white radome dome on its roof, plus a weather station with an anemometer and Stevenson screen, though I'm worried it overlaps with the tower. Now I'm positioning a lattice radio mast at the back-left, checking it clears the cabin's bounding box.

For the final pieces, I'm planning a wind turbine at the back-right, fuel tanks up front, and organizing the overall structure into five parts: terrain, buildings, lab module, comms/power (mast, turbine, solar panels, guy wires), and a yard section with a snowmobile, sled, crates, fuel drums, and flag poles—dropping the dog kennel idea to keep things focused.

Now I'm checking the overall dimensions and placements to make sure nothing overlaps: the mast base sits clear of the cabin, and the turbine's hub and blade span stay within bounds once I account for radius and height.

Working out the porch placement centered on the cabin door, with stairs extending down, and laying out the yard zones on both sides for the snowmobile and fuel tanks.

Since the yard needs to span two separate regions without overlapping the cabin box or the lab box, I'm planning to describe it as two explicit zones — left and right — with clear x/z boundaries that avoid those other structures.

For the terrain, I'm setting a flat snow height around 0.35 with the cabin and yard objects sinking slightly into it, while the terrain's own base sits at floor level zero so lowest points touch the ground. I'm also placing back-corner crags and a mast near z -3.0 to -3.6, keeping the lab's front door and entry step positioned at x 3.0 with a defined threshold.

I'm deciding to skip the frozen pond idea and instead sketch a simple stepping-stone footpath of packed-snow plates running from the porch stairs toward the front edge and over to the lab door. Now I'm drafting a Firewatch-inspired color palette with warm pink-white snow highlights, muted rose shadow tones, and deeper violet-gray shading for contrast.

Adding more palette colors...

Now I'm working out the cabin's structural proportions: floor level, pile heights, wall height of 2.1 units, and a pitched roof with ridge running along the x-axis, plus placing the chimney.

I'm also mapping out the cabin's footprint (width 4.2, depth 3.8), the porch and stairs extension, and figuring out where the corridor connects the cabin to the adjacent lab module at the shared wall.

Now I'm laying out the join points for each structure—cabin floor, porch deck, door, corridor join, lab floor and door, mast base, turbine base and hub, tank bed, and vehicle parking—mapping their coordinates so everything connects properly.

I'm also planning the power cable running from the turbine to the lab's back wall, plus guy wires anchoring the mast to the ground, all owned by the comms/power system. For the style, I'm settling on flat faceted colors with warm-lit sides and purple shadow sides, snow caps in warm white on each roof, and shadowed undersides—deciding to skip any sunset sun-disc flourish and keep the Firewatch mood understated. Now I'm ready to start writing out the full JSON description of all these parts.

I'm figuring out how to type the buildTerrain function's parameter object, deciding whether to rely on the module's provided Ctx type or define a safer local alias to avoid conflicts.

With no joints to attach to, I'm planning simple helper functions like `part` that wrap `b.part` with position, rotation, and scale options, treating everything as root-level static geometry. For the platform, I'm working out an octagonal slab using CylinderGeometry with 8 sides, reasoning through the vertex angles and rotation offset needed to get flat faces facing forward, and comparing circumradius versus apothem to hit the roughly 8.8m square footprint target.

I'm considering whether to make the octagon irregular by building a custom extruded polygon instead, working out cross-product math to determine the correct thickness axis for the extrusion.

For the layering, I'll stack three slabs of different heights and slightly different outline scales to create a snow-cap effect: a darker inset bottom slab, a mid-tone middle slab at full scale, and a lighter, slightly smaller top slab for a tapered look.

Computing octagon vertex positions...

Now I'm designing a drift helper for snow humps—flattened hexagonal bases with lighter caps on top, scaled by width/height/depth, settled into the snow with base around y=0.3 and peaking near 0.7 by the buildings. I'm placing these drifts around the cabin's edges and near the tanks to look naturally piled against structures.

I'm checking drift placement against obstacles: keeping clear of the tanks, stair footings, and lab steps, and verifying drift heights stay below the cabin floor level. I'm also planning drifts near the snowmobile and sled and along the platform corners, avoiding the front where vehicles sit.

Now I'm checking the mast base, turbine, solar panels, and crags to make sure drift placements stay clear of their footings, then mapping out a few more drift locations along the back and sides near the lab structure.

I also need to double-check that corner points stay within the octagon's boundary — since it has flat faces at the axes, diagonal points near 45° can easily fall outside the actual edge even if they're within the circular radius, so I'm recalculating using the apothem and corner-cut constraints to keep placements valid.

I'm checking each placement against the octagon boundary constraints, confirming the snowmobile position at (2.8, 2.9) fits within the platform edge even though it's tight. Now I'm planning out roughly 14 drift piles, making sure their positions avoid the stone path leading from the stair foot to the front edge of the platform.

For the path itself, I'm placing just two stones between the stair foot and the front edge, then considering a branching path toward the lab door that needs to route around the sled and other yard obstacles.

I'm trying to route the branch path around the sled without overlapping its footprint, testing a few different starting points near the porch and stairs to avoid collisions with the step width and porch edge.

Continuing to plot the stepping-stone path around the lab and porch, checking each coordinate against the yard, wall, and step boundaries to make sure stones don't overlap buildings, then working out a plausible route from the stairs toward the sled area.

Checking for overlap between the branch stones and the sled's footprint, since a couple of the coordinates edge close to the sled zone but stay just barely clear—acceptable risk. Now working out the stair-foot stone placements near the base.

Laying out stepping-stone geometry... flat octagon-ish cylinder prisms scaled and rotated randomly, with a thin lighter cap disc on top for highlight, roughly doubling the part count to stay within the overall budget.

I'm tallying the full scene budget: platform, snow drifts, crags with ice shards, far-edge rocks, path stones, flags, and optional footprints come to around 110 parts, leaving room to add extras like rim icicles or ice boulders for more visual interest along the front-left edge.

spec.name: Polar Night Station
spec.description: A Firewatch-style flat-colour diorama of an arctic research outpost: a rust-red timber cabin on stilts, a mustard barrel-vault lab linked by a glazed corridor, a guyed radio mast with a weather station, and a yard of fuel, sled and snowmobile, all on a layered snow-and-ice slab.
spec.layout: Static diorama on a chamfered rectangular slab, 15 m wide (x) by 13 m deep (z); the slab top is y=0.4 and the tallest point is the mast at about 9.6 m. Front is +Z. The main cabin is a long rust-red timber hut at left-centre (x -6.1..1.0, z -2.5..4.8 including porch and stairs). Its ridge runs along X, and it stands on stilts with its floor at y=1.0. The porch, door and stairs face +Z. A glazed corridor leads east from the cabin's east wall to the mustard-and-teal barrel-vault lab at right-centre (x 2.0..6.4). A solar array is behind the lab and the yard is in front of it. The radio mast stands at back-left (-4.4, -4.4) and is the tallest element. A Stevenson-screen weather station stands beside it. A yard of fuel tank, drums, sled, crates, snowmobile and flagpole fills the front-right corner. A frozen pond lies front-left, a rock outcrop at back-right, and a packed-snow path runs from the stairs to the lab door. Firewatch style: every surface is one flat colour with no gradients. Big simple blocky shapes are lit warm (rust, mustard, cream-pink snow) on top and sides facing the sun, and cool (lilac, deep blue-violet) on undersides and in shadow, so shadow tones are separate flat parts such as lilac drift wedges under eaves and dark underside slabs. Every roof, ledge and crate top carries a separate thick flat snow-cap slab in snowLit with a lilac snowShade lip below it. Windows and lamps are glowing windowGlow/glowOrange parts with dark ink frames. Details are small flat parts: trim boards, bolts, stripes, signs and rust patches.

parts.builds: The diorama base and natural scenery only. The slab is an extruded irregular chamfered rectangle, about 15 x 13 m with 1.2 m chamfered corners. It has three visible side strata: a top snow layer from y=0.28 to 0.4 in snowLit with a snowShade lip, a middle iceBlue/iceDeep band (stripes of two blues, with some chunky offset blocks for a cut-away look), and a rockDark/rockMid base from y=0 to 0.14, with a few jagged blocks poking out of the side. The top is flat snowLit, with a slightly different tone patch of snowShade here and there. Low drifts (flattened wedge or half-sphere slabs, snowLit top and snowShade lee side) pile against the cabin's front stilts, the lab's rear, and the mast base. A frozen pond (flat low-poly ice disc in iceBlue with an iceDeep rim, pale crack lines and a few paperWhite glints) sits at the pondCenter, about 3 m across. A packed-snow path (flat, slightly sunken strips in snowShade, offset in a staggered zigzag) runs from pathStart to pathEnd, with a few footprint pairs. A rock outcrop of stacked faceted rocks in rockDark/rockMid with snowLit caps sits at outcropCenter, rising to 3 m. A few scattered boulders (rockMid with snowLit caps) of 0.3-0.8 m lie around, kept clear of the cabin, lab, mast, yard and path. Bare ground patches of rockMid peek through the snow. No buildings, props or machinery.
parts.attaches: Its top face is groundTop (y=0.4). Every other part stands on it and builds down to y=0.4, sinking up to 2 cm into it. It must leave free the footprints of the cabin (x -6.1..1.0, z -2.5..4.8), the lab and solar array (x 2.0..6.8, z -4.6..2.0), the mast and weather station (x -6.4..-0.2, z -6.4..-2.6) and the yard (x 1.2..7.3, z 2.4..6.3). The pond sits at pondCenter and the outcrop at outcropCenter.

parts.builds: The main timber cabin on stilts. Eight stout stilts (square posts) with cross-bracing run from y=0.4 to the floor at y=1.0, in cabinDark, with snowShade drifts at their feet. The floor platform is cabinDark. The walls are a box x -5.6..0.8, z -2.0..1.8, up to y=3.5, built as cabinRust board slabs with thin vertical battens in cabinDark and trimCream corner posts, window frames and a trimCream belt line. Window set: front wall has two large windows each side of the door, and side and back walls have one or two each. Each window is an ink frame, a glowing windowGlow pane, cross mullions in trimCream and a small snowLit sill cap. A thick chunky door in cabinDark at cabinDoor (x -2.4) with a trimCream frame, a small round window, a handle and an ink-and-glowOrange lantern beside it. A gable roof with ridge along X reaches ridge y=4.9. It has overhangs of 0.5 m, is built from two roofDark slabs with cabinDark fascia boards, and carries thick snowLit snow slabs on top with drooping snowShade lips and a few icicle cones in iceBlue along the front eave. The east gable end has a door at cabinEastDoor leading to the corridor. A fat stone-block chimney at x=-4.2, z=-1.0, rising to y=6.0 in rockMid with a rockDark cap and snowLit top, with a flat-colour smoke puff stack of 4 stacked low-poly spheres of decreasing opacity-free tones (snowShade to paperWhite) drifting up and back. The porch deck at y=1.0 runs z 1.8..3.4 in woodLight with plank lines, with a railing of posts and rail in cabinDark, four porch posts and a small shed roof (roofDark with snow cap) at y=3.3..3.6. A staircase of 5 steps in woodLight with cabinDark stringers runs from porchFront down to stairsFoot, with railings. On the porch sit a firewood stack (stacked cylinders in woodLight with trimCream end-rings) against the front wall, a bench, a coil of rope in cabinDark, a hanging sign in trimCream with ink text lines for 'POLAR STATION 7', and a tiny signalRed emergency box. On the roof: a small metalGrey stove pipe and a roof vent.
parts.attaches: Stilts stand on groundTop. The east door aligns with corridorWest (0.8, 1.0, -0.2), where the lab's corridor meets the east wall. The stairs end at stairsFoot on the path start. The chimney and roof stay inside the box and clear of the mast part (z < -2.6).

I'm weighing whether merging per color might feel too coarse versus keeping logical groups separate for clarity — maybe bucketing by color plus group name is a better balance within the part budget.

Now I'm working out the actual dimensions and placement: the body box, the short stilts beneath the floor at inset corners, the timber floor rim slab, and small footing pads under each stilt.

Setting face coordinates for front, back, left, right walls, then planning seam details: vertical strips, a cream trim band near the top, a dark band near the bottom, and protruding cream corner posts at each corner.

I'm working out how seams, window frames, and door placement should overlap so the seams get hidden behind windows and doors, then calculating evenly spaced seam positions across the front face.

Now I'm figuring out a reusable helper for placing windows on each face by converting a local face coordinate (u, v) into world position and rotation based on each wall's normal direction and tangent axis.

Still working out positioning...

Working out window dimensions and placement, then designing the frame structure with cream backing, glass pane, cross muntins, and a sill box to give the windows depth and detail.

Now I'm thinking through shutters flanking each window, deciding whether to add slat details for texture, and being careful about which extra colors to introduce beyond the base palette to stay within budget.

Instead of slats, I'll go with a warm glow effect for the windows—adding a lighter accent pane and a curtain strip near the top in a soft orange tone. I'm also considering applying a glow kit to the window panes, beacon lamps, and portholes, making sure merged parts sharing a color still handle the glow material correctly.

Now I'm designing a bucket system where groups prefixed with "glow" automatically get a glow effect applied during flush, with different strength levels for panes versus beacons. Then I'm moving on to the door design, working out the frame and door panel dimensions so the door sits centered around the right height with a cream-colored frame surrounding it.

Adding door hardware details...

I'm also working out where to place a sign plate above the door, adjusting the trim band position to fit it in without feeling cramped against the door frame.

Then I'm figuring out the lettering effect with small varied-width bars on the plate, and moving on to positioning a beacon lamp on the roof ridge, calculating the eave overhang and roof slope angle to determine the ridge height.

Now I'm working out the slab geometry for the roof—its thickness, center position, length along the slope, and depth including front/back overhang—before setting up the gable triangles above the band on the front and back walls.

I'm working out the roofline geometry more precisely, calculating the centerline slope from eave to ridge and the resulting top and bottom surface offsets, so the gable triangle fill sits flush between the body top and the underside of the roof slab.

I'm adding small gable vent windows (cream-ringed glowing circles) to the attic faces, then placing thin cream bargeboards along the roof's gable edges at front and back for trim detail.

Now I'm working out a thin snow-cap shade slab offset slightly outward along the roof slope's normal direction, computing how the rotation angle affects which way that offset should point so it sits correctly on top of the sloped surface.

Computing snow top layer position stacked above the shade layer, making the shade slightly wider so it peeks out underneath for a layered look, then adding small lump boxes at the eaves to simulate snow draping over the edge.

I realize the ridge cap box overshoots the height limit at the roof peak, so I need to lower the pitch—shrinking the rise so the eave-to-ridge angle is shallower and the snow surface stays within the 2.5 ceiling.

I'm trimming the snow layer thicknesses so the beacon lamp mounted on the ridge still fits under the box limit, recalculating the stacked offsets so the top surface lands around 2.44 instead of 2.48.

Since the beacon's dome would still push past 2.5, I'm reconsidering the roof geometry itself — reducing the rise and recalculating the ridge height with a thinner slab, aiming to pull the snow-topped ridge down near 2.36 so there's enough clearance for the beacon.

Now I'm figuring out the chimney placement, considering putting it on the left slope offset from center, and computing the roof surface height at that offset point along the sloped centerline.

Working out the roof slope geometry with span and angle constants, then setting up a helper function to position each roof slab box in world coordinates based on the centerline and offset.

I'm adding eave lumps along the roof edges and small downward-pointing icicle cones in the ice color beneath them, then placing the beacon at the ridge center and the chimney offset to one side near the back.

For the beacon, I'm layering a metal base cylinder, a glowing red lamp sphere, and skipping the cap for simplicity, topping out around y=2.525. Then I'm moving on to the porch stairs extending outward from the front door with a timber deck.

Working through the step dimensions, I'm trying 3 treads with 0.12 risers down to snow level, but the planned tread depth overshoots the bounding box, so I'm reducing the depth to make the staircase fit.

Now I'm calculating the slanted stringer boards for each side of the stairs, finding the diagonal length and tilt angle from the rise and run, then working out how to rotate the slab geometry about the x-axis so it sits flush along that slope.

Placing riser boards under each tread edge, then working out the railing: posts at the deck corner and stair bottom, with a slanted handrail following the stringer angle above the treads.

Placing balusters at each tread center connecting the step top to the sloped rail line, then adding short horizontal deck-side rails near the porch between z 1.1 and 1.3 at a couple of heights.

Now I'm adding two thin support posts under the deck front corners and figuring out a fuel pipe running down one side of the body, likely on the left near z=-0.45 from a fill point down toward the ground.

For the pipe itself, I'm detailing a vertical metal run with a bend into the wall, mounting brackets every 0.4 units, a ground-level valve and spout elbow, a fill cap near the top, and a couple of yellow hazard rings as decoration.

But I realize this pipe position conflicts with the window and shutter placement on that side wall -- the shutters extend out far enough to overlap the pipe's z-coordinate, so I need to either shift the windows or move the pipe to a different wall to avoid the collision.

I'm positioning the shutters outward from each window frame so they clear the corner posts and pipe, checking spacing on both the left/right sides and the back face, and settling on a consistent window width of 0.32 with centers spaced ±0.34 for reuse across walls.

Checking the inner shutter spans confirm no overlap, and verifying the outer shutter clears the pipe at z=-0.55 with its radius. Now I'm working out front window placement since the front has the door, deciding to add two front windows at ±0.74 with narrower width and shutters for consistency.

Calculating the exact spans for front windows and shutters to make sure they clear the door frame outer edge, then settling on window height and y-center for sill placement, and adjusting back window width/spacing. I'm also considering adding small snow mounds near the base of the timber stilts for extra detail.

Now I'm positioning the four timber stilts beneath the cabin, calculating footing boxes and crossbraces, and working out rim joist and floor frame dimensions in x and z to make sure the floor overshoots the stilt positions properly.

Computing the side braces similarly, with rotation angles around the x-axis for symmetric diagonal struts on both sides. I'll skip adding extra floor detailing since the rim joist already covers it, but I want to scatter a few small snow patches on the deck and step treads for realism.

I'm also adding snow caps on the stilt footings and tiny snow boxes on the window sills, carefully positioning them just above the sill's top surface by working out the sill's vertical offset relative to the frame.

The overlap is minor so I'll keep the sill snow box as is. I'm skipping extra details like a lantern, but considering adding a cable running from the mast on the east side toward the cabin's wall entry point.

Adding a junction box and conduit stub...

I'll skip the firewood pile, wood stack, sled, and wall lamp as unnecessary scope creep, and skip the doormat too. Now I'm finalizing the color palette, including custom curtain colors with a warm orange tone and a light highlight.

Writing geometry helper functions...

For each bucket I merge geometries and create the part with flat shading, applying glow where needed. For the gable, I'll build it directly with a THREE.Shape extruded to a shallow depth rather than going through the helper, since that needs a part wrapper.

Then I'm setting up cylinder helpers for things like portholes, working out rotation axes so discs face the right way, and adding seam strips around the body while skipping the area covered by the door frame. I'm also planning a darker bottom band and a cream trim band around the cabin for visual detail.

Now I'm adding corner posts at each cabin corner that slightly protrude, overlapping cleanly with the bottom band, and deciding to skip a beacon light cone for now. I'm building a reusable window function that creates a cream trim backing, a glowing pane, and a small curtain strip above each window.

Adding muntins, sill, and snow on sill...

Adding shutter positions, slat accent lines, then working out face mapping for each box side with their coordinate offsets...

Now I'm figuring out the gable circle window placement as a rotated cylinder on the front face, and deriving the roofline geometry—computing the triangle apex height and how the roof's bottom surface slopes down from the ridge based on horizontal offset.

Checking the attic window fits within the gable triangle at that height, then placing the beacon at z=0.7 for visibility over the front. For the chimney, I'm positioning the flashing box at the roof height near the left side and sizing the pipe radius and height accordingly.

I'm building out the chimney's details: extending the pipe to about 2.45, adding a rain-cap cone and a small snow cap on top, and placing a metal strap ring partway down. I'm confirming the pipe passes through the roof correctly and considering a bit of snow accumulation around its base.

Then I'm working out the fuel pipe route down the side of the house: a vertical cylinder segment, an elbow sphere joint near the top, and a short horizontal stub connecting it into the wall, positioning everything relative to the house wall offset.

I'm adding a valve assembly with a vertical metalDark stem and a flat red torus handwheel oriented horizontally, then reconsidering the pipe extent since it pokes past the box boundary at x 0.6 -- I'll keep the horizontal run short with the elbow positioned closer in.

Still placing pipe details...

I'm also planning a junction box on the left wall below the window sill, sized and positioned to stay under the sill line, with a conduit and coiled cable running from it.

Now I'm setting up the core layout constants—wall positions, floor height, and corner coordinates—to drive the rest of the geometry.

Computing seam positions...

I'm considering whether to add a small awning over the door, but deciding the sign under the eave already provides enough visual interest there, so I'll skip it and just make sure the roof overhang extends properly on the front and sides.

Now I'll start writing the actual cabin-building function, importing the three.js utilities I need and setting up the destructured context parameters, keeping only the builder and primitive helpers I actually use.

Adding a helper to place geometries...

Still defining helper functions and naming conventions for each geometry bucket, then planning the flush step that merges geometries per group, creates parts, and applies glow effects to groups like glow/beacon/window.

Now I'm computing the stair tread dimensions and positions, building each step as a box with specific depth and height values.

Still working out deck and stringer placement...

Now I'm positioning the railing posts and handrail, calculating the top and bottom post heights based on the stair angle, then deriving the handrail's length, tilt angle, and center position to connect them.

Continuing to balusters at each tread center, sizing them to span from tread top to the sloped rail line, then adding deck-level railings and starting on the door frame layout.

Still working on door details...

Still placing door hardware...

I'm adding icicle details along the eaves using cone shapes, positioning them beyond the wall edges with randomized lengths spaced across the front and sides, skipping extra lighting details for now.

Now I'm building the stilt foundation structure: timber pads and mounded snow at the footings, vertical stilt posts spanning from the base up to a floor rim, with a dark timber rim framing the perimeter at the floor level.

Next I'm positioning diagonal corner braces front and back, calculating their lengths, rotation angles, and placement so they sit snugly under the floor rim between the stilts, along with matching side braces.

Then I'm setting up a roof helper function that computes slab positions using the roof pitch angle, projecting offsets along normal and tangent directions to correctly place each roof panel.

Still working out roof slab dimensions...

Now I'm figuring out where the ridge cap meets the top layer surface, then placing a rooftop beacon: a small cylinder base, topped with a red lamp sphere, keeping heights around 2.4-2.5 so it sits cleanly above the ridge.

Next I'm building the gable triangle fill for the body, extruding a triangular shape with front and back panels offset in z to give it depth, positioning each panel so the seams align with the roof structure.

Now I'm adding glowing attic window circles with cream rings on both front and back gables, positioned at the gable face depths. Then I'm setting up the main body as a red box with specific dimensions, checking that everything fits within the overall bounding box.

I realize the roof overhang slightly exceeds the body width, so I'm recalculating the span to 1.22 with a reduced overhang, recomputing the slope angle and slab length accordingly, and adjusting the fascia and eave lump positions to match the new span.

Positioning icicles, checking the roof's sloped centerline and gable height so the gap between roof and triangles is small but acceptable, then placing the chimney and its flashing with snow detail. I'm skipping extra decorative touches like a window box, doormat, wind chime, or ladder, just confirming the door, signs, and pipes are already handled.

Now I'm writing a helper function that places boxes on different walls (front, back, left, right) with proper offsets for depth, plus a similar helper for cylindrical shapes on front/back walls. I'm defining window placements and sizes for each wall and double-checking the shutter positions line up correctly on the back wall.

Checking the math for front and side shutter offsets to make sure they align against the door frame, then moving on to placing a wall lantern near the door on the front face.

Skipping snow banks since the floor is elevated, and adding a junction box on the left wall. I'm also working out icicle placement using cone geometries rotated to hang downward from the eaves, and planning a rain cap cone for the top of the chimney pipe.

Adjusting the pipe and cap dimensions so the snow cylinder sits properly on top without overshooting, then finalizing the component code with proper type signatures and color references.

spec.name: Arctic Research Outpost
spec.description: A Firewatch-style flat-colour diorama of a snowbound polar research station: a raised main cabin, a radio mast and dish, a weather and instrument yard, and a fuel and vehicle area, all on a small snow plateau.
spec.layout: A low snow plateau (about 6 x 6 m, 0.3 m thick) with gently faceted drifts. The main cabin (red-orange walls, cream trim, dark pitched roof with snow cap) sits left of centre (+X) with its door and a porch facing +Z. A tall lattice radio mast with a dish stands at the back (-Z) near the cabin. The weather yard sits at front right (-X, +Z): a Stevenson screen, an anemometer pole, a sample rack and a flag. Right of the cabin (-X) the fuel and vehicle area holds a snowcat, fuel drums and a generator shed. Flat colour only, with warm sunset oranges against cool blue shadows, thin dark window and door outlines as separate small parts, and glowing yellow windows.

parts.builds: Snow plateau: a faceted wide slab (snow top, snowShade sides, snowDeep base ring), several lumpy drift wedges and low snow mounds against the cabin and edges, a few rock outcrops (rock) poking through, small ice patches (ice), a packed path of snowShade slabs from the cabin door toward the yard, and footprints as tiny dark flat parts. Stays simple, sized to the other pieces.
parts.attaches: Top surface at groundTop (y=0.3); all other parts rest on it.

parts.builds: The hero: a boxy cabin 3.0 x 2.0 x 2.4 m on short wood stilts/skids, cabinRed walls with horizontal plank lines (cabinDark thin strips), trimCream corner posts, window frames and door frame, outlined windows with windowGlow panes and mullions, a door with handle, a porch with steps, railing and a lamp (lampGlow), a pitched roof of roofDark slabs with a snow cap on top and snow lumps along the eaves, icicles (ice) along the front eave, a steel chimney with a smoke-free cap, a stack of wood logs beside the wall, a hanging orange life ring and a small sign board with a simple emblem on the front.
parts.attaches: Floor at cabinFloor; door at cabinDoor; roof ridge at roofRidge; the back wall faces the mast near mastBase.

parts.builds: Tall lattice radio mast 3.9 m: three tapering steel legs with cross braces and diagonal rods (steel, steelDark), concrete-like base plinth (rock) with guy wires (thin rods) anchored to snow with small stakes, a platform ring near the top with orange and white banded segments, antennas whip rods, a red blinking beacon light (flagRed, glowing) on top, and a parabolic satellite dish (lathe dome in trimCream with steelDark arm and feed horn) at dishMount aimed forward and up. Also a small equipment box on the plinth with outlined door and cables.
parts.attaches: Base at mastBase on the terrain; dish at dishMount; sits behind the cabin.

parts.builds: The instrument yard at front left: a white Stevenson screen (trimCream, louvre strips, wood legs), an anemometer on a pole (three cups, vane) in orange, a rain and snow gauge cylinder, a wooden sample rack holding ice-core tubes (ice, steel caps), a flagpole with a flagRed flag and a trimCream stripe, a solar panel on a tilted stand (drumBlue with grid lines), a small snow-stake measuring pole with orange bands, and a couple of storage crates (wood, woodLight bands, outline label marks).
parts.attaches: Centred on yardCenter; rests on terrain; path leads toward cabinDoor.

parts.builds: Vehicle and fuel area at back left: a yellowCat snowcat with a boxy cab, tracks (rubber, with tread bars and steel roller wheels), glowing headlights, outlined cab windows with windowGlow, roof rack with a jerrycan and antenna, orange stripe and front blade in steelDark; a rack of fuel drums (drumBlue, drumGreen, orange) with band rings, lids and bungs, tipped with snow caps; a small generator shed (steel walls, roofDark roof, vent grille, exhaust pipe, outline door, small lamp) with hoses and cables running to the cabin; a sled with a tarp load behind the snowcat.
parts.attaches: Centred on fuelArea; rests on terrain; cable from shed runs toward the cabin side wall.
