spec.name: Chibi Axolotl
spec.description: A chubby chibi axolotl: a pink leucistic body with an oversized head, glossy black eyes, a wide smile, stubby limbs, a finned tail and six frilly hot-pink gill plumes.
spec.layout: Real axolotl scale (about 0.42 m nose to tail tip), chibi proportions. The animal lies flat on the floor in a neutral T-pose-like rest: head forward, body behind it, tail straight back along -Z, limbs splayed sideways with fingers fanned, and gills spread outward like a fan. Z runs from the snout at +0.17 to the tail tip at -0.255. The head is about 40% of the body length and about 0.16 wide, a broad, flat, rounded wedge with a blunt rounded snout, puffy cheeks and a wide upturned smile whose corners tuck into the cheeks. Eyes are big glossy black beads on the top-front sides of the head, each with a big and a small white highlight, small pink brow bumps above them and rosy blush discs on the cheeks. The torso behind the head is a fat rounded sausage with a pale belly sector underneath and a darker pink back with a few rose freckles. A low frilled dorsal fin runs from the back of the head over the back and continues into the tail fin. The tail is a vertically flattened oval tube with a fin skirt above and below, tapering to a rounded tip. Four stubby legs: front legs have 4 fingers, hind legs 4 toes, all with rounded fat toe tips and a darker pad. Three gill plumes per side sprout from the back of the head at upper, middle and lower height. Each plume is a tapered stalk with two rows of curled, tapering filaments, shading from deep pink at the root to light pink at the tips. They fan up, out and slightly back (about +/-0.165 m out at the widest) and are the signature feature, built bold and dense. Everything is faceted low-poly in flat colours, with a chunky, bold and cute look. Details (eyes, highlights, freckles, blush, nostrils, toe pads) are small parts seated on the surfaces in their own colours.

parts.builds: The big chibi head on joints head and jaw, as a separate upper head and lower jaw. Upper head: a broad flat rounded skull (squashed sphere or loft about 0.15 wide, 0.1 tall, 0.14 long) with a blunt rounded snout in skin pink, a slightly darker skinBack top cap, puffy cheek bulges, and two tiny nostril dimples in nostril colour at nostrilTop (x +/-0.012). Lower jaw on joint jaw: a smaller rounded wedge that closes under the upper head and ends at the chin at z 0.16, in skin with a pale belly-coloured underside. Mouth: a wide smile line in mouthLine, a thin swept tube along the lip seam between the jaws with corners curling up into the cheeks near cheekL/cheekR, plus a dark mouthInside sliver and a small tongue in tongue colour on the jaw, visible only as a hint. Eyes: big glossy beads (radius about 0.017) at eyeL/eyeR in eye colour with an eyeRing rim disc behind each, one big and one small eyeShine highlight sphere seated on the front-upper surface, and a small brow bump in brow colour above each eye. Rosy blush discs in blush colour on the cheeks at cheekL/cheekR facing outward and forward. A few freckle dots in freckle colour on the forehead. The back of the head tapers into the body at neckJoin and headBack, leaving room for the gill roots, which sit on the head's back sides. Nothing may sit in front of the face.
parts.attaches: Back of the head overlaps the body front at neckJoin and headBack. Gill stalks root at the gill*Root mounts on the rear flanks of this head. Dorsal fin begins at dorsalStart on the top rear of the head.

parts.builds: The fat rounded torso from neckJoin (z 0.07, tucked inside the head) back to the tail root at z -0.075, riding joints hips and chest. A loft or sweep with a slightly oval section about 0.1 wide and 0.085 tall, bellying wider at the chest, in skin pink with a skinBack top sector and a belly-coloured pale underside sector (use sweep sectors or loft colours). Belly sits at about y 0.005. A frilled low dorsal fin along the spine from dorsalStart to hipsTop: a thin membrane or extruded ripple fin in fin colour with a finEdge rim and small finRay ridge parts, rising about 0.012 to 0.015 m above the back. Small round freckle spots in freckle colour scattered over the back and sides, about 14 to 20 spots, seated on the surface. Shoulder and hip bulges in skin where the limbs attach, at shoulderL/R and hipL/R, small soft rounded mounds. Optionally a tiny cloaca bump on the underside near z -0.07.
parts.attaches: Front end tucks into the head at neckJoin. The rear end joins the tail at tailRoot (radius matches the tail start, about 0.036 wide by 0.04 tall). The dorsal fin continues into the tail fin at hipsTop. Limb roots seat on shoulderL/R and hipL/R.

parts.builds: The axolotl tail on joints tail1 to tail4, running straight back along -Z from tailRoot to tailTip at z -0.255. A smooth-skinned sweep with a vertically flattened oval section (about 0.034 wide by 0.04 tall at the root, tapering to a rounded tip about 0.006 wide), in skin pink with a pale belly sector underneath. A tall tail fin: a membrane or extruded skirt along the top and the bottom edge of the tube, in fin colour with a finEdge rim line along the outer edge, and fine finRay lines (thin sweeps or small parts) fanning across the fin. Fin height is about 0.03 above and about 0.02 below at the root, narrowing smoothly to the tip, and it continues the dorsal fin at hipsTop. A few freckle dots along the tail sides. Rounded, chunky and cute, and it bends smoothly with the chain.
parts.attaches: Starts at tailRoot, meeting the torso end. The top fin joins the dorsal fin at hipsTop. The tip is at tailTip.

parts.builds: Four stubby chibi legs, mirrored left and right, on the arm chains (shoulderL/R, elbowL/R, wristL/R) and the leg chains (hipL/R, kneeL/R, ankleL/R). Each limb is a fat tapered sweep (about 0.016 radius at the root to 0.011 at the wrist) in skin pink, with a rounded joint cap at the shoulder or hip where it meets the body. The hands sit on the floor at about y 0.012 and the feet likewise, so the lowest points touch y 0. Each hand is a flat paddle with 4 fingers fanned apart forward and outward; each foot is the same with 4 toes (splayed). Each digit is a short tapered rod with a round fat tip in toe colour, with a small toePad dot on the underside of each tip. Add a rounded palm or sole disc. The builder creates the digit joints itself with role digit and group limbs, named fingerL1 to fingerL4 and fingerR1 to fingerR4 on wristL/wristR, and toeL1 to toeL4 and toeR1 to toeR4 on ankleL/ankleR, each parented to its wrist or ankle joint. The digits splay in a fan about 70 degrees wide, pointing forward and outward, each about 0.03 long. Front limbs are slightly bigger than the hind limbs. A couple of freckle dots on each upper limb.
parts.attaches: Roots at shoulderL/R and hipL/R on the sides of the body; each limb root is buried slightly inside the torso. Feet and hands rest on the floor.

parts.builds: The signature frilly gills: three plumes per side (top, mid, low) on the chains gillTopL1/2, gillMidL1/2, gillLowL1/2 and the mirrored R chains (group gills, role fan). Each plume is a tapered stalk sweep along its joints, thick at the root (radius about 0.009) and thinning to about 0.004, in gillStalk colour, with a rounded gillRoot collar sphere where it meets the head at the gill*Root mounts. Along each stalk, filaments grow on both sides in two rows, 7 to 9 per side per plume. Each filament is a thin curved tapered sweep or spike (about 0.03 to 0.05 long near the middle, shorter near the tip), splayed 40 to 60 degrees off the stalk and curling slightly upward and back, coloured root to tip with gillMid and gillTip (bases in gillRoot or gillMid, tips in gillTip), with a tiny round bulb at each filament tip. Each stalk ends in a bunch of 3 short filaments. Bold overlapping fans, dense and fluffy, nothing thin enough to vanish. Top plumes reach up to about y 0.165, mid plumes spread widest to x +/-0.165, low plumes droop outward at about y 0.03. Make left and right match in mirror. Filaments ride the gill joint nearest their stalk point. Keep the gills clear of the face (they are behind the eyes, z at or behind about 0.05).
parts.attaches: Plume roots sit on the rear flanks of the head at gillTopRootL/R, gillMidRootL/R and gillLowRootL/R, which are slightly inside the head surface so they seat in it.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching the proportions for a chibi axolotl with frilly pink gills, thinking through realistic scale versus the exaggerated big-head chibi style, settling on roughly 0.36 wide by 0.17 tall by 0.42 long for the body dimensions.

Now I'm laying out the skeleton structure: placing hips as the root joint with a spine chain leading to the chest, then a head joint, a jaw hinge for the mouth, and a tail chain extending backward with multiple segments for flexible movement.

Still working out front and hind leg joint chains...

I'll let the limb builder generate digit joints itself with naming conventions like fingerFL1-4 for front hands and toe joints for hind feet, rather than pre-listing every one for determinism — simpler and conflicts should be minimal. For gills, I'm planning three branching stalks per side with frilly filaments, each needing its own parent joint chain.

Working through the gill joint placement now — positioning the stalk bases at the back-sides of the head and fanning them upper/middle/lower, trying to settle on clear naming like gillTopL, gillMidL, gillLowL so each chain's left/right and position is unambiguous.

Now I'm shaping the head: a wide, flat, rounded axolotl head with big chibi-style eyes on the top-front sides and a wide smiling mouth, sized larger than the body for the cute proportions. I'm setting the head bounding box and jaw position near the floor, then scaling the body down smaller in comparison to the oversized head.

For the body, I'm giving it a sagging belly resting on the floor and splitting the model into parts: a head group (skull, snout, jaws, eyes, cheeks, mouth details, spots) at a 200-part budget with head/jaw joints, and a body group with torso, belly, dorsal fin crest, and speckles at 150 parts, plus a separate tail piece with its fin membrane.

Beyond that I'm adding gills (six stalks per side with filaments at 250 parts) and four limbs with digits at 170 parts, keeping the total under 900. I'm defining the tail's vertical flattened cross-section continuous with the dorsal fin, and setting up mount points like hipsTop, neckJoin, tailRoot, and shoulder/hip joints so the body and tail builders connect seamlessly.

Now I'm sweeping the torso geometry from the head junction back to where the tail begins, sizing the tail's oval cross-section and tip position. I'm also setting up the leucistic pink axolotl color palette—body pink, belly cream, hot pink gills, dark eyes, and blush tones.

Still placing coordinates...

Combining limb boxes into one shared bounding region, deciding which parts should rest exactly on the floor (limbs yes, head no), and sketching out shoulder-to-wrist joint positions so the leg reaches down naturally to foot level.

Now I'm laying out the hip-knee-ankle chain for the hind legs, then building the joint hierarchy: root hips, chest, head, and jaw, each with position offsets and spine direction, working toward placing the jaw hinge near the back of the head so it can open toward the chin.

Jaw gets its role assigned, then I'm chaining out the tail segments from hips through four tapering bones. I'm planning to predefine all joints with b.joint before using b.chain and b.sweep to build the actual limb parts, assigning roles like "arm" and "leg" to the shoulder and hind joints and setting each joint's direction to aim toward the next in the chain.

Now I'm computing the shoulder, elbow, and wrist joint positions and directions for the arms, mirroring the left side to negative x for the right, and moving on to the gill joints anchored relative to the head's back position.

Still placing gill joints...

Now I'm adding mount points for head, mouth corners, and eyes, then defining the chibi style overall: big head proportion, stubby limbs, glossy highlighted eyes, blush, smile, and fluffy gills made of tapered comb-like filaments along each stalk.

Working out the part budgets: gill filaments with gradient coloring and small bulb tips, then dividing the roughly 860-point budget across body, head, gills, limbs, and tail, with each builder owning specific sub-features like shoulder caps, cheeks, eye sockets, brow, and the simple smiling mouth.

I need to write buildLimbs using the Ctx, creating digit joints like fingerL1 parented under wrist, tagged with role digit and group limbs, following the naming convention the spec calls for even though it's a bit ambiguous whether names should start with "limbs" or match the finger pattern—I'll go with the finger-named approach the spec seems to intend.

Category: Animal.
Subject: axolotl with frilly pink gills.
Style: chibi.

spec.name: Chibi Axolotl
spec.description: A chibi leucistic axolotl: a huge flat smiling head, a stubby pale-pink body, a paddle tail with a frilled fin and six feathery hot-pink gills, standing in a neutral rest pose.
spec.layout: UNITS ARE METERS, life-size axolotl (about 0.5 m with gills, tail and head). The model faces +Z, +X is the model's left, and it stands on y=0. The model is a low, wide salamander with a chibi head about 2x as wide as the body. Seen from the front: a very wide, flat, rounded head (width 0.2, height about 0.13) with two big black bead eyes high on the top corners, pink cheek blushes, a wide upturned smile and two tiny nostril dots. Three hot-pink gill stalks sprout from each rear cheek and fan sideways and up, carrying dense frilly filaments, so the gills span about x=±0.19 and are the loudest silhouette feature. The chunky body (width 0.13, height 0.10) lies behind the head and rests its belly on the floor. Four stubby limbs splay sideways with flat paws; each paw has long, rounded finger and toe tips fanned forward (4 digits on the hands, 5 on the feet). A laterally flattened tail tapers back to z=-0.31, with a scalloped fin running from behind the head along the back and round the tail tip, plus a short ventral fin on the tail. SKULL GEOMETRY (shared by head, face and gills): the upper skull is an ellipsoid centred at headCenter [0,0.083,0.14] with radii x 0.10, y 0.057, z 0.09 (top y=0.14, front z=0.23, rear z=0.05). The lower jaw is an ellipsoid centred at [0,0.035,0.15] with radii [0.088,0.026,0.078], hinged at jawHinge. The mouth seam sits at about y=0.056. The head ellipsoid is the only surface the face and gills seat on, so those parts must snap their details with b.surface(b.root).nearest(point) or .around(headCenter).at(az, el). Skull parts are built first, and the build order is head, face, gills, bodyTail, limbs. STYLE: stubby, rounded and cute, with chunky bold shapes, flat colours and low-poly facets (6 to 10 sided tubes, 8x6 spheres). Colour by place: pale rose on top, a cream belly and underjaw, darker rose back patch and freckle spots, then a deep-rose to hot-pink to pale-pink gradient along each gill filament. Fine detail (eyes, shine, blush, freckles, toe tips, fin ribs) is small separate parts in their own colours. Everything is left-right symmetric. Do not add a ground, rocks or water.

parts.builds: The chibi skull and jaws, which together read as one very wide, flat, rounded head. (1) Upper skull ellipsoid at headCenter with radii [0.10,0.057,0.09] in skin, shaded by a darker skinBack cap over the crown (a slightly smaller ellipsoid or flat lathe on top, y>0.1) and a few spot-coloured freckle discs seated on the crown (use b.surface/stick). (2) A snout bump: a small flattened ellipsoid at [0,0.07,0.205] so the front is blunt and cute. (3) Lower jaw on joint jaw: ellipsoid centred [0,0.035,0.15] with radii [0.088,0.026,0.078] in belly/cream, with a skin-coloured upper rim, so the mouth seam sits at y≈0.056. Inside the mouth, a small dark mouthInside tray on the upper skull's underside and a tongue (flat tongue-coloured ellipsoid) on the jaw floor. Both jaws overlap enough that the closed mouth has no gap. (4) Two low brow ridges above the eyes (small skin-coloured ellipsoids at eyeL/eyeR raised 0.012) so the eyes sit under a bump. (5) The throat/gular fold: 2 thin cream arcs under the jaw. Faceted low-poly spheres (10x7).
parts.attaches: Rides joints head (skull) and jaw (lower jaw, tongue). The back of the skull overlaps the body front at neckJoin. The gills and face build onto this skull surface at the mounts gillBase* and eyeL/R, cheekL/R and nostrilL/R.

parts.builds: Every facial detail, seated on the skull surface (snap with b.surface(b.root).nearest or b.stick; the head part is already built). (1) Two big chibi eyes at eyeL/eyeR, each layered: a dark eyeRing sphere (r 0.019), an eye bead sphere (r 0.016, glossy near-black), a thin eyeGold ring or crescent just under the pupil, and two white shine spots (one large at the upper outer side, one tiny lower inside) with r 0.005 and 0.0025. Eyes bulge slightly out of the skull and face forward-up. (2) A wide upturned smile: a mouthLine sweep (r 0.0012) draped along the mouth seam from the corner at x=-0.085 to x=+0.085, with both ends curling up 0.01, plus tiny dimple ticks at the corners. The line rides jaw/head and does not cover the jaw seam. (3) Blush: flat blush-coloured ellipses (about 0.03x0.02, 0.002 thick) at cheekL/R, aimed outward, plus 3 tiny darker blush ticks on each. (4) Nostrils: two tiny nostril-coloured dots at nostrilL/R. (5) A few tiny spot-coloured freckles across the snout. (6) A thin dark eyeRing arc brow lines above each eye. Everything stays small, layered as outline, main colour and highlight, and nothing hangs in front of the face.
parts.attaches: Seats on the head skull (head part) at eyeL/R, cheekL/R, nostrilL/R and mouthFront. The smile and mouth details are placed along the jawHinge seam and ride joint head for the upper features and joint jaw for the lower lip ticks.

parts.builds: The signature frilly gills: 3 stalks per side (6 total), the richest part of the model. Each stalk starts at gillBase{L,R}{1,2,3} (sunk slightly into the skull) and follows the joints gill{L,R}{n} and gill{L,R}{n}b (about 0.09 to 0.11 m long). Stalk directions are: stalk 1 out, up and back (reaching about y=0.2), stalk 2 out and a little up (reaching x≈±0.175), stalk 3 out and slightly down (low, nearly horizontal). Each stalk is a tapered smooth-skinned sweep (radius 0.007 to 0.003) on its two joints (gillStalk, with a darker gillDeep base collar of 0.01 radius where it meets the head). Along each stalk, 6 to 7 pairs of filaments branch both ways, built as slim leaf-shaped extrudes or flattened tapered spikes (length 0.03 near the base, 0.045 mid-stalk, shrinking to 0.02 at the tip), fanned about 50° to 70° away from the stalk, and curved a little backward. Filament colour runs root to tip: gillDeep or gillStalk, then gillFrill, then a gillTip pale-pink point or tiny bead. The filaments of the upper stalks arch up and those of the lower stalks droop, and the sides are slightly different lengths so the fan reads full and feathery. Each filament rides its stalk joint, so the gills can wave. A small cluster of 3 short filaments finishes each stalk tip. Mirror exactly across x=0. Use faceted 5-6 sided tubes.
parts.attaches: Roots at the mounts gillBaseL1-3 and gillBaseR1-3 on the rear cheeks of the skull ellipsoid (centre headCenter). Joints gill*, gill*b are children of head.

parts.builds: The torso, tail and fins. (1) A chunky body loft (chain/sweep over hips, spine and the neckJoin point) from z≈0.07 to z=-0.11, about 0.13 wide and 0.10 tall with a rounded oval section. It is centred at y=0.05 so its belly bottom rests on y=0, in skin, with a cream belly sector underneath (sectors or a separate flatter belly sweep) and a darker skinBack stripe sector along the back. (2) The tail is a swept chain on tail1..tail5 starting at tailRoot with the same section as the body end (half-width 0.045, half-height 0.045) and tapering to a flat paddle at tailTip (half-width 0.006, half-height 0.016) with a round or point cap, laterally flattened (taller than wide), cream belly sector underneath. (3) The dorsal fin: a membrane or extruded scalloped ridge from dorsalStart (just behind the head) along the back and the full tail round the tip, 0.025 high on the body rising to 0.035 on the tail, then falling to a rounded tip, in fin colour with a finEdge rim strip (a thin sweep along its outer edge), small rib lines (thin finEdge extrudes or rods) every 0.02, and scalloped bumps along the edge. A shorter ventral fin underneath the last 0.12 m of tail, same style. The fin rides the tail joints. (4) Markings: 10 to 14 spot-coloured freckle discs scattered on the back and tail sides (b.surface scatter, minDist 0.025), size 0.006 to 0.012. Subject: Baba Yaga's hut on chicken legs.
Style: Slavic folk art.

spec.name: Baba Yaga's Hut on Chicken Legs
spec.description: A Slavic folk-art diorama: a carved log izba with a red-trimmed gable roof, standing on two giant scaly chicken legs inside a skull-post fence on a small forest clearing.
spec.layout: Everything is centred on x = 0 and faces +Z, which is the front door and stairs. A round clearing disc (radius 3.5, top y 0.2) is the only floor piece. The izba floats on two chicken legs standing at x = ±0.75, z about 0.1, with feet planted at y 0.2 and toes splayed forward. Bottom to top: clearing y 0 to 0.2; legs y 0.2 to 2.0; a hut floor platform from y 1.85 to 2.0 (footprint x ±1.4, z ±1.3); honey-brown log walls y 2.0 to 3.5 (outer faces x ±1.3, z ±1.2, with log ends and rings sticking out 0.1 at the corners); then a steep gable roof with eaves at y 3.4 and x ±1.85, ridge at y 4.9 running along z from -1.65 to 1.75, overhanging the front. The front gable (door side, +Z) holds the door and the porch: a landing at z 1.2 to 2.0 and steep stairs down to the clearing, ending at z 3.1. A stubby brick chimney sits on the left rear slope. A horse-head ridge finial (konyok) crowns the front and back ends of the ridge. Folk art shows through one repeated motif, the six-petal rosette and sun, in red, yellow, blue and white. It appears on the door, window platbands, gable sunburst, porch balusters, fence posts and the clearing's border band. Carved platbands with zigzag cut-outs frame every window. Fretted barge-boards (polotentse) hang from the gable edges. Shingles alternate two browns with scalloped ends. The legs are chunky and bright yellow, with thick feathery rust-and-cream trousers at the top, scaled shanks, a spur, and three big dark claws plus a back toe on each foot. A skull-on-stake fence rings the clearing, with an open gap at the front for the stairs and a pair of gate posts. Birch trunks stand at the back corners, red-and-white fly-agaric mushrooms, flowers and stones decorate the edge, and a mortar and pestle rests near the stairs. The whole look is a chunky, simple primitive base with painted ornament built from small separate parts, and every surface is one flat colour.

parts.builds: Both giant chicken legs, mirrored, each running hip, knee (forward), hock (back) and ankle with a continuous smooth-skinned scaly tube. The tarsus is yellow (scaleYellow) with scaleDark scale plates, bands or ridges as small seated parts, and a sharp spur on the back of the hock. The thigh and knee wear a big shaggy trouser of overlapping feather blades in a root-to-tip palette (featherRust at the root, folkWhite and folkBlack tips), starting at y 2.0 so it tucks under the hut platform at hutUnderside around the hip mounts. The foot has three forward toes (toeL1 centre, toeL2 inner, toeL3 outer; toeR1 to toeR3 mirrored) and a back toe (toe4), each a tapered tube with knuckle bumps and a big curved dark claw (folkBlack, with a folkWhite highlight). Toe bottoms rest just in the clearing (ankle y 0.3, toe radius about 0.09). Ankle gets a folk-art red band with tiny yellow dots. Rigs: sweeps skinned over the leg chains, toes on digit joints. Shares the same left and right leg design, mirrored by sign of x.
parts.attaches: Hips at mounts hipL and hipR tuck under hutUnderside (y 1.85); feet plant at ankleL and ankleR just into groundTop (y 0.2). The feathers hide the seam at the hut platform.

parts.builds: The izba body. Floor platform (y 1.85 to 2.0, x ±1.4, z ±1.3) of dark planks with underside crossbeams and root-like knobs. Log walls y 2.0 to 3.5 built from stacked horizontal cylinders (about 6 courses, alternating logMid, logDark and logLight), outer faces at x ±1.3 and z ±1.2. Log ends protrude 0.1 at the four corners (notched corner crossings) and each end carries a small logEnd disc with a dark ring. A top plate logDark at y 3.5 and a moss patch or two (moss) on the base logs. Front wall: a door at doorCenter (x ±0.4, y 2.0 to 3.1) hung on the doorHinge joint, painted folkBlue with a folkRed border frame, yellow six-petal rosettes and a sun in the centre, iron-black hinge straps and a ring handle (folkBlack). It sits slightly proud of the wall. Left and right side windows at windowLeft and windowRight, and a back window at windowBack (opening about 0.5 wide by 0.6 tall, glowing warm folkYellow or glowWarm panes with folkBlack cross muntins). Each has carved platbands around it (folkRed frame, folkWhite zigzag cut-outs, a little folkBlue crown with a rosette on top, an apron below) and an open pair of shutters flat against the wall painted folkBlue with folkYellow rosette dots. The corner posts carry a thin folkRed painted stripe.
parts.attaches: Sits on hutFloor (y 2.0) over the legs at hutUnderside. Wall top at wallTop (y 3.5) meets the roof part. The front face at z 1.2 meets the porch landing at porchLanding and the stairs. Door rides doorHinge; everything else rides hut.

parts.builds: The steep folk gable roof and everything above wallTop. Two roof planes (thick slabs or lofts) run from eaveLeft or eaveRight (x ±1.85, y 3.4) up to the ridge at y 4.9, z -1.65 to 1.75, with a front overhang. They are covered by rows of scalloped shingle plates alternating shingleDark and shingleLight, and moss (moss) along the lower edges. A ridge beam (logDark) carries a carved horse-head finial (konyok) at ridgeFront and ridgeBack, painted folkRed with folkYellow trim and folkBlack eyes. A front gable triangle filled with vertical planks (logLight and logMid) fills from wallTop (y 3.5, x ±1.35) up to a point at about y 4.85. A round attic window sits at its centre with a folkYellow sunburst of 8 rays and a folkBlue ring, and a rosette row beneath. The gable edges wear fretted barge-boards (polotentse) in folkRed with folkWhite zigzag cut-outs and hanging pendant ends at the eaves. On the left rear slope a brick chimney (stoneDark with stone caps, folkRed brick courses) rises from chimneyBase, topped by a few puffs of smoke clumps (smoke) up to y 5.5. Small bone-white skull or rosette decorations are optional on the ridge.
parts.attaches: Roof eaves rest at wallTop (y 3.5) on the wall top plate; the gable triangle sits on the front wall at frontGable. The chimney stands on chimneyBase. Rides the hut joint.

parts.builds: The front porch and steep stair. A landing platform (planks logMid, edge beam logDark) with top at y 2.0, x ±0.85, z 1.2 to 2.0, at porchLanding. Eight steps run from stairTop (0, 2.0, 2.0) down to stairBottom (0, 0.2, 3.1), each a plank with rise about 0.225 and run 0.14, two stringers (logDark), and the front edge of each step carries a thin folkRed stripe with yellow dot accents. Railings on both sides: turned balusters (folkWhite with folkRed rings, small rosette caps) and a sloped handrail (logLight) following the stair, with carved newel posts topped with folkYellow balls at the landing. A hanging lantern (folkBlack frame, glowing glowWarm pane) on a bracket by the door at the landing's front-left. Small props on the landing and steps: a twig broom leaning on the rail (logLight handle, featherRust straw), a wooden bucket (logMid with folkBlack hoops), and strings of dried mushrooms or herb bundles (folkRed, folkWhite, folkGreen) hanging from a short beam at the landing's left edge.
parts.attaches: Landing meets the front wall at z about 1.2 near hutFloor and porchLanding. Stairs end at stairBottom on groundTop. Rides hut, whose stairs bottom just touches the clearing.

parts.builds: The diorama base and its dressing, kept simpler than the hut. A low round clearing disc (radius 3.5, y 0 to 0.2) in earth, with a grass cap (grass, with grassDark tufts as small cones, broad folk-style blades) and a dirt path (earth) from the gate to stairBottom. A folk border band around the rim: alternating folkRed and folkWhite wedges and folkBlue dots, repeating the rosette motif every ~0.7 m. A skull fence: stakes (logDark, pointed tops, one every ~0.45 m at radius about 3.15 with a gap of about ±22° around +Z) each topped with a folkWhite skull whose eye sockets glow glowGreen. Every third stake wears a folkRed painted band with a yellow dot. Two thicker gate posts at gatePostL and gatePostR carry bigger skulls. Behind the hut: two birch trunks (folkWhite with folkBlack bark dashes) at about (±2.7, z -2.3) rising to y 4.3, with a few angled branches and small folkGreen leaf plates. Along the fence and the sides, clusters of fly-agaric mushrooms (folkRed caps with folkWhite spots, folkWhite stems), big six-petal folk flowers (folkYellow, folkRed and folkBlue petals with folkGreen stems and leaves), and a few rocks (stone and stoneDark, faceted) with moss (moss) on top. A wooden mortar (logDark with folkRed band) with a pestle leaning in it, placed to the right of the stairs near (-1.7, z 2.5), and a fallen log and ferns near the back. All of this stays outside the stairs and the hut footprint.
parts.attaches: Disc top is groundTop (y 0.2): legs plant their feet on it and the stair ends at stairBottom (0, 0.2, 3.1). Fence gap lines up with the stairs between gatePostL and gatePostR. Rides ground.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching the diorama's component parts: the scaly chicken legs as the base, the log-walled hut body with carved door and window frames, and a steep gabled roof with carved horse-head ridge details, shingles, and a chimney.

Now I'm working out the overall layout — a circular ground base with a glowing skull fence, mushrooms, birch trees, and maybe a pestle and mortar for flavor, sized proportionally around the hut. I'm figuring out actual coordinates: the base disc radius, leg height and placement, hut wall footprint, and roof gable orientation, deciding the door should sit on the gable-facing side near the stairs.

I'm now placing a front porch with a small landing and stairs descending to the ground, accepting that the stairs will move with the hut's legs since this is a folk-tale structure. Next I'm sketching out the joint hierarchy, considering whether to root everything at the ground base or the hut itself.

Settling on "hut" as the root joint with spine role, I lay out the chicken-leg chains: hip, knee, ankle for each leg, then individual toe joints (three forward-facing, one hallux at back) for each foot, mirrored left and right, keeping all joint names alphanumeric without underscores. I'm also figuring out how the static base should attach—deciding it rides on the "hut" root since there's only one allowed root joint.

Working out the chicken-leg joint chain for the hut legs: hip bending forward to a knee, then back to a hock, then down to the tarsus and foot, trying to get believable bird-leg proportions and angles for each segment.

I'm also setting the bounding box for the legs part and placing the toes, spreading them forward and adding a back hallux, while checking for potential overlap between the toe spread and the front stairs geometry.

Now I'm breaking the hut body into components: chicken legs with feathered thighs, scaly shanks with spurs, and clawed toes in a yellow-and-orange folk-art palette with a budget around 190, followed by the hut walls starting with a foundation platform of root-and-bone beams beneath stacked log walls.

For the walls themselves I'm adding log ends at corner notches, chinking, a painted folk door, carved window frames with shutters, and a porch landing with railings and stairs, all at budget 200. I'm now organizing the model into five parts -- legs, hut walls with door/windows, roof and chimney, a porch with steps and lantern plus Baba Yaga's leaning mortar and pestle, and finally the diorama base with fence, skulls, and trees -- and sketching the porch's bounding box dimensions.

Working out the exact coordinates now: the hut floor platform sits around y=1.85–2.0 within its footprint, the porch landing spans z=1.3–2.0 at the same height, and I'm calculating steep stairs descending from the landing down to around z=3.3, figuring out step count and rise/run proportions to keep it feasible.

I'm sizing the overall diorama base disc to around radius 3.4–3.5 centered at z=0, making sure the stairs fit inside that boundary, and noticing the skull fence ring at radius ~3.1 would collide with the stairs at the front — so I'm planning a gap in the fence (roughly ±25-30° around the front azimuth) to act as a gate where the stairs pass through.

I'm working out step dimensions so the staircase descends from z≈2.0 to 3.12 over 8 steps with a rise of 0.225 and run of 0.14, placing the stair base near [0, 0.2, 3.1] and gate posts at x=±1.0, which puts them at radius ~3.26 — within the base boundary. I'm also setting the ground disc's top surface at y=0.2 so legs and other floor-resting elements sink slightly into the base.

Now I'm figuring out the roof geometry: wall top at y=3.5, eaves extending out to x=±1.85 at y=3.4, rising to a ridge at y=4.9, with the ridge beam spanning z from -1.6 to 1.7 and overhanging the front and back. I'm planning to crown the ridge with a carved horse-head ornament (an "ohlupen") on the front end.

I'm also working out the front gable triangle, filling between the wall top and the roof underside with a round carved window and sunburst motif, and placing a stone chimney off to one side near the back of the roof.

I'm figuring out the roof's shingle rows in alternating colors with scalloped edges, carved pendant barge boards, and moss patches, keeping the whole build within a budget of 200. Then I'm working through the hut wall dimensions, log-end protrusions at the corners, and the front door and porch landing placement relative to the wall surface.

Now I'm placing the side windows with carved platbands and shutters, deciding on a small back window, and sketching the gable triangle above the front wall. I'm also calculating the log courses for the walls, figuring six courses of 0.25-diameter logs to span the 1.5-unit height from floor to eave.

Then I'm planning the hut's underside platform and hip sockets where the legs attach with feathery fluff, mounting the hip joints, and sketching the leg "pants" overlapping the platform. For the diorama base, I'm laying out the ground disc with grass and dirt path, stone steps, a ring of skull-topped fence stakes with glowing eyes, scattered fly agaric mushrooms, and birch trunks at the back corners.

I'm adding more diorama details — birch placement relative to the roof overhang, folk-style flowers around the base edge, and a red/white/black triangle ornament band on the disc rim, with a 200-unit budget for that part. For the porch, I'm planning the landing, painted-stripe steps, railing posts with turned balusters, a glowing skull lantern, and hanging herb bundles, within a 120-unit budget.

Now I'm tallying the total budget across legs, hut, roof, porch, and base to confirm it stays under 900, and defining a limited color palette (≤24 colors) covering log tones, chinking, and the folk red/blue/yellow/white/black/green scheme used for ornamentation.

Still refining palette entries...

Trying to trim the palette down to exactly 24 colors, debating which near-duplicates to cut—chinking versus logLight, featherRust versus scaleDark—to keep the count tight while still covering logs, folk accents, shingles, scales, and terrain tones.

Now I'm starting to lay out the skeletal joint hierarchy for the hut structure, beginning with a root "ground" joint and a "hut" spine joint above it, defining positions and roles as I build out the rig.

Still mapping leg joint chains...

I'm settling toe thickness so bottoms embed properly into the ground top, keeping ankle height at 0.3. I decide to skip extra face-like features like a jaw or mouth, keeping the hut simple with legs, walls, roof, and porch all parented to the hut, and base parented to ground. Now I'm working out the base box dimensions along with fence skull heights.

I'm fitting the base box to hold the birches and mushrooms too, accepting overlap with other elements since it just needs to cover the ground dressing. I'm then setting bounding boxes for the legs (sunk into the base, floor false), the hut body, and the roof, with horse-head details rising above the roof's top edge at the ridge ends.

Now I'm defining the porch box with its railing height and lantern position, then listing out the mount points for the structure—ground top, hut floor, wall top, ridge line with its z-range, eave corners, hip and ankle points, and the door center—to anchor all the pieces together.

Still placing coordinates...

I'm now detailing the folk art styling — carved painted platbands, zigzag towel barge boards, ridge horse, scalloped shingles, and repeated six-petal rosette motifs across door, shutters, gable, base rim, and fence posts — then moving to write up the spec with budget, named joint groups, and JSON output, including leg/pants overlap positioning with the hut floor underside.

I need to write the buildChickenLegs function using the existing joint hierarchy—hipL, kneeL, hockL, ankleL, toeL1-4—placing geometry according to each joint's given position and direction along the leg chain.

Since the joints already exist rather than being created via a chain call, I'm planning to use sweep with a bone list option, passing the joint array so the mesh skins and bends at each joint. I'm figuring out radius tapering from thigh to tarsus and splitting the sweep into separate segments—thigh/shank in rust feather color bound to hipL, kneeL, hockL, and a distinct tarsus segment down to ankleL—to handle the color transition and joint positioning correctly.

I'll just pull joint positions directly from the J object rather than hardcoding mirrored arrays, trusting the hip-to-knee bone direction even though it's not perfectly aligned. For the foot, each toe becomes its own tapered tube starting near the ankle, sweeping outward with its own direction vector.

Adjusting toe y-positions and adding tapered segments with knuckle bumps, then sketching a curved claw sweep with a bezier path digging into the ground plus a highlight stroke on top.

Adding scale plate bumps along the toes...

For the tarsus, I'm figuring out the clock-angle convention: since this bone runs down and forward from the hock, angle 0 should correspond to the front/top-facing side, letting me place scale plate rows along that surface correctly.

Placing scale plates at angles -50, 0, 50 on top with sides at ±100, building them as flattened boxes oriented along the tangent direction using the sweep frame at each point along the path, and setting up the catmull path to compute the radius taper from knee to hock.

I'm deciding where the feather coverage ends along the leg, pushing the rust band down to about 80% of the way from knee to hock so it laps near the hock before transitioning to yellow tarsus coloring beyond that point.

For the feather geometry itself, since parts don't support textures, I'll build individual feather blades as extruded leaf-shaped outlines hanging downward, each defined by a local coordinate frame (sideways width, downward length) and attached to the bone, with a helper function to generate each blade's tapered leaf profile.

Now I'm tallying up my part budget of 170 total meshes — breaking down roughly how many parts each leg will need: the main leg sweep, scale details, ankle band, spur, four toes each with their own sweep/claw/knuckle components, and foot pads, to make sure I stay within the limit.

I realize individual feather parts would blow the budget, so instead I'll build feather geometry as extruded flat prisms and merge them by color and bone into a single mesh per group, letting me afford around 100 cheap feathers per leg while keeping triangle counts manageable within a roughly 12000-tri total budget.

Instead of setFromUnitVectors I'll use the SDK's aim(dir, up, "y") helper to orient each feather quaternion along its direction vector. For bone assignment, thigh feathers follow hipL and knee-area feathers follow kneeL, and I'm grouping feathers by bone and color using a root-to-tip palette—rust at the root transitioning to white/black tips—possibly splitting each feather into two colored pieces to achieve that gradient.

For the layered look, I'm assigning colors by row (rust for most rows, cream and white mixed in, black-tipped near the ends) and giving each feather a small proud tip-overlay kite offset slightly along the normal for a layered feather effect, which I'll implement as a feather(pos, dir, out...) construction function.

Building the two geometries per feather and merging them into maps keyed by bone and color, then checking that the extruded mesh normals and non-indexed geometry format stay consistent across all pieces so the materials render correctly without needing extra normal recomputation.

Now I'm working out how to position feathers along the leg's thigh path: for each row and ring angle, I derive the center and tangent from the path, build a perpendicular basis using cross products with the tangent, and use that to compute the radial direction for placing each feather around the limb.

I tilt each feather outward from the tangent by about 25 degrees (increasing with shagginess), burying the root near the surface and pointing it down-out with a length of 0.32 and width of 0.17, orienting feather thickness along the radial axis. I also check that the upper feathers near the hip, around y 1.85-2.0, stay hidden under the platform since the box top sits at y=2.05.

Now I'm planning the leg's feather layout: seven rows spaced along the leg, each with about nine or ten feathers around the circumference (roughly 63-70 total per leg), with radius tapering by row using a piecewise interpolation between hip, knee, hock, and foot key radii. I'm also considering rounding off the sweep cap at the hip end.

Checking the hip sphere's geometry against the hut platform: the cap at y=1.95 with radius 0.28 would extend up to about 2.23, overlapping the platform floor at 2.0, so I'm deciding to use a flat start cap and round end cap, positioning it so the flat side sits hidden beneath the platform rather than poking visibly through.

Now I'm working out the leg's Catmull-Rom spline path starting from the hip, through a knee point, hock, and down to the ankle, adjusting coordinates so the knee bends forward and down before the leg angles back toward the hock and ankle positions.

Setting the skinning bone list to the leg chain, noting the ankle joint owns nothing past the path's end which is fine. Planning to add scale plates along the tarsus using sweep.at sampling with inherited bone weights, and sketching a sharp spur jutting off the back of the hock.

Adjusting the spur's start position to sit inside the hock joint, tagging it with the hock bone. Now I'm working out the ankle band with yellow dots, trying to figure out how to orient a ring frame along the sweep path since the sweep's normal faces outward rather than tangentially, and wrestling with how to associate the ring with the nearest bone when there's no explicit chain to reference.

I'll use a wide open-ended cylinder as the band, then add small yellow sphere dots around its ring using a local basis, merged into one part. For bone attachment, I'm reasoning that the hock joint runs from hock to ankle with the ankle at its tip, so the band should follow the hockL bone rather than ankleL.

Now I'm adding the foot pad: a yellow sphere at the ankle position, weighted to ankleL since it's the parent joint for the toes.

Writing toe sweep code...

Setting the back toe joint at y 0.3, using base-to-tip of 0.285→0.255. I'm now working out directions and lengths for each toe per leg—inner and outer toes angled slightly from center, back toe pointing backward—and tracing how the hock and tarsus connect toward the ankle.

I'm generalizing the mirroring logic so inner/outer toe directions flip sign correctly between left and right sides, using a side multiplier and consistent joint naming like toe1 through toe4 for center, inner, outer, and back toes.

Now I'm working out the claw geometry as a curved bezier shape running outward and downward from each toe tip, picking control points that bend the claw down toward the ground.

Adding claw highlight sweep...

Now I'm planning knuckle bumps on the toes—small spheres and dark scale plates placed along each toe at a couple of points for texture.

Tallying part budget: each toe gets a sweep, claw, highlight, two bumps, three plates (roughly eight parts), times four toes times two sides adds up fast, so I need to keep the leg's main structures lean—sweep bands, plates, a band, dots, and spurs.

Adding ankle ball, feather tufts in rust/white/black, and a couple bone segments per leg brings each leg to around 58 parts, totaling near 116 overall, still under the 170 cap. I'll skip extra kneecap detail since feather tufts will cover that area, and just lay out plate rows along the tarsus at regular intervals.

Reworking the scale plate rows to alternate angle offsets per row for staggering, landing on about 13 plates per leg for the tarsus ring, with each plate sized as a small flattened box oriented along the surface normal and tangent flow direction.

I'm switching plate geometry to a hex cylinder shape for simplicity and rotational symmetry, with slightly smaller plates on lower rows, colored mostly scaleDark. I'm placing the ankle red band using a closest-point lookup near the tarsus end, with tarsus scale rows spanning a defined t-range and small accent dots positioned radially around the yellow spheres.

Working out band radius against the 8-sided tube's vertex geometry so a 12-sided band cylinder clears the tube's circumscribed radius, settling on roughly 1.14x the tube radius with dots placed slightly further out at the band's outer vertices.

I'm also considering adding thin yellow torus rings at the band edges as a decorative detail, then moving on to building the kite feather shape using tangent and position vectors along the path.

Writing kite geometry code...

Then I'm thinking through merging the extruded feather geometries using mergeGeometries from the BufferGeometryUtils addon, trusting the triangulation and attribute handling to work correctly.

Now I'm figuring out the feather row color pattern across the seven rows, alternating white and black tips with rust as the base, skipping an overlay on certain rows so the pattern reads naturally beneath the platform.

I'm also varying the base feather colors by row between rust shades for visual variety, and working out the draw order so lower rows of feathers overlap the upper ones properly as they fan outward and downward along the radial spacing.

Working out feather count per row based on circumference, scaling width with radius, and figuring out row spacing along the leg path from hip to knee.

Setting the color bands so the shank yellow shows between the feathers and hock, keeping the scaly-shank look readable. I'm confirming the sweep logic using bone lists and radius functions works, then setting up the aim/compose transforms so each feather orients using a quaternion toward its outward radial direction for proper thickness.

Now I'm checking that all the extruded feather geometries share compatible attribute sets for merging, and writing a basis function that computes perpendicular vectors from a tangent direction to orient each part correctly.

Working through the mirroring logic for leg paths across the s=-1/1 symmetry, and checking the hip-to-ankle point sequence for the leg curve to make sure the Catmull-Rom spline doesn't overshoot awkwardly at the knee joint.

Checking that the knee-forward, hock-backward bend matches typical chicken leg anatomy, and verifying the sweep radius is thick enough to handle the sharp joint bends without pinching at the corners.

I'll skip the ankle feather tuft and knee knuckle details to keep things simple, applying the scale plates with toe knuckle bumps on the tarsus instead. For the spur, I'm plotting a curved bezier path from the hock backward and downward to a tapered tip, giving it a tapered bone radius and a pale color.

Positioning the spur base precisely is tricky since the hock's tube geometry curves inward at the bend rather than sitting at the raw coordinate -- I need to account for that rounding so the spur sphere sits flush against the leg surface instead of floating outside it.

I'll cast a ray from behind the leg into the tube surface to find the actual contact point robustly, falling back to a manual estimate if the ray misses, then anchor the spur root at that hit location for both the spur and its base sphere.

For the spur's curve, I'm plotting it to extend backward from the root, curving down and inward along four control points so it reads like a chicken's spur, then checking whether bezier accepts Vector3 inputs directly.

Writing vector helper functions...

For the ankle, I'm flattening the sphere geometry slightly with a non-uniform scale to give it a more anatomical joint shape, and setting matching radii for the tarsus and ankle transition.

Now I'm working out toe knuckle bumps—interpolating sphere radii along the toe length and considering dark cylinder bands around each toe to suggest knuckle plates against the lighter scale color.

Settling on the design: each toe gets a yellow bump sphere plus a small dark plate sitting on top of it, bringing the part count per toe to seven, times eight toes totals 56 parts. I'm positioning the plate at the top of each bump by offsetting along the bump's radius in the up direction.

Now I'm writing the buildLeg function, pulling joints dynamically by name like J[`toe${S}${i}`] and J[`hip${S}`] so one function generates both legs symmetrically. I'll skip extras like heel pads, and start drafting the TypeScript code for this.

Setting up imports and function signature...

Building out the leg geometry function with catmull-rom path interpolation for joint positioning...

Finishing up the color bands and checking the bone joint list, I'm noting that the ankle joint sits right at the path's end so it effectively contributes no length and gets excluded from the sweep's influence.

Now I'm generating the feather rows, computing position and tangent along the path at each row, determining radial feather counts based on circumference, and assigning bone weighting (hip vs knee) along with jittered angles and tilt per feather...

Setting up plate rows along the leg using a random generator for jitter, placing alternating angle groups per row near the hock region, then starting to define the plate stick geometry...

Thinking about whether to share the plate geometry across parts or create a fresh instance each time to avoid baking issues, then adding a decorative band of dots further up with an open-ended cylinder so only the outer faces show.

Switching to a closed cylinder for the red sleeve part since open ends made it look too flat, then placing yellow torus rings and a cluster of small spheres as decorative dots merged into the geometry.

Now I'm setting up toe configurations for each of the four toes, defining their direction, length, and radius tapers from an ankle ball joint, with three forward toes spread by offset and one shorter back toe anchored near the same base point.

Checking that the sweep angle convention keeps the claw curving upward correctly, then placing small bumps along each toe with spheres and short cylinder plates sized relative to the toe radius at that position, with the back toe getting fewer bumps than the others.

For the merge step, I'm confirming each toe bone name matches the naming scheme, skipping webbing between toes, and guarding the merge call against null geometry before combining all feather meshes per bone. Tallying up part counts per leg across the main mesh, plates, bands, rings, spurs, ankle, and toes gives roughly 51 parts per leg, so around 102 total plus the merged feather geometry.

With colors multiplied across hip and knee bones the triangle count stays manageable even with dense feather rows. I'm double-checking that unused imports like Frame get skipped while the math helpers (aim, rng, catmull, bezier) are properly exported, and that the radius function type used in the sweep is correct. Now I'm working out the claw tip path, computing control points by offsetting the tip position along the direction vector to shape the curve.

I'm planning the function that builds porch stairs using the given context object, working out the geometry for the landing and the eight descending steps.

spec.name: Baba Yaga's Hut on Chicken Legs
spec.description: A Slavic folk-art diorama: a painted log izba with carved bargeboards and a horse-head ridge, standing on two giant scaly chicken legs inside a ring of glowing-eyed skull fence posts.
spec.layout:
STYLE: Slavic folk art (lubok, Khokhloma, painted carved wood). Every motif is a bold flat-colour shape, chunky and slightly exaggerated, with a dark ink (#1b1410) outline or underlay behind the main colour and small cream or yellow highlight dots on top. Colours are red, cobalt blue, sun yellow and orange on warm wood, with green foliage and cream accents. The repeated motifs are (1) the SUN ROSETTE: a yellow disc with 8 orange petals and a red ring, with a cream centre dot; (2) the TOOTH TRIM: a row of alternating red and blue triangles; (3) SCALLOPS: half-round cut-outs on carved boards; (4) the ROOSTER/TULIP: a stylised bird or flower of three flat petals. Reuse all four on the hut, door, gate posts and props.
SILHOUETTE (+Z is the front): the model is a round diorama base about 6.8 m across. At the centre a log hut about 2.3 m wide (x) by 2.7 m deep (z) stands on two huge chicken legs. The sill underside is at y=2.0, the wall top at y=3.55, the ridge at y=4.64, and a horse-head ornament and chimney reach about y=5.0. The legs are digitigrade: the thigh runs forward-down to a forward knee, the shin runs backward-down to the hock, and the tarsus runs forward-down to a foot with three forward toes and one rear toe. The legs sit at x=+-0.7 and the feet at x=+-0.75, z=0.25. The hut faces +Z with a door in the centre of the front wall, a small porch platform, and a steep ladder-stair going down to the ground at z=2.75. The roof is a steep gable with its ridge along Z, so the gable triangle faces front and back. It has fish-scale shingles and carved bargeboards. A carved horse head (konyok) sits on each end of the ridge, and a brick chimney with smoke is on the model-right roof slope.
GROUND: the base disc is r=3.4 with its grass top at y=0.15. A fence of skull-topped stakes forms a ring at r=3.0 over azimuth 40 to 320 degrees (azimuth 0 is +Z, 90 is +X), so the front is open and the path runs through. Two taller carved gate posts stand at az=+-40 degrees, which is (+-1.93, z=2.30). Birch trees stand behind the hut, with a mortar, pestle and broom, mushrooms, folk flowers and a black cat as small dressing. The feet stand on the base top. The only things that touch the model floor y=0 are the base disc and the fence stakes. The hut and legs rest on y=0.15.
Coordinate convention: +X is the model's left; mirrored parts use for s of [1,-1], with s=1 the left (+X). Rest pose: legs standing, door closed.

parts.builds: Both giant chicken legs, mirrored (L at +X, R at -X), built from the rig. Build them as a chain through hip, knee, ankle and foot (a limb/IK solve landing the foot on footL/footR, or sweeps through the joint positions), with smooth skin sweeps. THIGH: a fat feathered 'trouser' of radius about 0.28 at the hip tapering to 0.17 at the knee. It is a base sweep in featherA covered with 14-20 overlapping broad feather blades (flat extruded leaf shapes, or cards/spikes) in a root-to-tip featherA to featherB palette, pointing down and back, with a ruff of longer feather blades round the knee. KNEE and HOCK: chunky knuckle blocks in scaleDark. TARSUS (shin and lower leg): scaly yellow, radius about 0.11 at the hock tapering to 0.09, in scaleYellow. It carries a row of overlapping scale plates (small flat boxes or rounded plates, scaleDark) down the front, with a spur (an ink cone) at the back of the hock. Each hock gets a folk 'bracelet': a red (folkRed) ring sweep with 6-8 tiny cream dots round it. TOES: four per leg, one sweep each (radius 0.08 tapering to 0.05) along the toe joints toeX1..toeX4 (three forward, spread outward, centre and inward, plus one rear toe). Each has 2-3 knuckle bumps in scaleDark, a toe pad underside, and a long curved ink talon (a cone or curved sweep, 0.16-0.2 m) at the tip, which rests on the ground. The rear toe is shorter with a bigger spur-claw. Add a few lumps of earth (earth colour) over the toes and a small yellow-orange dot motif. At the top of each thigh a rounded hip cap in featherA tucks under the hut's sill at hipL/hipR (y up to 2.0). Use the joints hipX, kneeX, ankleX, footX, toeX1..4 and give the leg chain role 'leg' and the toes role 'digit'.

spec.name: Baba Yaga's Hut on Chicken Legs
spec.description: A folk-art log hut with a carved, painted roof, perched on two huge scaly chicken legs, with a skull-topped fence, a ladder and a glowing window.
spec.layout: A tall log cabin rests on two big yellow chicken legs standing apart on the ground (left leg +X, right leg -X). The hut's door and a short porch face +Z with a ladder-stair running down toward the front. The steep roof ridge runs along z, with carved end-boards (a sun and rooster motif) at front and back, and a stubby chimney. A fence of poles with glowing skulls arcs around the back and sides on the ground. Slavic folk art: bold flat colours, red, ochre and teal painted ornaments, zigzag and sun motifs on every board, rounded log ends, simple chunky shapes. Parts: legs and ground-claws, hut body logs, roof, porch with ladder, fence with skulls.

parts.builds: Two huge chicken legs: thick yellow tapering thigh, knee bend, shin and ankle with scale-ring bands in legDark, three forward toes and one rear toe each with claw spikes in claw colour, toe joint knuckle balls. Scaly feather tufts at the thigh in carveRed and cream. Chains named hipL/kneeL/ankleL and hipR/kneeR/ankleR, role leg, feet planted on y=0 toes spread in +Z.
parts.attaches: Thigh tops end at legHipL and legHipR under the hut floor.

parts.builds: Square log cabin walls 2.2 wide by 2.0 long and 1.5 tall: stacked horizontal log cylinders in log/logDark with logEnd round ends poking out at corners, a floor slab, a door in the front with carveRed frame, zigzag trim, iron hinges, a glowing window (window colour) with carved teal shutters on each side wall and a round one at the back, a painted sun disc beside the door.
parts.attaches: Sits on hutFloor on the legs; roof starts at eaveLine; porch attaches at doorFront.

parts.builds: Steep gabled roof in roof/roofDark with overhanging eaves, rows of rounded shingles as small boards, a carved ridge beam ending in rooster-head or horse-head finials in carveYellow and carveRed, gable end boards (pozarnye) at front and back with sun, zigzag and teardrop cut-outs in carveRed/carveYellow/carveTeal/cream, a stubby brick-and-log chimney with a little smoke puff in cream.
parts.attaches: Eaves rest on eaveLine over the cabin walls; ridge at mount ridge.

parts.builds: Small front porch deck in wood with two carved posts and a little pitched canopy in roofDark, painted carveRed balusters, and a steep ladder with rungs descending forward to y=0.4 where it ends in the air above a flat stone, with a cream-painted step. Hanging dried herb bundles and a tiny lantern in window glow colour.
parts.attaches: Deck at porchDeck meets the front wall at doorFront.

parts.builds: A ring-arc of sharpened pole fence in log/logDark around the sides and back, 0.7 to 1.4 tall poles of varied height, every third pole topped with a bone-coloured skull (sphere cranium, jaw box, dark eye sockets glowing skullGlow), a few rope bands in cream, a low grass-green ground pad disc in ground colour with a few tufts and mushrooms in carveRed with cream dots.
parts.attaches: Circles groundPad on the floor around the leg feet, clear of the legs and porch ladder.

calls.reasoning:
I'm working out how to build the fence function, considering whether static parts without a bone should attach to the nearest joint or just ride along with the hut's joint as scenery.

Now I'm sketching the geometry: a sunken ground pad disc, a box footprint for the legs, and a fence arc hugging the back and sides while leaving the front open, positioning the support poles near the leg bases.

Now I'm placing the fence poles around the arc, spacing roughly 17 posts over 220 degrees with sharpened cone tips and randomized heights between 0.7 and 1.4. Every third pole gets a small skull mounted on top instead of the bare tip, sized to stay within the 1.5 height limit when combined with taller posts.

I'm detailing the pole material with alternating log and dark log colors, a lighter cut-wood cone tip, carved dark bands, and a few cream rope wraps, plus sagging rope segments draped between some adjacent poles as rustic rails.

Now I'm building the skull detail: a scaled cranium sphere, jaw box, dark eye sockets each with a small glowing green orb inside using the glow kit, oriented to face outward from the hut.

Still placing skull components...

I'll skip extra glow effects and keep it to just the eye glow for simplicity, then move to building the ground pad as a flat scaled cylinder with the ground color, possibly adding a subtler secondary ring for texture while staying within the limited color palette.

Now I'm thinking through grass tufts as small clusters of thin cone blades scattered near the fence base, but I need to watch the total part budget carefully since poles, bands, skulls, and pad elements are already adding up fast—I'll need to tally parts per component to keep things under the limit.

Let me reconsider the spacing: switching to 19 poles with a skull every third one gives 7 skulls symmetrically placed at both ends. Recalculating the totals with 38 for poles, 63 for skulls, and the rest unchanged lands around 162 elements, still under budget, so I'll trim the tufts down to 7 to stay safe.

Now I'm working out pole heights and proportions—regular poles varying between 0.7 and 1.2m with some sine-based variation, while skull poles get boosted to around 1.22-1.3m so their tops stay under the 1.5m ceiling once the skull geometry sits on top. I'm defining the shaft as a thin heptagonal cylinder with a cone tip, and for skull poles giving them a flat top with a short peg instead of the usual cone.

I'm also adding rope-band details that connect some of the poles together at mid-height, picking alternating pairs so the fence looks tied together rather than perfectly uniform.

Now I'm figuring out how the ropes sag between poles using a smooth curved sweep, attaching each end near the top of adjacent poles and letting the middle dip slightly. I'm keeping the pole bases flush with the ground pad so they look planted rather than floating.

Next I'm starting on little mushroom decorations with cream-colored stems and caps.

For the fence and mushroom placement, I'm working out coordinates so they stay clear of the leg positions near the center and sit sensibly relative to the pad radius and fence ring, tucking a few mushrooms near the back corners outside the main structure.

I'm placing grass tufts as small tilted cones along the inside of the fence base, and settling on the color palette—reusing the existing log, bone, and ground tones while adding two new greens for grass and keeping mushroom stems cream.

Now I'm writing a helper function to place parts with position, rotation, and scale, then building out the skull geometry using a local coordinate helper that maps right/up/forward offsets around a pole-top anchor point, starting with the cranium.

Still placing facial features...

Total parts land around 155. I'm placing skulls along pole angles from 70° to 290°, computing positions and yaw from the ellipse geometry, and varying heights for non-skull clutter with a capped max. That should fit within tolerance, so I'll write it out.

I'm setting up a buildLegs function that destructures the context object and reuses existing hip joints, planning the hip and knee chains for each leg.

Since hipL already exists as a joint, I realize I can't name a new chain hipL too — names must stay unique. Instead, I'll manually create kneeL and ankleL joints parented to the hip joint, then build sweeps across the bone path [hipL, kneeL, ankleL] so the thigh and shin are smoothly skinned.

Now I'm thinking through the anatomy more carefully — for a proper digitigrade chicken leg, the hip should sweep forward-down to the knee, then the tarsus angles down-back to the hock before the toes point forward again, so I'm sketching out approximate joint coordinates for hip, knee, and ankle to capture that silhouette.

Checking the hip-to-ankle distance confirms the two-segment leg reaches with a natural forward knee bend, so I'll build the leg as a limb chain from hip to knee to ankle, then add a separate foot joint from ankle to a ball point for the toe base.

I'm deciding to tie thigh and shin radii to hip/knee/ankle thickness, using one continuous sweep along the polyline with radii varying by parameter t, letting the skin round over the joint bends rather than sweeping each segment separately.

For shin bands, I'm considering alternating color rings instead, maybe using torus geometry oriented along the limb's tangent direction to create ring-like segments rather than splitting the tube mesh itself.

For bone assignment, since the path is built from literal points with no bone data, I should explicitly choose joints rather than rely on nearest-joint defaults — thigh rings bound to hipL, shin rings to kneeL, pulled from the chain's joints array. This keeps rings static and rigid near joints, which is fine since there's no bending animation happening here anyway.

Now I'm working out ring radius matching and sweep geometry, using octagonal rings slightly inflated to approximate the circumscribed torus radius. For the shin, I also want small flattened plates running down the front, which means figuring out the correct dorsal-facing clock angle along the sweep so the plates land on the right side of the limb.

spec.name: Baba Yaga's Hut
spec.description: A Slavic folk-art diorama of a carved wooden izba standing on two giant scaly chicken legs, with a fenced yard of skull posts, a stump stair and a mortar and pestle.
spec.layout: The hut is a squat log cabin raised on two huge yellow chicken legs, with the front door facing +Z. The legs stand on a low round earth mound at the floor (mound radius 1.7, centred x=0, z=0). The cabin sits on a floor platform at y=1.2, and a steep two-slope shingled roof with a carved ridge horse-head at the front tops it. Carved folk-art window frames in red, blue and white with flower motifs flank the door. A small porch with a ladder-like stair reaches down from the door toward +Z, ending on the mound. Around the mound stands a ring of picket fence with glowing skull posts, a mortar and pestle sits at the front left, and a birch tree stands at the back right. Style: bold flat colours, ornate repeated sunburst, flower and zigzag trim motifs in red, white, and gold on every wooden surface, with chunky, blocky shapes.

parts.builds: The round earth mound (moss patches, a few stones) and the two huge chicken legs: each a thick yellow scaly tube with thigh, drumstick and shin segments (alternating legYellow and legDark scale bands), a bent knee, and a foot with three forward toes and one rear toe, each with a dark claw. Includes the gnarled crossbeam hip sockets that go up under the cabin floor at the legHip mounts.
parts.attaches: Leg tops meet the cabin underside at legHipL and legHipR (y 1.2). Feet at footL and footR on the mound.

parts.builds: The log cabin body from y=1.2 to y=2.35: stacked horizontal round logs with protruding corner-notch log ends (logEnd discs), a floor platform slab, carved door (trimRed frame, gold sunburst, iron hinges and ring handle) at doorBase on the front, two side windows plus one front window each with blue and white carved frames, flower motifs, glowing windowGlow panes and shutters. Includes the small porch deck, two posts with carved tops, and a stair of three steps descending from porchEdge toward +Z.
parts.attaches: Sits on the leg hips at cabinFloor; the roof starts at roofEave; the stair ends near yardFront.

parts.builds: The steep gabled roof from y=2.35 to 3.4 overhanging the walls: rows of overlapping shingle slabs alternating roofShingle and roofShingleDark, bargeboards with zigzag trim in trimRed and trimWhite, a front gable with a carved round window and sunburst, a ridge beam ending in a carved horse-head (ridgeFront) with gold mane, small gold finials on the rear, and a crooked clay chimney with a little smoke puff.
parts.attaches: Eaves rest on the cabin walls at roofEave. Horse-head at ridgeFront.

parts.builds: The yard dressing on the floor: a ring of picket fence posts around the mound radius ~1.75 with gaps at the front for the stair, with pointed tops in fence colour; every fourth post is a taller skull post with a skullBone skull (cranium, jaw, two glowing glowEye sockets). Also a mortar and pestle (iron mortar, long wooden pestle) at front left (x 1.5, z 1.3), and a stump with a mushroom or two.
parts.attaches: Fence is placed outside the mound edge; the stair end at yardFront remains clear between posts.

parts.builds: A tall slender birch tree at the back right (x 1.5, z -1.5) rising behind the hut to about 3.4 m: white trunk of stacked tapered segments with dark birchMark dashes, three bare branches, and clusters of faceted leaf blobs in leaf and moss colours, plus a small crow perched on a branch. A tuft of grass and two stones at the base.
parts.attaches: Stands on the floor beside the fence ring, behind the roof's rear corner.
