spec.layout: Four-legged, facing +Z, standing on y=0 with all four paws flat. Tapir proportions pushed toward print-block stylization: a long barrel torso (z -0.85..0.65, belly y~0.52, back y~1.25), short thick legs, a thick neck rising into a big wedge head with a domed forehead (top y~1.45, ears to 1.58). A short prehensile trunk grows from the muzzle (z~1.2) and hangs forward-down to a tip near [0,0.72,1.62]. Short ivory tusks flank the trunk root, and long whiskers sweep back from the muzzle. A flame mane runs from the forehead crest down the neck and back to the rump, with flame wisps rising from the shoulders and haunches, an ox tail ending in a big flame tuft behind (z to -1.5), and a shimenawa rope collar with paper shide and a bell at the neck base. A dream-cloud scroll curls up from the trunk tip at the front-left. Ukiyo-e look on every part: flat colour only; bold sumi-ink outlines made as slightly larger sumi parts or thin sweeps behind or around key shapes (eyes, ears, tusks, paws, mane blades); indigo base with a cream saddle band over the mid-torso (tapir marking). Stylized pattern shapes are small parts in their own colours seated on the surface: seigaiha wave scallops (teal and white arcs) on the saddle, vermilion kumo (cloud scroll) roundels on shoulder and haunch, zigzag fur-edge tufts at the cuffs. Colour is warm vermilion and gold on top and accents, cool indigo below. Every colour is one flat colour per part. Detail comes from many small seated parts, not from smooth shading. Keep blocky, faceted, low-poly primitives.

parts.builds: The body shell: one loft (smooth-skinned over hips, spine1, chest) running from the rump (z -0.85, about 0.55 wide x 0.55 high, centre y 0.86) through a barrel mid-section (z 0 to 0.2, about 0.78 wide x 0.72 high, centre y 0.88) to the shoulders (z 0.5), then a thick neck tube over neck1 and neck2 (radius 0.24 tapering to 0.2) ending at headSocket where the head part's skull overlaps it. Coat colours by place: indigo back and flanks, indigoDeep underside and upper belly, a cream (paper) saddle band over the mid-torso (z about -0.3..0.2) wrapped by sectors, and a paperShadow belly. Print details as small seated parts: rows of seigaiha wave scallops (teal and waveWhite half-disc arcs, with sumi outline lines) on both sides of the saddle; vermilion kumo cloud-scroll roundels (disc plus spiral curl, with a sumi rim and gold dot) on each shoulder and haunch; thin sumi contour lines along the saddle edges and the belly line; small indigoLight highlight patches on the shoulders and back. Use b.surface plus stick, loop and along to seat all of it. Does NOT include legs, mane, tail or collar.
parts.attaches: Spine joints hips, spine1 and chest. The neck end meets the head at headSocket. Legs sprout at shoulderL/R and haunchL/R. Mane and tail sit on the spine line (spineLineStart to spineLineEnd, tailRoot).

parts.builds: The head, a faceted wedge with a domed forehead (skull from z 0.8 to 1.25, top y 1.45), bound to joint head. It has a separate upper muzzle (head joint) and lower jaw (jaw joint: cream chin, vermilion mouth interior, small ivory teeth). The face is settled first. Two big bold ukiyo-e eyes at eyeL/eyeR: a sumi almond outline, an eyeWhite sclera, a gold iris with a sumi pupil and a tiny white highlight, heavy sumi brow bars with vermilion brow tufts above. A vermilion tomoe (comma) in a gold ring on the forehead. Round ears on earL/earR joints: sumi outline disc, indigo body, paper rim, vermilion inner. Short curved ivory tusks at tuskRootL/R curving down and out, each with a sumi outline. Cream cheek ruffs of zigzag tufts. Four long whiskers per side swept back, thin sweeps in paper and sumi. The cream muzzle ring around trunkRoot. Indigo skull colour with indigoLight highlights on the brow ridge and a sumi nose-bridge line. Does NOT include the trunk tube, mane blades or collar.
parts.attaches: Skull overlaps the neck end at headSocket (z 0.92). Trunk root at trunkRoot [0,1.2,1.2]. The jaw hinges at jawHinge. The mane starts at foreheadCrest.

parts.builds: The prehensile trunk: a chain of four joints trunk1 to trunk4 with one smooth tapering sweep (radius about 0.1 at the root to 0.065 near the tip). It runs from trunkRoot forward and down to trunkTip. Indigo with cream wave-ring bands spaced along it (thin sweeps or discs: paper, with teal and sumi lines), a paper tip with two sumi nostril dots, and an indigoLight highlight line along the top. The trunk root has a gold collar ring. Also the dream cloud: a stylized floating kumo scroll of flat extrudes and discs in dreamPale and dreamPurple with sumi outlines, curling up from trunkTip at dreamCloudBase to the front-left (x 0.1-0.45, y 0.85-1.45, z 1.35-1.7). A moon-yellow crescent (extrude) and three small gold four-point stars float inside it, built from emissive-capable flat parts (glow the moon and stars). A thin vapour wisp (a sweep in dreamPale) joins the trunk tip to the cloud.
parts.attaches: Root joint trunk1 at trunkRoot, parented to head. The tip ends at trunkTip. The dream cloud's wisp starts at the trunk tip.

parts.builds: All four legs, short and thick, each a smooth sweep or limb chain. Front legs: shoulderFL/FR, elbow, wrist and paw tip joints. Hind legs: hipHL/HR, knee, hock and paw tip joints (hocks bent back, knees forward). Radius is about 0.14 at the root, tapering to 0.09 at the wrist or hock. Indigo leg colour, with the upper legs overlapping into the torso and the root radius burying into it. Cream fur cuffs at the wrists and hocks made of zigzag tuft blades (paper with sumi tips, gold stitch ring above). Tiger paws: a chunky rounded paw pad (indigoDeep with a sumi outline, bottom at y=0) with 4 toes (front) or 3 toes (hind) as rounded ivory bumps, each with a sumi toe line and a curved ivory claw. Small vermilion toe-bean pad on each paw. A thin sumi contour sweep down the front edge of each leg. Two small seigaiha scallops in teal and waveWhite on each thigh and forearm. Paw bottoms rest on y=0, with sole centres at pawFL/FR/HL/HR.
parts.attaches: Front legs root on chest at shoulderL/R, hind legs on hips at haunchL/R. Leg chains parent as in the joints list. Paws land on the floor at the paw mounts.

parts.builds: The signature flowing decorations. (1) The flame mane: a solid indigoDeep crest ridge plus about 40 broad overlapping extruded blade shapes (curved leaves with a sharp tip, a sumi-outline duplicate behind each of the larger ones) along the spine line from foreheadCrest to the rump, tallest on the neck and withers (0.25-0.3 m) and lower on the back. Root-to-tip palette: indigoDeep, indigo, teal, paper, vermilion tip, with gold accents. All blades lean backward like blown flame. (2) Flame wisps: 3-4 vermilion-and-gold flame extrudes rising and curling back from each shoulder and haunch (mounts shoulderL/R, haunchL/R), seated on the torso flanks, each with a sumi rim. (3) The ox tail on joints tail1 to tail4: a tapering sweep (indigo, radius 0.07 to 0.04) ending in a big tuft of about 14 broad flame blades fanning down and back at tailTuft (paper, vermilion, teal tips, sumi outlines). (4) A shimenawa collar at collarRing: a thick twisted straw-coloured rope loop (sweep, with spiral binding bands in a darker straw) around the neck base, 6 zigzag paper shide strips (shideWhite with sumi edges) hanging from it, vermilion tassels, and a brass bell with a sumi slot hanging at the front of the throat.
parts.attaches: Mane blades sit on the torso and neck along the spine joints (spineLineStart to spineLineEnd) and the head crest. The tail chain roots at tailRoot on hips. The collar wraps the neck at collarRing on neck1. Wisps sit on the shoulder and haunch mounts.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning the design for a baku, a tapir-like dream-eating spirit, blending its traditional chimeric features—elephant trunk, tiger paws, ox tail, tusks—with classic ukiyo-e aesthetics like indigo and vermilion tones, flat color fields, black outlines, and motifs like waves and clouds rendered in sumi ink style.

I'm now working out proportions and spatial layout: a stylized elongated body roughly 2.6 to 3.2 meters long with a curling trunk extending forward, a flame-like mane ridge along the neck and spine, and distinct sections for torso, tail, and head with jointed trunk segments, tusks, and ornamental cloud-scroll emblems on the shoulders and hips.

For the remaining structure I'm settling on five total parts: body, head, four tiger-pawed legs with clawed toes and flame-cuff fur, and a mane/tail/ornament group that includes flame-blade mane, ox-tuft tail, a shimenawa rope collar with paper shide and a bell, plus a small glowing dream-cloud wisp floating near the trunk tip.

Now I'm working out the part budget -- roughly torso 160, head 190, trunk plus dream wisp 130, legs 190, and mane/tail/regalia 200, totaling around 870 out of a 900 limit. I'm mapping out the joint hierarchy with hips as root, then spine, chest, and neck segments at specific coordinates, and defining the torso as a loft shape running along the z-axis with a narrower belly and wider back.

Still defining the joint chain...

Now I'm working out the leg joint chains—shoulder, elbow, wrist, paw for the front legs, and hip, knee, hock, paw for the hind legs—with paw centers sitting just above the floor plane, plus parenting shoulders to the chest and hips to the hip region before moving on to the tail.

I'm laying out the tail as a chain of four joints extending back and slightly down from the hips, then considering whether to add a separate mane role before deciding it's unnecessary since mane blades can ride the spine joints directly. I'm also planning the full joint naming scheme with left/right suffixes, tallying roughly 34 joints total across the hips, spine, head, ears, legs, and tail, and now moving on to defining the color palette.

Now I'm picking a ukiyo-e inspired palette: deep indigo blues for the main coat with lighter and darker variants, cream and shadowed paper tones, vermilion reds, ochre gold, sumi black outlines, plus accent colors like moss green, teal wave blue, sakura pink, ivory for tusks, and brass for bells.

I'm finishing out the palette with straw yellow, dream purples and pale lavenders, moon yellow, and eye colors in white and gold, landing around 21 total colors. For style, I'm planning to layer the sumi outlines as slightly larger duplicated shapes behind each part to create a dark outline shell effect.

Then I'm thinking through surface patterns -- seigaiha wave scallops in teal/white along the flanks, vermilion cloud-scroll emblems on the shoulders and hips, and flame-like mane blades gradienting from indigo to teal to vermilion at the tips. For color distribution, I'm mimicking the real tapir's dark front/rear with a cream saddle band through the middle, giving the baku indigo head and hindquarters with a light-blue seigaiha-patterned saddle across the torso.

Now I'm defining the skeletal mount points -- neck base, head socket, trunk root and tip, shoulders, hips, tail root, mane start running from neck to withers to rump, a shimenawa collar ring at the neck base, jaw hinge, and ears. Then I'm starting to lay out the bounding boxes for the torso and head geometry.

I'll add a tiny moon and stars glowing inside the cloud for the dream effect, then define the legs box touching the floor. For the regalia—mane, tail, collar, shimenawa, shide, bell, and shoulder flame scrolls—I'm setting a bounding box spanning the back and neck, with mane blades reaching up to the ear height and the tail trailing behind.

Now I'm working out the overall size and resolving overlaps between parts: deciding that the torso owns the coat, seigaiha pattern, saddle, belly, and the vermilion swirl emblems on shoulder and hip, while the legs own the leg tubes and sprout from joints that bury into the torso to avoid gaps.

Since the builders can't see each other's geometry directly, I'm making sure the leg root radius at the shoulder is slightly larger than the torso's surface at that point so it reads as a natural muscle bulge rather than a floating gap. I'm also sketching out the torso's loft stations from tail to neck, with the torso sweep extending up into the neck and head attachment point.

Now I'm designing the tapir head: a long wedge skull with sloped forehead and crest, exaggerated ukiyo-e style eyes with gold iris and sumi outline, bushy brows, round cream-rimmed indigo ears with vermilion inner, and short curved ivory tusks near the trunk base.

For the lower jaw I'm giving it a cream chin, small teeth, and red mouth interior, with the upper jaw forming the muzzle root for the trunk, plus sweeping catfish-style whisker tendrils in teal and cream. I'm also placing a vermilion tomoe mark with a gold rim on the forehead as the baku's dream-eating emblem, then starting the trunk as a four-joint chain tapering in radius with indigo coloring, a cream tip, and wave-pattern wrapping.

Now finishing the trunk with cream interval bands, small dark nostril holes, and a dream cloud at the tip. For the legs I'm settling on indigo limbs with cream sock cuffs featuring sumi zigzag fur tufts, cream paws with sumi toe lines, and ivory claws on tiger-style paws.

For regalia I'm deciding the mane runs as flame blades from the neck crest along the spine to the rump, colored root-to-tip in indigo, teal, paper, and vermilion, shaped like curling leaf scrolls. I'm dividing ownership so the torso carries flat coat patterns like the saddle, seigaiha, belly stripes, and shoulder/hip kumo discs, while the regalia covers the mane, tail, a shimenawa collar with shide paper strips and bell, and flame wisps at the shoulders.

Now I'm working out the tail design as an ox-like chain of four joints ending in a big flame-like tuft of vermilion and cream blades, also owned by regalia, and tallying up part budgets across torso, head, trunk, legs, and regalia to total 890. I'm starting to write out the joint hierarchy in JSON, beginning with the hips and spine chain and their positions and directions.

Continuing to define joints...

Still placing joints...

Continuing tail segments down to the tuft, making sure the hanging blades stay above the floor and the overall tail span fits within bounds. Then I need to finalize the floor contact points for the legs and nail the overall height with ears and mane reaching near the top, before writing out the full concise description of remaining parts and their joint lists.

I'm planning the trunk sweep function, using the existing trunk joints as the bone chain and building a catmull-rom path through their positions.

I'll taper the radius from the base toward the tip and shade it with color bands, adding a narrow indigoLight highlight sector along the top for visual depth.

Mapping which trunk bone each ring belongs to using arc-length positions along the catmull path, splitting the path into four joint segments with approximate knot values and choosing the nearest bone for each sample point.

For the rings themselves, I'm building a perpendicular basis at each path point from the tangent direction, placing 8 circular points around it, then sweeping a closed catmull curve with a small tube radius to form each segment.

Now I'm layering the ring bands: flanking sumi rings in thin dark strokes, a wider paper ring in the middle, and a teal accent ring sitting slightly proud of the surface, each scaled relative to the local sweep radius at that point along the path.

I'm interpolating a taper radius function across keyed values to shape the body, placing four bands plus a tip region, and adding two small sumi spheres as nostrils near the end cap, offset symmetrically and positioned along the tangent direction where the tube terminates in a rounded dome.

Adding gold collar ring details...

I'm planning the trunk's outline path with bones attached along the trunk chain, then placing the dream cloud bounding box and sketching a wisp curve rising from the trunk tip toward it using a catmull spline.

Now I'm considering the cloud's orientation and thickness—whether to extrude it facing forward or to the side so it reads properly from multiple viewing angles, plus adding small puffy accent shapes along the wisp.

Computing the cross product confirms the orientation faces front-left, so I'm placing the cloud box centered around x≈0.28, z≈1.52, fitting within the available width. I'm setting up a local coordinate helper that converts u/v/w offsets into world positions using the x-direction, vertical axis, and normal, then starting to compose the puffy cloud body itself.

Building disc layers for cloud puffs...

Since all puffs share the same thickness, the layering order doesn't matter and overlapping pale faces will always hide the thinner sumi rims beneath. Now I'm sketching out the coordinates for the cloud's puff cluster, placing base puffs along the bottom edge to build the characteristic flat-bottomed kumo scroll shape.

Adding a small spiral curl near the top, like a wisp or tendril, using a thicker sumi tube with a thinner dreamPurple tube layered just above it for depth.

For texture inside the cloud, I'm also considering small purple ring-like arcs on the fronts of the puffs, built as thin torus arcs oriented flat against the surface for subtle decorative detail.

Next I'm working on the moon crescent shape, building it as an outline combining two offset circles -- an outer boundary and a smaller inner circle shifted to carve out the crescent sliver.

Now I'm converting that intersection into the inner circle's own angle, getting roughly 64.9° relative to its center, and tracing how the two arcs connect: the outer arc sweeps from upper to lower intersection through the left side, then the inner arc needs to close the shape by going back from the lower intersection to the upper one along its own left side.

Working through the point arrays, I'm making sure the outer set includes both intersection endpoints while the inner set skips them to avoid duplicates, and marking the tip points as sharp corners rather than smoothed. Now I'm planning a slightly larger duplicate crescent behind the main one as a sumi-style outline effect.

For the stars, I'm setting up four-point extruded shapes alternating long and short radii for the outline, placed at three spots with their own darker outline copies behind them, then applying a glow effect to both the moon and stars using flat color materials. I'm positioning the moon slightly off-center so it sits properly within the cloud layer.

I'm working out the depth placement so the moon sits forward on the cloud's face with its own thickness and a slightly thicker dark outline behind it, computing the extrusion so it's centered correctly along the local axis. I'm also confirming the orientation so the crescent's opening faces the right direction when viewed from the front, and laying out coordinates for the three star positions.

I'm placing the stars near the cloud's puffs so they read as floating just above its surface rather than buried inside it, while nudging the moon's center slightly off so it overlaps nicely with the nearby star without clashing — though I need to double check how all this looks from the back view too.

Since the cloud back has nothing on it, I'll give the moon and star shapes enough extrusion thickness so they poke out slightly on both front and back faces, centering them so they protrude evenly. The outline for the crescent shape should sit at a slightly smaller thickness than the moon itself so the moon's face reads above the outline rim.

I'm also considering adding a few small decorative puffs along the cloud's wisp trail, using pale disc shapes with dark outlines, and tracing the wisp curve starting from near the top of the cloud dome rather than from the trunk.

Checking the cloud box dimensions fit the shifted centre, then sketching the wisp geometry with small rounded caps and puffs. I'm working out a helper to find joint positions along the path using tangent and closest-t lookups for the ring placement.

For the radius profile, I'm setting up a keyed array that interpolates smoothly along the sweep, with the trunk shape kept as a simple faceted circle rather than oval for now.

I'm figuring out how to render the wave-ring bands as a seigaiha-style pattern—pale rings with thin teal inner lines, faceted rather than smooth for the ukiyo-e look, and considering adding small scallop decorations between the bands on each side of the trunk.

Still placing scallop discs...

Since the tangent points mostly downward, I'll place the nostrils near the bottom-front of the dome tip, offset slightly outward on each side, and flatten the nostril spheres along the normal direction so they sit flush against the surface. I'm also adding a thin sumi outline ring near the paper boundary at the tip to define its edge.

Now I'm adding a wrinkle ring for paper shadow near the base, plus a gold collar ring circling the root with a slightly larger radius than the stick itself, accompanied by thin sumi rings bracketing it. I'm considering adding small gold studs spaced evenly around the collar using a ring helper to position octahedron shapes.

Actually, I realize the ring helper's item callback doesn't pass along the bone reference properly since the frame comes from a literal without an associated joint, so geometry would just snap to the nearest joint instead. I'd rather skip that helper and compute the stud points myself so I can explicitly assign the correct bone.

Writing trunk path code...

Writing ring helper function...

Tuning the ring radius formula...

Working through the radii so the teal ring sits visibly above the paper ring's crest instead of being buried inside it, I'm adjusting the lift value until the teal tube's top surface clears the paper tube's top surface by a safe margin.

Bands should stay visible near the trunk's bend at t~.5, with rings kept perpendicular to the tangent. I'm placing tip rings (sumi at 0.9, paper shadow wrinkle at 0.95), then designing a gold collar at t=0.05 with sumi rings flanking it and small octahedron studs in vermilion for contrast against the gold.

Now working out the collar's actual position near the root, checking how it interacts with the cream muzzle ring, and settling on t=0.07 with radius 0.1. For the scallop pattern, I'm stacking discs at the trunk's side points (t=0.3, 0.5, 0.69) in a seigaiha-style layered look—sumi outer disc, then alternating wave-white and teal rings shrinking inward.

Working out disc embedding...

Checking the cloud's bounding extents against the box limits, I find the x-range runs slightly too wide once puff offsets are included. I need to shrink the center x and tighten the puff u-range so everything stays within the 0.45 boundary.

Checking the y-range translates fine, and now I'm working out the spiral curl positioned at the top-right, making sure it stays within bounds while joining smoothly with the cloud's top puff, plus adding a thin connecting stem between them.

I'm offsetting the second spiral by a small normal shift and checking tube overlap — tightening the radius too fast over 1.25 turns causes the sumi tube to overlap itself, so I'm easing to 1.0 turn with a larger end radius and thinner tubes for both sumi and purple strokes. I'm also planning some puffs to get purple ring arcs via torus shapes on their front and back faces.

Adding purple shading discs...

Simplifying to one pale tube with rounded caps plus three sumi-outlined puffs for the wisp. I'm working out the tube's path points, making sure the tip starts inside the dome geometry and threads out through the front correctly near the dome's center and radius bounds.

I'm placing small puffs along the wisp path at varying positions with small, tapering radii near the cloud bottom. Then I'm setting glow strength differences between stars and moon, and sketching an eight-point star outline alternating long and short radii, extruded along the cloud's drawing plane.

Now I'm positioning the crescent moon and figuring out where each star should sit relative to the puffs, checking that star centers fall within puff radii so they read as nestled inside the clouds.

I'm setting up the extrude outline types to allow mixed sharp/smooth points, then writing a function to generate the crescent shape using arc parameters.

I'm verifying the intersection angle computes correctly and confirming the outer arc sweeps counterclockwise while the inner arc closes clockwise, forming a valid simple polygon. Now I'm considering scaling the whole crescent outline outward for a thicker outline, making sure the tips and inner hole scale consistently.

For the puffs, I'm dropping the cylinder's radial segments to 10 for a slightly blockier low-poly look, and confirming the orientation helper correctly aims along the given direction vector. I'm also weighing whether to add extra decorative touches like small accent dots or a shadow bar, but leaning toward keeping it simple, and tallying up the rough part count across trunk, rings, and tip segments to estimate complexity.

Tallying the remaining parts—collar studs, scallops, nostrils, wisp puffs, cloud puffs, arcs, spirals, moon, stars, and contours—brings the total to around 112, comfortably under my 150 budget. I'm now working out the highlight sweep sectors along the top and underside, confirming the rings sit just above the surface, then moving to write the hit-detection geometry along the trunk and the joint threshold logic.

Checking that each named joint has an `.at` method confirms the positioning approach works, so I'm finalizing the color palette references and writing the stick-geometry calls with embedded hit points tied to the trunk bones. I'm planning the buildTorsoCoat function, working out how to loft the body shape along the spine using stations with varying widths and heights tied to the hip, spine, and chest bones.

For the color sectors, I'm mapping angular bands around the torso to mimic natural fur coloring - a cream saddle band wrapped around the back, darker indigo belly patches, and transitional strips so the colors blend smoothly without gaps or overlaps at the seams.

Now I'm figuring out the neck geometry - whether to sweep across a chain of joints or build an explicit path connecting the neck base joints.

I should extend the torso toward the neck with tapering stations to blend the transition smoothly, narrowing width and height as z increases toward the shoulders, with the belly bottom resting around y 0.52.

Thinking through the loft setup, I'll use bone joints at hips, spine1, and chest for the path, assume the loft function accepts sweep options and faceted sections with elliptical cross-sections, and plan to use surface raycasting (skin.ray) to seat details like limbs onto the body at specific positions.

For the seigaiha pattern, I'm designing it as concentric stacked discs seated on ray-hit points: an outline disc, then alternating teal and white rings of decreasing radius and slightly increasing height to create a layered scallop effect, using a helper function that raycasts to find the surface hit point and null-checks before placing each disc.

I'm picking layer heights so the discs stack with slight overlap, then checking the curvature gap against the barrel radius to figure out how much the disc needs to sink below the surface to avoid visible edges. I'll handle this by translating the cylinder geometry downward instead of relying on the embed parameter.

Since true seigaiha scallops need overlapping fish-scale arcs rather than plain circles, I'm faking it with staggered rows of discs where lower rows get slightly taller heights so they visually overlay the ones above, avoiding z-fighting. I'm settling on roughly 3 rows by 5 columns per scallop section on each side of the saddle.

That's way over the 150-part budget, so I need to merge geometries per color group instead of instancing separate parts. Positioning cones to point downward along the tangent, flattening them, and placing them along the saddle's lower edge at the correct height.

Building the tooth geometry...

subject: baku
pitch:
Category: Fantastical creature.
Subject: baku, the dream-eating tapir spirit.
Style: ukiyo-e woodblock print.

spec.name: Baku, Dream-Eating Spirit
spec.description: A stylised ukiyo-e woodblock-print baku: a tapir-bodied spirit with an elephant trunk, rhinoceros eyes, tiger paws and an ox tail, drawn in flat indigo, cream and vermilion with sumi outlines, spiral medallions, seigaiha waves and drifting dream-mist clouds at the tip of its trunk.
spec.layout: Stands on four legs facing +Z. Front to back: kasumi dream-mist clouds and glowing dream orbs (z 2.15 to 2.5), a trunk hanging from the snout and curling up at the tip (z 1.5 to 2.2), a tapir-shaped head with big round rhinoceros eyes and a white-tipped upper lip (z 1.0 to 1.55), a short thick neck with a flame-blade mane, a deep barrel torso (z -0.95 to 0.9, belly y 0.6, back y 1.38), a high rounded rump, and an ox tail with a tuft hanging behind (to z -1.45). Only the four tiger paws touch y = 0. Legs are short and sturdy with chunky paws. Ukiyo-e look: every surface is one flat colour with no shading tricks. Key shapes sit on a slightly larger sumi underlay so a bold dark outline shows. Colour comes in hard stepped bands (the bokashi gradient is three flat bands, never a blend). Pattern is built as small parts: vermilion spiral medallions on shoulders and haunches, a cream saddle cloth with seigaiha wave arcs, and cloud scrolls. The body is indigo, fore and hind quarters dark and the mid-body cream like a tapir. The palette is limited to woodblock pigments: indigo, vermilion, cream paper, ochre, sumi black.

parts.builds: Torso, neck and all the printed pattern on them. One loft or sweep body skinned over hips, spine1, spine2 and chest: deep barrel, half width about 0.4, height about 0.76 (belly y 0.6, back y 1.38), rump rounded and slightly higher than the withers. A short thick neck sweep over neck1 and neck2 (radius about 0.2 tapering to 0.16) ending inside the skull at headPivot. Colour in hard stepped bands, no blends. Fore and hind quarters are indigo (sectors), the mid-body is a wide cream (paper) tapir saddle with a sumi-outlined edge (a slightly larger sumi underlay strip, then the paper strip on top). The belly is a pale-blue (paleBlue) band below it, with a thin midBlue step between paleBlue and indigo. The neck is indigo with a paper throat band. On top of the body: a woven saddle cloth in deepRed with a gold trim border over the paper saddle (a flat box or loft bulging only slightly), carrying a seigaiha (blue-wave) pattern of 3 to 4 concentric arcs per wave, in waveWhite, midBlue and indigo, as small flat half-rings (thin cylinders or sweeps, each about 3 cm) in overlapping rows. A shimenawa-style rope (twisted ochre and paper sweeps) loops round the girth with 4 vermilion tassels and tiny paper zigzag shide on it. Spiral medallions in vermilion with cream centres and sumi outlines (swept spiral paths, about 0.2 m across) seated on the shoulder at (±0.4, 1.05, 0.5) and the haunch at (±0.4, 1.05, -0.6), the signature karashishi swirl motif. Sumi outline pieces on the chest and rump. A cream cloud-scroll (kasumi) band along the flank, each cloud a flat scalloped extrude. Rump: tail root plug in indigo at tailRoot. Bone: put pieces on the nearest of hips, spine1, spine2, chest, neck1, neck2.
parts.attaches: Hind legs hang from hipL and hipR (hips); front legs from shoulderL and shoulderR (chest); neck sweep ends at headPivot and the head part continues from it; tail begins at tailRoot; the extras part's mane rides the neck and back from maneStart to maneEnd and sits on the surface.

parts.builds: Head, trunk, jaws, ears, tusks and face. Skull is a tapir wedge: braincase about 0.36 wide and 0.4 tall from z 1.0 to 1.3, tapering to a broad snout. The upper jaw and snout is its own piece in indigo with a paper-white lip tip (tapir white lip) outlined in sumi. Lower jaw is a separate piece on joint jaw (z 1.2 to 1.5, under the snout), indigo with a paper chin and a row of small ivory teeth; the mouth can open. Elephant trunk: a thick sweep over trunk1..trunk4 and trunkTip, root radius 0.11 tapering to 0.05, from trunkRoot hanging down and curling up at trunkTip. Cream ring ribs every 6 cm as thin torus or sweep rings, paper underside stripe (sector), two nose-hole discs in nose colour at the tip, and a vermilion band cuff halfway. Two ivory tusks curl up from the upper lip beside the trunk root. Rhinoceros eyes: big round eyes at eyeL and eyeR (radius about 0.055) built in layers: a sumi underlay disc, an eyeGold iris, a vermilion ring, a sumi slit pupil and a small waveWhite highlight; heavy indigo brow ridges above, with rose-and-sumi lashes or brow flicks in ukiyo-e line style. A vermilion tomoe (comma) emblem on the forehead at foreheadEmblem, outlined in sumi and gold. Round ears on joints earL and earR: indigo outer disc, paper rim, a rose inner disc and a few ochre fur tufts. Cheek ruffs of 5 to 6 overlapping flame-blade shapes in indigo, midBlue and paper on each side. Everything is flat colour with an outline underlay layer beneath the key shapes.
parts.attaches: Skull base meets the neck sweep at headPivot (head joint). The jaw hinges at jawHinge. The trunk starts at trunkRoot and ends at trunkTip. Ears root at earRootL and earRootR. The mane begins just behind the skull at maneStart; nothing of the head part lies behind z 0.95.

parts.builds: All four legs, short and sturdy, with chunky tiger paws. Front legs are sweeps skinned over shoulder, elbow and wrist joints (radius about 0.11 to 0.075); hind legs are skinned over hip, knee, hock and foot (thicker thigh about 0.16, hock bending back). Legs are indigo with a midBlue step on the lower leg and paper socks. Each foot is a big rounded tiger paw (a squashed sphere or capsule about 0.15 wide) in paper with a sumi outline underlay, four toes as small paper spheres or capsules, a rose pad under it, and four ivory claws peeking out in front. Paw soles rest on y = 0 (sink at most 2 cm). Vermilion garter bands with gold studs at each wrist and hock, with a small cloud-curl tuft above them. Fur ruffs at elbow and hock made of 4 to 5 overlapping flame-blade extrudes in indigo, midBlue and paper. A small vermilion spiral on the outer upper hind thigh. Thighs and shoulders tuck into the torso volume, so no gaps show. Put pieces on the leg joints of their own side, mirrored for x-positive L and x-negative R.
parts.attaches: Front legs start at shoulderL and shoulderR on the chest, hind legs at hipL and hipR on the hips, buried into the torso. Foot centres are at x of plus or minus 0.3, y 0.07, z 0.6 (front) and z -0.62 (hind). The body part's shoulder and haunch spirals sit just above and outside them.

parts.builds: Mane, tail and dream mist. Mane: a crest of broad overlapping flame-blade extrudes (ukiyo-e wind-swept hair) from maneStart down the neck and along the spine to maneEnd, each about 0.15 to 0.3 long leaning backward, in a root-to-tip palette of deepIndigo, indigo, midBlue, paper, with a vermilion tip on every third blade, over a solid indigo ridge sweep; a few gold-edged curls at the base of the skull. Ox tail on tail1..tail4: indigo tapering sweep (radius 0.06 to 0.035) with a big tuft at the end made of 8 to 10 overlapping flame blades in indigo, paper and vermilion tips, plus a gold band at the tuft base. Dream mist (the dreams the baku eats): around dreamOrigin, in front of trunkTip at z 2.15 to 2.5, within x plus or minus 0.45 and y 0.85 to 1.95 (never on the floor, nothing touching the legs). Four flat kasumi clouds made of scalloped extrudes (waveWhite, paleBlue, rose, each with a thin sumi or midBlue offset underlay for the outline), stacked in loose bands. Three or four dream orbs (dreamGlow, dreamViolet, vermilion spheres of radius 0.04 to 0.07, with tiny waveWhite highlights), some with swirling spiral tails. A thin spiral wisp sweep in dreamViolet and waveWhite flows from the clouds into the trunk tip. Use the glow kit on the orbs and a few wisp pieces. All details are small seated parts in their own flat colours. Put the mane on the neck1, neck2, chest, spine joints, the tail on the tail joints, and the mist on trunkTip or the root.
parts.attaches: Mane sits on the neck and back surface from maneStart to maneEnd, just behind the head's skull. The tail roots at tailRoot on joint tail1, continuing the rump plug. Mist hovers at dreamOrigin just beyond trunkTip, and its wisp ends at trunkTip, touching the trunk.

Category: Fantastical creature.

spec.name: Baku, Dream-Eating Tapir Spirit
spec.description: A stylized ukiyo-e woodblock-print baku: a tapir-bodied spirit with a trunk-like snout, tiger paws, an ox tail and swirling indigo cloud-wreathed mane, standing in rest pose.
spec.layout: A long-bodied tapir-like beast facing +Z, standing on four sturdy legs with tiger paws. The front half is a deep indigo-black coat; a cream saddle band runs across the barrel and the belly and legs are cream, as on a tapir. The head is carried low and forward on a thick neck, with a long drooping prehensile snout, small round fringed ears, big golden ox-like eyes with heavy black outlines, and small curved ivory tusks. A curling Japanese-style cloud mane (vermilion and white swirl blades) runs down the neck and spine. Short tail with a tuft tipped in vermilion. Ukiyo-e style: bold black outline-coloured shapes, flat colour blocks, repeated wave and cloud (kumo) motifs as small parts, red seal-like markings on the shoulders and haunches, and vermilion flame-like wisps rising from the back. All colours are flat.

parts.builds: Barrel body as one loft over hips and chest in coat indigo, with a wide cream saddle band, cream belly sector, lighter coatLight back highlights, wave-pattern trim bands (small wave-blue crescents repeated) along the flanks, vermilion seal-style emblems (small square plus inner glyph) on shoulders and haunches, and a rump with the tail root. Includes the tail chain (tail1, tail2) as a tapered sweep ending in a vermilion and cloudWhite tuft of overlapping blades.
parts.attaches: Neck at neckBase, front legs at shoulderL/R, rear legs at hipL/R, tail at tailRoot, mane along spineTop.

parts.builds: Four sturdy legs, each a sweep through hip, knee and paw: indigo upper leg fading to cream lower leg and socks, with chunky tiger paws (dark pawDark rounded block, three toe bumps, pale claw spikes) on the floor. Cream fur-tuft blades at the elbows and hocks, a vermilion anklet ring on each leg, and a small cloud-swirl motif on each thigh.
parts.attaches: Top of each leg at shoulderL/R and hipL/R mounts, under the torso.

parts.builds: Thick neck sweep from neckBase to headPivot. Tapir head: a rounded skull, long drooping trunk-like snout (tapered sweep curving down, with a pink nostril tip and ink nostrils and cream upper lip patch), separate upper and lower jaw (jaw joint) with a small pink mouth interior, ivory curved tusks, large gold ox eyes with thick ink outlines, black pupils and white highlight, heavy ink brows with vermilion eyeshadow, round ears with cream rims and ink inner, whisker rods, and a vermilion forehead mark (third-eye flame emblem).
parts.attaches: Neck joins torso at neckBase; mane starts at the crown of the head; jaw hinges at jawHinge.

spec.name: Bauhaus Songbird
spec.description: A small songbird perched on a short branch, built from circles, triangles and rectangles in red, yellow, blue, black and white, in the style of a Bauhaus poster.
spec.layout: Real songbird scale (about 12 cm of bird on a 44 cm branch). The branch lies along X, resting on the floor with its top at y=0.036. The bird perches on it centred at x=0 and faces +Z. Body axis is tilted about 30° (breast up and forward, rump low), with the tail trailing back and slightly down. The head is a big round yellow ball sitting almost neckless on the top-front of the body. The beak is short and conical, red, split into separate upper and lower jaws. From front to back: beak tip at z≈0.125, then the head, then the red chest disc, the blue back and white belly, the folded wings, and the black/blue/yellow barred tail ending at z≈-0.145. Short black legs with 3 forward toes and 1 hind toe grip the branch top. The only forms are discs, spheres, cones, flat triangles and rectangles. Every colour block has a hard edge, and no part is covered in decoration. Colour roles: yellow head, blue back, red chest disc and wings, white belly, black ink for outlines, bars, legs and tail. Each coloured disc or emblem sits on a slightly larger black disc, 1.5 mm proud of the surface, as a poster-style outline. All colours are flat, with no gradients and no paint. Left is +X, and L joints and parts are at +X. Mirror every paired part for R at -X. Rest pose: wings folded but slightly separated from the body, beak closed, legs apart, toes spread.

parts.builds: The body and its colour blocking. The body is a low-poly ellipsoid about 0.16 long along the body bone and 0.05 radius, a swept or lofted egg shape riding the body and neck joints. The back and top are blue (sectors or a separate cap). The lower half is a white belly with a hard horizontal edge, kept as a separate shape. A big red disc (radius about 0.028) with a black outline disc behind it sits on the breast at chestFront, facing forward and slightly up. A yellow triangle sits on the rump, a black collar ring or band marks where the neck meets the body, and a thin blueDeep saddle stripe runs across the shoulders. Small geometric accents repeat the motif: a yellowDeep square at each flank and 2 or 3 small white or black discs along the belly edge. The body carries the neck joint, and the neck can be a short blue cylinder or sweep that hides the join with the head. It does NOT build wings, legs, tail or head.
parts.attaches: Head sits on top of the front at neckBase and headCentre. Wings meet at shoulderL and shoulderR on the flanks. Tail starts at tailRoot on the rump. Legs emerge from the belly at hipL and hipR.

parts.builds: A round yellow head (low-poly sphere, radius about 0.032, centred at headCentre) with a yellowDeep cap disc or crown ring. The beak is a separate upper jaw (red cone or wedge, about 0.03 long) and a lower jaw (a smaller redDeep cone). It is built at beakBase, hinged at jawHinge, with the jaw riding the jaw joint and the upper beak riding head. A black line marks the mouth. Two big eyes sit on the sides and show from the front: a black outline disc, then a white disc, a blue iris disc and a black pupil, each layered 1 mm apart, and a tiny white highlight. A black brow bar over each eye. A blue circle cheek patch behind each eye, and a crest of three flat triangular blades on the crown (red, blue and black, tallest in the middle, fanned fore-to-aft). A small black dot nostril on each side of the upper beak. Nothing blocks the eyes or beak from the front.
parts.attaches: Sits on the body top-front at headCentre and neckBase. The beak tip is the foremost point of the model at z≈0.125.

parts.builds: Both folded wings, mirrored, and the tail. Each wing is a red rounded-triangle or quarter-disc covert slab on the flank (extrude, riding wingL1/wingR1 and wingL2/wingR2), with a black outline slab behind it. Below it are 4 long flight-feather blades in a stepped fan (blue, yellow, blue, black, each a thin extruded elongated rectangle or triangle with a pointed tip). A yellow disc and a white bar sit on the covert, and the tips end in alternating black and white squares. The wings lie slightly apart from the body, tips near [±0.095, 0.085, -0.115]. The tail has 5 flat feather blades (extruded long rectangles with a notched or pointed tip) fanned slightly, colours black, blue, black, blue, black, with a yellow band stripe and a red tip triangle on the middle feather, and a white bar across all feathers. It sweeps back and slightly down from tailRoot to a tip at about [0, 0.058, -0.145], riding tail1 and tail2.
parts.attaches: Wings attach at shoulderL and shoulderR on the body flanks. The tail starts at tailRoot under the rump triangle.

parts.builds: Both legs, mirrored. Each has a rounded thigh puff (a small sphere at hip, white on the inner side and yellowDeep on the outside), a thin black tarsus rod from hip to ankle, a red ring band at the ankle (a small cylinder), and a foot with 3 forward toes and 1 hind toe. Each toe is a thin black rod or capsule of 3-4 mm radius, about 0.02 long, spread and gripping across the top of the branch (toes lie at y≈0.040 and curve slightly down at the tips). Each toe ends in a small red cone claw, and each knuckle has a tiny yellow disc. The legs are about 4 cm apart. Everything rides the matching leg and toe joints.
parts.attaches: Hips attach at hipL and hipR on the belly. Feet rest on the branch top at perchTop (y=0.036), toes touching it.

parts.builds: The perch. A straight, slightly tapered rod along X from x=-0.22 to x=0.22 (radius about 0.016, axis at y=0.02, bottom touching the floor, top at 0.036) in branchDark. Colour bands, as short slightly larger cylinder rings, repeat red, yellow, blue and white at set spacing, with the middle 0.07 left plain under the bird's feet. The ends are flat black cut discs with a white inner ring. A short forked twig rises from the left end region (+X, around x=0.15) at about 50°, with a smaller twig branching from it, made of black rods with colour-ring bands. The twigs carry geometric leaves: a red disc, a yellow triangle, a blue half-disc and a white square, each on its own black outline shape. A small knot disc and 2 stub nubs sit along the main branch. A second short stub rises on the right end (-X) with a blue disc leaf. Twigs stay below y=0.16 and clear of the bird. Everything rides the perch joint.
parts.attaches: The branch top at perchTop (y=0.036, x=0) is where the toes land. It is the lowest part of the model and rests on the floor.

spec.name: Bauhaus Songbird on a Branch
spec.description: A life-size songbird perched on a gently curved branch, built from Bauhaus primary-colour geometry: a red sphere body, a yellow sphere head, blue half-disc wings, a black blade tail and a branch ringed in red, yellow and cream, with squares, circles and triangles for leaves.
spec.layout: Units are metres and the bird is life-size, about 0.25 m from beak tip (z +0.118) to tail tip (z -0.13). The branch runs along X (-0.25 to +0.25) and curves gently upward at both ends. Its lowest point, at x=0, rests on y=0 with axis y=0.02 and radius 0.02, so its top at x=0 is y=0.04. That top is the perch. The bird sits across the branch facing +Z, feet on the perch at x=±0.026. From the front the bird reads as stacked primitives. A big red ellipsoid body (about 0.055 half-width, 0.05 half-height, 0.075 half-length, centre [0,0.115,0.005]) carries a cream oval belly and a yellow triangle emblem on the breast. A black thin collar ring separates the body from a yellow sphere head (radius about 0.036, centre [0,0.165,0.062]). The head has big concentric-circle eyes (black, cream ring, yellow dot) at x=±0.027, a small red circular cheek disc under each eye, a red conical beak split into upper and lower jaw, and a crest of three flat triangles (red, blue, black) leaning back from the crown. The wings are folded on the flanks, angled slightly back and out, about 15 degrees off the body so they read as separate. Each is a blue half-disc or quarter-disc plate stack with a black bar, a cream stripe and a red triangle tip. The tail is a flat fan of three overlapping blocky rectangular blades in black, with a red centre stripe and a yellow tip square, sloping gently down and back from [0,0.108,-0.06] to [0,0.085,-0.13]. The thin black legs end in three forward toes and one back toe that wrap over the branch, with cream claw tips. The branch is charcoal, with alternating red, yellow and cream ring bands and two side twigs. One twig rises at x=-0.15 and carries leaves as flat blue squares, yellow discs and red triangles. The other twig points forward at x=+0.14. Every surface is a flat colour from the palette, and every motif (circle, triangle, square) is its own small part seated on the surface. Facets are visible (6 to 14 segments per primitive), nothing is smooth, and the layout is symmetric about x=0 except the branch twigs. Use primary colours for large areas and black, cream and charcoal for contrast; secondary hues are the only shading.

parts.builds: The red faceted ellipsoid body, a cream oval belly plate on the underside and chest, and a yellow triangle emblem seated on the breast. A blue half-disc rump patch sits at the lower back above the tail root. A black thin ring collar sits at the neck base [0,0.13,0.045], between body and head. A short yellow cylinder neck rises from the collar into the head. Add a black circle dot at the centre of the belly oval, and a row of three small cream squares down each flank under the wing root as Bauhaus trim. Everything is flat-coloured primitives (spheres, cylinders, extruded triangles, discs), 8 to 14 segments each. Wings, legs and tail attach to the body but are built by other parts. The body ellipsoid is about 0.055 half-width, 0.05 half-height and 0.075 half-length, centred at bodyCenter. It must leave room under it for the hips at y=0.085, and its lowest point stays above y=0.062.
parts.attaches: Neck cylinder top meets the head part at mount neckBase and headCenter. The wing parts start at wingRootL and wingRootR on the flanks. The tail part starts at tailRoot behind the rump patch. The leg part's hips at hipL and hipR sit just inside the lower belly.

Now I'm working out the wheel track width based on the real Spitfire's 5.75 ft spacing, positioning the legs slightly splayed outward from the wing attachment down to the wheel centers, then moving on to place the tailplane further aft on the fuselage.

I'm now sizing the tail assembly—fin height, tailplane span and chord—scaling them against the real aircraft's dimensions, then checking the propeller spinner and blade radius against the fuselage centerline to make sure the prop tip clears the ground properly.

Adjusting the nose height formula, I'm balancing the overall model size so the prop tip, not the tail, sets the bounding height at 3.25, with width fixed at 11.2 (wing tips ±5.6) and length spanning from spinner to tail at roughly 9.15 units. spec.name: Spitfire Cyanotype Blueprint
spec.description: A Supermarine Spitfire Mk I fighter standing on its main wheels and tailwheel, rendered as a cyanotype blueprint: every surface in Prussian-blue tones with white drafting linework, rivets and panel lines as small parts.
spec.layout:
Real Spitfire Mk I size (about 11.2 m span, 9.1 m long) in a three-point ground stance. Fuselage axis is horizontal at y=1.75, nose toward +Z. From front to back: three-blade propeller disc at z=4.0 (radius 1.6, tips clear the floor by 0.15 m), a white-tipped spinner, a round Merlin cowl with 6 fishtail exhaust stacks per side, the long slim fuselage, a framed bubble canopy at z -1.7..1.0, a turtleback fairing, then the tail cone carrying a tall rounded fin and elliptical tailplane. Low elliptical wings (dihedral about 6 degrees, root y=1.22 rising to y=1.62 at the tips) with a straight leading edge and a curved trailing edge. They carry an oil cooler under the left wing (+X) and a radiator under the right wing (-X), four gun barrels in each leading edge, and ailerons and flaps. Main gear legs splay outward to wheels at x=+-1.4, z=0.6; the tailwheel sits at z=-4.05. Nothing else is on the floor and there is no ground plane.

STYLE: everything is cyanotype blue. Underside = light sky blue (skyPale/sky), top and side skin = cobalt with disruptive camouflage patches of prussian, darker shadow zones in navy, deepest ink for tyres, exhaust, gaps and recesses. Linework is WHITE and pale: panel lines, rib lines, stringers, rivet rows, control-surface hinge lines and bright edge trim along leading edges and tips are thin small parts seated on the surface, so the plane reads as white drafting lines on blue paper. Roundels are concentric flat discs (outer navy ring, pale ring, sky ring, white centre); the fin flash is three vertical bands (sky, white, navy). Details are fine and fussy; the silhouette stays simple, blocky and bold. Glowing cyan (cyanGlow, via the glow kit) is used only for the gunsight reflector and the wingtip and tail lights. Colour by place: lighter on top, darker below, soot at the exhausts, a pale chipped strip on the wing-root walkway.

spec.name: Spitfire Blueprint
spec.description: A Supermarine Spitfire Mk I fighter drawn as a cyanotype blueprint: deep Prussian-blue airframe with white-line panel seams, ribs, rivets and callout details, standing on its undercarriage.
spec.layout: Single-engine low-wing monoplane facing +Z. Propeller spinner at z=+4.2, long nose with Merlin cowl, cockpit with bubble canopy at z~0 to -0.9, tapering fuselage to a tail at z=-4.4 with fin and tailplane. Elliptical wings span x=+-5.6 at y~1.0, with a slight dihedral, round tips, and the gear legs under the wing at x=+-1.4. Tail wheel under the rear. Everything is a flat cyanotype colour: Prussian-blue hull panels, paler cyan wing skin, and white linework as thin parts (panel seams, ribs, rivet rows, roundel rings, stencil bars) seated on surfaces. Lowest points (tyres) rest on y=0. Roundels are concentric flat discs: white, mid blue, pale cyan.

parts.builds: Engine nose forward of z=0.8: Merlin cowling loft in hullBlue, exhaust stacks (3 per side as small deepBlue cylinders with line rings), cowl panel seams and rivet rows in line, spinner cone in deepBlue with a line band, the three-blade propeller on the propeller joint (prop blue, white tip stripes), radiator scoop under the nose.

Cyanotype style: every surface is one of a few blues (deep Prussian body, mid blue panels, pale cyan highlights); white linework is built as thin parts seated on the surface: panel seams, rivet rows, rib lines on the wings, roundels as concentric rings, outline stripes along wing edges, and a faint grid of white thin rods under the model as drafting marks. parts.builds: Tail assembly: swept fin and rudder (extruded, rudder with chalk hinge line and rib lines), two elliptical tailplanes with elevators and seams, tail cone end cap, tail lamp, tailwheel strut, small tailwheel and its fork, chalk outlines and rivet rows throughout.

parts.attaches: Leg tops at gearL and gearR mounts under the wings; wheels rest on the floor.

spec.name: Brutalist Housing Block
spec.description: A monumental raw-concrete slab block on massive tapered pilotis, with a deep loggia facade of coloured panels, a rooftop terrace with vaulted crèche and chimney stacks, and two free-standing rear service towers linked by bridges.
spec.layout: Static architectural model, real scale, no joints. +Z is the loggia front, +X is the building's left. Structural grid: bay lines at x = -27 + 6k (k = 0..9, so -27, -21 ... 27). Facade cell n (n = 0..8) spans bay lines n..n+1, with centre x = -24 + 6n. The slab block is 54 m wide, 18 m deep (z -9..9), with its soffit at y = 6 and its roof slab top at y = 30. There are 8 storeys of 3 m; storey n has floor level y = 6 + 3n and n = 0..7. Silhouette from the front: a long horizontal slab lifted on huge tapered piers (open storey 0 to 6 m); a dense 9 x 8 grid of deep recessed loggias in the facade, with thick concrete party walls, balcony slabs and coloured panels; a parapet and roof clutter above (central vaulted pavilion, chimney stacks, stair/lift caps); and at the back two tall slender towers (x about +-16, z -13..-10) rising to about 36 m, tied to the slab by short bridges at y = 12, 18 and 24. Everything is raw board-marked concrete. Style shows through these elements: chamfered edges and heavy chunky proportions; horizontal formwork ribs as thin dark inset strips; rain-stain streaks as thin vertical parts in concreteStain under every ledge, sill and parapet; patches of lighter and warmer concrete in concreteLight and concreteWarm; moss on upward ledges; and primary-colour panels (red, yellow, blue, green) as the only bright notes, with a few warm glowing windows. Nothing is smooth or glossy. Parts count meshes, so builders should merge small repeated pieces with mergeGeometries per colour, using `b.part` with `at: [0,0,0]`, to stay within budget. Keep the facade clear of anything standing in front of it. Do not add any ground, trees or scenery beyond what each part lists.

parts.builds: Ground storey and plaza. A low paving plinth slab (y 0..0.3) across x -27..27, z -9..9, with a asphalt strip and kerb at the front. Under the slab, 8 pairs of huge tapered concrete pilotis (about 1.6 x 2.4 m at the top, widening to roughly 2.2 m at the base, chamfered, board-form ribs, concreteDark footing blocks) at x = -21, -15, -9, -3, 3, 9, 15, 21 on both pier rows z = +5 and z = -5. Each pier is built from a lower and an upper tapered block, and a couple of piers carry a lighter 'cast' patch. Two heavy end piers at x = +-26 form blind walls z -9..9 that are 2 m thick. A glazed double-height entrance lobby centred x = 0, z 3..8, y 0.3..5.2 (glassDark panes in steel mullions, a doorOrange door pair, a concrete canopy slab with a tapered edge). A sculptural concrete ramp and wide steps from the plaza to the lobby, and a sturdy rail. Concrete planters (concreteLight with moss tops) in two groups. Low sculptural concrete benches. Bike-rack bars in steel. A white signage bar above the lobby door made of small separate letter-block parts. Under-slab lamp discs in windowGlow (glow) at every second bay. Add rain-streak and wear parts at pier feet. Does not build the soffit ribs, which belong to slabCore.
parts.attaches: Piers top out flush at soffitLevel (y = 6), where the slabCore soffit begins. The lobby canopy fronts slabFrontFace and stops short of facadeOuterEdge. The paving plinth ends at x = +-27 and z = +-9, with no overhang past the slab.

parts.builds: The main concrete mass of the slab from y 6 to 30, x -27..27, z -9..5, with the back facade at z = -9 and the end gables. The core mass is built as several stacked or horizontal blocks, not one box: a soffit with coffered ribs and thick ducts (concreteDark, y 6..6.8); eight floor bands of concrete with a 0.35 m spandrel slab at each level, which projects 0.25 m past the wall on the back face; and a roof slab (y 29.6..30) with a thickened edge. Horizontal board-form ribs are thin inset strips in boardSeam that run along the back and gable faces at 0.6 m spacing, and patches of concreteLight and concreteWarm break them up. The back face (z = -9) has a regular rhythm of narrow vertical slit windows (glassDark with concreteDark reveals, two per cell, cells as on the front) and a few windowGlow lit ones (glow). It has chunky concrete lintel hoods over each slit, stair-light slots, kitchen-vent boxes in steel, a deep vertical shadow joint every 6 m, and doorOrange entrance doors with concrete door hoods at x = +-16, y = 12, 18, 24 (the bridge landings; keep the door area clear). The gables at x = +-27 are huge blind walls with a stepped relief in concreteDark, three tall vertical slit windows with chamfered concrete frames, and a big recessed circular or stepped motif panel. Rain-stain streaks in concreteStain (thin tall parts) run under every ledge, and moss patches sit on the upward faces of the slab edge overhangs. The top is flush at roofSlabTop.
parts.attaches: Sits on the piers at soffitLevel y = 6. Its front face z = 5 meets the frontFacade back wall at slabFrontFace. Its back face z = -9 receives the tower bridges at the bridge mounts. Its top slab surface at y = 30 carries the roof part.

parts.builds: The loggia facade in the zone z 5..9, y 6..30. A 9 column x 8 row grid of deep recessed cells, each 6 m x 3 m. Structure: a thick floor/balcony slab at every level (y = 6 + 3n, 0.4 m thick, from z 5 to 9, full width, with a chamfered, tapered edge and a heavier hood slab at the top row); and 10 vertical concrete party walls at the bay lines (x = -27 + 6k, 0.5 m thick, z 5..9, chamfered, k = 0..9; the end ones are thicker, 0.9 m). The cell back wall is at z = 5..5.6 and the glazed loggia door/window wall is on it: concreteDark reveal, a steel mullion frame, glass or glassDark panes, an inner door in wood or doorOrange in some cells, and a solid spandrel strip. In every cell a coloured panel (panelRed, panelYellow, panelBlue or panelGreen, chosen with rng(seed) so the pattern looks pseudo-random but is evenly distributed, about 40 percent of cells) covers the cell's back wall or its side wall (a flat slab seated 3 cm proud, with a thin concreteDark frame). In some cells, a vertical concrete brise-soleil fin set (3 to 5 thin deep fins) fills the open side. A steel railing (railing colour, a top bar, thin posts and a mid bar) runs on every balcony at z = 8.8, 1.0 m tall. A few cells hold small details: a potted plant block in moss, a hanging laundry bar, an AC unit box in tankGrey, and a lit windowGlow pane (glow) in about 12 cells. Every cell is seated precisely on the grid, and every slab and wall has a stain streak below its lower edge in concreteStain. Board-form ribs show on the party walls. Nothing stands in front of z = 9.
parts.attaches: Back wall at z = 5 against the slabCore front face (slabFrontFace) and the cell grid. It sits on the lobby canopy zone only from y = 6 up, and the soffit level is y = 6. The top balcony slab (y = 29.6..30) is flush with roofSlabTop, where the roof parapet continues.

parts.builds: The roof terrace, y 30..37, over x -27..27, z -9..9. A parapet of concrete (y 30..31.2, 0.5 m thick) runs around the whole perimeter, with a board-form rib, a chamfered cap and a stain streak below, and gaps for drainage spouts (concrete spout blocks in concreteDark). The roofTar roof surface sits inside it, with a lighter gravel border and paving walkways in paving. A central vaulted crèche pavilion at roofPavilionCentre (x -9..9, z -4..2, up to y 36.5): the walls are board-marked concrete, with a barrel-vault roof made of 7 to 9 overlapping segments or stepped slices tapering to a point, a glazed front with steel mullions and glassDark panes plus windowGlow (glow) lights, and a doorOrange door. Next to it, a lower sculpted concrete sports-court wall and a climbing wall with colour holds (panelRed, panelYellow, panelBlue). Large chimney/ventilation stacks at roofStackLeft and roofStackRight (about 4 each, tapered, chamfered, up to 34.5 m, with stepped caps and a dark vent slot), and two or three stair-and-lift overrun boxes near x = +-16 on the back side (z -8..-5, height up to 34, flat roofs, doors, a slit window). A rooftop pergola of concrete beams with thin cross rafters in wood, two cylindrical water tanks in tankGrey with steel bands, a railing around the roof edge on the inner side, a few moss patches, and a line of small skylight pyramids. A fine concrete handrail serpentine path for decoration is allowed but optional.
parts.attaches: Rests on roofSlabTop (y = 30) across both slabCore and the facade top slab. The parapet outer faces align with the slab outer edges at x = +-27, z = +9 and z = -9. The stair overruns sit above the towers' bridge line (x = +-16) but do not touch the towers, which are behind z = -9.

parts.builds: Two free-standing rear service towers (lift and stair cores) on the back side at towerLeftBase (-16, 0, -11.5) and towerRightBase (16, 0, -11.5). Each is 6 m wide (x +-3 of its centre), 3 m deep (z -13..-10) and 0 to 34 m tall, topped with a heavy cantilevered cap slab and a lift overrun block up to y 36. They are built as a chunky tapered foundation plinth (concreteDark, y 0..1.2, within z -13.5..-9.5... keep it inside the box), a stack of storey bands with horizontal board-form ribs, and vertical slit stair windows (glassDark in concrete frames, a diagonal stair flight silhouette made of small slanted parts, some windowGlow lit, glow). The faces have rain-stain streaks, a top cornice, moss at ledges, and a steel ladder or antenna mast on each cap. Bridges: concrete walkway bridges at levels 12, 18 and 24 (mounts bridgeLeftLevel12/18/24 and bridgeRightLevel12/18/24), each a 3 m wide box (z -10..-9, 2.6 m high) with a thick floor slab, a roof slab, side parapets, a small window slot and an orange-framed door on the slabCore side. A ground-level entrance in each tower is a doorOrange door with a concrete hood, plus a number plate made of small white blocks. A small number sign in white on the top of each tower, lamp discs in windowGlow, a steel fire-escape stair on one tower's side, and a couple of steel cable runs from cap to cap in railing colour.
parts.attaches: The bridges end at z = -9 on the slabCore back face, at the doors on x = +-16 (mounts bridge*Level*). The tower bases rest on the ground at towerLeftBase and towerRightBase. No part of the towers goes above y = 36, and none goes beyond z = -13.5.
