Category: Architecture.
Subject: brutalist housing block.
Style: raw concrete brutalism.

spec.name: Brutalist Housing Block
spec.description: A raw board-marked concrete slab block on massive pilotis, with deep eggcrate loggias, rear access galleries, a freestanding lift and stair tower at one end and a roof terrace with plant and a vaulted pavilion.
spec.layout: Static architectural model, 1 unit = 1 m, built at full real size. +Z is the long front facade, +Y is up, and the model is centred on x = 0. The long slab runs along X from x=-32 (right end seen from the front, the model's right) to x=18. It sits on pilotis: a 6 m open ground storey, then 7 residential storeys of 3 m each (y=6 to 27), then a roof terrace from 27 to about 31. The tower is a separate heavy concrete shaft with a cantilevered crown at the left end (x 18 to 32) and is the tallest element at y=31. Grid: 10 structural bays of 5 m on the slab at x edges -32,-27,...,18 (edge i = -32+5i). Storey floor levels are y=6+3k, k=0..7. The slab core is a solid block x[-32,18], y[6,27], z[-7.5,7.5]. FRONT (+Z) is an eggcrate of deep loggias: concrete party fins at every bay line and floor and ceiling slabs project from the core wall at z=7.5 out to z=11. Each loggia is 4.65 m wide and 2.65 m high and 3.5 m deep. The loggia back walls are painted panels in rotating primaries, with glazed sliding doors, railings and planters. BACK (-Z) is the access side: continuous gallery decks at each storey projecting from z=-7.5 to z=-9.5 with solid 1.1 m parapets, and three full-height stair towers projecting to z=-11. The GROUND storey has massive tapered piloti columns, transfer beams, a recessed glazed lobby, an entrance canopy, steps and a ramp. The ROOF has a parapet, plant rooms, chimney-like ventilation stacks, a water tank and a vaulted concrete pavilion. STYLE: raw concrete brutalism. Heavy, blocky, chunky proportions. Every concrete surface is built from several flat greys, so that the pour lines and wear read as geometry. Board-marking is thin horizontal strips about 3 cm proud in boardMark. Tie-rod holes are small dark discs on a regular grid. Cast joints are thin dark recessed strips. Rain staining is vertical streaks in stain and mossStain, below ledges, parapets and window heads. Rust runs sit under metal fixings. Concrete tones vary between neighbouring panels (concreteLight, concreteMid, concreteWarm, concreteDark) so the pour sequence shows. Colour comes only in small doses: the loggia panels, lit windows, doors and plants. No smooth or glossy surfaces. Chamfers are minimal, edges are crisp, and geometry is boxes, slabs, wedges and half-cylinders. Do not add scenery, ground, trees or props beyond the subject and the listed planters, bike racks and lamps.

parts.builds: The solid mass of the residential slab, x[-32,18], y[6,27], z[-7.5,7.5], and its two end gables. Use several adjacent concrete boxes in different grey tones (concreteLight, concreteMid, concreteWarm), one per pour lift, with a thin shadowRecess cast joint between lifts every 3 m of height and board-marking strips on every face. Build the front wall (z=7.5) and back wall (z=-7.5) as plain concrete planes, with sliding-door and gallery-door openings left to the facade parts. Build a thin roof slab edge band at y=26.7-27. Add vertical expansion joints (shadowRecess strips) at x=-7 and x=3. Add tie-rod hole grids on the walls at both ends. Left gable x=-32 and right gable x=18, the latter partly hidden behind the tower: a large blank concrete wall with a tall narrow stair-light slit, a big white painted storey-number emblem built from small boxes, rain streaks (stain, mossStain) and a rust stain under the roof edge. Deep concreteDark soffit strip along the underside at y=6. Do not build loggias, galleries, fins, windows or panels. Those belong to the front and back facade parts.
parts.attaches: Sits on the pilotis and transfer beams at pilotisTop (y=6). Its front wall at frontCoreWall (z=7.5) and back wall at backCoreWall (z=-7.5) are where the facade parts attach. Its roof top at slabRoofTop (y=27) is where the roof part stands. The right gable abuts the tower at towerJoin (x=18).

parts.builds: The +Z loggia eggcrate, z[7.5,11], 10 bays by 7 storeys. Build concrete party fins, 0.35 m thick, at each of the 11 bay lines x=-32+5i, running full height y[6,27] and z[7.5,11], with board-marking strips and alternate tone variation. Build floor and ceiling slabs 0.35 m thick at each storey level y=6+3k (k=0..7), spanning the full width and projecting from z=7.5 to z=11, with a darker front-edge band and rain streaks down from slab edges. Inside each loggia, 4.65 m by 2.65 m, add a coloured painted back-wall panel just proud of z=7.5 (panelRed, panelOchre, panelBlue, panelWhite and panelGreen in a pseudo-random but deterministic pattern, about one in three loggias left raw concrete). Add a glazed sliding door in frameDark and glass with a glassLit interior on about one in four, and a solid timber door leaf. Add a metalRail balustrade at the slab front edge in about half the loggias, and a planter box with planterSoil and plantGreen in some. Add an occasional hanging laundry line or a chair block. Every bay at the top storey gets a deeper concreteDark shadow strip under the roof slab. A horizontal pair of thin signWhite house-number plates at the left end. Use boxes, not tubes, for rails (thin posts and a top bar).
parts.attaches: Backs onto the core wall at frontCoreWall (z=7.5). The outer frame edge lies at frontLoggiaEdge (z=11). Its bottom slab sits at y=6 on the pilotis, and its top slab reaches y=27, where the roof parapet starts.

parts.builds: The -Z access side, z[-11,-7.5]. Build continuous gallery decks 0.4 m thick at each storey y=6+3k (k=0..7) projecting from z=-7.5 to z=-9.5, over x[-32,18]. Add 1.1 m solid concrete parapets on the outer edge with a metalRail top bar, board-marked and rain-stained. On the core wall behind, one entrance per 5 m bay: a timber door in frameDark with a small glassLit window beside it, a doormat or number plate in signWhite, and a thin concrete canopy slab over every other door. Between doors, a long high kitchen window in frameDark and glass. Build 3 full-height stair towers at x centres -22, -4 and 12, each 4.5 m wide, running y[6,27] and projecting to z=-11. They are heavy concrete (concreteDark and concreteMid) with tall narrow vertical slit windows (glass with a glassLit stripe) and a flat cantilevered cap slab at y=27, with board-marking and stains. Add connecting bridge decks at each tower where the gallery meets it, and a cluster of drainpipes (thin metalRail boxes) at the bay lines. Vertical rust streaks below the parapet fixings.
parts.attaches: Backs onto the core wall at backCoreWall (z=-7.5). Gallery edge at backGalleryEdge (z=-9.5), stair-tower faces at backStairTowerEdge (z=-11). Bottom at y=6 on the pilotis, top at y=27 under the roof parapet.

parts.builds: The open pilotis storey, y[0,6], x[-32,18], z[-11,11], resting on the floor. Build massive tapered piloti columns, each a pair of stacked frustums or chunky tapered boxes about 1.6 m by 3.2 m at the base and 2.4 m by 3.6 m at the top, with board-marking and rough concreteDark lower sections where splashed. Place them in two rows at z=-5.5 and z=5.5, at x=-27, -17, -7, 3 and 13, plus a heavier pair at each end. Add transfer beams at y[5,6] along each row and across between the rows (concreteMid), which fill the underside under the slab. A recessed glazed lobby box at x[-10,0], z[-5,5], y[0,4.6] with frameDark mullions, glass, a glassLit interior, a sign above the door and a timber double door. An entrance canopy slab projecting forward to z=11 at x[-10,0] and y=4.6-5, and wide concrete steps and a ramp with metalRail handrails at lobbyDoor. A low plinth strip along the front. Cycle store: a row of bike racks with simple wheel frames. Planter boxes with planterSoil and plantGreen. Two tall post lamps with glassLit heads. A big painted 'blok' lettering, or signWhite house number emblem, on a pier. Concrete splash stains and moss near the bottom of piers, and rain streaks.
parts.attaches: Top face at y=6 (pilotisTop) carries the slab core, front facade and back galleries. The tower stands at towerJoin (x=18) immediately to its right. The lobby door is at lobbyDoor (x=-5, z=11).

parts.builds: The freestanding concrete lift and stair tower at the left end, x[18,32], z[-7.5,7.5], y[0,31], resting on the floor and abutting the slab end gable at towerJoin (x=18). The shaft is a stacked set of boxes (different concrete tones and pour lifts, each 3 m) with board-marking, tie-rod grids, expansion joint strips and heavy rain and moss staining. The base is wider and darker (concreteDark) up to y=2. Vertical full-height glazed slits, glass with frameDark mullions and a stripe of glassLit, on the +Z face and on the +X end, with deep concreteDeep reveals. A projecting stair-landing bay on the front face: small cantilevered balconies, 1.5 m deep, at y=6,12,18 and 24, with solid parapets. Link bridges to the slab at y=6+3k, as short concrete decks between x=17 and x=19. The CROWN, y[27,31]: a heavy cantilevered concrete box on top overhanging the shaft by 0.8 m on the front and sides (a wide band of shadowRecess underneath), with a strip window ribbon and a flat roof slab, and a small signWhite emblem plus a red panelRed stripe on the +X face. A rooftop crane or lift motor box, 2 chimney stacks, a lightning rod (thin metalRail box, 1.5 m, no taller than y=31) and aviation lights as small glowing panelRed boxes. Rust streaks under the crown overhang.
parts.attaches: Its -X face meets the slab right gable at towerJoin (x=18). Its link decks align with the slab storey levels y=6+3k. Its crown base at towerCrownBase is y=27, flush with the slab roof level.

parts.builds: Everything on the slab roof, y[27,31], x[-32,18], z[-9,9]. A continuous concrete parapet 1.2 m high (y 27 to 28.2) around the slab, set at z=±7.5 and x=-32 and 18, with a thin coping slab in concreteLight, board-marking, rain stains and scuppers (shadowRecess boxes) every 5 m with long vertical stains below. A flat roof deck in concreteMid with expansion joint lines. A vaulted concrete pavilion (a half-cylinder or arch-shaped barrel roof about 12 m long, 5 m wide, 3.5 m high) at x[-20,-8], with glazed end walls (glass and frameDark, glassLit inside) and chunky piers. A rectangular plant room with louvres at x[0,10], z[-4,4], 2.6 m high, and a water tank (a drum of metalRail with stair ladder and rust bands). 5 ventilation stacks of various heights, up to y=31, in concreteDark with cap slabs. A row of skylights, small pyramids or boxes in glass. A running track or sundeck ellipse is not needed. Add low wall benches, a few planters with plantGreen shrubs along the parapet, and a flagpole no taller than y=31. Rust and moss patches on the roof deck.
parts.attaches: Stands on the slab roof at slabRoofTop (y=27). Its parapet follows the outer edge of the front facade top slab (z=11 is not covered, so the parapet stays at z≤7.5, or overhangs to z=11 only as a thin coping slab) and the back gallery top. Roof deck reference at roofDeck.

calls.reasoning:
I'm sketching out the spec for a static brutalist housing block, no joints, thinking through realistic dimensions like a multi-storey slab around 20-24m tall and 56-60m long, with a pilotis base.

Now I'm working out the orientation so the long facade faces +Z, landing on a size roughly [64, 31, 22], with a body raised on chunky piloti up to about 6m, seven storeys of slab above, and a roof terrace with plant equipment. I'm also placing a taller stair/lift tower at one end of the block to break up the massing.

Breaking the design into five parts, starting with the pilotis and ground level: tapered board-marked concrete columns, entrance lobbies, canopy, ramp, and steps forming a plinth beneath the main slab.

Next I'm planning the slab itself, splitting it into a solid structural core (concrete mass, end gables, floor plates, and rear facade) separate from the front facade's loggia grid, balconies, brise-soleil, and windows, sharing mounting points between the front and back facade planes for alignment.

Splitting the gable ends between front and back halves feels awkward, so I'm reconsidering the division: instead, let the slab core part own the entire volume including floor plates, end walls, and party-wall fins, while the front facade part owns everything attached beyond z>9.5 like balconies, brise-soleil, and window assemblies.

That gives six parts total (slab core, front, back, ground, tower, roof), with a combined budget of 900 split across them. I'm planning the concrete detailing for richness—board-marked bands, slab edges, expansion joints, stair slit windows, murals, tie-rod holes, stains—and sketching the concrete color palette with light and mid tones.

Rounding out the palette now with warm concrete, board-mark, stain, moss, rust, shadow recess, glass (plain and lit with a warm glow), dark frames, and accent panel colors (red, ochre, blue-grey, white), plus metal railing, timber, soil/plant greens, and signage white—capping it at 24 total colors for the loggia and accent details.

Now I'm working out the building's mounting coordinates—front and back slab faces, the pilotis top level, roof slab, gable end extent, and tower join point—along with storey heights of 3 meters stacked from a base of 6, and laying out the front facade into bay divisions roughly 5 meters wide spanning the 50-meter width.

I'm separating the core structure from the loggia system: the core's front wall sits recessed, while the loggia floor slabs and party-wall fins project forward to form balconies, with brise-soleil frames extending even further out as sun-shading elements.

For the back facade, I'm placing stair towers with slit windows and continuous access galleries at every storey, each with solid parapets, projecting back from the main wall plane to give depth and rhythm to the rear elevation.

For the side tower, I'm working out a blank concrete shaft with lift slits and cantilevered vertical windows, topped with an overhanging boxy crown, then reconciling its width against the slab core so the join at x=18 lines up cleanly, with the tower rising to the full building height of 31 while the roof pavilion and chimneys cap out just below that.

For the ground floor, I'm planning the piloti grid beneath the slab, with tapered columns spaced roughly every 10 meters in two rows flanking the center, plus a recessed glass lobby box, entrance canopy, ramp, steps, and small site furnishings like bike storage and planters, all sitting on a low podium slab that meets the core's underside at y=6.

I'm deciding the core owns the slab itself while the ground floor owns the transfer beams running up to that same datum, and I'm planning simple flat-colored materials throughout with no joints or bones needed since everything builds as static boxes. For details, I'll add board-marked concrete texture as thin proud strips and small dark discs for tie-rod holes, keeping everything at real-world meter scale with low geometry segment counts.

Now I'm working out the actual bounding boxes for each structural volume — the slab core, front and back facades, ground floor, and tower — figuring out how the tower's crown cantilever and end gable should align with the core's end wall so nothing clips or leaves gaps where they meet at x=18.

For the roof I'm setting its box to span from the core's top down to where the tower begins, keeping chimneys rising above the parapet, then dividing a budget of 900 total across the six elements (core, front, back, ground, tower, roof) so each gets a proportional share. I'm also sketching the layout grid — ten 5m bays along x and seven 3m storeys along y — to place loggia units per bay per floor.

I'm defining each storey's loggia as 5m wide and 3m tall, framed by thick concrete party-wall fins at every bay line and floor/ceiling slabs at each storey height, creating an eggcrate pattern of open loggias roughly 4.65 by 2.65 meters with 3.5m depth, with painted back walls set slightly forward as part of the front facade.

Now I'm adding glazing sliding doors on the core wall, plain concrete behind, and varying the loggias with coloured panels in a rotating palette, balcony railings, planters, lit windows, and laundry details for variety. For the back facade I'm setting up galleries at each storey level with parapets, doors, windows, and doormats per bay, plus placing stair towers at several x-positions along the building.

subject: brutalistBlock
pitch:
Category: Architecture.
Subject: brutalist housing block.
Style: raw concrete brutalism.

spec.name: Brutalist Housing Block
spec.description: A raw board-marked concrete slab housing block with deep balconies, a stair and lift tower, pilotis, and a roof terrace with plant.
spec.layout: A long slab running along x, 24 m wide, 9 m deep, 16 m tall, facing +Z. Ground floor is open pilotis: chunky tapered concrete columns on a 4 m grid with a recessed glazed lobby. Above sit 4 storeys of maisonette boxes. The front facade is a deep egg-crate grid of projecting concrete balcony boxes, 6 bays by 4 floors, each with a parapet, an inset dark window and a coloured infill panel in a few bays (ochre, rust, teal) so it reads as a stacked grid with shadow depth. A taller separate stair and lift tower stands at the left end (+X) rising above the roof, joined by short bridges at each floor. Roof carries a terrace parapet, a lift overrun box, ribbed ventilation stacks and a water tank on legs. Everything is raw concrete in three tones (light, mid, stained), with board-marked horizontal ribs as thin small parts, rain stains as dark vertical streaks below sills, and dark window glass. The back (-Z) is a simpler facade with access deck walkways and rails and stair slits.

parts.builds: Ground level: a thin concrete plinth/podium slab, 18 tapered concrete piloti columns on a 4 m grid in two rows with board-mark ribs and dark stained bases, recessed glazed lobby with door frames and glowing lit panes, a cantilever entrance canopy, a few steps, and the thick soffit slab (transfer slab) at the top at y=4 with beam ribs underneath.
parts.attaches: Top face meets slabBlock at pilotisTop (y=4). Tower stands beside it at towerBase.

parts.builds: The main housing slab core from y=4 to y=16 and its front: the main concrete box (mid grey) with the egg-crate grid of 6 bays by 4 floors of projecting balcony boxes (light concrete frames with thick sides, floors, parapets), dark glass windows with mullions, and a handful of coloured infill panels in ochre, rust and teal, board-marked rib strips, drip grooves and rain stain streaks under sills, a few lit windows.
parts.attaches: Sits on pilotisTop; front plane at frontFacadePlane; roof starts at roofDeck; tower joined via bridgeLevel1.

parts.builds: Rear facade at z -4.5 to -5.5: continuous access deck walkways on each floor with concrete parapets and steel rail posts, door recesses with small windows and numbers-like small plaques, stair slit windows, plus the two gable end walls with narrow vertical window slots, board marks and stain streaks.
parts.attaches: Attaches to the back of the main box at backFacadePlane and meets the tower via the walkway ends at bridgeLevel1.

parts.builds: Separate tall tower at the +X end, 3.5 m wide x 4 m deep x 17.5 m tall, in darker concrete with vertical slit windows stacked on the stair, a cantilever top cap with chamfered edge, board-mark ribs, diagonal stair flight silhouettes seen as small dark slanted slabs in slits, concrete bridges at each floor connecting to the slab at bridgeLevel1, base buttress, lit slit lights, and a small roof lift overrun on top.
parts.attaches: Stands on the floor at towerBase and bridges meet the main block at bridgeLevel1.

parts.builds: Roof at y=16 to 17.5: thick parapet with coping and board marks, a recessed terrace area with moss patches, lift overrun box, 3 ribbed ventilation stacks with caps, water tank on stilts with banded ring ribs and ladder, aerial masts, skylight blisters and roof access hatch, stained parapet drips.
parts.attaches: Rests on roofDeck at y=16 above the main slab.

Positioning the door and merging the handle into the rail geometry, then laying out horizontal wall ribs across each bay at intervals between the window top and ceiling for the lower floors.

Tallying up the triangle budget across the merged parts, stains, and ribs to make sure it stays near 5000 total. I'm also planning which bays get moss coping and starting to size the rain pipes with a cylinder geometry for the gutters.

spec.name: Brutalist Housing Block
spec.description: A slab-style raw concrete housing block with a stepped, cantilevered facade of deep balconies, a pilotis podium, a stair and lift core tower, and a roof terrace with plant.
spec.layout: A long east-west slab, about 30 m wide (x) and 12 m deep (z), 22 m high, standing on y = 0. The ground level is an open pilotis podium of chunky board-marked concrete columns with a recessed glazed lobby. Above it, five residential storeys of 3 m each, with deep egg-crate balcony boxes on the front (+Z) facade, staggered so the silhouette reads as stepped. A taller windowless stair and lift core tower rises at the left end (+X) to 22 m with slit windows. The roof carries a plant room box, a parapet and chimney-like vents. Every surface is flat grey concrete in a few tones, with darker recessed window and balcony voids, thin board-marked seams as small dark strips, rusty steel rails, and a few warm lit windows. No ground, trees or props beyond the block.

parts.builds: Ground level pilotis: 14 chunky square concrete columns in two rows with board-marked seam strips, a thick transfer slab on top (podiumTop), a recessed glazed lobby with a red door, a concrete canopy, entrance steps and a ramp in lighter slab colour, and stained dark bands at column feet.
parts.attaches: Top face at podiumTop supports the residential slab; the core base at coreBase stands beside the podium and shares its x edge.

parts.builds: The main residential volume from y 4.5 to 19.5: a concrete box 24 m wide, 8 m deep, five storeys with dark void window bands, glass panes, scattered warm lit windows, horizontal floor-edge seams, vertical board-marked seam strips, a back facade with small windows and access-deck walkways with rust railings, and end walls with weathering stains.
parts.attaches: Sits on podiumTop. Its front face slabFrontFace receives the balconies. Its right end meets the core tower. Roof at roofDeck.

parts.builds: The egg-crate front facade: staggered deep concrete balcony boxes projecting from z 4 to 6 on the slab front, each with a dark inner void, a thick concrete frame, a rust steel rail, a slab floor, and occasional potted moss plants, plus fins between bays and a deeper cantilevered block at the top two storeys giving a stepped profile.
parts.attaches: Back sits flush on slabFrontFace; the lowest row starts at podiumTop.

parts.builds: The stair and lift tower: a tall 8 by 10 m windowless concrete shaft from the floor to 22 m at coreBase, with narrow vertical slit windows glowing warmly, board-marked seams, a heavy overhanging cap slab at coreRoof, a projecting vertical stair fin, bridge walkways linking to the slab, a rust steel door at ground, and dark stain streaks.
parts.attaches: Stands at coreBase beside the podium and slab; the walkway bridges touch the slab end at x 10.

parts.builds: Roof terrace at roofDeck: thick parapet ring, a plant room box with louvres and a steel door, three chunky ventilation chimneys, water tank cylinder on legs, skylight boxes, rust ladders, moss patches, and drainage spouts jutting from the parapet.
parts.attaches: Rests on top of slabBody at roofDeck; adjacent to the core cap at coreRoof.

spec.name: Calder Mobile
spec.description: A hanging abstract mobile in the manner of Alexander Calder: a ceiling hook and black wires carrying balanced arms, with flat red, yellow, blue, white and black sheet-metal shapes hung in a cascade that reaches down to the floor.
spec.layout: STATIC model (joints: []), centred on x = 0, standing on y = 0. It hangs from one ceiling hook at the top, y = 2.78. A thin black wire runs down to the top arm (A). Below it the mobile splits into a right (+X) cascade and a left (-X) cascade, and the right cascade ends in a low tier whose biggest black leaf just touches y = 0. Arms are thin black tapered rods in the horizontal plane at the stated y. Their yaws differ (A along X, B and D diagonal, C along X, E and F along Z), so the mobile reads as 3D from every side. Every hanging element uses one convention: a straight vertical black wire (radius 0.004, 5 sides) runs from a small black wire loop (torus, tube 0.006, radius 0.02) on the arm end down to a small eyelet ring on the top point of the shape. Shapes are flat sheet-metal cutouts (extrude, thickness 0.012, tiny bevel) in a vertical plane. The plane's normal is the local +Z turned by the stated yaw about Y, and the shape hangs so its top eyelet is directly under the wire. Every shape also gets a darker twin of its colour, 4% larger and 0.006 thick, seated just behind its back face, which reads as a painted edge. A few shapes get a small contrasting inset dot or ring as a separate part (Calder's cut-out accents). All balanced pivots are marked by 3 tiny coil rings (torus) wrapped on the arm at the pivot, plus a tiny black ball of radius 0.025 on each arm tip beyond the loop. Style: bold primary colours (red, yellow, blue) with white and black, flat, thin, airy and sparse; wires are the structure and the shapes are the weight. Nothing sits on the floor but the lowest leaf tip. No ground, no stand, no extras.

parts.builds: Top of the mobile. A small round ceiling plate (plate colour, r 0.07, thick 0.015, centred y 2.81, seated at the ceilingHook) with a steel S-hook or ring under it. A black wire (r 0.005) from ceilingHook straight down to topPivot. Arm A: a tapered black rod along X from topEndL to topEndR at y 2.4, radius 0.012 tapering to 0.007 at each end, with a loop torus at each end and a tiny black ball past each tip. Three coil rings and a small steel clamp collar at topPivot where the wire joins. One small hanging yellow leaf (length 0.28, width 0.14, leaf or lens outline, yaw 40 degrees) on a 0.12 long wire from midHangA. Its eyelet is at [0.3,2.28,0], so the centre is at about [0.3,2.14,0]. Give it a yellowDark twin and a small white inset dot. Does NOT build the wires below topEndL or topEndR; those belong to the child parts, which attach to the loops here.
parts.attaches: Arm ends topEndL and topEndR carry loops where the leftCascade and rightCascade wires hang. The ceilingHook is the model's top.

parts.builds: Middle right (+X) tier. Wire from topEndR down to rightPivot. Arm B: a tapered black rod from rightEndBack to rightEndFront at y 1.8 (diagonal in XZ), with coil rings at rightPivot and a loop and tip ball at each end. Big red disc (radius 0.2) with a redDark twin, hung from rightEndFront by a 0.32 wire, centre [1.3,1.28,0.5], yaw 25 degrees. It has a small white ring and a small ink dot on its face as inset accents. Wire from rightEndBack down to rightPivot2. Arm C: a tapered black rod along X from cLeft to cRight at y 1.3, coil rings at rightPivot2, loops and tip balls at both ends. A yellow leaf (length 0.4, width 0.22, pointed leaf outline, yaw -35 degrees) hung from cLeft by a 0.15 wire, eyelet [0.15,1.15,-0.4], centre about [0.15,0.95,-0.4], with a yellowDark twin and a thin ink midrib line as a part. A small blue disc (r 0.09, blueDark twin, yaw 0) hung from cBlueHang by a 0.22 wire, centre about [0.92,0.97,-0.4]. Does NOT build the wire from cRight downward (the lowTier owns it); it only builds the loop at cRight.
parts.attaches: Hangs from topEndR (crown). The loop at cRight carries the wire of the lowTier.

parts.builds: Lowest tier, below cRight. A black wire from cRight straight down to lowPivot. Arm F: a tapered black rod along Z from fBack to fFront at y 0.85, with three coil rings at lowPivot, loops and tip balls at the ends. The big black leaf hangs from fFront on a 0.15 wire. It is a tall elegant leaf or blade outline 0.7 tall and 0.3 wide, yaw 60 degrees, eyelet at [1.2,0.70,0.25], centre [1.2,0.35,0.25]. Its lowest tip is at y = 0.0, the lowest point of the whole model. Colour ink with a wire-colour twin behind, plus a white midrib line and 3 small white dots as inset accents. A blue disc (radius 0.14, blueDark twin, yaw 0) hangs from fBack on a 0.25 wire, centre [1.2,0.46,-1.05], with a white ring inset and a small red dot at its centre. Add a small red ball of radius 0.05 on a 0.3 wire hung from lowPivot-adjacent point [1.2,0.85,-0.12] on arm F, so it hangs between the two large shapes.
parts.attaches: Wire top at cRight (rightCascade loop). Nothing else attaches below.

parts.builds: Upper left (-X) tier. Wire from topEndL down to leftPivot (a 0.5 black wire). Arm D: a tapered black rod diagonal in XZ from leftEndA to leftEndB at y 1.9, with coil rings and a steel collar at leftPivot, and loops and tip balls at both ends. A large yellow disc (radius 0.22, yellowDark twin, yaw -20 degrees) hung from leftEndB by a 0.3 wire, centre [-0.2,1.38,-0.45]. It has a black concentric ring inset (outer r 0.12, inner r 0.1) and a black centre dot of r 0.03 as separate parts. A small white ball (radius 0.05) hung from the arm at [-0.45,1.9,-0.225] by a 0.2 wire, centre y 1.65. Also a thin curly black wire spiral (a flat swept spiral of 1.5 turns, radius 0.05, 0.003 thick) hanging 0.2 below leftEndA is NOT built; leftLower owns that wire. Builds only the loop at leftEndA.
parts.attaches: Hangs from topEndL (crown). The loop at leftEndA carries the wire of the leftLower tier.

parts.builds: Lower left (-X) tier. A black wire from leftEndA down to leftSub (0.55 long). Arm E: a tapered black rod along Z from eBack to eFront at y 1.35, with coil rings and a steel collar at leftSub and loops and tip balls at the ends. A red kidney or crescent leaf (length 0.36, width 0.2, redDark twin, yaw 70 degrees) hung from eFront by a 0.15 wire, eyelet [-1.2,1.2,0.85], centre about [-1.2,1.02,0.85], with 2 small white dots inset. A black fish or teardrop leaf (length 0.5, width 0.22, wire-colour twin, yaw -50 degrees) hung from eBack by a 0.3 wire, eyelet [-1.2,1.05,-0.15], centre about [-1.2,0.8,-0.15], with a thin white midrib line and a small yellow dot. A small white disc (r 0.07, yaw 90) on a thin 0.15 wire hung from the arm at [-1.2,1.35,0.2]. A coiled spring: a thin black wire spiral (3 turns, radius 0.035, tube 0.003) hanging down from leftSub, 0.2 long, ending in a small blue ball r 0.04.
parts.attaches: Wire top at leftEndA (leftUpper loop).

spec.name: Calder Hanging Mobile
spec.description: A Calder-style hanging mobile: black wire arms nested five tiers deep, balanced on solder knots, carrying flat painted sheet-metal discs and leaves in red, blue, yellow, black and white.
spec.layout: The mobile hangs from a ceiling canopy at the very top (y=2.4); its lowest shape bottoms out near y=0.25 and nothing rests on the floor. The main arm A (a thin black wire, about 1.7 m long) sits at y=1.95 and hangs off a single wire from the ceiling hook at x=0. It has a long arm to +X (the model's left) and a short one to -X, yawed about 12 degrees in plan, so the whole mobile reads as a 3D drifting composition and not a flat drawing. From the +X end of A, a wire drops to the pivot of arm B (y=1.4, yawed about -30 degrees). Arm B carries a big red disc on its +X end (the anchor shape, radius 0.28, hanging furthest right) and, on its -X end, a wire dropping to arm D (y=1.0, yawed about 20 degrees). Arm D carries a black leaf (tall, narrow, 0.48 high) on its -X end and a smaller yellow disc on its +X end. From the -X end of A, a wire drops to the pivot of long arm C (y=1.2, yawed about 25 degrees, reaching to x=-1.5). Arm C carries a big blue leaf or kidney shape on its far -X end and, on its short +X end, a wire dropping to arm E (y=0.85, yawed about -20 degrees). Arm E carries a small white disc with a black ring on its -X end and a black teardrop (the lowest element, bottom at y=0.25) on its +X end. Lengths of the wire drops are varied: some short, some long. Style: Alexander Calder. Every arm and drop is a thin dark wire (radius 0.005 to 0.008) with small bent hook loops (tiny torus rings) at the ends and brass solder knots (tiny spheres) at each pivot and joint. Every shape is a flat, thin cut-metal plate (extrude thickness about 0.012 to 0.018, with a small bevel). Each plate has a slightly bigger, darker 'deep' plate behind it, offset 0.004, so the edge reads as a painted rim. The shapes are matte flat primary colours. Small details are separate parts seated on the plates: a white dot row on the red disc, a black quarter-circle cut-out on the yellow disc, a thin white stripe on the blue leaf, a white centre dot on the black leaf, a black ring on the white disc, and a red bead on arm E. Shapes hang in different orientations: yaw them 20 to 70 degrees around the vertical so no two face the same way, and tilt each a few degrees. Plates have bold, simple outlines: a circle, a leaf, a kidney, a teardrop. Use only palette colours.

parts.builds: The top of the mobile. A thin round ceiling canopy (a lathe or flat cylinder in ceiling with a ceilingEdge rim ring and a small screw head), a wire hook eye (torus in wire) at hookEye, and the suspension wire down to the armA pivot with a solder knot. Main arm A: a long thin wire rod from armAEndL to armAEndR through armAPivot, with a hook loop ring at each end, a solder collar at the pivot, and a small black bead counterweight near the short end. Two hanging wires with hook loops at both ends: one from armAEndR down to pivotB, one from armAEndL down to pivotC. Wire is in wire, with a few thin wireHighlight rods alongside for gleam. Brass solder blobs at every knot. No shapes hang here.
parts.attaches: The wire to pivotB ends at the loop on arm B (branchB); the wire to pivotC ends at the loop on arm C (branchC). The arm A joint is armA; the canopy and hook ride mobile.

parts.builds: Arm B: a wire rod from armBEnd1 to armBEnd2 through pivotB, with a loop at pivotB to take the wire from crown, hook loops at both ends and a solder knot. At armBEnd2 a drop wire with hook loops goes down to redDiscTop, carrying the big red disc: a circle of radius 0.28 and thickness 0.015, yawed about 50 degrees, with a redDeep plate behind it (radius 0.285, offset 0.004), a ring of small white dots (about 10) near the rim, and a black quarter-circle cut-out wedge (flat sheet in black) near the centre. At armBEnd1 a drop wire with hook loops goes down to the pivotD loop, where arm D (branchD) takes over. The red disc rides redDisc and the arm rides armB.
parts.attaches: pivotB is where crown's wire ends. The wire to pivotD ends at the loop at the top of arm D. The disc is hooked at redDiscTop.

parts.builds: Arm D: a short wire rod from armDEnd1 to armDEnd2 through pivotD, with a loop at the pivot to take the wire from branchB, hook loops and solder knots. At armDEnd1 a drop wire down to leafBlackTop holds a black leaf plate (tall pointed ellipse, 0.48 high, 0.2 wide, thickness 0.014, yawed 70 degrees) with a blackDeep plate behind it, a white centre dot, and a thin white midrib line. At armDEnd2 a drop wire down to discYellowTop holds a yellow disc (radius 0.15, yawed -30 degrees, tilted slightly) with a yellowDeep plate behind it, a black quarter-circle cut-out wedge and a tiny black dot. Leaf rides leafBlack, disc rides discYellow, arm rides armD.
parts.attaches: pivotD is where branchB's wire ends. Shapes hook at leafBlackTop and discYellowTop.

parts.builds: Arm C: the longest lower arm, a wire rod from armCEnd1 (far -X) to armCEnd2 through pivotC, with a loop at the pivot to take the wire from crown, hook loops and solder knots at the pivot and both ends. Bottom to top: red-soled white sneakers on the floor (y 0 to 0.075), jeans legs, cardboard shin boxes (y 0.10 to 0.40, x 0.10 +/- 0.075, z +/- 0.085, wider than the legs inside), blue shirt hem and jeans waist (y 0.36 to 0.46), the torso box (y 0.42 to 0.90, x +/- 0.26, z -0.16 to 0.18), the head box (y 0.90 to 1.36, x +/- 0.22, z -0.18 to 0.20) and two spring antennas (up to y 1.56). The head box has a rectangular face window in front (x +/- 0.13, y 0.97 to 1.20, z 0.20). The kid's round cartoon head sits inside it (centre [0,1.08,0.04], radius 0.12), recessed 4 cm behind the window, so the face reads from the front: big eyes, brows, small nose, a wide grin with a separate lower jaw. The arms go out sideways in a T-pose at y 0.80, passing through torn holes in the torso sides (x +/- 0.26). Visible parts of each arm: blue shirt-sleeve elbow, red glove. Over the upper arm (x 0.27 to 0.43) and forearm (x 0.50 to 0.68) sit foil-wrapped cardboard tubes with tape rings. Between them the blue sleeve shows at the elbow (x 0.43 to 0.50). Red gloves start at the wrist (x 0.68) with separate fingers and thumb, palms down, thumb toward +Z, fingertips at x +/- 0.85. Legs stand shoulder-width apart (x +/- 0.10), straight, toes forward. The style is cardboard craft. Every box is a plain tan cuboid with chunky, visibly thick edges (about 1 cm slabs), cut flaps, torn edges and darker corrugation-rib strips along the cut edges. Silver tape strips cross the corners and seams. Hand-drawn marker details (black outlines, red and blue scribbles) are thin dark and coloured plates seated about 2 mm proud of the cardboard. Bottle caps (yellow, green) are buttons, white glue blobs sit at joins, and foil is crinkled with faceted flat-shaded facets in two greys. Colours are flat per part, warm tan on top faces and darker tan below. The kid parts are soft chunky shapes (round-ish, sphere/capsule based) that contrast with the hard box costume.

parts.builds: The kid's head and neck, seen through the box's face window. Chunky cartoon head (rounded boxy skull sphere, radius ~0.12, centre [0,1.08,0.04], skin). Neck cylinder from y 0.88 to 0.97 (skin) with a blue shirt collar ring (shirt) around its base. Face: two big eyes (white sclera, brown iris, tiny white highlight, thin dark marker-colour upper lid line) at x +/-0.045, y 1.10, front z about 0.15. Thick eyebrows (hair colour) angled up for a happy look. Small round nose (skin, slightly pinker via cheek) and round cheek blush discs (cheek) at x +/-0.075, y 1.04. Mouth: upper jaw is part of the head (lips-colour upper lip arc, row of white upper teeth); the lower jaw is a separate piece on the `jaw` joint (skin chin block, lips lower lip, white lower teeth, pink-red tongue in lips colour) forming a wide open-ish grin. Ears (skin, with cheek inner disc) at x +/-0.12. Hair (hair colour): a solid cap over the top and back of the head plus a modest number of overlapping broad blades for tousled bangs over the forehead and a cowlick, built big and clear; hair shows through the top of the window. Keep every feature behind z 0.185 so nothing pokes through the window plane at z 0.20.
parts.attaches: Neck base on mount neckBase (the neck rides joint neck, the skull and hair ride head, lower jaw rides jaw, hinge at jawHinge). Sits inside the headBox, whose window is at faceWindow; the neck passes down into the torsoBox top at torsoTop.

parts.builds: Every visible part of the kid except head and neck. Pelvis and lower torso: blue shirt hem block and a jeans waistband visible below the torso box (y 0.36 to 0.46) and a stub of shirt chest inside the box top (hidden). Legs: chunky jeans (jeans colour) capsules or sweeps on the chains hipL/kneeL/ankleL and hipR/kneeR/ankleR, radius ~0.05 thigh to 0.04 ankle, with small patch pockets, seam stitching strips and rolled cuffs. White sneakers on the toe/ankle joints (x +/-0.10, y 0 to 0.075, z -0.05 to 0.17): sneaker body, rounded toe cap, red sole slab (sole), laces as small crossing strips and a tongue, heel tab. Arms: blue shirt-sleeve tubes (shirt) on shoulder/elbow/wrist chains along y 0.80 from x +/-0.20 to +/-0.70, radius ~0.04, with soft cuffs at the wrists. Hands: red gloves (glove) from x +/-0.68, palm block about 0.10 wide in z and 0.06 along x, palm down, separate finger capsules on every digit joint (thumbL1/2, indexL1/2, middleL1/2, ringL1/2, pinkyL1/2 and the R mirror) so fingers and thumb are separated and extended, with a lighter white cuff band and a small marker-colour star or dot on the back of each glove. Mirror left/right exactly.
parts.attaches: Rides hips, spine, chest, shoulder/elbow/wrist/hand and digit joints, hip/knee/ankle/toe joints. Arms pass through the torso box side holes at shoulderHoleL/R and are covered by the limbSleeves tubes between upperArmTube and forearmTube mounts. Legs go through the shin boxes at shinBoxTop/Bottom mounts. Shoes sit on y=0.

parts.builds: The body of the costume: a large cardboard box (cardTan) x +/-0.26, y 0.42 to 0.90, z -0.16 to 0.18, built as thick wall slabs with visible edge thickness and darker corrugation-rib strips (cardDark) along cut edges. Open bottom hem and top with the head box sitting on the top face. Folded-over top flaps (cardLight inner faces, cardDark outer) around the neck opening. Side walls have rough torn round arm holes at shoulderHoleL/R (cardInside dark ring with jagged torn tabs) that the arms pass through. Front chest control panel at chestPanel: a lighter cardboard rectangle plate glued on (cardLight) with a marker outline (marker), a rectangular drawn screen (screenCyan plate, glowing, with marker zig-zag waveform and a small smiley), three big dial knobs (bottle caps: capYellow, capGreen, markerRed with marker tick lines), a row of 4 push-buttons, a toggle switch row (small rods with caps), two scribbled vent grilles (parallel marker bars), a kid-lettered 'ROBO' (blocky letter plates in markerBlue) and a name tag sticker (white plate with marker scribble). Silver tape strips (tapeSilver) cross all four vertical corners and a diagonal across one chest corner, with glue blobs (white). Back at backPanel: a small cardboard jetpack box with two foil tubes (foil/foilShade, faceted) and a red tape stripe, plus a hand-drawn gear. Belt at beltLine y 0.42 to 0.46: cardTan strip band around the box bottom with a big capYellow bottle-cap buckle and marker stitches. Nothing sticks out past z +0.26 front or z -0.26 back.
parts.attaches: Rides joint chest. Bottom edge at torsoBottom/beltLine, top face at torsoTop where headBox sits and kid neck enters. Arm holes at shoulderHoleL/R (x +/-0.26, y 0.8).

parts.builds: The robot head: a cardboard box x +/-0.22, y 0.90 to 1.36, z -0.18 to 0.20 (cardTan, thick wall slabs with cardDark corrugation ribs on edges). The front wall is built from four slabs around a rectangular face window (x +/-0.13, y 0.97 to 1.20, z 0.20) so the kid's face is visible, with a cut-edge frame in cardInside lining the opening, a hand-painted marker rim (marker, thin plates) around it and little yellow-marker lightning rivets in the corners. Tape strips (tapeSilver) over the top corners and a torn flap on the window top edge. Top face: folded-open flaps (cardLight inner, cardDark outer) on top and a silver tape cross. Two spring antennas at antennaBaseL/R (thin coil sweeps in foilShade, about 0.12 tall, tilted slightly outward) each ending in a bottle-cap or foil-ball tip (capYellow and markerRed), one at x +0.10 and one at x -0.10, topping out about y 1.56. Ear tubes at earTubeL/R: cardboard rolls (cardDark/cardLight rings) sticking out of each side wall to x +/-0.30, with foil end discs and a marker spiral. Front above the window: drawn eyebrow marker bars (marker) and two small round 'eye lights' (capGreen caps) as decoration, a mouth-grille of marker lines on the chin strip beneath the window (y 0.91 to 0.96). Sides and back have marker-drawn bolts, an arrow decal and a gear doodle. Glue blobs (white) at the seams.
parts.attaches: Rides joint head. Rests on torsoBox top at torsoTop (y 0.90). Face window centre at faceWindow around the kid's face from kidHead; keep the window opening empty.

parts.builds: Costume tubes and boxes on the kid's limbs, mirrored left/right. Arms: foil-wrapped cardboard tubes (foil with foilShade faceted creases as strips) as sweeps or rods around the sleeve, upper arm tube from x +/-0.27 to +/-0.43 (radius ~0.065) at upperArmTube and forearm tube from x +/-0.50 to +/-0.68 (radius ~0.06) at forearmTube, each with raised tapeSilver rings at both ends, a markerRed stripe, a few capYellow rivets/caps and glue blobs, torn cardboard edge cuffs (cardTan) at the wrist end and a cardDark inner ring. Between the tubes (x 0.43 to 0.50) only the kid's blue sleeve shows, with a small cardboard elbow guard disc (cardLight) beside it. The pieces ride shoulder/elbow joints appropriately (upper tube on shoulder joint, forearm tube on elbow joint). Legs: cardboard shin boxes (cardTan, thick wall slabs, open top and bottom, x 0.10 +/-0.075, z +/-0.085, y 0.10 to 0.40) on each leg, with cardDark corrugation ribs on the vertical edges, silver tape wraps on top and bottom, a folded flap collar at the top (cardLight inner), a marker-drawn arrow or lightning bolt on the front (markerBlue and marker), a capGreen bottle-cap 'knee light' on the front, and a foil-wrapped kneecap strip with tape ring at kneeL/R. Shin boxes ride kneeL/kneeR joints. Keep box bottoms at y 0.10 so shoes stay visible.
parts.attaches: Arm tubes wrap the arm sleeves at upperArmTubeL/R and forearmTubeL/R and start outside the torso hole at shoulderHoleL/R; they end at the wristL/R mounts where gloves begin. Shin boxes wrap the jeans between shinBoxBottom and shinBoxTop mounts around kneeL/R.

calls.reasoning:
I'm picturing a kid around 1.2 meters tall in a cardboard-box robot costume: a box torso, boxy helmet head, tube-like arms and legs, all styled with corrugated brown cardboard textures, foil accents, and duct tape details for that handmade craft look.

Now I'm working out the exact proportions -- deciding whether the kid's face peeks through a cut-out window in the head box or sits beneath it, then pinning down coordinates for feet, knees, hips, shoulders, and head box placement so the torso and helmet boxes line up naturally over the child's body.

I'm also mapping out the arms as cardboard-tube sleeves over the kid's real arms, held in a T-pose with gloved hands, and sketching hip-to-leg placement for the lower body.

Now sizing the whole costume: legs get box sleeves on the shins, overall width stretches to cover extended arms, and I'm adding an antenna with springs and bottle caps on top of the head, bringing total size to roughly [1.5, 1.55, 0.52] once depth from torso, feet, and chest panel details are accounted for. Then I start breaking the model into parts, starting with the kid's head and face.

Now I'm thinking through the humanoid rig and how to divide the costume into manageable groups — separating the kid's head/face/hair/jaw/neck from the limbs (pants, shoes, hands/fingers), and grouping the torso as its own box piece with the control panel, buttons, dials, tape, and straps.

I also want a headBox group for the box helmet with face window, antennas, ear bolts, and visor, plus a limbCostume group covering the cardboard/foil arm tubes, shin boxes, elbow joints, and bracers. For joints, I'm planning shoulder-elbow-wrist chains per arm with hand/finger digit joints for the mitten thumbs.

Settling on 5 digits per hand with 2 joints each, 10 joints per hand, 20 total, and starting to lay out the full joint hierarchy from hips up through spine, chest, neck, and head with positions and directions for a T-pose rig.

Now I'm figuring out the jaw hinge placement relative to the head geometry, checking that the head box dimensions and the kid's head sphere radius line up proportionally.

I'm adjusting the face window so it sits flush with the forward position of the kid's head, shifting the head center and box depth so the face isn't recessed oddly inside the box, then aligning the torso box top edge with the head box bottom so the neck fits naturally between them.

Now I'm placing the arm holes and shoulder joints at the torso box edges, roughing out shoulder-elbow-wrist positions for a stylized chunky arm proportion matching the kid's overall scale.

Deciding the kid wears a long-sleeve shirt rather than bare arms. Now I'm building the leg joint chains: hip, knee, ankle, and toe for each leg, positioning them down to the floor with shoe height accounted for and assigning parent-child relationships and leg roles to each joint.

For the geometry, I'm sketching shin boxes around the legs and shoe boxes around the ankles, sizing them so shoes touch the floor while shins stay above it, and checking the overall depth of the figure from head to the front of the shoes.

Now I'm working on the head and face: eyes, brows, nose, mouth, jaw as a separate piece for expressions, ears, cheeks, hair tucked under the head box but peeking through the window, plus an antenna with a spring and ball cap sitting on top, finalizing overall height around 1.55.

Then I'm setting up the skeleton hierarchy - neck and head joints, a hips-spine-chest chain for the torso, with the torso and head boxes riding their respective joints, and defining the arm chain from shoulder through elbow to wrist.

Now I'm extending the chain to the hand tip, with thumb and finger joints positioned for a T-pose with palms down, spacing index through pinky across the palm at different depths.

Total joint count comes to 42, which works. I'll skip rigging the antenna separately since it's rigid on the head, and no flap hinges are needed either. For the cardboard craft aesthetic, I'm defining a color palette with tan and dark cardboard tones, corrugation edge stripes, silver tape, duct tape grey, foil highlights, and marker colors for details.

Continuing the palette with button green, a cyan for the marker-drawn screen glow, skin tones with cheek blush, hair colors, blue shirt, jeans, white sneakers with a red sole, red glove, eye and iris colors, pink lips, and glue blob white for craft details.

Now I'm working through the cardboard-robot styling: corrugated ridges, torn and folded box flaps, crisscrossed masking tape, hand-drawn marker knobs, bottle-cap buttons, a bendy straw, a paper clip, and lettered labels like "ROBO" and a "MAX" name tag. Then I start assigning body parts, beginning with the kid's head (skull, face, eyes, hair, jaw) with its joint and bounding box setup, and I'm moving into the limb assignments next.

Now the torso box needs a chest panel with dials, buttons, screen, tape and name tag, plus a cardboard back-pack with foil tubes, with torn arm holes and spine/chest joints — budget 200. Then the head box needs a face window, cut flaps, and an antenna spring.

I'm also adding a hip belt with a bottle cap buckle to the torso box, and sizing the arm tubes to wrap around the kid's arm radius with upper arm and forearm sections spanning specific x ranges, leaving a gap at the wrist for gloves.

Now I'm cataloging all the mount points for the costume pieces: neck base, head center, face window, head box top/bottom, shoulder holes, elbows, wrists, knees, ankles, shin box edges, chest panel, backpack, belt line, and hip points.

For colors, I'm sticking with tan cardboard with lighter flap interiors, and thinking through how the face window should be built as a cutout framed by four strips rather than a solid panel with a hole. Similarly, I'm planning the arm holes in the torso as a solid wall with a dark torn-edge ring flange where the arm tube passes through, keeping construction simple for the builder.

Now I'm settling on a limited 24-color palette covering cardboard tones, tape and foil materials, marker colors, bottle cap colors, and skin and hair tones for the figure.

I'm still paring down the palette, trying to land on exactly 24 colors by cutting redundant shades like hairLight and skinShade while keeping the essentials: cards, tape, marker tones, skin, hair, shirt, jeans, and sneaker colors.

Now I'm checking the part budget totals to stay under the limit, trimming numbers down from 900 to around 860. Then I'm moving on to writing out the joint hierarchy with coordinates for hips, spine, chest, neck, and head.

Placing joint positions...

Now mapping out the kid's head: a chunky blocky skull with big front-facing eyes, ears at the sides, tousled hair blades peeking through the window, small nose, and an open grin with upper/lower jaw teeth. I'm positioning the neck and shirt collar around y 0.88-0.93 attached to the head group, and defining the face window so the kid's face shows through at the right depth.

With the eyebrows settled, I'm ready to write out the final JSON.

I'm planning the buildKidHead function, figuring out how to attach head geometry to the bone joint using model-space positions and defining the head's center and radius.

Now I'm calculating precise positions for facial features — eyes, sclera, iris, and highlight — by computing where each sphere's surface intersects with the skull given their offsets and radii. Then I move on to the jaw and mouth, working out the chin block's dimensions and where the lower jaw bone should sit relative to the skull's bottom curvature.

For the smile, I'm shaping a torus arc rotated 180° to form the lower half of a circle, positioning it so it sits flush against the face surface at the correct z-depth.

I'll build the lips as a chain of small spheres along a curved path computed from head coordinates, connecting them with capsules for a smoother mouth shape.

Now I'm placing upper teeth as small white boxes beneath the lip line, then working out the chin geometry as a sphere positioned to protrude slightly past the skull's natural curve for a chunky jaw look.

Continuing with the lower lip as a capsule chain sitting just below the upper lip, with a gap between them creating an open mouth. For the dark interior I'm defining a custom color and placing a thin plate behind the lips on the head bone, plus a flattened tongue sphere using the lips color.

Now I'm positioning lower teeth as small white boxes on the jaw, confirming the jaw hinge placement works fine since parts just follow the bone. For cheeks I'm working out thin disc geometry oriented along the surface normal, computing the normal vector from center to cheek position and solving for the z-coordinate using the sphere surface equation.

I'm computing the exact cheek position, then adding a helper that lifts points outward along their normal by a small offset to avoid z-fighting with the skull surface. I'm also checking that a low-poly faceted sphere's deviation from the true analytic surface stays small enough that a 4mm lift covers it, settling on 20x14 segments for the skull.

Still working out skull proportions...

Now I'm working out the eyebrow shape, debating whether inner or outer ends should sit higher to read as a gentle happy arch rather than angry, and positioning the brow arc along the head's curved surface near y≈1.14.

I'm realizing a single hair cap angled to cover the whole scalp would also cover down over the eyes, so I need to split it into separate back and front sections with different angular ranges to keep the hairline above the eyebrows while still covering the back and sides.

Placing the hair sphere around the head center with a slight offset, checking it stays within the head bounds. For bangs, I'm considering flattened cone shapes as blades draped over the forehead, oriented to follow the scalp's curve.

Working out the bang placement math: seven blades spaced across the hairline, each with a base point computed from spherical coordinates on the skull, and an apex direction blending a downward tangent with an outward normal so the bangs curve naturally off the forehead.

I'm checking the geometry against eyebrow and eye positions to make sure the bangs land just above the brows without covering the eyes, adjusting the hairline angle and blade lengths until the tips sit around y≈1.16.

I'll add a few extra cone shapes for stray hair tufts and a cowlick spike angled upward near the crown, plus some flatter overlapping cones for the main bangs. For color, I'm planning to keep the palette mostly in the hair tone but add a subtle darker highlight shade for some strands.

Now I'm working out the eyes: white sclera spheres squashed along z, positioned just proud of the head surface near the front, oriented so they face outward along the local normal direction.

Bumping pupil lift to 0.0145 fixes the hidden-pupil issue, and I'm placing a small white highlight sphere offset from center with its own lift so it reads above the iris. Now I'm working out the top eyelid as a thin curved capsule line arcing over the sclera, picking y-coordinates and lift values so it sits proud of the eye's curvature.

I'm outlining the upper eyelid as a thin arc sitting proud of the skin, then dialing back the sclera and iris proportions so the eyes read as cartoonish rather than bulging bug eyes, adjusting lift and scale values for a more natural front profile.

Working through the pupil and highlight placement to ensure the highlight sits just outside the iris surface while the pupil stays recessed slightly behind it, confirming the geometry lines up correctly. Then starting on the nose as a scaled sphere positioned on the head surface.

I'm recalculating the nose dimensions to keep the tip just under the maximum offset limit, settling on a smaller lift and radius so the front point lands around 0.177. I'm also deciding to give the nose tip a slightly pinker tone using the cheek color rather than pure skin color, and skipping nostril details for now before moving on to the mouth.

Now I'm mapping out the mouth geometry—placing corners, computing surface offsets for the smile curve, and planning small dark capsule shapes for corner dimples, then sketching the upper lip curve and teeth box dimensions and positions.

Placing seven teeth under the lip line, orienting each box so its depth aligns with the surface normal, and tuning the lift so teeth sit just proud of the skin while staying tucked behind the lip. Now I'm planning a dark interior plate to fill the gap between upper and lower teeth for mouth depth.

Since the grin was nearly closed, I'm widening the vertical gap to around 0.018 by redefining the upper lip height and recalculating where the teeth centers and bottoms fall relative to it, aiming for a more open, friendly expression.

Now I'm placing the lower teeth as a row of six small rectangles centered beneath the lower lip curve, then checking how the chin surface geometry recedes to make sure the lip sits naturally against the jaw.

Still working through jaw geometry...

Checking the teeth positions against the jaw ellipsoid surface at a few sample points, the values line up reasonably well. For the lip geometry, I'm placing the lower lip chain slightly offset from the jaw surface, lifted along the ellipsoid's approximate surface normal computed from the gradient.

Now I'm sketching the overall structure: a shared surface helper for both skull and jaw ellipsoids, with the skull as a sphere-like shape above and the jaw ellipsoid covering the lower face below the mouth. I'm verifying the seam where the jaw meets the skull at the sides stays consistent in width at the hinge point.

For the dark interior mouth plate, I'm positioning it just in front of the skin surface so it's visible through the gap between jaw and skull, checking the surface heights at the relevant y-coordinates to get the lift value right.

That's not quite working either. I'll try a chain of small dark boxes across the gap instead, like individual teeth segments, each sized to the local gap height and positioned against whichever surface sits forward at that point — or maybe just fill the gap with a tongue shape instead of dark boxes.

Adding neck geometry...

I'm adding small mouth corner markers, tiny freckle dots near the nose bridge, and defining the hair color palette with a main shade plus highlight and darker back tones. Then I'm setting up the jaw joint and bone hierarchy before working through the part-building function's parameters.

Writing head geometry code...

I'll clamp q so it stays stable near edges, then write a small helper that places a part at a surface point using its position and normal as direction, tagged to the bone. For axis alignment I'll allow overriding to "y" for disc shapes, and I'll add a chain helper that connects points with capsules for joints.

Now I'm tallying up the expected part counts across the skull, jaw, ears, eyes, brows, nose, freckles, cheeks, and mouth to sanity-check the build.

Adding skull, jaw, neck, ears, nose, cheeks and trimming freckles to 4 brings the total to 102, comfortably under the 120 budget. Now I'm working out the lip curve coordinates, using quadratic functions for the upper and lower lip shapes with six segments each for the capsule chains.

Placing the lower lip proud of the jaw surface with a slight lift, and positioning lower teeth just above it with their own depth and lift values. For the interior mouth pieces, I'm stepping across x-positions to compute heights between the upper teeth bottom and lower lip, deciding whether to anchor each piece to the skull or jaw bone based on whichever surface sits higher.

Still placing teeth...

Finishing lower teeth positions on the jaw, then checking the gap between upper and lower teeth stays positive across the curve. Then I'm placing a small flattened sphere for the tongue, anchored to the jaw just behind the lower teeth.

I need to make sure the tongue's front edge doesn't poke out past the teeth, so I'm adjusting its scale and vertical offset so it stays tucked slightly behind, letting the jaw surface itself hide the back portion.

Now I'm figuring out the mouth corners, computing marker positions along the skull using offset points near the lip ends.

For the hair, I'm working out the back cap sphere geometry's phi/theta ranges to make sure it covers the correct side of the head given the coordinate orientation.

I'm adjusting the back cap's theta angle to avoid overlapping the ear geometry, tightening it to 95° so the hair sits just outside the ear position.

Now I'm defining the front cap sphere geometry so it covers the top of the window, leaving the bare sides between ear and eye intact for sideburn cones.

Merging back and front hairline caps with overlapping radii, giving the back cap a darker shade while keeping the front lighter. Then setting up bangs as a loop over angle, length, tilt, and color data to build out each strand's direction vector.

Placing cowlick cones on top...

Placing more back and side tufts, angled downward-backward near the ear region, using five tuft positions at symmetric azimuths to fill out the hair coverage.

Now I'm adding sideburns in front of each ear, calculating base position on the skull at roughly 68° azimuth and elevation so they sit just forward of the ear, pointing downward along the cheek.

That brings my hair part count to 20 total: 2 caps, 8 bangs, 3 cowlicks, 5 tufts, and 2 sideburns. I'm also planning to add a highlight stripe color on a few bangs for visual interest, then moving on to positioning the eyes symmetrically with irises looking slightly forward and defining the lid outline as a small arc of points around each eye.

Now I'm working out the sclera and lid geometry, making sure the lid sits slightly outside the sclera outline, and adding a small outer lash flick extending outward and upward from the corner of each eye.

I'm also placing the eyebrows with three control points per side, giving them a slight tilt and hair-colored thickness, while checking they don't overlap too much with the hairline bangs above.

For the skull, I'll use a smooth sphere geometry rather than flat-shaded facets to avoid papercraft-style seams, skipping extra scaling since the mismatch is negligible. For the neck, I'm sizing a small cylinder to connect skull bottom to jaw, checking that it sits properly inside the jaw ellipsoid without poking through.

Now I'm adding a shirt collar using two small tori at slightly different radii and heights for a layered look, skipping the V-neck detail and extra flaps for simplicity. For ears, I'm placing scaled spheres on the head bone with a smaller inner disc sphere for the ear canal, carefully adjusting positions and scale so the inner piece stays just inside the outer ear bounds.

Now I'm setting up the color palette constants to use across the eyes, skin, hair, shirt, and other features for consistency.

I'm writing a helper function that places geometry parts onto the head bone using position, direction, and axis orientation, letting me construct eye pieces like the sclera with proper scaling and placement.

Now I'm figuring out the facial feature positions and dimensions—cheek discs using cylinder geometry oriented along the y-axis with small radius and thickness, then the nose as a scaled sphere positioned slightly forward on the skull surface, with a smaller tip sphere offset lower and further out to create the nose shape.

I'm placing freckle spheres symmetrically on both cheeks using small radius dots positioned slightly off-center, and building the jaw as a scaled sphere attached to the jaw bone for skinning.

Now I'm working out the interior teeth row, stepping across the mouth width to compute box dimensions between upper and lower jaw curves, sizing each tooth so they blend with the lips at the mouth edges while sampling depth against both skull and jaw surfaces to pick the correct z-position.

Still writing helper functions...

Checking the geometry so each hair cone's base sits just inside the scalp cap radius while the tip emerges outward, verifying this works for both back tufts near θ 78 and front bangs near θ 31 where the cap boundary differs.

Now setting up sideburns with mirrored angles for left/right symmetry, then defining the bang parameters as a list of angle, length, and sweep values, with sweep direction mostly positive for a side-swept fringe look across the forehead.

Moving on to the eyes, I'm placing white sphere eyeballs flattened slightly on one axis for both left and right positions, then adding iris spheres...

Checking that the iris size fits proportionally within the sclera bounds.

I'm working out the function signature for buildKidBody, and since I'm unsure whether a Ctx type is actually exported, I'll just define my own loose inline type covering the body, joints, parts, and mesh data instead of relying on an import.

I'm also sketching out the body layout using capsules and boxes positioned relative to the joints—rigid limb segments attached to each bone rather than smooth skinned sweeps—then mapping out the torso, hem, and waistband geometry with approximate y-coordinate ranges for the shirt and jeans.

Defining chest stub dimensions with shoulder ball joints, then setting up leg bone chains with hip, knee, and ankle positions and tapered thigh/shin capsules, plus shin boxes for pocket details.

Since most of the thigh is hidden under the torso box, I'm adding a rolled ankle cuff visible between y 0.085-0.125, deciding to rig it to the ankle bone for simplicity, then starting on sneaker geometry rigged to ankle and toe bones.

Splitting each sneaker into sole and upper sections: the heel/mid portion of the sole and upper attach to the ankle bone, while the front portion attaches to the toe bone, dividing roughly at z 0.09.

Still working out shoe geometry...

Still positioning sneaker parts...

Still defining arm geometry...

Working out palm geometry spanning roughly x 0.69–0.78, sizing it as a rounded box centered near 0.735 wide in z, and deciding to attach it to the wrist bone rather than the hand joint since the hand joint sits at the fingertip end. Also placing a lighter cuff band near the wrist transition into the sleeve.

Working out finger segment lengths and capsule endpoints for each digit, adjusting for cap radius so fingertips land around x=0.85, with finger radius 0.0125 for a chunky glove look and fingers spaced across the palm width in z.

spec.name: Cardboard Box Robot Kid
spec.description: A cheerful kid in a homemade corrugated-cardboard robot costume, standing in a T-pose with a face window in the box helmet, foil-wrapped tube sleeves, bottle-cap dials and duct-tape seams.
spec.layout: Kid about 1.2 m tall in the box, 1.46 m with the antennas. Front is +Z, left is +X. From the floor up: red sneakers (y 0 to 0.08); cardboard shin boxes over blue leggings (to 0.30); bare knees and thighs of leggings to the torso box bottom (y 0.52); the big torso box (y 0.52 to 1.02, 0.52 wide, 0.38 deep) with a control panel on the front; a smaller helmet box (y 1.02 to 1.36, 0.42 wide, 0.39 deep) sitting on top. The kid's face shows through a rectangular window cut in the front of the helmet. Arms stick out sideways through round holes in the torso box sides at y 0.92, in a T-pose with palms down, wearing foil-wrapped cardboard-tube sleeves with open fingers. Everything built by the costume is flat-shaded cardboard craft: kraft-brown box faces with a lighter inner-corrugation colour on every cut edge (a thin darker-brown layer strip along the cut rim of every hole and flap, showing the wavy corrugation as small ridge parts), tan masking-tape strips across all seams and corners, dark marker outlines and hand-drawn symbols, bottle-cap and button lights in bright colours, silver foil on tubes, and white hot-glue blobs at joins. Shapes are chunky, slightly imperfect boxes: flaps a few degrees off square, tape strips a bit crooked. The kid is a stylised chunky child with a big head, round cheeks and big eyes. spec.name: Cardboard Box Robot Kid
spec.description: A child in a handmade cardboard-box robot costume with foil, bottle-cap buttons, duct tape and marker details.
spec.layout: A 1.2 m tall kid, chunky and cute, standing in an A-pose on the floor and facing +Z. A big cube box torso (0.5 wide, 0.5 tall, 0.34 deep) sits over the kid's body, with a smaller box helmet (0.38 cube) on a kid head. A square visor window in the front of the helmet shows the kid's face with big eyes. Arms are foil-wrapped tube sleeves (cardboard tubes) with mitten claws, legs are small boxes over kid legs with sneakers. Cardboard is flat brown and tan, with a visible corrugated edge as small stripe parts, duct-tape seams in silver and red, bottle-cap buttons, a marker-drawn control panel, a bendy-straw antenna with a pom-pom, and wobbly hand-cut edges built as slightly rotated boxes. Every part is a flat colour; the style shows through tape strips, flaps, staples and marker lines seated on the surfaces.

parts.builds: The kid underneath: head (rounded skull, ears, hair cap with tufts, big eyes with highlights, brows, nose, smiling mouth built as separate upper and lower jaw on the jaw joint, cheeks), neck, shirt-blue torso under the box, shorts-length pants hips, bare-skin hands inside the costume sleeves. Head visible through the helmet visor, so face is on the front at z about 0.12 and clearly readable.
parts.attaches: Rides hips, chest, neck, head, jaw; head sits at mount headCenter, inside the helmet from costumeHelmet.

parts.builds: The big cardboard box torso: main box in cardboard with lighter top and darker bottom flaps (open folded flaps at the shoulders, wobbly), corrugated edge stripes, silver and red duct-tape seams and cross, a marker-drawn control panel on the chest with bottle-cap buttons in red, yellow and green, a dial, a drawn grille, a stapled-on label, arm holes with torn rims, shoulder straps of tape, and a cardboard backpack box with a tube vent on the back.
parts.attaches: Rides chest and hips; arm holes at shoulderL and shoulderR; neck hole under helmet at mount neck; bottom at hips.

parts.builds: The box helmet over the head: a cardboard cube with a rectangular visor cut-out on the +Z face (dark rim, cut-edge corrugation visible, clear thin plastic suggested by a pale translucent-looking pane held by tape corners), two foil-wrapped ear cylinders with bottle-cap centers, a bendy-straw antenna with kink segments in pink and a yellow pom-pom on top, a marker-drawn smile vent, tape strips, a lightning-bolt marker emblem on the side, and wobbly flaps on the top.
parts.attaches: Rides head; sits on the torso top flaps at mount neck; face opening aligned to headCenter.

parts.builds: Both arms in A-pose: foil-wrapped cardboard tube sleeves for upper arm and forearm, accordion-like dryer-hose texture rings built as small ring parts, tape cuffs, elbow joints made of cardboard discs with brass fasteners, big boxy mitten claws made of two cardboard pincer prongs each with a thumb, silver foil shading stripes and red tape bands.
parts.attaches: Mirrored on both sides (x from 0.28 to 0.7 for left); rides shoulderL/elbowL/wristL and the R equivalents; roots at the torso arm holes at mounts shoulderL and shoulderR.

parts.builds: Both legs: kid legs in pants-blue with a small cardboard box shin guard on each leg (corrugated edge, tape band, marker bolt dots), knee discs, chunky white sneakers with red soles, laces as small bars, toe caps, and foil-wrapped ankle cuffs. Feet rest on y=0, toes pointing +Z, legs slightly apart.
parts.attaches: Rides hipL, kneeL, ankleL and the R equivalents; tops at mounts hipL and hipR just under the torso box bottom.
