I'm planning a Warcraft-style dwarf blacksmith figure with a skeleton rig, around 1.4m tall and broad-built with a large beard, positioned facing an anvil with a hammer gripped in the right hand.

I'm thinking through the pose: arms in a slight A-pose angled forward, with a hammer held vertically in the right hand and tongs gripping a glowing ingot in the left, positioned over the anvil. I'm breaking the model into parts—torso/legs with spine and leg joints, head with beard and face details, arms with pauldrons and gear, and the anvil with its stand.

For the anvil setup, I'm keeping it simple with an anvil on a tree stump, a glowing ingot, and sparks, skipping extra forge details like a water bucket. I'm settling on five parts total—body, head/beard, arms/hands, props (hammer, tongs, ingot, sparks), and anvil/stump—budgeting roughly 170 units each for a total under 900, and now working out the dwarf's overall height including a possibly horned helmet.

Now I'm laying out the exact vertical coordinates for hips, shoulders, neck, head, and helm top, along with the horizontal extents for shoulders and arms, plus placing the anvil and hammer within the overall bounding box. I'm starting to define the skeleton's joint hierarchy beginning with the hips as the root.

Still placing leg joints...

Bending the arms slightly forward with wrists around (0.60,0.66,0.22) and (-0.62,0.66,0.22), adding simple hand joints with thumb and finger digits per side, left holding tongs and right holding a hammer grip point at the wrist.

I'm angling the hammer head forward-up at roughly 45°, computing its position by extending along the grip direction, and checking placement against the anvil (stump 0–0.42, anvil top around 0.85-0.88) to make sure there's no collision while positioning it near the strike surface.

spec.name: Dwarf Blacksmith at the Anvil
spec.description: A stocky Warcraft-style dwarf smith with braided red beard, plate pauldrons and leather apron, hammer raised over a glowing anvil beside a small forge.
spec.layout: The dwarf is about 1.35 m tall (huge Warcraft proportions: broad shoulders, big hands and boots, short legs, big head), standing at x=0, z=-0.15, facing +Z. In front of him (+Z) stands a heavy iron anvil on a log stump, centred at z=0.45. His right arm (model -X) is raised holding a big hammer above the anvil; his left arm (+X) holds tongs with a glowing bar on the anvil. A small stone forge with glowing coals sits behind-left (x=0.65, z=-0.45). Chunky, faceted, bold shapes; oversized pauldrons with rivets and spikes, braided beard with metal rings, saturated warm palette with glowing orange accents. Everything is flat colours and small seated detail parts.

parts.builds: Legs with boots (wide cuffed leather boots with gold buckles, cloth trousers), hips, belt with big gold buckle and hanging tools (pouch, small hammer), leather apron with stitched trim and soot stains, barrel torso with cloth shirt, and the neck. Uses the legs/hips/chest/neck joints. Boots must touch y=0 and be big and chunky.
parts.attaches: Shoulder mounts shoulderR/shoulderL for arms and pauldrons; neck mount for the head.

parts.builds: Big square characterful head: heavy brow ridge, big bulbous nose, deep-set eyes with white and dark pupils and bushy brows, ears, a separate upper skull and lower jaw (jaw joint), mouth hidden behind the beard. Huge braided red beard flowing down the chest in two braids with gold rings and tips, layered overlapping blades from beardLight to beard, moustache with curled ends, red hair with a topknot, and a small plate helmet band with a gold rune stud across the forehead.
parts.attaches: Sits on the neck mount; beard drapes over chest front without covering the belt.

parts.builds: Both arms and gear: oversized plate pauldrons with rivets, gold trim and spikes; leather bracers; muscular skin forearms with hair; big gloved hands. Right arm (-X) raised, gripping the hammer handle at handR; left arm (+X) forward holding long tongs gripping a glowing bar at handL. The hammer: wooden haft with leather wrap, big iron head with gold bands and a rune; head glows faintly at the striking face.
parts.attaches: Roots at shoulderR/shoulderL on the chest joint; hands reach handR and handL.

parts.builds: Heavy iron anvil (horn, face, waist, base feet) with a bright steel face, gold maker's mark, on a thick log stump with bark rings, axe marks and iron bands. A glowing orange-yellow bar on the face with a few spark particles (small hotYellow and ember cubes) floating above. Static, no joints.
parts.attaches: Top surface at anvilTop where the glowing bar lies for the tongs and hammer.

parts.builds: Small chunky stone forge behind-left: stacked rough stone blocks forming a hearth with a chimney hood, glowing coal bed (ember and hotYellow faceted lumps), iron grate, leather bellows with wooden handles, a bucket of water, and a rack with tongs and chisels on the wall side. Also a few small flame shapes in ember/hotYellow. Static, no joints.
parts.attaches: Centred on forgeCenter; stands on the floor beside the dwarf, not touching his arms.

calls.reasoning:
I'm working through how to implement buildAnvil as a static part with no joints — since parts without an explicit bone get auto-rigged to the nearest joint, I need to make sure the anvil at z=0 doesn't accidentally attach to something like a dwarf joint.

I'll simplify by setting bone explicitly to J.hips for every part, since hips is the root joint and gives deterministic placement using the provided `at` coordinates. I'll also need to locally declare a minimal Ctx type for the function signature rather than relying on an import that may not exist.

Now I'm sketching the actual geometry: a bounding box roughly x±0.35, z 0.1–0.95, y 0–0.95, with the anvil top sitting around y=0.78 centered near z=0.45. The stump is a cylinder of radius 0.3 (spanning z 0.15–0.75, x ±0.3) reaching up to y=0.42, and the anvil body sits on top with height 0.36 to reach y=0.78, oriented with its long axis along X so the horn extends toward +X while the dwarf faces +Z. I'm leaving room above for floating spark particles near y=0.95.

Now I'm detailing the stump's bark texture with low-poly ridge plates in a darker wood tone, thin lighter rings at the cut top where visible past the anvil, iron bands with rivets wrapped around the stump, small angled axe-mark gouges, and flared root wedges at the base.

Writing part definitions...

Still working out the geometry...

I'll build a custom frustum geometry function generating 8 vertices and indexed triangles for the tapered shapes, then start laying out the anvil's feet and stump proportions from y=0.42 to 0.78.

Continuing the waist into a widening body frustum, then a steel face plate box at the top, keeping to a limited six-colour palette with a brighter steel tone for the plate. Now starting on a horn piece extending from the +X side.

Refining horn geometry...

Now I'm working out the heel/tail block on the opposite side, sizing a small box projection flush with the face plate to hold the hardy and pritchel holes, positioning it around x -0.23 to -0.30 at the anvil's top height.

I'm adding the hardy hole as a small dark square cutout and the pritchel hole as a round dark cylinder, both embedded in the face plate near the heel, then positioning the heated bar lying across the face so it extends toward the tongs grip point.

Working out the bar's exact position and rotation now — calculating the yaw angle so it angles correctly toward the handle, then setting up a glow effect with a hot yellow core and ember-colored outer edge for the heated metal.

I'm layering an inner hot core and outer ember box, both glowing, with the color cooling toward one end and brightening to yellow at the tip, split into three segments for the gradient. I'll import the glow kit and apply it directly to flat-colored parts. Now I'm positioning a small gold maker's mark emblem on the anvil's front face.

Still placing anvil decoration...

Adding U-shaped staples and nail spikes at the base plate edges to anchor it into the stump. For the palette, I'm settling on a limited set around six custom colors—steel highlights, scorch marks, dark holes, and a touch of mossy green on the stump for natural detail.

Now I'm working out the axe-gash coloring, using a deep near-black brown for the cut interior and a lighter pale wood tone for the exposed fresh chips, keeping to roughly six custom colors total. For the stump itself, I'm planning a dark bark cylinder body with alternating lighter bark ridges, and a paler heartwood tone for the cut top surface.

For the top of the stump, I'm placing a thin cut-wood disc slightly smaller than the trunk radius, sitting just above a 0.40-tall dark bark cylinder, with concentric growth rings rendered as thin rotated ring shapes facing upward at increasing radii, colored in the mid-tone wood shade. I'm accounting for the anvil's base plate partially covering the center of the stump, so I'm keeping the visible rings positioned nearer the edges where they won't be hidden.

Now I'm adding root flares at the trunk's base for a more natural look, planning to use wedge-shaped forms angled outward in a radial pattern around the bottom of the trunk, considering simple tapered box or cone shapes to approximate the flared root silhouette.

I need to keep roots within the bounding box, checking that the z-extent stays under the 0.35 limit by adjusting the root start radius to 0.245 and profile length to 0.09. I'm also considering bark ridge placement—using 12 vertical boxes positioned at the vertices of a 12-gon cylinder with radius 0.285, computing the apothem to figure out proper ridge spacing.

Now I'm adding texture details: thin vertical ridge boxes rotated to face outward, bark knots and gouges as dark small boxes, and axe marks as thick dark diagonal slashes positioned tangentially with rotation. I'm also placing axe gashes on the top cap near the edges, working out the angle-based positioning formula so each element rotates correctly to face outward from the trunk's center.

Confirming rotation uses degrees as documented. Now I'm working out the iron bands: two cylindrical bands near the base with slightly larger radius than the trunk to cover it, adding a thin highlight ring at the top edge of each for depth, and placing six rivets per band at the face centers of a 12-gon cross-section, sized and positioned just outside the band surface.

Still placing rivets and figuring band details...

Now I'm adding the cap geometry above the trunk — a flattened cylinder disc with bark rim ridges beneath, sized slightly wider than the trunk top so it overhangs, and adding a few radial crack details etched into the cap surface at different angles.

Then I'm working out the spark effects: small glowing cubes in hot yellow and ember tones, randomly rotated and positioned above the campfire bar within a bounded region, roughly 16 of them with added glow material and strength, plus some elongated streak-like sparks for variation.

I'm also layering in a heat glow beneath the bar—thin flat orange plates positioned just below the bar's surface to suggest radiant heat, carefully offsetting each layer by tiny increments to avoid z-fighting between the bar, halo, and scorch patches.

For hammer dents, I'm adding small scorched cylinders scattered randomly along the face but keeping them clear of the bar's footprint, offsetting their z-positions outward so they don't visually clash with the bar geometry.

Picking edge highlight colors...

Okay, with six colors settled (edge, scorch, hole, moss, cut wood, gash), I'll make the face plate use P.plateLight, the frustum sides and horn use P.iron with ironLight highlight lines, and the gold mark use P.gold. I'm also adding a thin highlight strip along the body's upper edge below the face using P.ironLight to suggest a chamfer line.

Now I'm writing a helper function to build a frustum shape (tapering box) from base to top dimensions, using flat-shaded non-indexed geometry so each face reads as a distinct plane, and placing it centered on x/z with y running from the base to the height.

I'm carefully working out the correct vertex winding order for each side face so the outward normals point away from the shape correctly, checking cross products to make sure I'm not accidentally reversing a face inward.

Rather than reasoning through every face manually, I decide a more robust approach: compute the normal for any quad's triangle, compare it against the direction from the object's center to the face centroid, and automatically flip the winding if the dot product is negative. I'm estimating the total triangle count stays small, with maybe around 120 parts overall.

Now I'm tallying up the part counts across components -- anvil, stump trunk, cap, ridges, bands, rivets, roots, moss, gashes, cracks, rings, bar, halo, sparks, dents -- landing around 120 total, well within budget. Writing part placement code...

Still working out the emblem placement...

Right, extrude doesn't accept rotation directly, so instead I'll define custom x/y axis vectors for the extrusion to tilt the thickness direction to match the surface slope, computing the cross product to get the correct offset direction. Then I'm layering the emblem: an outer gold hexagon, a slightly thicker dark scorch hexagon inset to protrude a bit more, followed by a gold anvil shape on top.

Working out anvil silhouette coordinates...

Defining root geometry next...

I'll add a thin moss patch at the cap rim too, then move to generating sparks — placing 16 randomized particles near the bar's hot end with varied sizes, colors, rotations, and glow strength, plus a few tiny embers on the face. For the bar itself, I'm setting up a yawed rotation and building segments with a helper function that positions each piece along the local axis.

Writing bar segment colors...

Positioning the tip piece and recalculating the bar's vertical center so it sits properly on the shell face. For the halo glow, I'm reconsidering flat rectangular planes since they'd look artificial, and switching to a thin hexagonal cylinder shape instead for a more natural glowing effect.

Adding scorch mark details...

Now I'm positioning the hardy and pritchel holes relative to the bar's footprint, checking clearance so the square hardy hole sits left of the bar's left end and the round pritchel hole clears its right end, keeping both away from the face edges.

I'm also adding small details like nails and straps at the base plate corners, plus a staple-like bar across the flange to suggest a tie-down for the anvil's plate.

I'm working out the strap tabs bending down into the stump surface, adjusting positions so they clip slightly into the wood but align properly with the plate edges, then sizing the base plate to overlap the frustum. Now I'm starting to write the code, setting up a degree conversion helper and a frustum geometry function.

Still writing frustum geometry...

Adding ridge color alternation, dark knot details at face centers, and axe-mark slashes carved into the trunk surface at angled intervals...

I'm sizing concentric rings positioned near the top of the anvil, checking their radii against the plate corners so they stay visible, and working out the rotation needed to make the ring geometry face upward correctly after transforming it from its default forward-facing orientation.

Writing part placement helper...

Mapping local scale to world axes after rotation, so vertical radius becomes 0.066 and depth radius 0.0975, placing the horn base at y=0.714 with the tip sloping down to 0.73. I'm checking the cone's x-span against the box boundary at 0.35 and trimming the length to 0.13 centered at x=0.285 so the tip stays within bounds, with a small sphere to cap the tip.

Adding tip cap sphere and ironLight horn base band...

Now checking the face plate overhang against the horn position, sizing the heel block with its bounding box and color, and confirming the face plate authentically stops short of the heel to expose the hardy hole. Time to write the final code, importing the glow module from the kit path.

I'm planning the buildHead function, setting up the neck, head, and jaw joints with their positions and orientations, and defining the bounding box dimensions for the head geometry.

I'll create a helper function for placing parts under bones, and figure out how to give the skull a blocky, faceted look using low-segment geometry with scaling rather than a smooth sphere, positioning the face front and beard to drape naturally down the chest.

Working out the flat-face rotation math for the faceted cylinder head, I get the front face sitting at about z=0.057, so eyes should go near y=1.24, z=0.05. Then I'm planning the jaw as a separate box/cylinder piece hinged near (0,1.15,-0.02), extending down to cover the lower face.

For the mouth and beard, I'm thinking a dark slit mouth mostly hidden by facial hair, with the beard's main mass attached partly to the jaw bone so it moves naturally when the jaw opens, even though a large beard there is a bit unusual rigging-wise.

For the neck joint, I'm adding a thick cylinder skin section around y 1.02-1.12 that stays mostly concealed under the beard, plus considering additional plating there.

Now turning to the eyes, I want them deep-set beneath a brow ridge box positioned around y 1.285, angled downward toward the center to give an angry expression. I'm working out the rotation math for each side's brow piece—since the inner edge should sit lower, I need to rotate around Z so the outer edge lifts up, figuring out the correct sign of the angle for the positive-x side.

Beyond the brow box itself, I'm layering in bushy eyebrow geometry using the hair color, plus small cones jutting from the outer ends for texture. For the eyes themselves, I'm planning a dark socket ellipsoid, white sphere, pupil sphere, and a highlight dot, and checking that the eye x-position still falls within the flat front face of the head at that height.

I'm adjusting the eye depth so the white sphere protrudes slightly from the face surface, with the pupil sitting just in front of it and a darker socket sphere recessed behind for depth. I'm also tweaking the head's z-scale slightly to adjust how far forward the flat face sits, making sure the eyes and brow still land correctly on that facet.

Now I'm sculpting the nose as a bulbous sphere scaled and positioned below the brow, adding small nostril nubs on either side and a bridge wedge connecting it upward, using a warm skin tone for the whole assembly.

Cheekbones become scaled skin-shaded spheres on each side, ears are flattened pointed spheres with darker inner shading and a tiny gold ring on one lobe, and now I'm working on red hair, starting with a back-of-head mass and considering a helmet-like band across the forehead to fit the head's overall proportions.

Switching approach to a scaled cylinder band instead of a lathe, since lathe geometry can't easily match the head's z-axis squash — using a simple cylinder sized slightly larger than the head and scaling it to fit.

I'm now fine-tuning the vertical placement of facial features: adjusting eye height to 1.225, brow center to 1.262 with bushy extension to 1.275, and repositioning the band to 1.30-1.34 so it clears the brows, with the head top at 1.35 and hair dome at 1.34.

I'm also adding a hair mass behind the head and side tufts spilling under the band over the ears, plus a small gold rune stud plate on the band's front center.

Still writing details for the band's gold rivets positioned around its flat faces at evenly spaced angles, skipping the front face where the stud sits.

For the topknot I'm adding a small hair sphere with a gold tie ring, then checking the height math carefully against the 1.42 box limit, adjusting scale and center position until it fits just under the ceiling, plus a few small tuft cones angled upward and back for texture.

Now I'm moving on to the beard, which needs to be a signature layered feature draping from the jaw and cheeks down toward the chest, working out where it should sit in z-depth relative to the torso and chest front so it reads naturally against the body geometry.

I'm planning the overall beard shape: a wide layered mass from jaw down to around chest height, with two braids hanging below featuring gold rings and tips. Checking the available vertical space, the beard needs to span from near the head's bottom down to roughly chest level, so I may need to extend it lower to give the braids enough visible length.

Now I'm working out the braid construction — stacking small alternating tilted ellipsoid segments to form each braid, spacing them along the x-axis with slight offsets, and adding thin gold torus rings between segments plus a cone-shaped tip at the bottom of each braid.

Writing blade helper function...

Working out the rotation math for splay and lean angles, verifying the axes stay perpendicular, and figuring out the sign on the lean so the blade bottoms tilt forward correctly.

For blade coloring, I'm planning each blade as two overlapping parts—a darker base layer and a lighter inner streak offset slightly forward—to give a fur-like gradient effect, keeping the part budget in mind.

Now I'm working out the beard layer positions relative to the jaw and chest geometry, realizing the back layer risks getting buried inside the chest mesh under the chin when leaning forward, so I need to adjust the z-depth and lean angle to keep it visible.

Still working out blade splay angles...

Then I'm positioning the main braids hanging from beneath the layers, adjusting their start and end points so they overlap naturally with the blade layers above. Now I'm planning the moustache as a handlebar shape with thick tapered sweeps curling outward and up from under the nose, using a curved path per side.

Adding moustache points...

Now I'm thinking about sideburns and cheek beard using flattened spheres along the jaw at x=±0.17, plus a thicker beard mass under the chin for fuller coverage.

Next I'm placing the jaw itself as a skin-toned block beneath the beard, and adding a dark slit for the mouth between the moustache and lower beard to keep the layering readable.

Adding small white teeth peeking from the jaw under the moustache, then re-adjusting the vertical layout: upper skull cylinder spanning 1.11 to 1.35, eyes centered around 1.225, nose at 1.17, mouth at 1.125, and jaw positioned slightly below with a joint pivot near 1.15, accepting a bit of overlap with the skull.

I'm swapping the jaw box for a narrower cylinder shape to better match the skull's octagonal width, positioning it forward for the chin while letting the beard hide any protrusion, then working out the eye socket placement using trigonometry to position it correctly on the angled face surface.

Placing the socket, white, pupil, and tiny highlight spheres at increasing depths and scaling them for an almond shape, with the brow ridge extending forward to create a deep-set look.

Now working out per-side brow ridges and bushy brow geometry, adding small cone tufts at the outer and inner ends for texture, and deciding on a contrasting hair/beard color for the brows.

Skipping forehead wrinkles and eyelid details for simplicity, but adding cheekbone bumps and under-eye shaping with skin-toned spheres. For the nose, I'm building a bridge wedge, a scaled bulb sphere in a warmer nose tone, and small flared nostril spheres.

For the ears I'm placing flattened spheres with pointed cone tips on either side of the head, positioning them to align with the rotated flat facets of the head shape so they sit naturally against the skull.

Adding an earring and hair dome...

Now I'm placing the back hair mass behind the head and adding a few spiked cone locks near the ears pointing down and back for extra texture, then coloring everything with hair and beard highlight shades.

Adding gold temple discs and thin trim cylinders around the helmet band, keeping skip on fine ear tufts since they're minor details.

Realizing scale order matters: applying z-scale after rotating squashes along the wrong axis, so I should bake the rotation into the geometry itself with a rotateY call, then apply part scale afterward so it stays aligned to world axes. I'll make a helper for building octagon-shaped geometry this way.

Now I'm working out facial feature placement — the mustache sweep, neck cylinder positioning near the jaw, and sizing the beard mass sphere so its front tip sits just past the chin without overshooting too far forward.

Next I'm laying out braid geometry: positioning twin braids near the temples, tapering segments downward from the hairline, alternating rotation and offset per segment to create a plaited look, then adding small ring torus accents along the braid length.

Calculating positions for the braid layers over the blades, checking forward lean angles so the bottom z-coordinates stay within bounds while keeping braid radius consistent.

I'm also checking whether the beard covers the belt (it doesn't, stays clear) and tallying up the total part count—head, jaw, hair pieces, band with trims and rivets, runes, discs, and the eye components—landing around seventeen parts before eyes.

Tallying the rest: eyes, brows, nose, cheeks, ears with rings, moustache, sideburns, blades across all four size groups, braids with segments and rings, topknot, locks—bringing the total to roughly 140 parts, with triangle counts staying manageable since the spheres are low-poly. I decide to skip adding a glow effect to the gold rune stud to keep things simple, then start setting up the head-building helper function.

I'm assuming the Ctx type and its contents (bone, joint references, part builder) are already available in scope rather than declaring them myself. Now I'm writing small utility functions: one for creating sphere geometries with adjustable radius and segment counts, and another "put" helper that wraps the part-placement call with sensible defaults for bone, scale, rotation, and direction, checking whether passing undefined for optional fields will work cleanly.

Still writing helper functions...

Adding highlight streak geometry...

Assigning beard/streak color pairs across the layers, mixing dark and light tones, then settling on a small palette of around five custom hex colors for beard, ear inner shading, and mouth darkness, reusing the skin shade where possible to stay within budget.

Working out blade positions and angles for one side, checking overlap with the jaw cylinder's front z-coordinate to confirm the blades sit correctly against the head geometry, then checking how the outer blade aligns with the jaw's octagonal cross-section.

Now checking the moustache placement against the nose bulb — making sure the moustache sits below the nostril bottom without clashing into the nose geometry, and confirming its front z-extent clears the nose's lower bound.

spec.name: Dwarf Blacksmith at the Anvil
spec.description: A stocky Warcraft-style dwarf blacksmith with a braided beard and heavy hammer, mid-forge at an anvil on a stump, with a glowing forge-fire brazier beside him.
spec.layout: Scale is chunky Warcraft: the dwarf stands about 1.35 m tall with oversized head, huge shoulders with big riveted pauldrons, thick forearms and giant fists and boots. He faces +Z in a neutral rest pose, arms extended slightly forward and out, holding a huge hammer in his right hand (model -X). The anvil on a stump sits directly in front of him at z 0.55. A glowing coal brazier stands at his left (+X). Colours are bold and saturated, with exaggerated, faceted shapes. Warm orange glow against cool steel and leather browns. Details such as rivets, straps, runes and braids are small separate parts in their own colours.

parts.builds: Big square-jawed head: skin skull, heavy brow ridge, big nose, two eyes with whites and dark pupils plus bushy brows in beard colour, ears, separate lower jaw on the jaw joint. Huge braided beard flowing from the cheeks down to the belt as broad overlapping blades (beard to beardTip) with two gold beardBand rings, a moustache with curled ends, and a steel-and-leather horned helmet with gold rim and small rivets.
parts.attaches: Neck joint at neckBase; the beard hangs over the chest front without touching the arms.

parts.builds: Barrel torso and wide hips: cloth tunic, leather vest with straps and gold buckles, wide belt with a big gold buckle and hanging tools (tongs, pouch), leather apron down the front with scorch marks and rivets, small neck collar. Includes steel shoulder pauldrons on both sides with spikes, rivets and gold trim, mounted at shoulderR and shoulderL.
parts.attaches: Hips and chest joints; arms attach at the shoulder mounts; legs at the hip joints; head at neckBase.

parts.builds: Both arms. Thick skin forearms with leather bracers and gold studs, cloth sleeves on the upper arms, big mitten-style fists with finger blocks and a thumb. The right fist (at handR) grips a huge war-hammer: wooden handle with leather wrap, big steel head with gold bands and a rune. The left fist (at handL) holds steel tongs gripping a glowing orange ingot on the anvil.
parts.attaches: Shoulder joints at shoulderR and shoulderL; the hammer head rests above anvilTop; the ingot sits on anvilTop.

parts.builds: Short, thick legs: cloth trousers, leather knee wraps, big steel-capped boots with leather cuffs, gold buckles and thick soles resting on the floor. Both feet point forward with toe caps; a little ash on the boots.
parts.attaches: Hip joints at hips; the tops are hidden under the torso belt and apron.

parts.builds: The workstation, no joints. A wooden stump with bark and rings and iron bands, a big steel anvil on it (base, waist, face, horn, hardy hole, highlights and scratches) and a small ingot-glow spot. Next to it at brazier, a stone brazier of rocks holding glowing coal and flame blades (ember to emberHot), plus a water bucket with iron hoops, a few tools leaning on the stump, and a few sparks flying above the anvil.
parts.attaches: The anvil sits on stumpTop; the top of the anvil is at anvilTop; the brazier stands beside the dwarf's left arm without touching it.

spec.name: Cathedral Gargoyle
spec.description: A chunky, chisel-faceted stone gargoyle crouched on a weathered cathedral ledge, wings half-open, grinning with fangs and gripping the stone edge with its claws.
spec.layout: Everything is one gothic stone carving: blocky, faceted primitives in a grey stone palette, with moss, soot and chips as their own small parts. The ledge is a stone cornice slab, 1.7 wide, 0.3 tall and 1.76 deep, at z -0.88..0.88. Its front edge has a stepped moulding and three corbel blocks under it, and its top has a shallow rain-gutter groove. The gargoyle crouches on its centre line, with the pelvis low and back at z -0.2 and the shoulders high and forward at z 0.3. The spine arches up from pelvis to chest, the neck is short and thick, and the head is thrust forward and slightly down at z 0.58..0.95, with its top at about y 1.45. Hands are planted on the ledge at z about 0.7. Hind legs are digitigrade: thigh forward and up, shin back and down, flat clawed feet at z about 0.2. The tail runs back from the rump, curls along the ledge to the model's right (-X) and ends in a diamond spade tip at about [-0.72, 0.45, -0.4]. Bat wings are half-open: each arm bone rises and sweeps out to the side, three finger bones fan back from the wrist, and a thick stone-slab membrane stretches between them and to the flank. The wings peak at y about 1.6 and span x ±1.15. Identity cues are built big: a heavy beetle brow, a wide grinning mouth with a separate upper jaw and lower jaw and 4-6 chunky fangs, two swept-back ridged horns, big pointed ears, a pug nose with flared nostrils, and a stone beard or chin tuft. Eye sockets are deep and carved, with an amber glowing eyeball inside. The body gets stone blocks and chisel ridges: a row of spinal knobs, plated belly bands, ribs, knuckle studs and brow ridges. Colour goes by place: lighter stone on top and front faces, darker stone below and in recesses. Moss sits on upward faces of the ledge, shoulders, back and wing tops. Soot and water-stain streaks run down the ledge front and under the chin. A few dark crack lines and pale chip patches sit as thin parts seated on the surface. Every surface is a flat colour.

parts.builds: The cathedral ledge the gargoyle crouches on. A stone slab, 1.7 wide, 0.3 tall and 1.76 deep (stone, with a darker stoneDark base course), topped by a slightly overhanging cornice slab (stoneLight) with a stepped moulding on the front and side edges. Three or four corbel blocks (stoneDark) under the front edge. A shallow rain-gutter groove across the top (stoneDeep) and a small square plinth block (stone) under the gargoyle's body. Masonry joints are thin mortar-coloured strips on the front and sides, with a few offset block faces. Moss patches (moss, mossDark) as low flat blobs on upward faces and the corners. Soot and waterStain streaks running down the front face under the gargoyle. Two rust-coloured iron cramps on top, chips and cracks (crack) as small thin parts, and a few pale chip patches. Keep it simpler than the gargoyle and well inside its box, and do not build anything above y 0.36 except small moss and the plinth.
parts.attaches: Top face at the ledgeTop mount (y 0.3). The gargoyle's feet, hands and tail rest on it; all geometry is static on the root joint pelvis.

parts.builds: Torso and tail of the gargoyle. A hunched loft or sweep body riding pelvis, spine2 and chest: heavy rounded-box pelvis and haunches mass, a deep barrel chest with high shoulder blocks (shoulder mass at the shoulderL and shoulderR mounts, radius about 0.2), and a tucked belly. Colours: stone body, stoneLight on the top and front, stoneDark on the belly. Carved details: a row of 7-9 spinal knobs and ridge blades (stoneLight) from tail base to neck, 5-6 pairs of rib arcs on the flanks, 4-5 plated belly bands (stoneDark), and chest pectoral plates. Wing root sockets (stoneDark blocks) at wingRootL and wingRootR. The tail runs from tailRoot through tail1..tail5, tapering from radius 0.1 to 0.04, in a curl to the model's right ending at tailTip with a flat diamond spade tip (stoneLight, with a stoneDark midrib), and small ridge spines along its top. Moss on the back top and shoulder tops (moss), a soot patch near the haunch, a crack or two. The tail rests on the ledge, with its underside at y >= 0.32.
parts.attaches: Neck base meets the head part at neckBase. Arm sockets at shoulderL and shoulderR (the limbs part starts there). Hip sockets at hipL and hipR. Wing roots at wingRootL and wingRootR. Skins over pelvis, spine2, chest and tail1..5, and bears no limb or head geometry.

parts.builds: The hero head, the richest part, on neck1, neck2, head and jaw. A thick neck sweep (stone) from neckBase. A broad blocky skull (stone) with a heavy overhanging beetle brow ridge (stoneLight, with chisel notches) and deep eye sockets (stoneDeep). In each socket sits an amber eyeball (eyeGlow, to be glowed) and a dark slit pupil (soot). A wide flat muzzle with a pug nose block, flared nostril holes (stoneDeep), cheek bones and cheek ruffs. An UPPER jaw on head and a separate LOWER jaw on joint jaw (hinge at jawHinge): the upper lip has 4-6 chunky fangs (fang) with two big canines, and the lower jaw has an underbite row of 4 fangs, a protruding chin and a chunky stone beard tuft (stoneLight over stoneDark), a tongue slab (rust) and a dark mouth interior (stoneDeep). Two big swept-back horns (stoneLight at the base, stoneDark ridges, claw-coloured tips), each curving back and up from the brow, tip at y <= 1.55. Two large pointed bat ears (stone with stoneDark inner slabs), a row of small head ridge blocks, moss on the crown, a soot streak under the chin and crack lines. The face is built forward, with nothing in front of it.
parts.attaches: The neck sweep starts at neckBase (y 1.08, z 0.38) overlapping the chest. The skull centres on headBase [0, 1.2, 0.58] and the lower jaw hinges at jawHinge [0, 1.12, 0.72]. The head faces +Z and tilts slightly down.

parts.builds: All four limbs, built mirrored for left (+X) and right (-X). Arms: shoulderL, elbowL, wristL and handL, and likewise on the right. They are thick sweeps (radius 0.11 at the shoulder down to 0.07 at the wrist) with a muscular upper arm, an elbow knob (stoneLight) and a forearm, ending in big chunky hands planted flat on the ledge at the handL and handR mounts (y about 0.34). Each hand has a palm block and three splayed fingers plus a thumb, with a knuckle stud on each finger and a curved claw (claw) on each tip. Finger and toe digit chains are created by this part as `b.chain` with names like fingerLA1, fingerLA2, fingerLB1... (letters and digits only, role digit, parent handL, handR, footL or footR, 2 joints each). Legs: hipL, kneeL, ankleL and footL, digitigrade and crouched, with a bulky thigh haunch, a knee knob, a shin tapering to the hock and a long flat foot with three forward toes and claws (toeLA1 etc., parent footL), planted at y 0.3-0.34 on the ledge. The right side mirrors. Stone colours: limbs stone, with stoneLight top planes, stoneDark undersides, chisel-groove stripes, a moss patch on the thighs, and scuffs of soot near the feet.
parts.attaches: Arm tops start at shoulderL and shoulderR (inside the torso shoulder mass). Hand claws touch the ledge at handL and handR. Hip tops start at hipL and hipR. Feet rest at footL and footR on the ledgeTop height y 0.3. Rides joints shoulder, elbow, wrist, hand, hip, knee, ankle and foot on both sides, plus its own digit joints.

parts.builds: Two bat-style wings, built mirrored for left (+X) and right (-X), half-open and swept up and out in the rest pose. Each wing's arm bone is a chunky sweep (stone, radius 0.07 tapering to 0.05) through wingArmL, wingElbowL and wingWristL, with a shoulder block, an elbow knuckle and a wrist claw hook (claw). Three finger bones (wingRib, radius about 0.03 tapering to 0.012, created as chains named wingFingerL1, wingFingerL2, wingFingerL3 with 2 joints each, parent wingWristL, role wing, and likewise wingFingerR1..3) fan back and out from the wrist, ending in small claw-coloured tips at about [1.1, 1.55, -0.7], [1.05, 1.0, -0.85] and [0.85, 0.65, -0.75], mirrored for the right. The membrane is a thick stone-slab skin between the arm, the fingers and the body flank (wing colour, with a scalloped trailing edge, thickness about 0.03), with raised ribs (wingRib) running along each finger, panel seam lines (stoneDeep), a few carved chips, moss along the upper arm tops (moss), and a soot or waterStain gradient near the lower edge. The overall span is about x ±1.15, with its highest point at y about 1.6 and the lowest edge above y 0.6, and nothing in front of z 0.2.
parts.attaches: Arm bones start at wingRootL and wingRootR on the torso shoulder sockets (chest joint). The wrist is at wingWristL and wingWristR. The inner membrane edge attaches to the flank near the pelvis, behind the arms, without blocking the limbs.

spec.name: Cathedral Gargoyle
spec.description: A hunched gothic stone gargoyle crouched on a weathered cathedral ledge, with bat wings folded up, horned head, fanged jaw and curling tail.
spec.layout: Crouched on a stone ledge slab (top at y=0.18) facing +Z. Haunches and bent hind legs at the back (z about -0.3), a heavy hunched torso rising forward to broad shoulders (z about 0.1), arms straight down in front with clawed hands gripping the ledge edge (z about 0.45). A thick neck juts forward and up to a large head at z about 0.55 and y about 1.0 with brow ridge, horns, pointed ears, a separate upper and lower jaw with fangs, and glowing amber eyes under the brow. Bat wings with finger bones and stone membranes rise from the shoulders and fold upward and back, tips at y about 1.35. The tail curls from the rump around the left side of the ledge. Everything is chunky, faceted stone in grey tones with moss on upward faces, soot and rain streaks below, and chiselled details such as brow lines, claws, ribs and cracks as small separate parts.

Wider than the gargoyle's footprint. Colours: ledge, ledgeTop, stoneDark, moss, soot, crack.
parts.attaches: Top surface at mount ledgeTop; the feet, hands and tail rest on it.

parts.builds: Hunched torso and haunches: chest loft with ribs and spine ridge of chiselled bumps, pelvis, tail with six segments curling around the ledge with a spade tip, plus bent hind legs (thigh, shin, foot) with three-toed clawed feet gripping the ledge. Chisel marks, cracks, moss on the back, soot below. Colours: stone, stoneLight, stoneDark, moss, soot, horn for claws.
parts.attaches: Neck at mount neckBase, arms at shoulderL/R, wings at wingRootL/R, hips at hipL/R, tail from tailBase.

parts.builds: The large head and neck: thick neck, boxy skull, heavy brow ridge, snout with nostrils, separate upper and lower jaw with rows of fangs and tusks, tongue, two big glowing amber eyes with dark pupils under the brow, two curved horns, large pointed ears with inner detail, cheek ridges, chin beard of stone blocks, cracks and moss on top of the skull. parts.attaches: Neck joint at neckBase, head joint at headCenter, jaw joint under the skull.

spec.layout: Static prop, no joints. It stands vertically, tip down, with the tip at y=0 (sinking at most 0.02). The blade faces +Z: the sharpened single edge runs along z=+0.075 and the flat spine at z=-0.05, with blade faces toward ±X. The blade is 0.9 m long, 0.12 m wide in z and 0.03 m thick in x, with a swept, slightly forward-curved point. The revolver barrel lies on the back of the spine (center z=-0.075, radius 0.03) and runs from a muzzle at y=0.34 up to the cylinder, so the blade and barrel point the same way like a bayonet. The revolver cylinder (axis along Y, center y=0.97, radius 0.055) sits on the spine side at the blade root, above a compact revolver frame (y 0.88-1.06). Above that is a winged gold guard (y 1.06-1.12, x +-0.16). A trigger guard loop with a trigger projects toward +Z (to z~0.2) at y 1.06-1.2. A hammer curves out the back (-Z, to z~-0.2) at y 1.1-1.2. The straight leather-wrapped grip runs y 1.12-1.36. A lion-motif pommel sits at y 1.36-1.47, with a short chain and a Griever-style lion pendant hanging at x=+0.09. Style is Final Fantasy VIII: polished silver steel with pale cyan bevels and engraved panels, black gunmetal, gold trim and filigree, dark brown leather wrap, and small glowing blue energy inlays in the fuller and cylinder. Shapes are chunky and bold, built from primitives with faceted low-poly edges. Detail comes from small parts seated on the surfaces: rivets, bands, engravings, flutes, chambers, notches and gems. spec.name: Revolver Gunblade
spec.description: A Final Fantasy-style gunblade with a bright steel sword blade, a revolver mechanism at the hilt, a barrel along the spine, gold filigree, glowing sapphire and cyan accents, and a hanging lion pendant, standing upright on its pommel.
spec.layout: The weapon stands upright with the blade pointing up (+Y) and the round pommel resting on y = 0. It is a flat-bladed sword, so the blade is thin in X (about 0.04 thick at the base) and wide in Z (0.14). The cutting edge faces the front (+Z) and the spine and barrel face the back (-Z). All axes run through x = 0; the z extent runs from about -0.26 (hammer tail, trigger guard) to +0.14 (guard front). From bottom to top: pommel (y 0-0.09), leather grip (0.09-0.40), crossguard and trigger guard (0.34-0.47), revolver receiver with a side-facing cylinder and rear hammer (0.40-0.70), blade (0.70-1.50), with the barrel riding the spine from y 0.70 to 1.34 (z -0.15..-0.07). The lion pendant hangs on a short chain from a lug on the left guard wing (+X side, x about 0.105) beside the grip, and ends near y 0.17. Final Fantasy look: elegant, slightly exaggerated, polished-steel silhouette with bold gold filigree, dark gunmetal mechanics, and a few glowing sapphire and cyan accents (pommel gem, cylinder jewel, fuller runes, muzzle). Every surface is a flat colour. Engravings, trim, rivets, runes and glints are small separate parts seated on the surface, layered as a dark outline, a main colour and a bright highlight. Light steel on the blade's top, deep steel and gunmetal in the lower mechanism, warm gold for every ornament.

parts.builds: The lower handle from pommel to grip top. (1) Pommel: a faceted lathe cap with a flat base on y=0, radius about 0.05, height 0.09, in gold with goldDeep underside bands, a ring of small gold studs, and a glowing sapphire gem (a small faceted sphere or cone) set in the bottom face and the rounded front. (2) Grip: an 8-sided tube radius 0.03 from y 0.09 to 0.40 in leather, with a diagonal leatherDark cord wrap built as thin rings or a spiral sweep, leatherHi highlight strips on the front, and gold collars (rings) at top and bottom with goldDeep edges. (3) A short sapphire or ruby bead band mid-grip, tiny rivets, and a thin goldPale highlight line on each collar. Everything is centred on x=0, z=0 and stays within x ±0.05 and z ±0.05. No chain here; the charm part hangs beside the grip.
parts.attaches: The pommel base rests on y=0 at pommelBase. The grip top collar meets the receiver's crossguard plate at gripTop.

parts.builds: The revolver mechanism and guard. (1) Frame: a gunmetal housing from y 0.40 to 0.70 with a chunky chamfered front edge, side plates at x ±0.04 with gold trim lines and rivets, and gunmetalHi highlights on the top faces. (2) Crossguard: a gold plate at y 0.40-0.44 spanning x ±0.12 and z -0.06..+0.12, with upswept wing tips and goldDeep underside. On the left wing (+X) is a small ring lug at chainAnchor. A sapphire jewel sits at the hub on the left face (+X). (4) Trigger on the joint 'trigger': a small gold crescent lever hanging from triggerPivot down and back. (5) Trigger guard: a gold sweep loop from guardLoopFront down and back round to guardLoopRear (touching the grip's rear face at z -0.03), about 0.016 thick. (6) Hammer on the joint 'hammer': a gunmetal hooked hammer with a gold spur and a ruby stud at its pivot, pointing back to z about -0.25. (7) Breech block: a gunmetal rear block y 0.60-0.70, z -0.15..-0.07 where the barrel starts, with a gold ring at its top (breechTop). (8) Blade lock collar: a gold and gunmetal band y 0.68-0.70 around the blade root (x ±0.035, z -0.075..+0.095) that the blade passes up through. Colours: gunmetal, gunmetalHi, gold, goldDeep, black, sapphire, ruby, steelDeep.
parts.attaches: Sits on the grip at gripTop and guardPlate. The chain lug is at chainAnchor. The blade root enters at bladeBase through the collar. The barrel starts at breechTop and barrelBase. The cylinder, trigger and hammer ride the joints at their pivot mounts.

parts.builds: The sword blade, thin in X and wide in Z, from y 0.70 to the tip at y 1.50. Build the outline as an extrude (outline in the Z-Y plane, thickness along X) with a straight spine at z -0.07 and an edge at z +0.09 at the base. The edge side swells slightly just above the guard, then tapers with a gentle curve to a clipped diagonal point at bladeTip (z about +0.03, y 1.50). Details: (1) A steelBright main body; a steelShade bevel strip along the cutting edge as a thinner overlapping extrude, with an edgeWhite sharp edge line on the very rim. (2) A recessed fuller groove (steelDeep) along the centre from y 0.80 to 1.38 on both faces (+X and -X) with a thin edgeWhite highlight on its upper rim. parts.builds: The gun barrel assembly riding the blade's spine, from barrelBase (y 0.70) up to the muzzle (y 1.34), centred on x=0, z=-0.105. (1) Main barrel: an octagonal gunmetal tube radius 0.04 tapering to 0.034, with gunmetalHi top-facing highlight strips and black underside seams. (2) Shroud sleeve: a thicker gunmetal section y 0.72-0.95 with a row of cooling slots (small black inset boxes) and gold band rings at its ends and middle. (3) Spine clamps: 4 steel and gold bracket bands that wrap from barrel to blade spine at intervals, bridging z -0.07 to -0.11. (4) Muzzle: a gold and gunmetal flared muzzle brake with a black bore and a glowCyan ring inside the lip, plus a faint glowing sapphire dot. (5) Front sight: a small gold fin on the back of the muzzle and a rear sight notch near the breech, a thin ruby line, and tiny rivets. (6) Gold filigree scroll or vine small parts running along the barrel's -Z side, and a thin glowCyan line along the shroud. Colours: gunmetal, gunmetalHi, black, gold, goldDeep, goldPale, steel, glowCyan, sapphire, ruby.
parts.attaches: Starts on the receiver breech block at barrelBase and breechTop. Its +Z face touches the blade's spine at spineLine. The muzzle is at the top of the barrel.

parts.builds: The hanging lion pendant, Squall's signature charm, on a chain from the left guard wing lug at chainAnchor (x 0.105, y 0.40) hanging straight down. (1) Chain: a tube or sweep of small link bars (alternating oriented chain and chainDark short rod or capsule links) bending smoothly over joints chain1, chain2, chain3 from y 0.40 down to y 0.24, with a small gold jump ring at the top that loops through the lug. (2) Pendant on the joint 'pendant': a lion head medallion of radius about 0.05 centred at (0.105, 0.22, -0.04), seen from the front or +Z with its disc facing +Z and thin in z (about 0.02 thick). It has a gold rim ring, an outer mane of 10 to 12 gold spikes or shaped blades in a goldDeep to goldPale root-to-tip gradient, an inner lionFace disc, two eyes (black with a small white highlight), a small nose triangle and a muzzle with a mouth line, two small ears, and a sapphire gem on the forehead. Everything must be in the flat colours gold, goldDeep, goldPale, lionFace, chain, chainDark, black, sapphire. Keep x within 0.055-0.155 and y within 0.16-0.41.
parts.attaches: The top ring meets the left crossguard lug at chainAnchor. Joints chain1, chain2, chain3 and pendant run straight down along x about 0.105 and z -0.04, beside the grip (grip radius 0.03, so there is no collision).
