spec.name: Hydra of the Broken Mere
spec.description: A colossal five-headed Norse-style hydra in a God of War look: scarred slate-green hide, bone horns, iron-bound leather and broken weapons embedded in its flesh, with ember, frost and venom runes glowing on each head.
spec.layout: A huge four-legged beast, centred on x=0 and facing +Z. A heavy barrel torso (z -2.4..2.3, top about y 3.4) stands on four thick reptilian legs; rear legs are digitigrade and bigger, front legs are shoulder-heavy with big clawed paws. A long thick tail trails behind to z -6.8 and the tip rests on the floor. FIVE long muscular necks rise from the shoulder hump (z about 1.3..1.7) and fan out like a hand, each ending in a head that looks forward and slightly down. The centre head (C) is the tallest and biggest: skull top y about 5.9, horns to y 6.4, snout to z 4.6. The inner heads (IL at +x, IR at -x) sit about x ±1.75, y 5.1, and are a little smaller. The outer heads (OL at +x, OR at -x) hang lower and wider at x ±2.85, y 4.3, with necks curving outward then forward. From the front the five necks read as a spread fan with a clear gap between each pair. Hide: dark slate-green scales (scaleDark back, scaleMid flanks, scaleLight highlights on ridges) over a bone-yellow belly and throat made of broad plates. God of War style: brutal, heavy and angular; chunky blocky plates, a desaturated cold palette with small hot accents; deep scars with pale ridged edges; Norse rune glyphs carved as small straight-stroke parts; broken axe heads, spear shafts, arrowheads, iron-bound leather straps and chain remnants embedded in the body. Ember orange (fire), frost blue and venom green glow only on small parts: eyes, nostrils, runes and cracks. Each head has its own identity: C = ember crown, IL = frost, IR = venom, OL = ember, OR = bone and iron muzzle. Mouths are rest-pose slightly open: the lower jaw hangs about 8 degrees below the upper. Every surface is one flat colour; scars, runes, teeth, eyes, straps and rivets are small parts seated on the surface. Use the glow kit on ember, frost, venom and eye parts.

parts.builds: The torso and the front half. (1) Torso: one loft through the mount torsoStations_zYWH (each entry is z, centre y, full width, full height), flat-box-ish and heavy, skinned to [hips, chest]. Painted by sector: scaleDark back, scaleMid flanks, belly/bellyDark underside as broad separate bone-yellow ventral plates (a row of 8 wide flat plates under the chest and belly, each a thin slab with a dark outline strip). (2) Shoulder hump: a big rounded mass over the front shoulders (z 0.8..2.2, top y 3.5) that swallows all five neck roots (neckBaseC/IL/IR/OL/OR); at each neck base put a fat iron-and-leather collar ring (sweep ring of iron with 6 rivets and a leather strap), radius about the neck base radius (C 0.5, IL/IR 0.42, OL/OR 0.38) + 0.06, so the neck sweeps from the heads' builders slot out of it. (3) Front legs FL and FR: thick sweeps through shoulder/elbow/wrist/hand joints (radius 0.5 at the shoulder, 0.3 at the wrist, an armoured forearm), big paws with 4 chunky toes each ending in dark horn claws (cones, horn colour with hornTip tips), and a rear dew claw. Each leg wears an iron-bound leather cuff and a few overlapping armour-like scale plates (scaleLight). (4) Dorsal ridge: a row of 12 bone-coloured angular plates/spikes (extruded blades leaning back, tall and thin at the shoulders, getting lower toward the hips) seated on the top line of the torso from z=2.0 to the mount dorsalRidgeEnd, with boneDark bases. (5) Battle damage and Norse details: three deep scars across the left flank and one on the right (scar-coloured long thin slabs with pale bone ridge edges), a broken axe head (iron blade + rust edge, leather-wrapped haft stub) buried in the right shoulder, two snapped spear shafts (leather and bone) with iron arrowheads in the left flank, a chain remnant (chain-coloured torus links, about 10) draped across the chest ending in a spiked iron shackle, and rows of small carved runes (thin dark stroke parts with frost glowing inlays, glow kit) on the chest plate and each shoulder. Chest centre carries a big cracked bone-coloured breastplate shape with an ember glowing crack (emberHot).
parts.attaches: Neck sockets receive the head parts' neck sweeps at mounts neckBaseC, neckBaseIL, neckBaseIR, neckBaseOL, neckBaseOR; the rear of the torso (z=-2.4, width 1.2) ends where the tail begins at tailBase, and the dorsal ridge ends at dorsalRidgeEnd; the hindquarters part builds the rear thighs starting at rearHipL and rearHipR, inside the torso side. Rides joints hips, chest and the front leg joints.

parts.builds: The back end. (1) Rear legs BL and BR: massive digitigrade legs along hip/knee/hock/foot joints, with a big muscular thigh (radius 0.6 at the hip, tapering), a thinner shin angled back, a hock spur (bone spike) and a long foot with 3 forward toes and a rear toe, each with horn-coloured claws. Scales in scaleMid with scaleLight plates on the thigh front, bellyDark at the inner thigh, an iron-bound leather strap around each shin with 4 rivets, mud-dark (scaleDark) streaks at the feet. The left thigh has a chain-wrapped broken spear stuck in it. (2) Tail: a long thick tail from the mount tailBase (radius 0.6) through tail1..tail5, tapering to about 0.15 at tailTip (the tail tip must rest on y=0). Skinned to tail1..5, scaleDark on top, belly strip underneath, with a bone ridge of 14 plates getting smaller, and 5 spaced iron rings with spikes (a spiked war-collar look) along its length. The tip ends in a heavy bone-and-iron blade: a wide extruded leaf-shaped blade (bone with iron edges and a rust chip) plus two side barbs, and three runes glowing ember on the tail's flank. Some scars and one embedded rusted axe stuck in the tail's side, broken sword stubs, and a faded leather harness strap. A dark scar-coloured crescent wound on the rump with pale edges.
parts.attaches: Begins at mount tailBase, where the torso ends; rear legs start at rearHipL and rearHipR inside the torso's flanks (this part's thigh masses overlap the torso rear, z -2.5..-0.6), and the feet touch the floor at footContactBL and footContactBR; the tail ends at tailTip on the floor. Rides joints hips, tail1..tail5 and the rear leg joints.

parts.builds: The centre head C with its neck: the hero head, the biggest of the five. Neck: a thick sweep from neckBaseC through neckC1..neckC3 up to headC with radius 0.5 tapering to 0.36, scaleDark back with scaleMid sides, with a front row of bone-yellow ventral throat plates (about 8 slabs), a ridge of bone dorsal spikes (9, shrinking toward the head), a leather-and-iron collar with a few rivets mid-neck, and glowing ember runes (small straight strokes, glow kit) along each side. Head (skull from z 2.6 to 4.2, width 0.95, height 0.8, skull top about y 5.9): a heavy wedge skull, a long blocky snout with a flat top, a separate upper jaw and a separate lower jaw hinged at jawC (build the lower jaw as its own part on joint jawC, rest-opened about 8 degrees), both lined with thick off-white teeth (tooth colour; about 10 per side on top, 8 on the bottom, with 2 big fangs) set in mouth-red gums, a tongue (mouth) inside, and inside the mouth a faint ember glow. Face: two glowing eye (amber) spheres with eyeSlit vertical pupils under heavy scowling bone brow ridges (angular slabs), the left eye scarred with a long scar cut (scar with pale edge) across the brow and cheek; nostrils with small ember glows. Crown: four big back-swept curved horns (horn at the base, hornTip on the points, with iron cap bands and ember-glowing rune rings), two smaller cheek horns, and a fin-like frill of 5 extruded bone blades fanning back from the skull. A broken axe blade (iron with a rust edge) is stuck in the cheek, with a leather strap trailing. Chin: 3 bone spikes under the lower jaw. The mood is ember/molten: emberHot cracks on the snout.
parts.attaches: The neck starts inside the collar at mount neckBaseC (the torso part builds the socket); the head sits on mount skullC with the jaw hinge at jawHingeC. Rides neckC1, neckC2, neckC3, headC, jawC.

parts.builds: The two heads on the creature's left (+x) with their necks: inner-left IL and outer-left OL, each built with the same recipe as a smaller version of a hydra head (skull 1.35 long, 0.75 wide, 0.62 high; neck radius IL 0.42→0.3 and OL 0.38→0.27, sweeps from neckBaseIL/neckBaseOL through neckIL1..3/neckOL1..3 to headIL/headOL, bone [neckX1, neckX2, neckX3, headX]). Each has: separate upper jaw and lower jaw (jawIL/jawOL, rest-opened about 8 degrees) with rows of teeth and a mouth-red interior and tongue; two glowing eyes with slit pupils under angular brow ridges; nostrils; back-swept horns; a cheek frill of extruded blades; ventral throat plates and a dorsal spike row on the neck; a leather-and-iron collar with rivets. IL (frost head): frost-blue glowing eyes, glowing frost runes (glow kit) down both sides of the neck, horns of hornTip bone with frost-glowing crystal-shard tips, icy rime plates (scaleLight, frost) on the snout, a bone-coloured horn crown. OL (venom head, hangs lower and wider, angled down): venom-green glowing eyes, mouth and nostril glow in venom, drooling venom drips (small green teardrop parts) from the lower jaw teeth, a snapped-off left horn capped with an iron band, a long scar down the snout, a pair of tusks, and a chain with spiked iron shackle clamped round the neck. OL also gets rows of rust-coloured iron bolts along the jaw.
parts.attaches: Necks emerge from the iron collars at neckBaseIL and neckBaseOL (built by the torso part); heads sit at skullIL and skullOL, jaws hinge at jawHingeIL and jawHingeOL. Rides neckIL1-3, headIL, jawIL, neckOL1-3, headOL, jawOL.

parts.builds: The two heads on the creature's right (-x) with their necks: inner-right IR and outer-right OR, mirrored in position from the left heads but with their own identity. Each is built with the same recipe as a smaller hydra head (skull 1.35 long, 0.75 wide, 0.62 high; neck radius IR 0.42→0.3 and OR 0.38→0.27, sweeps from neckBaseIR/neckBaseOR through neckIR1..3/neckOR1..3 to headIR/headOR, bone [neckX1, neckX2, neckX3, headX]). Each has: separate upper jaw and lower jaw (jawIR/jawOR, rest-opened about 8 degrees) with teeth rows, mouth-red interior and tongue; two glowing eyes with slit pupils under angular brow ridges; nostrils; back-swept horns; a cheek frill of extruded blades; ventral throat plates and a dorsal spike row on the neck; a leather-and-iron collar with rivets. IR (venom head): venom-green eyes and runes (glow kit) down the neck, fanned horns in horn colour with hornTip points, venom-glow rim along the jaw, an arrowhead and a snapped spear shaft in the neck, scar slashes across the muzzle. OR (bone-and-iron head, hangs lower and wider, angled down): ember-glowing eyes, a heavy iron muzzle-cage (iron bands with rivets across the snout), a bone-plated skull crest of overlapping slabs (bone/boneDark), a broken-off horn on one side with a rust cap, long jagged tusks, chain links dangling from the muzzle band and a few ember glowing runes on the neck.
parts.attaches: Necks emerge from the iron collars at neckBaseIR and neckBaseOR (built by the torso part); heads sit at skullIR and skullOR, jaws hinge at jawHingeIR and jawHingeOR. Rides neckIR1-3, headIR, jawIR, neckOR1-3, headOR, jawOR.

calls.reasoning:
I'm designing a five-headed hydra in a gritty God of War aesthetic, with rune-carved scars, glowing marks, and frost/battle-worn texture. I'm planning the structure as a sturdy four-legged body with a tail and five long serpentine necks, dividing the build into body and neck/head sections for separate crafting.

Settling on five parts: bodyLegs, tail, headCenter, headsLeft, headsRight. Now I'm sketching the skeleton proportions — overall size roughly 7x6x9 units, with torso centered around the hips, four legs splayed, necks fanning out from the shoulders at varying heights and forward reach, and the tail extending backward to balance the total length.

Now I'm planning the joint hierarchy: a root hip joint, a chest joint, and then per-neck chains (base, mid, tip, head, jaw) following a consistent naming pattern so each head/neck builder can reference its own set of joints.

Now I'm sketching out actual coordinates for the body — chest position, torso box bounds, and leg placements for front/rear pairs — then designing each neck as an S-curve with three joint positions feeding into the sweep geometry.

I'm working out the outer limb positions, spreading the second branch's heads lower and outward for variety while keeping mouths closed in a resting pose, then checking the overall width budget comes out around 6.8 units. Now I'm setting up the head joint frames anchored at the back of each skull.

I'm figuring out jaw hinge placement relative to the skull geometry for the center head, estimating coordinates near the rear-bottom of the mouth, then starting to work through naming conventions for the limb joints since underscores aren't allowed in the regex pattern.

Settling on a naming scheme using prefixes like "IL" (inner left), "OL" (outer left), "IR", "OR", and "C" for center, applied consistently to neck, head, and jaw joints. I'm also laying out the skeleton hierarchy: hips as root, chest as child of hips, then neck segments chaining up to head and jaw, with legs branching off hips.

Now I'm figuring out actual coordinates for the hips and chest, then working through the rear leg chain for a digitigrade reptilian stance—placing hip, knee, hock, and foot joints so the leg bends forward at the knee and back at the hock like a bird or lizard leg.

Naming the four legs consistently (hip/knee/hock/foot for back, shoulder/elbow/wrist/hand for front) using BL/BR/FL/FR suffixes, then laying out five tail joints trailing back and down so the tip rests on the floor.

Now I'm plotting the three neck-and-head chains (center, inner-left, outer-left) with arching joint coordinates and jaw positions, planning to mirror the inner/outer chains to the right side, before starting to list out the actual body parts beginning with the torso loft.

For the overall aesthetic I'm leaning toward a Norse God of War-style hydra: cracked stone-like scales, glowing orange rune carvings, embedded broken weapons from fallen warriors, fur pelts, iron rings, and scarred chest armor, with neck-root collars where the heads emerge from the shoulder mass.

I'm now picking out a muted, desaturated palette—swamp green-gray scales with darker shadow tones, bone-yellow belly, reddish scar marks, ember-orange glow for rune carvings, icy blue glow accents, and dark iron tones.

I'm also allocating my element budget: keeping the total under 900 units, splitting roughly 220 for the body/legs, 130 for the tail with spines and embedded axes, 150 for the central head, and 200 each for the left and right heads.

Each head part needs to own its neck geometry, sweeping from joints at the torso base, so I'm defining mount points like neckBaseC, neckBaseIL, and neckBaseIR with varying root radii—around 0.5 for the center neck and slightly smaller for the outer ones—anchored near the top of the torso.

The torso itself peaks around y3.3 at the shoulders, with a hump structure built by the leg system that buries the neck roots in its collar area; the tail similarly attaches at a hip joint mount near the rear taper of the torso, with its own base radius and a dorsal ridge running along its length.

I want to give the dorsal ridge a defined path using the torso's top profile line, tracing height values from the shoulders back to the tail tip so ridge plates can seat correctly at each station despite the torso and tail being built separately.

Continuing down the tail segments, I want the tip to taper and actually touch the floor, so I'm adjusting the radii and heights so the last segment grazes the ground, maybe adding bone spurs or a blade-like fin at the end for a hydra-style flourish.

I'm assigning the dorsal ridge ownership: torso owns the ridge on its back, while the tail owns its own ridge continuing down the length, so the boxes don't overlap. I'll flesh out the tail part further with bone ridge plates, a fan-shaped blade tip, and iron shackle rings with broken chain remnants for extra detail.

Then I'm rethinking the split so bodyLegs doesn't get overloaded—maybe the tail part should also claim the rear legs and haunches, leaving bodyLegs with just the torso, front legs, neck sockets, and chest, so the hindquarters become their own grouped region with its own bounding box.

Now I'm working through the polygon budget allocation across body parts: tail and rear legs with claws for hindquarters, then torso front with belly plates, chest armor, embedded weapons, and runes, plus three separate heads each needing their own budget. Adding it up I'm over 900 total, so I need to trim allocations down—reducing bodyFront to 210, hindquarters to 140, and center head to 150 to bring things back in line.

I'm settling on a grim Norse God of War aesthetic with scarring, embers and frost, rune carvings, and broken weaponry, then building out a restrained color palette of under 24 hues covering dark and light scale tones, belly colors, scars, bone, horn, iron, rust, leather, chain, and ember accents.

Now I'm working out the shared head anatomy — wedge skulls, snouts, brow ridges, horns, frills, glowing nostrils, slit eyes, jaws with teeth, necks with belly plates and spikes — and giving each head its own identity: the crowned center head with four horns and a scarred blind eye, the inner-left head with a horn crest, the outer-left head with a tusk and iron-capped stump, and the inner-right head with frost-blue runes, assigning each an elemental theme like fire, frost, and venom.

I'm settling on a final elemental assignment across the four heads — center as ember/fire, one head frost, another venom green, and considering a bone-spiked variant with an iron muzzle shackle and chain for added character — then moving into describing the rest pose with necks separated and mouths closed slightly.

Now I'm building out the joint hierarchy: hips as root, chest as parent, then the tail chain through five segments, assigning positions and directions for each to set up the spine and tail structure.

I'm also working out the rear leg chain from hip through knee, hock, and foot, estimating positions and directions so the leg bends forward at the knee and back at the hock before planting the foot with toes pointing forward.

For the front legs, I'm placing shoulder, elbow, wrist, and paw joints down the chest, with the elbow angled back and the wrist curving forward into the paw. Then I'm setting up the neck joints branching from the chest, grouping each head's chain under its own named group like "headC".

Now I'm working out the skull mounts — defining the neck base, head center, jaw hinge, and mouth tip positions, plus torso and tail reference lines and foot contact points. I'm sizing the skulls: the center head longer and wider than the two outer heads, with the lower jaw proportioned similarly but slightly shorter. I'm also tapering the neck radii from base to head for each of the three necks before working out the sweep path connecting neck to skull.

Settling on final size [6.8,6.5,11.4] with the hydra centered on x, and linking the body's dorsal ridge seam to where the tail ridge begins. Now I'm thinking through part descriptions and lighting—using glow selectively for embers, frost, eyes, and runes since painted surfaces can't glow—and locking in the God of War style guide: brutal, chunky, scarred, cold desaturated palette with ember/frost accents, carved rune glyphs, bone, horn, and iron detailing.

Working out the neck and head joint chain coordinates and tangent directions, positioning headC and jawC so the skull geometry (spanning roughly z 2.5 to 4.6 with teeth included) lines up correctly with the third neck joint.

Continuing outer layer neck joints through to the jaw, then starting to lay out bounding boxes for the head and neck regions.

Defining mount points...

I'm figuring out how to type the function signature for buildHeadsLeft, deciding whether Ctx is already defined in scope or if I need a fallback type to avoid errors.

Now I'm planning the actual geometry: using catmull-rom sweeps through the neck joint chain from base to head, then constructing the skull and snout shapes positioned relative to the head joint's local coordinate frame, with a helper function to place points using forward/up/side offsets.

Working out the jaw hinge position relative to the head joint, then sizing the lower jaw to extend forward from that hinge roughly matching the upper skull's length.

The jaw's direction vector points slightly differently than the head's, so I'm thinking through whether to pose the jaw open after building it, since rigid parts attached to a joint should rotate along with it. I'll build the jaw geometry in a closed position relative to the head's orientation first, then apply the rest-open rotation afterward.

I should build all the jaw and teeth parts first, since their positions are computed relative to the head frame anyway, and apply the jaw pose rotation last so everything rides along with the joint. I'll make sure every part explicitly specifies its bone and anchor point rather than relying on surface attachment, keeping things consistent through local frame placement.

For head orientation, I realize geometries built with default world axes won't align with the slightly tilted head direction, so I need to apply the joint's quaternion to rotate local geometry axes into the bone's forward/up convention -- designing shapes in joint-local coordinates where X is right, Y is forward along the bone, and Z is up, then letting h.quat handle the actual world alignment.

I'm planning a helper function that places geometry at a joint using word-based offsets and the joint's quaternion, optionally composed with an extra local rotation for fine adjustments. I just need to confirm the quaternion is valid and current after posing, since I'm applying poses before placing geometry.

Since the head joint is the parent of the jaw, posing the jaw shouldn't affect the head's own transform. I'm aligning the jaw parts to the head's orientation first, then rotating the jaw open by roughly 8 degrees about world X relative to that base, which should look right even though the jaw's actual hinge axis differs slightly from head alignment. For left/right placement, I'm treating positive "left" as the model's +x direction in word-based offsets.

Now I'm sketching out the head's block dimensions — cranium width, length, and height in meters relative to the head joint, with separate scale factors for inner and outer layers, plus a sloped back-skull section to avoid a purely blocky look.

I need to work out the snout geometry too, but I'm catching an important subtlety: the local-direction helper interprets numbers as "model forward/up/left" rather than along the bone's own axis, which differs from how array-based frame coordinates work. I need to reconcile these two coordinate conventions before building the frustum boxes for the snout.

Setting local x to negative L confirms left offset, and I verify the quat orientation matches the aim direction convention. For the snout, I'm writing a tapered box helper that builds a unit BoxGeometry and remaps vertices along the length axis, interpolating width and height from base to tip.

Now I'm planning out the per-head part budget—roughly 100 parts each for 200 total—and sketching the cranium and snout pieces with layered colors (mid, dark top plate, light ridges) using tapered boxes at specific dimensions and offsets.

I'm working out the precise vertical coordinates for the skull: cranium spanning roughly -0.31 to 0.31, the jaw hinge around u=-0.2, upper snout from 0.2 down to the palate at -0.12, and the lower jaw sitting below with a small gap to form the mouth interior, figuring out heights and centers for each box so they align correctly.

I'm planning gum strips (thin red boxes under the upper snout and atop the lower jaw), a tapered tongue box using a darker mouth-red variant, and a small interior glow element near the back of the mouth to hint at venom, frost, or ember breath depending on variant.

For teeth, I'm figuring out counts per jaw (upper rows with fangs, lower rows) and realizing the part budget is tight, so I'll merge each jaw's teeth into a single geometry using BufferGeometryUtils' merge function rather than keeping them as separate parts. I need a helper that transforms each tooth's local geometry into model space using the head's position/rotation before merging, so the combined mesh sits correctly relative to the skull.

I realize ExtrudeGeometry is non-indexed, so mixing with indexed geometries breaks merging — I'll normalize everything to non-indexed with just position/normal/uv before combining. For neck details like the collar, runes, and spikes, I'll place them using sweep frame matrices along the neck chain, sticking geometry at each frame and merging to keep part counts low.

For rigging, I'll derive orientation from each frame's quaternion and assign each item a single nearest bone based on position along the sweep, bucketing merges by bone name plus color so the total part count stays under control, roughly 200 or so.

Now I'm working out the clock-angle convention for the neck — 0° marking the dorsal/back side and 180° the ventral/front side, but since the neck rises up and tilts forward at 45-60°, I need to reconsider which side actually counts as ventral once the tube is no longer purely vertical.

So confirming: 0 is up, 90 is −X, meaning left side is −90. Both runes sit at ±90, but I need to figure out which outward orientation applies to each head's left side specifically.

Now I'm working through the torso-to-neck connection: the collars form at the neck base, with each neck following a path through its segment mounts into the head joint. Since the skull spans forward to about -0.35 and the neck enters from behind-below, I need to extend the neck path slightly into the cranium so it doesn't poke through visibly at the joint.

I'll keep the existing joints for the curve and set color sectors so the belly and dark scale bands wrap around the body, with bone-yellow throat plates layered on top near the midline. Then I'll call the sweep function with the neck's joint list, radius, color, and sector settings to build the mesh.

Writing plate geometry code...

Rotating by −θ instead, with spikes shrinking in height toward the head, using bone and boneDark colors for the base cones. For the mid-neck collar, I realize a torus works perfectly since its axis aligns naturally with the tangent direction at that point on the sweep, so I can position it right at t≈0.45 using the frame's Z axis.

I'm computing the torus center by offsetting from the sweep point along the normal by the radius, then layering an iron band torus, a leather strap torus offset along the tangent, and six small rivet spheres arranged around the ring using cosine/sine positions in the frame's XY plane.

Now I'm planning the frost rune decorations running down both sides of the collar at roughly ±80-90 degree angles, sampling along the sweep path and building each rune from a thin dark carved base box.

I'm designing a rune glyph builder that generates stroke segments in a unit square, merging the glow-enabled inlay pieces per bone into buckets keyed by name, color, and glow strength so they render efficiently together. For orientation, I'm setting up each rune's local frame so it lies flush against the neck surface, drawn in the across/tangent plane with its thin thickness along the normal direction.

I'm working out the correct rotation math so each segment's box aligns with its intended direction vector, then adding a darker carved base patch beneath each rune's glowing inlay for visual depth, and composing the transform matrices for the sweep frames.

Checking that the rune patches sit correctly on the curved neck surface without excessive sag given the cylinder's radius, and confirming the geometry stays hidden properly on side faces. Now I'm starting to define the head builder function that will take a config object specifying tag and head joint data.

Still defining head config structure...

Checking the actual joint offset against my approximated hinge position, the discrepancy comes out tiny — maybe a centimeter or so of shift, which is negligible since rotating about the joint location barely affects the rest pose at this scale.

Now I'm verifying the skull geometry stays within the bounding box: checking that the snout tip, cheek frills, and swept-back horns don't exceed the box limits for width and height on both the outer and inner layers.

I'm also placing the eyes on the cranium sides, deciding on their position and outward-forward orientation, and working out the slit pupil shape as a thin dark box inset into each eye.

Still orienting eye geometry...

Working through the rotation sign so that the inner brow end tilts downward correctly for each side, I derive θ = −0.35·e, flipping sign depending on which side e represents.

Now I'm placing facial details: nostrils positioned near the snout tip with small flattened glow spheres and dark recesses, plus bone-colored bumps on the snout tip for texture.

I'm adding angular armor plates across the snout and cranium in a "God of War" style, then building cheek frills from five extruded blade shapes fanning backward per side, mapping each blade's local plane to curve outward and up from the head.

Working out blade orientation for each...

I'm fanning the frills horizontally like a triceratops crest, spreading blade directions from backward to outward angles with slight vertical staggering per spike, sized around 0.38-0.5 long and 0.14 wide, and coloring them bone with a darker band near the base.

For the horns, I'm planning backswept curved sweeps using catmull paths with banded coloring—bone-colored shaft transitioning to a frost-glowing crystal-shard tip, plus a small crown ring of bone spikes near the base.

I'm laying out the horn structure per head: two larger upswept horns plus two smaller secondary ones, computing their path points in head-local coordinates. For the "snapped-off" variant, I'm handling the left horn separately with an iron band cap replacing the crystal tip.

Still placing horn tip coordinates, checking they stay within the head-size constraint box, and making sure the backswept horn curve doesn't collide with the frill geometry near the cheek.

Now I'm working out teeth placement along the snout edge—seven teeth per side spaced along the tapering snout width, positioned at the palate's bottom edge, using small downward-pointing cones that need their rotation flipped to aim correctly in local coordinates.

I'm also adding bigger fang cones near the front, a small incisor row, more teeth lower down, and planning the curved tusks jutting from the lower jaw as called for.

Now I'm figuring out bone assignments: skull parts to the head bone, teeth and jaw plates to the jaw bone, and the tusks as sweeps that ride along the jaw's path. I'm also adding venom drip shapes—teardrop forms with a green glow—attached to the lower jaw teeth.

For posing, I'm applying the jaw rotation and head tilt last, after all geometry is attached, so the hierarchical bone poses propagate correctly. For the ice variant specifically, I'm placing frost-colored eyes, runic markings along the neck, crystalline tips on the horns, and rime plates along the snout, keeping the plates a darker frost tone rather than glowing.

I'm settling on a small custom palette for the ice variant—pale rime, dark frost, dark tongue, and dark mouth interior—plus a dark venom tone, and arranging a ring of bone spikes across the back of the cranium leaning backward for the horn crown. Now I'm starting on the other variant's specifics, giving it glowing venom-colored eyes and a glowing mouth.

For the venom-themed details, I'm adding glowing green venom pooling in the mouth and nostrils, hanging teardrop drips below the lower jaw teeth, a snapped horn with an iron band repair, a long scar with bone-ridge edges down the snout, paired tusks, a spiked iron shackle-and-chain around the neck, and rows of rusted iron bolts along the jawline. Writing chain link geometry...

I'm alternating link rotation about Y and tying each to its bone. Now I'm planning neck collars with rivets for each head, placing them at different points along the neck depending on side, plus adding scars—a long one on the snout for one head and a smaller neck scar for flavor on the other. I'm also shaping a tapered tongue box positioned in the lower jaw.

Next I'm working out a faint glow element deep in the throat, positioning it behind the gums so it's only visible through the jaw gap when opened, using frost/venom coloring with moderate glow strength. I'm also sketching the lower jaw's tapered geometry and starting on the underlip plate bones.

Thinking about chin detailing, I'll skip extra bone spikes and keep it simple, coloring the lower jaw with scaleMid and the chin plates with belly tones. I'm also adding a jaw hinge piece connecting the cheek block to the lower jaw, tapering the box and setting a rotation point so the rear portion tucks up into the cranium when the jaw moves.

For the skull rear I'm adding an occiput box with a dark top plate, stacking small light-colored slabs along the snout bridge as a ridge, and placing rivets along the ridgeline. For the eyes I'm building a dark sunken socket sphere behind each eye, with the eyeball itself a smaller glowing sphere using slit pupils, varying the glow color by faction. I'm organizing all these pieces into merge buckets grouped by bone, color, and glow to keep the part count manageable.

Adding ~25 colors across a few bones per head keeps the total around 100 parts, well under the 200 limit, and I'm checking the neck sweeps and sectors to see how many separate meshes each needs before moving on to the triangle budget count.

Tallying up the triangle costs: teeth cones at ~10 tris each across 60 per head, chain link toruses reduced to lower segment counts to stay near 720 tris, boxes at 12 tris, neck sweep rings around 400 each, and extruded blade shapes at roughly 30 tris apiece — all adding toward the 12000 total budget for both heads.

I'm deciding to pass flat:true on all merged parts for crisp faceted shading, checking that non-indexed geometries will compute proper faceted normals, and setting neck sweeps to use 8 sides with smooth shading disabled to keep the blocky low-poly look consistent.

Now I'm working out the neck radius tapers as arrays for both heads and sketching path points for the neck curves.

For the OL side, I'm checking the geometry where the neck meets the skull: since the neck rises up-forward while the head pitches down, the neck tip approaches the skull from below-behind, which keeps it tucked inside the cranium correctly.

Now I'm setting up helper types and a bucket system to group geometries by color and bone for building out the mesh pieces efficiently.

I'm working out a placement helper that composes world transforms for each bone joint, converting left-forward-up coordinates into the scene's coordinate system, and confirming uniform scaling and matrix application stays consistent across parts.

Mirroring only applies to position, not geometry, since rotated or extruded pieces use proper rotations rather than flipped winding. Now I'm starting to define the per-part builder functions, beginning with the head construction logic.

Writing part placement helpers...

I'm working out the local axis conventions—X right, Y forward, Z up—and how rotations map to pitch, yaw, and roll for the head geometry. I'm also sketching a taperBox helper that scales a unit box's x/z dimensions along its y-axis to create tapered shapes like teeth or horns.

Writing taper function...

Now I'm calculating the actual dimensions for the head components — cranium taper spans and the top plate position, working out how they stack with slight overlaps so the plate sits just above the cranium.

Adding cheek plates and occiput, then adjusting the overall skull proportions so the snout length brings the total closer to the target 1.35, repositioning cranium and snout boundaries accordingly.

Now I'm working out tapered width functions for the upper and lower jaw shapes, figuring out how the snout narrows toward the front and how the jaw planes slant relative to each other.

I need to check that the upper and lower teeth don't overlap awkwardly—upper teeth hang down while lower teeth point up, and I'm positioning them along the width so they interleave visually rather than clash.

Now I'm placing the gums: a tapered strip under the upper jaw attached to the head, and another along the top of the lower jaw attached to the jaw bone, both in mouth color. I'm adding a small tongue shape with its own reddish color riding on the jaw bone, plus a glow slab inside the mouth cavity for visual depth. I'm considering whether a palate detail is needed too.

I'm skipping that and moving to brow ridges, working out where eye sockets sit relative to the cranium's tapering width at that height, computing the eye sphere's protrusion past the skull surface, and figuring out the local-space normal vector to position each pupil correctly on the eye's outward-facing side.

Still writing geometry helpers...

So θ simplifies to 0.35*e for the brow rotation about local Y, confirming the sign convention matches three.js's axis-angle rotation. I'll also consider adding a small dark scowl wedge beneath the brow near the inner edge, though it might be skippable in favor of a heavier brow using the horn color.

Now I'm working out the snout tip geometry — placing dark recessed nostril boxes near the front face with a small glowing inset, and considering whether to add a tapered snout cap plate at the very tip rather than a separate nose bump.

For the snout ridge I'm adding a dark plate along the top plus three lighter transverse plates that step down in height toward the top, positioned just above the computed top curve. For the rime variant, I'm placing frost-colored side plates along the snout and scattering small four-sided crystal cones on the snout top and brow for a frosted look.

Now I'm working on the horns, sweeping a tube along a curved path of transformed points through the horn's bone matrix, tapering the radius and coloring it with a band split near the tip for a lighter horn-tip shade.

I decide to add iron cap bands as separate torus rings positioned along the horn using its sweep frame — building a helper that places a ring's center by offsetting from the sweep curve by its local radius. I'm setting the horn's base radius and tapering it down toward the tip.

Now I'm designing crystal tips at the horn's end: an elongated octahedron scaled and oriented along the sweep tangent at t=1, with a frosty glow and smaller angled shards accenting it.

For the smaller horns, I'm placing back-swept cheek horns near the jaw and brow outer edges, adjusting their paths so they don't collide with the frill fan positioned lower on the back.

For the snapped left horn, I'm sweeping a shorter stub path with a flat end cap, then adding an iron band cylinder ring around the broken tip plus a small jagged bone fracture cone for the damaged look.

Now I'm working out neck plate placement, figuring out which neck joint each sweep point should bind to for fallback safety, then setting up the sweep frame matrix using position and quaternion. Writing neck plate geometry loop...

Still writing belly plate geometry...

Now thinking through dorsal spikes along the neck—placing nine cones, sinking their bases slightly, then leaning them backward along the tangent direction to follow the neck's curve naturally.

Next I'm planning the rune glyphs running along the neck sides, with four positions per side and distinct glyph shapes built from small segments in unit coordinates.

Still defining rune coordinates...

Defining a generic placement helper...

For the scar details, I'm planning a diagonal box scar on the OL snout with paler bone-colored edges flanking it, plus small cross-tick boxes to suggest stitches. spec.name: Hydra of the Broken Axes
spec.description: A scarred, battle-worn five-headed Norse hydra in a gritty God of War style: slate-green scales, bone horns, rusted iron bands and embedded broken weapons, with ember-orange eyes and frost-blue runes glowing against the muted pelt.
spec.layout: A huge four-legged reptilian brute standing on a bare floor. It faces +Z. The body is a heavy barrel with a high shoulder hump, from z -2.0 to 2.3 and about y 1.2 to 3.3. Four thick pillar legs stand at x = ±1.1..1.55: short stocky forelegs at the front and digitigrade hindlegs behind. A long low tail runs back to z = -5.1, tapering to a bone spade tip. Five necks rise from the shoulder hump (z ~1.5, y ~2.8) in a fan, each an S-curve ending in a head that looks forward (+Z). From the centre outward the head heights are: centre (x 0, head y ~5.0, tallest, alpha, biggest, scale 1.25), inner pair (x ±2.0, head y ~4.5, scale 1.0), outer pair (x ±2.95, head y ~3.55, lowest, angled outward, scale 0.85). Rest pose: necks spread apart and extended, every jaw built as a separate upper and lower jaw so it can open, tails and legs extended and neutral. Style (God of War): heavy, brutal, weathered, grounded. Chunky blocky silhouettes and faceted low-poly forms. Desaturated cold slate-green hide with paler weathered ash-bone belly and throat plates. Every part is scarred: long pale scar-tissue gashes, cauterised burn patches, broken horn tips wrapped in iron bands, chipped teeth. Worn rusty iron and bronze bands, chains and rivets show past battles. Broken weapons (axe heads, spear tips, a chain-link wrap) are embedded in hide. Warm ember-orange glow on eyes, wounds and scars, and cold frost-blue glow on carved Nordic runes. Colour is only by place: darker scales on the back, lighter belly and underside, ash/mud at the feet, rust at the iron. Parts reach the same joints through shared mounts so seams hide inside overlapping volumes. Necks start buried inside the torso.

A big shoulder hump with five collar mounds (scaleMid, each ringed with small bone spikes) where each neck enters, at neckBaseC/IL/IR/OL/OR, so the necks emerge from inside the body. A dorsal ridge of broad overlapping bone plates and spikes (bone with boneDark bases) running from the hump to the rump, big at the shoulders and small at the hips. Rib bands and belly plates (bellyDark rows). Battle damage: three long pale scar gashes (scar) across the flanks, with a few ember-glowing seams, and two cauterised burn patches (ash and blood). Embedded broken weapons: an axe head (iron with a rust edge and a broken leather-wrapped shaft stump) stuck in the left flank, and a snapped spear tip in the right shoulder. A rusty chain (ironDark/rust torus links) loosely wrapped diagonally around the barrel with an iron buckle plate. Carved Nordic rune brand on each flank, 5 runes as small parts glowing frost, in a ring of ironDark. spec.name: Hydra of the Blighted Marsh
spec.description: A five-headed hydra in a God of War style: a scarred, armored Norse-myth beast with a bulky body, four legs, a heavy tail, and five fanged heads on long necks, each with a glowing eye, with chains, runes and broken weapons stuck in its hide.

Dark green-grey scaled hide has paler belly plates, and cold blue-iron armour plates with rivets are chained onto the shoulders and back. Carved pale-blue glowing runes, scar slashes, broken spear shafts and axe blades stuck in the hide, and bone spikes down the spine give the God of War look. Every colour is a flat colour per part.

spec.name: Hydra of the Broken Pass
spec.description: A five-headed hydra in a God of War style: a scarred, armoured swamp-beast with five fanged serpent necks, chained iron-shackled limbs, rune-lit scars and bronze-bound horns.
spec.layout: A massive four-legged reptile body low to the ground, lying along Z with the chest toward +Z and a thick tail trailing to -Z. Five long S-curved necks rise from the shoulders and fan out in a rest pose: one centre neck straight up and forward, two left and two right spread wide at about 25 and 55 degrees, with heads at differing heights (2.6 to 4.4 m). Each head is a blocky wedge with separate upper and lower jaw, big fangs, glowing amber eyes, brow ridges and swept horns. The body is covered in dark slate scale plates with bone-coloured ridge spikes along the spine and the necks. Broken iron shackles with chain links hang from the forelegs and some necks, with rusted bronze bands. Glowing red-orange rune scars and an ember chest wound light the body. Palette is ashen grey-green hide, blood red accents, bone, rusted bronze and ember glow. Heavy, brutal, angular shapes with chunky stylised proportions.

parts.builds: Hulking body loft from hips to chest in hide/hideLight with a pale belly sector, scale-plate paint, a row of bone spine spikes along the back, shoulder and hip armour mounds, ember-lit rune scars (small glow parts) across the flanks and a glowing chest wound, rusted bronze bands with iron plates around the barrel. parts.attaches: Legs hang from legFL/FR/BL/BR joints at the torso sides; the tail starts at tailRoot.

parts.builds: The centre neck (neck0a, neck0b) and the inner left and right necks (neckL1a/b, neckR1a/b): tapered S-curved sweeps in hide with belly-pale underside, bone ridge spikes along the top, bronze bands, iron collar with hanging chain pieces on one, and the three heads (head0, headL1, headR1) each with upper skull wedge, separate lower jaw on its jaw joint, mouthRed interior, rows of bone fangs, nostrils, glowing eyeAmber eyes with ink slits, brow ridges and swept horns in bone/bronze.

spec.name: Nostromo Galley
spec.description: A cutaway corner of a grimy 1979 commercial-tug galley: steel counters, range with hood, tall fridge and lockers, a bolted mess table with benches, exposed pipes and amber CRT glow.
spec.layout: A cutaway room module, 3.8 m wide (x) by 3.8 m long (z) by 2.6 m tall, viewed from the open front (+Z). The deck slab is y 0..0.08 and covers x ±1.9, z ±1.9. Two walls stand on it: the BACK bulkhead (inner face z = -1.8, outer face z = -1.9) and the RIGHT bulkhead (inner face x = -1.8, outer face x = -1.9). Both are 2.6 m tall. The LEFT side (+X) is open apart from a short end bulkhead with a round hatch doorway at x = 1.85 (z -0.5..0.8); the front stays open. Along the back wall runs the counter-and-range run (x -1.1..1.75, depth to z -1.1). Along the right wall runs the fridge and locker run (a tall fridge in the back corner, then base units and a dispenser out to z = 1.0, depth to x -1.1). A long bolted mess table with a bench on each side stands in the centre (table x ±0.55, z -0.7..0.9). Overhead sit a hood over the range, a pipe bundle, ceiling beams, lamp panels, a hanging utensil rail and a swing-arm CRT monitor. Style: everything is hard-edged boxes and cylinders in dull, dirty, lived-in industrial plastic and steel. The walls are faded beige-cream panels with dark ribbed seams, and every cabinet has rivet rows, recessed handles and scuffed darker strips at the kick plates. There are yellow/black hazard stripes, stencilled numbers and warning labels built as small thin boxes, orange and copper pipes, and chunky toggle switches. Each lived-in detail is its own thin part (grime streaks, rust patches, drips). Only the small lights and screens glow (amber, green CRT, cyan, red). Everything else stays matte. No curves beyond 8-12 segment cylinders.

parts.builds: The room enclosure and its dressing. The deck slab (deckGrey) y 0..0.08 over x ±1.9 and z ±1.9, with diamond-plate-style grating strips (grating, thin boxes in a grid) laid on the deck walkway between the table and the counters, and bolted floor plates with rivet heads. A yellow/black hazard stripe border (many alternating thin hazardYellow/hazardBlack slanted boxes) along the front edge of both counter runs and around the hatch. The back bulkhead and right bulkhead are built from tall wallBeige panels (about 0.6 m wide, 0.04 m thick) separated by wallDark vertical ribs and horizontal seam bars at y 0.95, 1.5 and 2.3. They carry rivet rows, hullGrey base skirting with a grime strip, a few rust and grime streak patches, stencilled number plates (small panelCream plates with dark thin bars as digits), warning label rectangles (hazardYellow with hazardBlack bars) and conduit runs (orangePipe and copper small tubes with clamps) running vertically near the corners. The left end bulkhead at x = 1.85 has a round hatch frame (octagonal ring of steelDark, with a wheel lock handle) and wall segments either side. Includes the wall light-switch panels and a few cable bundles (blackRubber) hanging along the walls. It builds NO furniture, counters, ceiling beams or lamps.
parts.attaches: Inner wall faces are the mounts backWallFace (z = -1.8) and rightWallFace (x = -1.8). The deck top (y = 0.08) is the mount deckTop that every other part stands on. The hatch is at leftHatch. Nothing from other parts should be built inside the wall thickness.

parts.builds: The counter run along the back wall, x -1.1..1.75, depth z -1.78..-1.1, standing on the deck at y 0.08 with its top at y 0.95. Base cabinets of steel (steel/steelDark) with recessed handle bars, rivet rows, door seams and a grime kick plate (blackRubber, 0.1 m high). A countertop slab (stainless) with a raised lip and scuff marks. Left part (x -1.1..-0.6): a prep counter holding a cutting board (panelCream), a knife block and a utensil pot. Sink (x -0.6..0.2, centred at sinkCentre): a double stainless basin with dark recesses, a swan-neck faucet in copper/steel with a handle, a drain grille and a dish rack with plates. Range (x 0.2..1.2, centred at rangeCentre): a stove with four burner rings (blackRubber rings, steelDark grates, small amber glowing indicator dots), a front control panel with five chunky knobs and tiny label strips, an oven door with a window (blackRubber with an amber glow strip) and a handle bar, plus a pot with a lid and a steaming kettle on the burners. Right part (x 1.2..1.75): a coffee machine (hullGrey body with a cyanLed glowing display, a red LED, a drip tray and a carafe), a stack of food trays, and a small microwave unit (panelCream with a dark window and a glowing timer digit panel in greenCRT). Shallow wall shelf blocks above are NOT included. The hood is built by the overhead part.
parts.attaches: Rests on deckTop. Back faces touch backWallFace (z = -1.8). The range centre is the mount rangeCentre, the sink the mount sinkCentre and the counter top the mount counterTop. Its x = -1.1 end meets the fridge's side at the back-right corner (the fridge body occupies x < -1.1).

parts.builds: The cold storage and locker run along the right wall (inner face x = -1.8), occupying x -1.78..-1.1. A tall fridge in the back corner (z -1.78..-1.1, height 2.0, centred at fridgeFront): a panelCream and hullGrey body with a two-door split (freezer on top), heavy vertical handle bars, a steel latch with a lever, hinge cylinders, a seal strip (blackRubber), a hazard label plate and a frost-blue recessed vent. A glowing cyanLed temperature display with a tiny digit block and a red LED. Then base units along the wall (z -1.1..1.0, top y 0.95, rightCounterTop): drawer fronts (steel) with recessed handles and rivet corners, a rounded-box trash compactor with a foot pedal and a warning label, a built-in drink and soup dispenser (hullGrey housing, 3 nozzles, a drip grille, a glowing amber display with a greenCRT cursor bar and push buttons), and a countertop set with a toaster, a stack of bowls (mugWhite), a canned goods stack (steel cans with foodRed and foodGreen label bands) and a bread box. A locker bank on the wall above the base units (y 1.25..2.0, z -1.0..0.9): five small steel hatch doors with latches, number stencils and an orangePipe strip. Everything stays at x < -1.1 on the room side and is flush against the wall at x = -1.8.
parts.attaches: Rests on deckTop. The back face touches rightWallFace (x = -1.8). The fridge corner shares the back-right corner with the back run's end at x = -1.1. The base units' top is the mount rightCounterTop.

parts.builds: The central mess table set and the two benches. The table (tableCentre, top at y 0.78) has a thick hullGrey top slab (x ±0.55, z -0.7..0.9) with a steel edge rim and rivet heads, a grime-worn scuffed centre strip and a hazard-yellow edge stripe at each end. Two chunky pedestal bases (steelDark, square, each with a bolted foot flange and floor bolts) at z -0.35 and z 0.55. Two bolted benches (x ±0.65..±0.95 around the table, seat height 0.46) with panelCream padded seats, blackRubber seat edge strips, steelDark legs with cross braces and foot plates. Tableware: six steel food trays with compartments (alternating foodGreen and foodRed blobs as flattened spheres and boxes), mugs (mugWhite cylinders with handle loops and a dark coffee disc on top), a water pitcher, salt and pepper shakers, a sauce bottle with a red cap, forks and spoons (thin steel boxes), a folded napkin, a dropped spoon, a half-eaten food tin with a lid, a handheld data-pad with a small greenCRT screen, and a smear of grime and a spilled drop (small flat discs). Items sit on the table top at y 0.78 or on the bench seats.
parts.attaches: Feet rest on deckTop. The table centre is the mount tableCentre, the bench seats are benchSeatL (x +0.8) and benchSeatR (x -0.8). It clears the back run (z < -1.1) and the right run (x < -1.1).

parts.builds: Everything hanging above y 1.45 plus wall-mounted fittings. The range hood above the range (x 0.2..1.2, z -1.78..-1.05, centred on hoodBase y 1.65..2.1): a tapered steel box with a dark underside grille, a greasy grime band, an amber glowing lamp strip underneath, and a rectangular duct rising to the ceiling at y 2.55 with clamp bands and rivets. Ceiling: five steelDark I-beams across x at y 2.45..2.55 (z -1.6, -0.8, 0, 0.8, 1.6), rib bars along z, and four recessed flat lamp panels (panelCream frames with an amber/cream glowing face) between the beams. A pipe bundle (pipeBundle, x -0.9, y 2.4) of four parallel tubes (orangePipe, copper, steel, hullGrey) along z -1.8..1.0 with flanges, valve wheels (red, small) and drip stains. A hanging utensil rail at utensilRail (y 1.6, z -1.72, x -0.9..1.7): a steel tube with ladles, spatulas, a whisk and a hanging pan with a cast-iron look (blackRubber) and hook rings. Two wall shelves above the sink (y 1.4 and 1.8, x -0.7..0.1) carrying jars and cans (rust, foodGreen, steel) with stencil labels. A swing-arm CRT monitor on the right wall (monitorArm at x -1.7, y 1.75): an articulated steel arm of three segments and a boxy hullGrey CRT housing with a black bezel, a glowing greenCRT screen with scanline bars and a tiny text-line blocks and a red power LED. A ceiling-mounted yellow rotating warning beacon in the front-left (x 1.5, z 0.2, y 2.35) with a cage. An intercom panel on the back wall at x 1.5, y 1.6 with a speaker grille (small parallel bars) and a cyanLed button. A ventilation grille at x -0.2, y 2.3 on the back wall (slatted steelDark). Its parts stay above y 1.45, except the shelves, rail and arm, which are fixed to wall faces.
parts.attaches: Wall fittings seat on backWallFace (z = -1.8) and rightWallFace (x = -1.8). The hood sits above the back run's range at hoodBase, with its underside at y 1.65, 0.7 m above the counter top. Ceiling beams and the duct reach the ceilingUnder level (y 2.5..2.6). It floats above the floor; nothing touches y = 0.

calls.reasoning:
I'm thinking through a prop group for an Alien Nostromo-style galley kitchen, deciding to keep it static with no joints for simplicity, and sketching out room dimensions and layout with counters along the walls.

I'm breaking the scene into parts: a floor deck and back bulkhead shell, a back wall with stove/hood and sink, a side wall with fridge and storage, a central mess table with benches and tableware, and an overhead layer of pipes, rails, and warning details to add Nostromo-style grime and clutter.

I'll split the scene into five roughly equal-budget parts, working out the overall shell dimensions, ceiling height, and deck thickness, then pinning down exact coordinates for the back counter and wall positions so everything aligns within the enclosing box.

Now I'm working out how the back counter and right-wall runs meet at the corner, dividing up which x/z ranges each part owns so there's no overlap and a doorway gap is left open on the left side.

For contents, I'm placing base cabinets, countertop, a 4-burner range with overhead hood, sink and faucet, microwave, and a coffee machine with glowing indicators along the back run, while the right run gets a tall fridge, cold storage lockers, freezer drawers, a dispenser with glowing display, and base counter storage.

Now I'm laying out the central mess table with bolted benches on either side, set within a bounded box that stays clear of the right run, and scattering trays, mugs, bowls, cutlery, sauce bottles, fruit, and food tins across its surface.

For the overhead zone, I'm placing ceiling lamp panels, a range hood with exhaust duct, a hanging utensil rail with pots along the back wall, shelves above the sink, an overhead pipe bundle, a swing-arm monitor, a warning light, hazard signage, and a ventilation grille, all bounded within the upper ceiling box and considering whether ceiling beams belong here too.

Now for the shell layer: deck grating, back and right wall panels, a doorway, baseboard conduits, floor hazard stripes, wall number stencils, and wall ribbing rising to the ceiling height. Since the shell forms the enclosure its box naturally overlaps everything else, which is fine, but I need to keep the wall panels at the inner face so mounted items like shelves and rails at the back wall don't collide with the plain shell geometry, and I'm working out where the doorway wall sits relative to the right-side x-range.

I'm picking a gritty Nostromo-style palette -- grimy beige and grey-green plastics, dull steel, amber CRT glow, hazard orange and yellow, dark charcoal rubber, faded cream panels, worn olive tones -- to color the hull, walls, deck, grating, and warning stripes.

Now I'm laying out key mount positions: deck, counter, and table heights, back/right wall and ceiling planes, door location, plus centers for the range, sink, and fridge fixtures.

I'm working out the right-side counter run's extents, figuring the fridge sits in the corner facing outward while the rest of the run holds the dispenser, drawers, and trash compactor, keeping depths and x-ranges consistent so nothing overlaps.

Now I'm budgeting part counts across sections—shell, back run, right run, table, overhead—keeping the total manageable, and noting style conventions: flat-colored parts, small stenciled label pieces, and glow kits reserved for indicator lights. Then I'll move to writing out the final JSON structure.

I need to write a function that builds the mess table, accepting a context object with destructured fields. Since the Ctx type isn't explicitly imported, I'll define my own local type for it to stay safe against typecheck issues rather than assuming it's global.

With no joints defined in the shared builder, parts without a bone reference will just stay in model space, so I'll use helper functions like box and cyl for geometry placement along with a glow kit import for screen elements. For colors, I'll reference the palette object directly by name, like P.hullGrey, P.steel, P.rust, and similar entries for the various materials.

Now I'm working out the table dimensions — slab thickness, top height, edge rim details, pedestal supports with foot flanges and bolt cylinders, figuring out exact coordinates for each component to build the physical structure piece by piece.

Moving on to the bench: positioning it at seat height 0.46 with a cream seat pad over a steel base plate, sizing the dimensions to roughly match the table's scale so the furniture set feels proportional.

I'm adding surface details like seam strips, wear patches, and rivets on the table and bench, but need to stay within my part budget of 170. To afford these small details I'm planning to merge geometries by color into a single part per color group, since the rule allows one part per bone and color combination.

Setting up the merge bucket system...

Still defining box/cylinder/sphere helpers and laying out table slab, rim, and leg positions using these coordinate placements...

Working out the slanted bar geometry...

Placing rivets along the inside rows and rim at regular z intervals, then adding a worn centre strip with subtle grime streaks layered slightly above it to avoid z-fighting.

Now I'm thickening the top slab to 0.08 units with a darker steel apron beneath it for a sturdier look, then placing two pedestal supports at specific z positions with a flange detail at their base to anchor them to the ground.

Adding more pedestal details...

Now I'm laying out the table placement, adding a center stretcher beam with bolts connecting the two pedestals, then planning the tableware arrangement on top—working out positions and sizes for food trays along each side of the table.

Each tray gets a steel base box with raised rim walls and internal dividers creating three compartments, holding flattened blob shapes for green and red food items, with mirrored compartment layouts for trays on the opposite side.

Now I'm detailing the fork and spoon utensils: thin steel handles with small heads, the fork having tiny tine boxes and the spoon having a flattened oval sphere for its bowl, varying food contents and occasionally leaving a tray with fewer items for variety.

I'm working out the exact placement of the utensils beside each tray, fitting them in the narrow gap between the tray edge and the table rim, and adjusting the rivet positions so they don't overlap with the forks and spoons.

Now I'm setting up the mug geometries for the center strip, using a cylinder for each mug body and a small arced torus to form the handle loop.

Adding the pitcher, salt and pepper shakers, and sauce bottle now—steel-blue tapered pitcher with handle and lip, cylindrical shakers with contrasting caps, and a dark red-brown sauce bottle with a narrow neck and red cap.

I'm placing a folded napkin box with an offset fold line, a dropped spoon resting on the floor near the table, and a half-eaten food tin with a steel body, greenish interior disc, and a partially open lid.

Now I'm designing a data-pad prop: a steel body with a rubber bezel and glowing green CRT screen, dark text bars and small amber/red button lights, positioned at a slight tilt on the table, plus some flat grime smear discs scattered around.

Next I'm placing a coffee spill with a stained disc and tiny droplets, plus a ring mark on the table. Then I'm laying out the center strip objects — pitcher, and three mugs positioned around the table and bench seat, adjusting rotations so handles face outward.

I continue refining positions: a fourth mug near the top, salt and pepper shakers spaced closely with small radii, the sauce bottle shifted lower, and a napkin angled near a tin container, keeping everything within the tray's bounds.

Checking hazard stripes and tray zones along the z-axis for the second scene to make sure the mug, pitcher, and tray don't overlap—then I start placing a data-pad object.

I move it slightly to avoid collisions with mug B, settling on coordinates (0.02, 0.28) with a size around 0.11x0.16, and adjust mug B's position to (-0.085, 0.28) to keep clearance tight but acceptable given its handle orientation. I then start positioning mug A at (0.085, -0.12), orienting its handle outward.

I'm placing the napkin near the tin on the table, keeping both within safe gaps between trays. Then I'm figuring out bench item placement—maybe a mug or dropped spoon on the bench seats, making sure each item sits properly on the table top or bench surface.

I'm also working out the bench seat's worn texture details, like darker grime stripes and small tufting buttons placed at regular intervals, plus adding a tiny stenciled number plate to the bench base for a worn, hazard-marked look.

Now I'm building a reusable helper for drawing seven-segment digit displays out of small boxes, so I can stamp plate numbers like "03" onto the pedestal front faces and bench ends, deciding which faces are actually visible given the cabinet's open front.

I'm also adding small details like hazard stripes near table feet, grime strips on bench legs, bolt heads and rivets along the rubber strip edges, and leg brackets at the bench frame span.

Now I'm working out the bench leg frame geometry itself — leg boxes, foot plates, cross braces, and diagonal X-braces connecting them at the proper positions and spans.

Placing bracket plates, then working out the bench geometry for both sides: seat pads, base plates, legs, and rubber edge strips, aligning their heights and positions so everything stacks correctly from ground to seat level.

Skipping that detail. Adding grime patches and rust streaks on the seat and pedestal for wear, then writing the tray function with its base box and side walls.

Now I'm working out the tray's internal layout using local coordinates flipped by x, placing dividers to split the big compartment from the smaller ones, and positioning the contents (a scaled sphere, a small box, and another scaled sphere) with color variants inside each section.

Writing utensil generation code...

Still writing the geometry helpers...

I'm grouping geometries by color and glow, then merging each bucket at the end with mergeGeometries from BufferGeometryUtils and adding them as parts at the origin, applying glow where needed. Since there are no joints defined, I'll skip bone assignment and just rely on the root. All the shapes use indexed position/normal/uv attributes so merging should work cleanly, and I'm using flat shading to recompute normals after the merge.

I'm checking the color budget against the shared 64-color palette, picking a small set of my own colors (coffee, pitcher blue, worn pad) alongside foodRed and grime for accents, keeping it to just a few extras. I'm also planning glow intensities for the CRT green screen and small amber/red LEDs, then starting to write the seven-segment digit rendering logic facing forward.

Now I'm positioning the number plates on the pedestal face and designing a hazard warning label for the side faces—yellow plate with black top/bottom strips and a small warning triangle, using a sub-context helper function to rotate it to face outward on either x side.

I'm simplifying the warning symbol to a black bar and dot forming an exclamation mark, rotating a cylinder so its axis aligns with the facing direction. I'm also adding grime streaks and rust drips on the pedestal, then writing a reusable hazard-stripe function that builds a yellow base strip with black diagonal bars for the table edges.

I'm splitting the right side into three locker doors plus a wall bench with a coffee machine topped by a monitor and shelf. For the back wall, I'm placing a centered hatch door with hazard stripes, making sure the counters and lockers stay clear of it, and reserving the back wall for hatch, panel, pipe runs, vents, and ceiling lamps.

Now working out the mess table area: table centered small, benches on either side with stools at the ends to keep the aisle clear against the counter front, settling on bench dimensions around 0.28 wide running along z from 0 to 1.2.

I'm tallying part budgets: shell, galley counter, mess table, locker wall, and services sum to 880 out of a 900 cap, with no extra joints needed. I'm noting conventions for builders—floor:true means a part's base sits at y=0, while other parts rest above the floor plane at y=0.1, like the table pedestal which starts there without needing the floor flag.

Now I'm detailing the shell construction itself: a grated deck with slat patterns and hazard striping at the door, beige paneled walls with seams, rivets, and a darker grimy dado near the bottom, corner ribs, and an open ceiling made of a perimeter and cross beam grid rather than a solid surface, with the front side left open and end posts marking the walls.

With the shell box defined, I'm now placing the kitchen counter unit, packing it with cabinets, a steel countertop, a four-burner cooktop with a pot and pan, a glowing oven window, sink, extractor hood, overhead cabinets, a utensil rail, dish rack, and small indicator lights, all kept under the height limit. Next I'm positioning a lockers unit along the opposite wall.

Now I'm working out clearance zones so ceiling pipes, lamps, and service runs along the back wall don't collide with the cabinet tops or locker heights, checking x and y ranges carefully to keep everything above the furniture but below the ceiling.

I'll split into an overheadServices part and a backWall part, adjusting heights so lockers top out at 2.1 and overhead elements start just above that. For hanging lamps over the table, I'm narrowing the overhead box to a central x-range with a lower y-start around 1.75 so they can hang down appropriately without colliding with the side counters.

calls.reasoning:
I'm planning the buildMessTable function using the provided Ctx parameters, keeping it static with no joints, using flat color strings for parts, and designing the table geometry centered at the table top height.

I'm working out the table dimensions and positioning four stools around it, adjusting their placement so they tuck under the table edges without clipping the bounding box. I'm also planning a hanging ceiling lamp above the table center with a cord and cone-shaped shade.

Minor detail, won't matter much. I'm sketching out helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and spheres attached to joints, falling back to the root joint if none exist. For the rounded table top, I'm working out an extrusion approach using an outline in the x-z plane with the correct thickness direction via cross product.

Writing table geometry...

I'm planning decorative top details—thin inlaid seam lines, grime stains as flat dark cylinders, and bolts spaced along the perimeter edges and corners. Then I'm sizing out four trays, one per stool, placed near the long sides.

I'm planning tray colors and food blobs in olive and cream tones, plus stainless mugs with torus handles and dark coffee discs. Now I'm adding hazard details: a small "MESS" label plate with dark text bars on the table edge, and considering hazard stripe accents near the pedestal base flange. I'm also sketching the pedestal's floor flange as a darkSteel cylinder positioned near the grated floor level.

Now I'm planning the pedestal: a steel cylinder with collars running from just above the deck up to the mounting plate beneath the tabletop, plus angled corner braces, and matching the seat height so the effective clearance above the deck works out properly.

Adding a copper conduit pipe with clamps running up the column, then a darkSteel skirt under the table with crossmember ribs and a cable tray. Now starting a stool function with rotation and base parameters.

Still writing seat details...

Stools are backless swivel type, positioned at four spots so the two nearest the table edge tuck slightly underneath it. Now I'm placing the lamp at the table center with a thin cord running down from above.

Designing the shade shape...

For the warning rim I'll add a thin torus ring rotated flat to sit at the base, then handle the bulb glow using the glow kit on the light panel material, plus a small diffuser disc underneath for softened illumination.

Thinking about extra tabletop details, I decide to add a small call-button control panel near the tray end—a dark box with tiny glowing bars and an amber LED—positioned near the far edge of the table.

For the lamp, I'm working out the finishing touches: a simple bulb sphere nested in a dark steel socket cylinder, a neck connecting to the shade, and a small dark steel cap capping the top above it.

Placing rivets along the cone surface...

Now I'm designing the tray objects: a grey base box sitting on the table, darkSteel rim edges, and dividers splitting it into compartments—one large and two smaller. For food I'm adding a flat olive cylinder for mash plus small green sphere clusters for peas.

I'm picking colors for other food items—cream, dark red, and warnOrange for carrot cubes—and deciding to keep mugs as separate table objects rather than tray compartments. Then I'm writing a transform helper that converts each tray's local coordinates into world space based on its position and y-rotation, so all the sub-pieces (boxes, dividers, food) inherit the tray's rotation correctly.

For tilted parts like pouches I'll just build rotations directly in world coordinates rather than composing local offsets precisely, since the tilts are small enough that exact Euler order won't matter visually. I'll skip geometry caching since triangle counts are small, and I'm roughly budgeting part counts across the table's top, bolts, seams, stains, and pedestal.

Tallying up the full scene—trays, central items, stools, and the lamp—I'm overshooting the part budget of 240, so I need to trim stool and tray complexity down. I'll avoid merging geometries for bolts since there's no clear bone/joint structure to anchor them, so instead I'll just reduce bolt counts directly on the table and stools before writing the actual code.

Finalizing the color palette now, keeping it within six colors for the main materials plus a small set for pouch and hazard accents. Setting up the module imports and beginning the function signature for building the mess table.

Adding helper functions for placing geometry...

Still writing rounded rect geometry...

Still working out table geometry...

I'm relocating the control panel to avoid overlap, settling it near x=-0.2, z=0.3 with a small footprint, and reserving the central strip between the trays for the salt shaker, pouch, cutlery, and mugs.

Now I'm repositioning the trays to four corner-ish spots and adjusting the stools so they sit just inside the table edges at the front and back, nudging their z-coordinates slightly to keep the seats from clipping the table boundary.

For the surface details, I'm adding thin seam boxes at the tabletop level that protrude just slightly for a visible seam line, then plotting a few grime stain discs plus a streak box for texture. Finally I'm placing bolt elements along periodic rows on the tabletop, positioning them near the seam intersections.

I'm adding a matching label plate at the opposite end with a red tint and small stenciled text boxes. Then I'm working on the under-table structure: cross beams, a center mounting plate, and a pedestal column connecting down to the base, plus small corner brackets for support.

Still adding pedestal details...

Adjusting to 12 parts with 6 bolts at a smaller radius. For the pipe I'm positioning a copper cylinder running up the column offset from its surface, with cylindrical clamps at two heights instead of boxes. I'm also adding an amber status LED with a glow effect on the column's front face plus a small dark plate beneath it.

Then I add a yellow warning collar band with a thin black stripe below it, and I'm writing a helper function to compute local-to-world coordinates for placing trays at arbitrary angles around the structure, defining the tray dimensions and base height next.

Still placing tray components...

That gives 52 parts total for four trays, with color variants between them. Now I'm placing the separate tabletop items—mugs positioned between the trays, plus a pouch pile and salt shaker scattered in the central strip.

I'm working out mug placement in the gap between the left and right tray columns, then adding a small darkSteel cutlery block nearby.

Adding a fifth loose pouch nearby, then setting up a rotation helper for placing crimp pieces along the local z-axis. Now I'm building a cutlery block with a dark steel box body and four protruding handle shapes at staggered positions to suggest spoons and utensils.

Finishing the cutlery block with a small red label plate on the front face, bringing that part count to eight pieces total. I'm also sketching out a control strip with a dark steel base tray and a glowing green CRT-style element with a black bezel.

I'm noticing the corner panels overlap slightly where the back and side walls meet, which could cause z-fighting on coplanar faces, though mostly it's hidden interior geometry. I'll adjust the back panel columns to 7 segments of 0.5 width, spanning -1.75 to 1.75, to align cleanly with the side panels.

Setting up basis vectors for each face orientation and computing the origin point so the local coordinate system aligns properly, then applying the transform matrix to position and orient the extruded shape correctly in world space.

Writing hazard checker boxes...

Now I'm working out the door leaf geometry: a thin grey panel positioned at the opening face, sized to span the door height and width, with horizontal darkSteel rib strips protruding slightly at a few heights, plus a vertical seam marking the split between sliding halves.

Adding porthole windows with steel rings and dark glass, plus handle bars and small glowing lock indicators near the frame.

Now I'm working on the ceiling: a grey slab with ribs running across it every 0.2 units in dark steel, plus structural beams running along the long axis with lower flanges for a steel-frame look.
