Dropping the flange idea in favor of small bolt protrusions below the beam bottom, then placing light panels at x=±0.9 with recessed frame borders and a glowing diffuser box, plus a thin divider bar down the middle.

I'm splitting the diffuser into two lightPanel halves with amberLight strips along the edges for warmth, adding corner bolts pointing downward, then starting the vent grille frame on the back wall as a recessed darkSteel box.

Building out the vent grille: a black backing panel, six tilted steel slats, and corner bolts, while checking it clears other counter items like spice racks. I'm also considering whether to add a second ceiling duct or grille near the front, though that may be unnecessary.

I'll add a ceiling sprinkler head and smoke detector at the beam intersection, including a small disc detector with a tiny red LED glow. For the walls, I'm skipping a chair rail on the left since it would interfere with the spice rack mounting height, keeping the rail only on the right wall, and considering a yellow hazard band across both walls around y 2.0-2.05.

I'm working out a thin yellow warning band with black pinstripe accents above and below it, routing it across the left wall while avoiding the fire cabinet, but running into a conflict on the right wall where the band height overlaps the door header and frame -- so I'm adjusting to place a plate above the door instead and keep the band elsewhere.

For the left wall fire cabinet, I'm building a red box body with a window panel showing an offwhite cross, a steel latch, and a yellow "FIRE" label strip on top, using a wall-mounted box helper that positions elements by depth, height, thickness, and offset along the face.

Now I'm setting up helper functions for mounting items onto walls: one for placing a box flush against a face with proper lift and center offset, one for bolts oriented along the face normal, and one for text labels built from small randomized plate segments.

I'm working out specific label placements on the back wall and right wall, figuring out coordinates for a "WARNING" label and a yellow vent-area label, making sure the u/v axes map correctly to world x/z depending on which wall I'm placing them on.

Then for the right wall, I'm adding a control box near the door and a small notice board with a few paper sheets, keeping things simple by skipping rotation since the placement function doesn't support it.

I'm also working through the conduit and door header placement — the conduit at the upper wall height conflicts with a label plate near the door, so I'm reworking the header geometry (raising it slightly to 2.0–2.14) so the plate can sit cleanly on the header face instead of overlapping the conduit run.

Adding the hazard strip above the door header, then placing conduit pipes along both side walls at y=2.17 with small radius, checking clearances against the header and crown molding so nothing overlaps.

I'll drop the cables on the right wall to avoid clashing with the door header and just keep conduit there, skipping extra pipe detail. For the back wall I'll skip the overhead pipe run too, and instead add subtle grime streaks as thin offset boxes along panel faces, including narrow streaks beneath bolts.

I'll scatter streaks below roughly 30% of bolts using the rng, add a handful of wider grime stains, and cap the total streak count around 30 to keep it manageable. I'll also add floor-level oil stains as flattened cylinders positioned to overlay the grating bars near the bottom of the walls.

Now I'm placing additional dirt-film stains near the door and counter areas, avoiding the threshold hazard zone, and considering a rubber mat strip in front of the counter.

I need to check the mat dimensions don't collide with the stools around the table—trimming the mat's z-range so it stays clear of the stool positions near x=0.4-0.8.

I'm thinking about adding a wall-mounted speaker grille on the right wall—a layered cylinder design with a dark steel base, black disc cover, and thin steel rings for detail, plus an amber glow lamp above it. Building speaker grille layers...

Estimating total triangle count across floor bars, borders, bolts, wall panels, base slabs, hazard markers, streaks, ceiling ribs, and their bolts—landing around 10,000, comfortably under my 15,000 budget—and considering simplifying bolt geometry to use fewer radial segments to save on triangles.

Tightening floor bolt spacing while recalculating seam line counts to stay safe within budget, then moving on to writing the hazard stripe geometry function that generates angled warning markers along a length...

Still writing geometry code...

Working out the left and right wall bases and floor threshold orientation...

Placing the door frame's black base plate and computing stripe positions along the threshold, fitting a single diagonal stripe within the 0.9-length span.

Adjusting the hazard stripe parameters so width, skew, and period scale off a separate stripe-size variable, then picking h=0.35, s=0.1 for the floor to fit roughly four stripes across the span.

Now I'm working out the jamb geometry, defining its basis vectors and origin so the cross product gives the correct outward normal, then setting up a dark base box for the jamb itself.

Adding black base plates for jamb and header, placing the hazard stripe marking on the header with its own basis and origin, then computing the z-center positions for the left and right jambs before defining their frame bodies.

Now I'm positioning the door leaf within the frame recess, calculating offsets so the leaf face sits correctly relative to the wall panel surface without clipping through it.

Adding door ribs, window rings, and handle bars...

Still placing room elements...

Still placing corner posts and frame edges...

I'm positioning a smoke detector where ceiling beams intersect, with a small glowing red LED underneath, and double-checking the ceiling panel and rib coloring before considering adding a duct along the left ceiling corner.

For the light panel glow effects, I'm setting up a helper to collect emissive colors keyed by color and strength, flushing them at the end. For the random streaks, I'm using the kit's `rng(seed)` function which returns a random number generator to pass in as the `rand` callback.

Now I'm starting to write the shell-building function, setting up the material constants for beige, off-white, streak, and oil colors, along with floor, ceiling, and back wall position references.

Setting up geometry buckets...

Adding cylinder helpers and glow variants...

Defining bolt helper and wall panel logic...

Still writing styles...

I'm adding lighting panels and remaining room details like door windows, vents, fire cabinet, speaker, and notice board, then generating streak marks across wall faces with slight offsets to avoid z-fighting with the panels.

Now I'm adding streaks beneath wall bolts with a probability check so roughly 45% of bolts get a narrow drip mark below them, keeping the geometry lightweight, and I'm about to add larger grime stains near the base of the walls.

Adding grime patches...

Working out the layered stripe depths over the floor grating and base plate, then shifting to the door face geometry — positioning the window ring and glass panel offsets relative to the door's right edge so they sit flush and proud correctly.

Writing ceiling light panel code...

Checking the amber strips and divider positioning against the diffuser bounds, those look fine, and verifying the ribs on the slab underside don't collide with the light diffuser since the diffuser sits below them. Now I'm moving on to checking the beam positions along the z-axis.

Confirming the beams and frames don't overlap and that the lights sit far enough from center, plus placing the smoke detector correctly. I'm working through the floor stain geometry scaling and rib spacing along the x-axis to finalize the layout.

Now I'm adding the ceiling-wall conduit pipe along the z-axis, with evenly spaced brackets clamping it to the wall, plus the paired black cables running below it on both sides to keep everything visually distinct from the band.

Still placing wall details...

I'm positioning the beacon structure with a steel base and glowing dome cap near the door, then shifting focus to the fire cabinet details on the left wall, placing its red label panel at the right size and position.

Adding a notice board on the right with a dark steel frame, beige inner panel, and a few scattered off-white paper sheets with thin text lines and tiny red pin markers to give it a cluttered, realistic look.

Now I'm defining a label helper function for generating text bars on surfaces, plus placing a back-facing vent with a framed rectangular opening built from four bar segments.

Still placing labels...

Still writing wall panel generation logic...

Verifying the base panel spans align correctly, then adding the streak function and large interior stains before finalizing the hazard end caps and ceiling bolts.

I'm planning a single static function that builds the pipe wall using the provided context object, with no joints, relying on the module's existing Ctx type and part geometry/colors.

I'm laying out the wall contents along the x-axis within the box bounds: a tall fridge-freezer near the right with handles and vents, locker banks on the left split into lower and upper rows of doors, and a control panel in the middle with a CRT-style screen, all mounted just in front of the back wall face.

Below the panel I'm adding a low equipment cabinet with grilles and gauges, then running horizontal and vertical pipe networks near the ceiling with flanges, valve wheels, gauge dials, and cable bundles to fill out the industrial detail.

I need to keep the part count under 220, so I'm thinking about merging bolts of the same color into a single geometry instead of adding separate parts for each, using a helper that accumulates transformed geometries by color and merges them at the end.

I'll go with a mixed approach: merge small repetitive pieces like bolts by color into the collector, but keep larger structural elements as individual parts for clarity. Simplicity matters more than preserving per-part names, and triangle counts stay low with basic box geometry.

I'm building a collector that groups geometry by color and applies a glow option per group—importing the glow kit so I can light up specific colored groups like the green CRT glow or amber panel lights. I'm also setting flat shading across the board so cylinders and boxes read with crisp, faceted surfaces instead of smooth normals.

Writing the collector's grouping logic...

All the Three primitives share compatible attributes for merging, so boxes, cylinders, spheres, and tori can combine cleanly. Cables are a different story since they need individual sweeps along catmull-rom paths, colored black and kept separate from the merged geometry.

Now I'm sketching helper functions for boxes, cylinders along different axes, and bolts, plus thinking through how to fake number labels without textures -- building digits out of tiny boxes like a 7-segment display since actual text isn't an option here.

For warning stripes I'm figuring out a cheap way to approximate diagonal hazard chevrons using rotated rectangular boxes alternating yellow and black, since true clipping isn't available and the rotated shapes need careful sizing to stay within the strip bounds.

Now I'm mapping out wall and zone coordinates: placing back plates flush against the wall near z=-1.45, with lockers occupying one x-range and the counter and fridge filling the remaining space to the right.

I'm sketching the locker bank dimensions—four doors sized and spaced along x, with a carcass box set at a given depth and height, plus thin door panels in front and a kick plinth with a warning strip at the base.

For the upper bank, I'm placing it higher up with slightly less depth, keeping four doors matching the lower bank's width, separated by a shelf strip and cap with visible wall panel and cable bundle in the gap. Each door gets a latch handle with a rubber grip near the inner edge and a small number plate.

Still designing door hardware...

Then for Zone B, I'm laying out a low equipment unit with grille vents, two gauge dials, and a valve wheel, topped by a wall-mounted control panel frame holding three glowing CRT screens.

Each screen gets a black bezel with scan-line details and dash-like text, plus a toggle switch row, amber push buttons with red labels, knobs, and a hazard strip along the panel's top edge. I'm also adding a steel counter-ledge to bridge the gap between the equipment unit and the panel above, then starting Zone C with the fridge's dimensions and placement.

Above the fridge I'm adding a duct box and condenser pipes running to the ceiling, giving the fridge body a beige panel finish with a taller freezer door on top and shorter fridge door below, separated by a black seam strip. I'm detailing vertical stainless handles with mounts, an amber status light and small green display, rubber gasket outlines, a black plinth, grime stains, and a bottom vent grille, positioning the door front and protruding handles in depth.

Tightening the fridge's depth so the handles sit just proud of the door front, then laying out overhead copper and grey pipes running along the ceiling above the lockers and control panel, careful to route them around the duct and keep consistent radii and spacing.

Simplifying instead: dropping the duct idea and just running pipes above the fridge up to the ceiling as a condenser coil. I'm laying out positions for copper and grey horizontal pipes at varying heights and radii with flanged ends, plus starting a vertical pipe run.

Figuring out where the vertical pipes fit without overlapping the lockers and panel—adjusting locker widths and gaps so I can tuck a grey vertical pipe into the narrow gap between the locker bank and the panel, then another copper vertical pipe into the gap between the panel and the fridge.

Now I'm placing condenser lines above the fridge as thin grey vertical cylinders, then planning the pipe assembly itself—main horizontal pipes with flange rings and bolt details, plus wall-mounted clamp brackets to hold them up.

Adding valve wheels and clamps...

Designing a gauge function with bezel, cream dial face, ticks, red zone, and needle, placing three on the lower unit and two on the pipes with simple wall-mounted stems. I'm also planning black cable bundles as looping bezier curves running from the locker top up toward the pipes.

Still writing cable sweeps...

I'm planning the CRT screen with a dark bezel, a glowing green display showing text bars, a waveform, and a border frame, then setting up the buildPipeWall function signature using only the needed context parameters.

Writing pipe geometry code...

Adding helper shortcuts for boxes, cylinders, and torus rings, plus a bolt helper that composes a hex cylinder along the z-axis.

Now I'm defining a seven-segment digit encoder with bitmasks for digits 0-9 and figuring out the segment positions based on height, width, and thickness ratios.

Still writing hazard stripe logic...

Now I'm moving on to defining the zones, starting with locker bank placement and considering backing plates behind the panel area for walls.

For the lower bank I'm working out the carcass box dimensions and position, color scheme for doors and panels, and adding the plinth with a hazard stripe along its front edge.

Now I'm placing the individual doors across the carcass front, calculating their x positions and gaps, then detailing each with an inset panel, corner bolts, and a latch mechanism with handle near the edge.

Adding door hardware details...

Adding the top cap for the upper bank, and considering a red warning label in the gap zone. For doors, I'll keep 4 lower tall doors and 4 upper doors rather than splitting further. Now moving to Zone B, laying out its lower cabinet unit with a beige-grey carcass and plinth base.

Still working out panel positions...

Adding the LED row with glowing amber/green/red cylinders and label plates, plus a bottom pull handle with standoffs. Then I'm working out placement of the valve wheel on pipe V1, checking its stem and radius against the gap between lockers so it doesn't clip into the locker front plane.

Now placing a second wheel and a small gauge further up V1, then starting the control panel frame positioned between the lower unit's top cap and the shelf gap.

Building the panel's layered construction: a dark steel frame box, a grey face plate in front, and an angled hood on top with a hazard stripe detail. Laying out the face into rows -- starting with three small CRT screens across the top row.

Still designing panel details...

Adding corner bolts, then moving to the fridge: positioning it beside the panel with a dark plinth base, beige body and doors with steel edge trim, sized to fit the remaining width and depth of the scene.

Shifting the fridge body back to fix the overshoot, I recalculate door and handle positions so standoffs sit cleanly between -1.08 and -1.065. Now I'm adding door detailing: a recessed black seam between the two doors, inset lighter panels with bolt rows, a brand plate, and edge trim, plus a frost "-18°" marking on the freezer door for realism.

Finishing the warning diamond with a black exclamation mark, then adding a vent grille and grime stripes to the fridge door's lower section. I'm also building the condenser unit on top with a steel box housing and vertical pipes running up to a ceiling flange.

Adding flange rings and bolt details...

Checking where vertical and horizontal pipes cross and adjusting their z-offsets slightly so they intersect cleanly, then adding tee-joint spheres and collars at those crossings for a convincing plumbing look.

I'm figuring out how pipe ends should terminate against the walls and counter edges with flange caps, then starting to lay out cable bundle sweeps running up from the floor near the left side.

I need to work out spacing so the second cable run doesn't collide with the V2 copper pipe near the panel-fridge gap, so I'm adjusting its x-position and radius, then deciding to reroute that cable loop over the lockers instead to avoid the tight gap, before settling on coiled strand positions for the first cable bundle.

Now I'm placing a few more hanging cable loops near the lower unit and panel, checking each against nearby pipe positions to avoid overlap, and skipping the ones that clash. I'm also planning a caged amber warning lamp above the lockers and near the panel, checking its height against the panel hood and the copper pipe runs to find a clear spot.

I'm also designing a reusable gauge component: a steel housing cylinder, a bezel ring, a cream face disc layered just in front of it, a row of tiny tick marks arranged in an arc, and starting to add a red indicator element at the end.

Continuing, I'm adding the gauge needle as a thin box rotated to point at its angle with a black hub, plus a simple valve wheel assembly (steel stem, body, torus rim, three spoke boxes, and hub), an LED helper with housing and glowing cap, and a toggle switch made of a base plate, collar, and lever.

Still positioning lever parts...

Adding a pointer indicator and tick marks around the knob base for visual orientation...

Now I'm defining a CRT screen function that renders glowing lines of text with randomized widths to simulate a terminal display.

I'm also adding waveform and bar chart visualization modes for the CRT, with randomized heights and corner borders to complete the screen effect.

Now I'm layering in surface details: a bright green header block, stenciled dash text lines, red label plates with bordered stencil text, and sparse grime streaks using a dark muted color scattered across the panel for texture.

For the pipes, I'm adding floor flanges with bolts where vertical pipes meet the ground, checking that V2's position threads cleanly between the panel and fridge without colliding, and verifying V1 doesn't overlap the lockers or lower unit in x or z. I'm also doing a rough triangle budget check since merged boxes at roughly 1200 units times 12 triangles each is getting uncomfortably close to the 15000 limit, so I need to be careful about adding more geometry.

I'm now tallying up locker door details -- bolts, latches, plates, digits, hinges, streaks, vents -- across all eight doors, estimating roughly 30 small objects per door at about 14 triangles each, which puts lockers alone around 3400 triangles, so I'll need to keep bolt and hinge geometry as simple boxes rather than cylinders to stay within budget.

Adding up the control panel too -- CRTs, toggles, buttons, knobs -- pushes the total objects toward a thousand, which risks exceeding the 15000 triangle cap, so I'm planning to trim digit counts, simplify cylinders to low segment counts only where needed, and track a running triangle counter as I build so I can skip optional details once I'm close to the limit.

Extending this plane approach to digit segments and decorative marks, with small z-offsets to avoid z-fighting. For bolt heads I'm weighing low-poly cylinder versus box shapes to keep triangle counts minimal.

Tallying triangle counts...

Continuing the locker tally, then estimating polygon counts for the control panel (CRTs, toggles, buttons, knobs, sliders, bolts, labels) and the lower unit's slats, gauges, knobs, LEDs, handles, and bolts.

Total adds up to roughly 12.5k, safely under the 15k cap, but I want a safety guard anyway — I'll track a running budget and have low-priority extras like grime streaks and bolts silently skip being added once the count gets close to the limit, adding those last so core geometry is always preserved.

The part count stays fairly low with merged color groups plus sweeps, which should be fine since visual quality doesn't depend on part count. I'm passing flat shading for the merged geometry and picking a small custom palette (stencil cream, dark CRT green, red LED, lighter panel/door tones) layered on top of the existing palette colors, keeping custom colors to a handful.

Setting up imports and structure...

Adding plane and cylinder helpers...

Now I'm setting up seven-segment digit masks and a digit-rendering function using positioned plane segments to form numerals.

Working through the viewer orientation, I confirm that with the model facing +z and the camera looking toward -z, the model's left corresponds to the viewer's right, so text should read left-to-right with increasing x on a +z-facing plane. Now I'm planning the dashes function to compute randomized segment widths before placing them, and considering how to build a hazard-bar pattern using yellow plane segments.

For the bars I'm using rotated rectangular planes against a black base, layering the yellow stripes slightly above the surface to avoid z-fighting -- settling on roughly 0.003 unit offsets for depth separation at typical viewing distances. Then I move on to detailing the remaining props: wheel, gauge, LED, toggle, knob, CRT, bank, fridge, and pipes.

Writing pipe and flange geometry...

Still adding geometry details...

Checking V1's intersection with P2, which seems fine, then verifying lamp placement and panel clearance relative to P3's range—shifting c1's cable end slightly for better fit. Now working out the strand positions for c1's cable detail.

Mapping out the second cable running from the panel hood up and over toward the fridge's back top area, keeping it behind the pipes, then planning a third loose hanging loop with two color strands.

Skipping a few extras like a coiled cable and a hanging loop to keep the scene lean, settling on five total cable sweeps. I'm weighing adding grime details, yellow arrow chevrons made from rotated planes, and red label plates to the panel, but deciding to skip a fire extinguisher or first-aid box since there's no good spot for them.

Now I'm writing the locker bank function, parameterizing the carcass dimensions, door width, and hinge side so I can generate each locker door with proper positioning...

Adding door inset details...

Adding number plates with stenciled digits, hinge cylinders positioned opposite the latch side, vent slots on lower bank doors, and a red label plate on an upper door, plus planning grime streaks and the latch handle positioning relative to each bank's front z-depth.

Now I'm building the fridge: a plinth box at the base, a grey panel body above it, and freezer/fridge doors sized to the body width.

Still placing fridge details...

Adding the amber status light housing with glow, plus warning diamond decals, a red stenciled label plate, and a "No. 3" stencil number for detail.

Now I'm adding fridge door vent slats, a grime streak panel, a kick-plate nameplate, and corner bolts for both doors, then sketching duct pipework above with vertical pipes feeding into a horizontal copper manifold.

Adding manifold flanges...

Placing a gauge on the second vertical pipe, checking clearances so it sits between the adjacent panel and fridge front without colliding.

Now I'm skipping the condenser grill detail and confirming the upper bank stays clear of the panel's x-position. I'm blocking out the lower unit carcass and plinth with a hazard marking stripe on the plinth face.

Continuing to place the cap trim and front panels, then adding a row of nine slats with a steel lip along the left panel's front face...

Adding knobs and LEDs below the gauges, checking spacing against tick marks so labels don't overlap, then placing a lower handle bar with standoffs and a stenciled number plate behind it on the control panel.

Now I'm building the panel frame and face plate dimensions, making sure the plate protrudes slightly in front of the frame. I'm also adding a small lip or shelf beneath the panel to cap the lower wall unit, positioning a steel box as a foot lip at the panel's base.

Now I'm laying out the panel's interior details: three CRT bezels in the top row, a red/yellow label strip, and a row of eight toggle switches with tiny dash labels beneath each one, all positioned with precise x/y coordinates to fit within the plate bounds.

Adding the knob boxes, then placing an emergency stop button with a yellow-black guard ring and "EMERG" label plate, plus a hazard dash strip along the bottom row. Then I'm starting the hood geometry as a dark steel box that protrudes forward from the panel.

Now I'm positioning the vertical pipe assembly's valve wheels and gauge housing, figuring out stem lengths and front face offsets to keep everything flush against the pipe body.

Then I'm placing P2's wheels and lamp, checking that each wheel sits below the gauge above it with proper clearance, and confirming the lamp's top edge clears the wheel beneath.

Now I'm assigning colors and materials across the pipe assemblies: copper for P1 and P3, grey for P2, mixed finishes for the valves and condenser manifolds, with warning yellow insulation bands marking select pipe sections.

I'm sketching out extra details like floor flanges at the valves, hazard stripes near the ceiling, and a grime/streak function to scatter weathering marks under door latches and other surfaces, while deciding to skip cable clamps and ID tag greebles as unnecessary.

Now I'm double-checking the vertical placement math: plinths sitting flush at y=0, pipe flanges starting just above the floor, and pipe runs capped below the 2.3 ceiling limit, then setting the lower cabinet bank's carcass to start right above its plinth at y=0.09.

For the carcasses, I'm defining the lower bank at y0=0.09 with height 0.87 and a separate plinth box offset in front, positioning the hazard label flush on the plinth face since it sits slightly deeper than the doors. Then I'm setting up the upper bank starting at y=1.06 with a shallower depth and door height, and working out numbering labels for each cabinet door using two-digit strings since letters aren't supported.

Now I'm filling the gap between the banks with a support ledge, then adding a simple cable tray detail under the upper bank using thin horizontal black cylinders to represent cables with a clip.

I'm verifying the triangle counts stay reasonable, then checking how `b.part` handles merged geometry without explicit bone or joints -- confirming it defaults to the origin joint when the model has none defined, and that `flat: true` properly recomputes normals on the merged mesh for a faceted look.

For the sweeps, I'm working out the cable tube parameters -- hexagonal cross-section, round caps, and ring density based on bend angle -- then mapping out the gauge tick positions, spacing seven ticks evenly across a -130° to +130° arc using sine/cosine to place them around the dial radius.

Computing needle and housing z-depths...

Adding knob cap, pointer, and tick marks for the gauge, then moving to toggle switches and the CRT screen setup with glow planes and dashed-line text content for each mode.

For the CRT, I'm sketching out waveform samples, bar heights, corner brackets, and a header bar before compiling everything into the final code.

Now I'm thinking through the merge logic: grouping geometries by color and glow strength, merging them per group, creating parts, and applying glow materials where needed, plus adding stenciled digits on the door plate and a hazard function.

For the hazard stripe pattern, I'm writing a function that draws a black base plane and tiles diagonal yellow warning stripes across it, working out the rotated rectangle's bounding dimensions so the stripes fit cleanly within the panel height.

Now I'm sketching helper functions for digits, a grime streak effect, and a random number generator, confirming that `rng(seed)` returns a callable function matching the SDK's expected interface before finalizing the code.

Next I'm detailing the pipe flange geometry, adding a cylindrical collar with bolt heads arranged around its circumference, slightly proud of the flange face.

Adding a small cable clamp detail, then writing out the final answer.

spec.name: Nostromo Galley
spec.description: A cramped, grimy 1979 industrial-spaceship galley kitchen: a steel counter with hob and sink, wall cabinets, a cold storage locker, a dining table with stools, and a pipe-filled ceiling lit by sickly amber and cyan indicators.
spec.layout: A walk-in galley bay in a retro-industrial utilitarian style. Floor deck plate at y=0 (a slab 4.0 x 0.1 x 3.6). The back wall (z=-1.8) carries the long steel counter run (hob, sink, prep surface) with wall cabinets above. The left wall (+X) holds a tall cold-storage locker and a bulkhead hatch. A round-cornered dining table with four stools sits in the front-centre. The ceiling (y=2.6) is crowded with pipes, conduits, a vent and strip lights. Everything is worn grey-beige plastic, stained steel, hazard-yellow stencils, amber and cyan glowing indicators, and dark grime where surfaces meet. Blocky, chunky, practical forms with small details (knobs, labels, rivets, handles, screens) built as separate small parts in their own colours.

parts.builds: Floor deck slab with plate seams, bolt heads and hazard-yellow edge stripes and grime stains; back wall, left wall and right wall panels in wallBeige with riveted seam strips, dirty streaks (wallDirty) and stencilled labels; a bulkhead hatch with wheel and yellow-black frame on the left wall near the front; corner trim and skirting.
parts.attaches: Provides floorTop, backWall, leftWall surfaces the other parts rest on.

parts.builds: Steel counter along the back wall: base cabinet boxes in steelDark with plastic doors, handles, grime kick plate; steel worktop; recessed sink with tap and drain; four-burner hob with knobs and amber glowing rings; a small oven with window and dial; a rack of utensils and pots (cylinders, ladle) on the counter; a cyan-screen timer.
parts.attaches: Sits on floorTop, backs onto backWall at counterTop height; wall cabinets above start at y=1.45.

spec.name: Strandbeest Windwalker
spec.description: A Theo Jansen-style kinetic beach creature: yellow PVC-tube lattice body on two crankshafts, eight Jansen-linkage legs, bottle-and-cloth wind wings, a bottle-eyed head with a split jaw and a windvane tail.
spec.layout: Long, low insect-like walker facing +Z. Everything is thin yellow PVC tubes (radius 0.02 to 0.035) joined at black ball joints and wrapped with black zip ties and blue tape rings, with translucent blue bottles and white sail cloth as the only broad surfaces. Bottom to top: eight sand-padded feet on y=0, eight identical Jansen linkage legs hanging from the frame, with 4 leg planes at x=+0.5, +1.0, -0.5, -1.0 on each of two crankshafts (front axle z=+1.0, rear axle z=-1.0, both at y=1.2). Above them the lattice frame (two lower rails at x=+-0.25, y=1.45, one spine at y=1.95, zig-zag W trusses between them) runs z=-1.8..1.7. Two big bottle-sail wings rise from the spine with a dihedral (root x=+-0.45,y=1.95; tip x=+-1.3,y=2.25), chord z=-1.4..1.4. A bank of blue pressure bottles hangs under the middle of the frame between the axles. A tube head with a bottle muzzle, separate upper and lower jaw, and two bottle eyes sits at the front. A three-segment windvane tail trails at the back. The Jansen look shows everywhere: no smooth skin, only rods, balls, ties, tape and bottles; every node has a black ball joint. All units in the leg spec below are meters, scaled so the rest pose is a standing walker with all feet on the floor.

parts.builds: The structural lattice and drive, all in pvcYellow tubes (radius 0.03 main, 0.02 braces) with jointBlack ball/elbow connectors (sphere r 0.045) at every node, zipBlack ties, tapeBlue tape rings and pvcYellowDark end plugs. (1) Two lower rails at x=+-0.25, y=1.45, from z=-1.7 to z=1.7. (2) One spine tube at x=0, y=1.95, from z=-1.5 to z=1.5 (ends flare down via braces). (3) Zig-zag W lattice: slanted braces from each rail up to the spine, one every 0.3 m in z, alternating lean (about 24 braces), plus horizontal cross-ties at x=0..+-0.25 every 0.6 m. (4) Front and rear converging truss: rods from rail ends (+-0.25,1.45,+-1.7) and spine ends up/down to the mounts headBase [0,1.65,1.75] and tailBase [0,1.65,-1.75] (frame rods END at those mounts; head/tail parts start there). (5) Two crankshafts along x at y=1.2, z=+1.0 (joint crankF) and z=-1.0 (joint crankR), each a steel tube radius 0.025 from x=-1.22 to x=1.22, with brass end knobs, jointBlack bearing blocks at x=+-0.25 and posts (radius 0.02) rising from each bearing to the rails at y=1.45. (6) Two pivot axles along x at y=1.28, z=0.62 (pivotF) and z=-1.38 (pivotR), pvcYellow tubes radius 0.02 from x=-1.12 to x=1.12 with posts to the rails, and tape rings where each leg plane (x=+-0.5, +-1.0) meets them. (7) A drive chain loop in the plane x=0 between two toothed sprockets (lathe discs, steel, radius 0.1, at the crank axle centres) made of small zipBlack link boxes along two straight runs. (8) Two flat sail-mast stubs where the wings mount: short yellow tubes from the spine at (+-0.45,1.95,0) pointing up and outwards, topped with jointBlack hinge blocks (the wing parts start at the wingRoot mounts). Trim: accentRed tape ring on the crankshaft centre, zip ties in pairs on every lattice node.
parts.attaches: Crankshaft centres at mounts crankF/crankR (legs builders draw their crank arms from these points). Pivot axles at pivotF/pivotR (legs hang from them). Truss ends at headBase and tailBase. Wing roots at wingRootL/R.

parts.builds: Four identical Jansen linkage legs on the FRONT crankshaft (axle centre C = crankF = [x, 1.2, 1.0]): one at each plane x = +0.5, +1.0, -0.5, -1.0. Use this exact planar linkage in leg-local coordinates (u = world z offset from the axle, v = world y offset from y=1.2, x = plane x): C(0,0) crank axle; Cp(0.10,-0.11) crank pin; P(-0.38,0.08) fixed pivot (sits on pivotF axle at world [x,1.28,0.62]); A(-0.35,-0.33); D(-0.62,-0.17); K(-0.52,-0.60); E(0.18,-0.62); F(-0.14,-0.91); T(0.12,-1.12) ankle/foot centre (world y 0.08). World point = [x, 1.2+v, 1.0+u]. Rods (pvcYellow, radius 0.018, flat caps): crank arm C-Cp (brass, radius 0.022, laid on the outer layer), P-A, Cp-A, P-D, A-D, D-K, A-K, Cp-E, A-E, shank K-T (passes through F, pvcYellowLight, radius 0.022), E-F, E-T. Layering: rods of the crank arm, Cp-A, Cp-E and E-F/E-T sit on the outer layer (x offset +0.04 away from the mid-plane, so for negative x planes offset toward -x); all other rods sit on the plane x. Every node gets a jointBlack ball (r 0.032; r 0.04 at P, Cp and K), brass crank pin, a steel crank hub disc (cylinder r 0.06 along x) at C, and zipBlack ties (small boxes) at the nodes. Foot: sandPad sphere r 0.08 centred on T with a flatter sandDark disc cap under it, a capOrange bottle-cap ring above and a short tapeBlue wrap on the shank above it. Bones: hipXX0/1 own the P-A, P-D, A-D, D-K, A-K, upper rods; shankXX0/1 own the shank K-T below F, E-F, E-T and the foot (names hipFL0 shankFL0 hipFL1 shankFL1 hipFR0 shankFR0 hipFR1 shankFR1). Feet bottoms on y=0.
parts.attaches: Hangs on the pivotF axle (frame) at P and wraps the crankF shaft at C (hub sits on the shaft).

parts.builds: Identical copy of the front legs, on the REAR crankshaft (C = crankR = [x, 1.2, -1.0]), same four planes x = +0.5, +1.0, -0.5, -1.0, same direction of travel (+Z). Exact planar linkage in leg-local coordinates (u = world z offset from the axle, v = world y offset from y=1.2, x = plane x): C(0,0) crank axle; Cp(0.10,-0.11) crank pin; P(-0.38,0.08) fixed pivot (world [x,1.28,-1.38] on pivotR); A(-0.35,-0.33); D(-0.62,-0.17); K(-0.52,-0.60); E(0.18,-0.62); F(-0.14,-0.91); T(0.12,-1.12) (world y 0.08). World point = [x, 1.2+v, -1.0+u]. Rods (pvcYellow, radius 0.018, flat caps): crank arm C-Cp (brass, r 0.022, outer layer), P-A, Cp-A, P-D, A-D, D-K, A-K, Cp-E, A-E, shank K-T through F (pvcYellowLight, r 0.022), E-F, E-T. Outer layer (offset 0.04 away from the mid-plane in x): crank arm, Cp-A, Cp-E, E-F, E-T; the rest on the plane. jointBlack balls (r 0.032; 0.04 at P, Cp, K) at every node, brass crank pin, steel hub disc (r 0.06 along x) at C, zipBlack ties at nodes. Foot: sandPad sphere r 0.08 at T, sandDark flat disc below, capBlue ring cap above (blue instead of orange, to read as the rear set), tapeBlue wrap on the shank. Bones: hip/shank joints named hipRL0 shankRL0 hipRL1 shankRL1 hipRR0 shankRR0 hipRR1 shankRR1 with the same ownership split as the front legs (upper rods on hip, shank/E-F/E-T/foot on shank). Feet bottoms on y=0.
parts.attaches: Hangs on the pivotR axle (frame) at P and wraps the crankR shaft at C.

parts.builds: Two mirrored bottle-sail wings (left joint sailL / sailTipL at +x, right sailR / sailTipR at -x), each rising from its wingRoot mount (+-0.45,1.95,0) to its wingTip mount (+-1.3,2.25,0): a dihedral of about 19 degrees. Each wing: a root spar and a tip spar (pvcYellow tubes radius 0.025) running along z from -1.4 to +1.4, a leading and trailing edge tube joining them at z=+-1.4, jointBlack corner balls, and a centre rib. Between the spars a row of 14 translucent bottleBlue bottles (lathe or tapered cylinder, radius 0.085, length 0.8 along the span direction, 8 segments, with a bottleBlueDeep shoulder ring and a cap alternating capBlue and capOrange at the outer end) are strapped side by side along z, with sailWhite cloth triangles (thin extrudes, sailShade on their lower faces) stretched between bottle pairs on the trailing side, rope (rope colour) lashing bands and zipBlack ties around every bottle at the spars, and an accentRed pennant on each tip. The inner half of each wing rides sailL / sailR, the outer half rides sailTipL / sailTipR. Keep the top at y<=2.3 and the width at x=+-1.3.
parts.attaches: Wing roots hinge on the mast stub blocks at wingRootL/R (built by the frame).

parts.builds: Three self-contained pieces on the body line. (1) HEAD starting at mount headBase [0,1.65,1.75], joint head, extending to z=2.2: a yellow tube skull frame (a diamond of rods radius 0.025, jointBlack balls) with a bottleBlue bottle as the muzzle forming a rigid upper jaw (cap capOrange at the tip, rope bands) and a separate lower jaw of two yellow tubes plus a smaller bottle on joint jaw (hinge at [0,1.6,1.95]); two big bottle eyes on the sides at x=+-0.13: eyeWhite spheres r 0.07 with pupil discs and a tapeBlue ring, capOrange brow caps above; two long thin feeler rods (pvcYellowLight, r 0.012) swept up and forward from the brow with jointBlack ball tips; an accentRed tape band across the skull. (2) TAIL starting at tailBase [0,1.65,-1.75], joints tail1 tail2 tail3, three tapering yellow tubes (radius 0.03 to 0.015) running back to z=-2.2 with jointBlack knuckles and zipBlack ties, ending in a small sailWhite triangular windvane (extrude) with an accentRed edge. (3) BELLY BANK centred at bellyBankCenter [0,1.25,0] on joint body: 2 rows x 4 bottleBlue pressure bottles lying along z (radius 0.07, length 0.28, capBlue caps at the rear, 8 segments) at x=+-0.14, y=1.25 and y=1.25 stacked rows at z=-0.55..0.55, strapped with rope bands and a hose of thin zipBlack tube linking the caps to a small steel pump cylinder, hung from the rails (ties up to railL/railR at y=1.45). Keep the bank clear of the legs (|x|<0.3 only).
parts.attaches: Head and tail start exactly at headBase / tailBase where the frame truss ends; the belly bank hangs from the lower rails at railL/railR.

On the frame's back half stands a tall rig: a central mast and two spread triangular wing-sails of pale paper on tube ribs, topping out at y=2.4. In front of the mast, over the frame's middle, sits a standing rack of translucent blue pressure bottles with red caps, joined by a manifold of thin tubes. All structure is chunky round PVC tube in yellow, with darker end-sleeves and elbow connectors at each junction. Tiny black cable-tie boxes and silver bolts sit at joints. spec.name: Strandbeest Tube Walker
spec.description: A Theo Jansen style kinetic beach creature: a spine of yellow tubes carried on twelve linkage legs with a sail wing, standing in rest pose.
spec.layout: Long low creature facing +Z. A central yellow tube frame (two parallel main rails, crossbars and a pair of crank shafts) sits at y 1.0-1.5. Six Jansen linkage legs per side hang below it, each a triangulated set of thin tubes ending in a rounded foot on y=0, with joints capped by small white nylon-sleeve connectors. At the front a rounded tube head with two big round eyes and a separate upper and lower jaw. At the back a tail of tapering tubes with a fan of sail-cloth wing panels on a tube mast. Every piece is a plain yellow, white or grey tube, rod, sleeve or flat sail panel, giving a bare kinetic sculpture look.

parts.builds: The central yellow tube chassis: two main rails, crossbars every 0.4 m, a diagonal bracing lattice, the steel crank shaft with offset crank arms, white sleeve connectors at every crossing, and the top ridge tube.
parts.attaches: Carries all other parts at frameCenter, frameFront, frameBack, mastBase, legHipL, legHipR and crankShaft.

parts.builds: Six Jansen linkage legs on the model's left (+X): each a triangulated set of thin yellow tubes (upper link, two thigh links, shin, ankle) with white sleeve joints, steel pivot pins, a dark yellow brace and a rounded black foot. Staggered phases so the feet are spread along z and alternately lifted a few cm, with the lowest feet resting on y=0.
parts.attaches: Hips at legHipL, riding the crankShaft line, hung off the frame rails.

parts.builds: Mirror of the left legs on the model's right (-X): six linkage legs with the same tube, sleeve, pin and foot construction, phase offset by half a cycle from the left side.
parts.attaches: Hips at legHipR, hung off the frame rails.

parts.builds: Front creature head: a neck tube, a rounded yellow tube-loop skull, two large round white eyes with black pupils on tube stalks, a separate upper jaw and lower jaw (flat-ish tube frames with white sleeve teeth), and two forward antenna tubes with red ribbon tips.
parts.attaches: Neck begins at headMount / frameFront; neck, head and jaw joints.

parts.builds: Rear section: a tapering two-segment tube tail with sleeve joints and a small steel foot-rest tip, plus a vertical tube mast at mastBase carrying a fan of cream sail-cloth panels (flat extrudes, alternating cream and shade tones) on spar tubes, with red ribbon streamers and cord tubes back to the tail.
parts.attaches: Tail joints from frameBack; mast on mastBase.
